question: A company needs to optimize the cost of its Amazon EC2 instances. The company also needs to change the type and family of its EC2 instances every 23 months. What should the company do to meet these requirements?

options.A: Purchase Partial Upfront Reserved Instances for a 3-year term.
options.B: Purchase a No Upfront Compute Savings Plan for a 1-year term.
options.C: Purchase All Upfront Reserved Instances for a 1-year term.
options.D: Purchase an All Upfront EC2 Instance Savings Plan for a 1-year term.

declencheurs: change type and family every 23 months
radar.signal: Besoin de changer type/famille + horizon 1 an -> Savings Plan 1 an (All Upfront = remise max), PAS de Reserved 3 ans fige

pieges.A: RI 3 ans = engagement fige, impossible de changer de famille pendant 3 ans
pieges.B: Compute SP No Upfront = flexible mais remise plus faible que All Upfront
pieges.C: RI 1 an = lie a un type d'instance precis, moins souple qu'un Savings Plan

explication: On veut le maximum d'economies (All Upfront) tout en gardant la liberte de changer de famille tous les ~2 ans. Un terme de 1 an permet de re-acheter un plan adapte a la nouvelle famille au renouvellement, alors qu'un Reserved 3 ans verrouille. L'EC2 Instance Savings Plan All Upfront (D) donne la remise la plus forte compatible avec ce cycle.

question: A solutions architect needs to review a company's Amazon S3 buckets to discover personally identifiable information (PII). The company stores the PII data in the us-east-1 Region and us-west-2 Region. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.A: Configure Amazon Macie in each Region. Create a job to analyze the data that is in Amazon S3.
options.B: Configure AWS Security Hub for all Regions. Create an AWS Config rule to analyze the data that is in Amazon S3.
options.C: Configure Amazon Inspector to analyze the data that is in Amazon S3.
options.D: Configure Amazon GuardDuty to analyze the data that is in Amazon S3.

radar.signal: PII + S3 + decouvrir -> Amazon Macie ; multi-Region -> configurer Macie dans chaque Region

pieges.B: Security Hub agrege la posture de securite, ne scanne pas le contenu PII
pieges.C: Inspector = vulnerabilites EC2/containers, pas le contenu S3
pieges.D: GuardDuty = detection de menaces via logs, ne classifie pas les PII

explication: Amazon Macie est LE service manage de decouverte et classification de donnees sensibles (PII) dans S3. Comme Macie est regional, on l'active dans us-east-1 ET us-west-2. C'est la solution avec le moins d'overhead operationnel car entierement gere.

question: A company runs a stateless web application in production on a group of Amazon EC2 On-Demand Instances behind an Application Load Balancer. The application experiences heavy usage during an 8-hour period each business day. Application usage is moderate and steady overnight. Application usage is low during weekends. The company wants to minimize its EC2 costs without affecting the availability of the application. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Use Spot Instances for the entire workload.
options.B: Use Reserved Instances for the baseline level of usage. Use Spot instances for any additional capacity that the application needs.
options.C: Use On-Demand Instances for the baseline level of usage. Use Spot Instances for any additional capacity that the application needs.
options.D: Use Dedicated Instances for the baseline level of usage. Use On-Demand Instances for any additional capacity that the application needs.

radar.signal: Charge de base previsible -> Reserved Instances ; pics variables + app stateless -> Spot

pieges.A: Spot pour TOUT = risque d'interruption sur la charge de base -> dispo affectee
pieges.C: On-Demand en base = plus cher que Reserved pour une charge previsible
pieges.D: Dedicated = tres couteux, inutile ici

explication: On couvre la charge de base constante avec des Reserved Instances (remise sur usage garanti) et on absorbe les pics avec des Spot (les moins chers). L'application etant stateless, une interruption Spot sur la capacite supplementaire n'affecte pas la disponibilite.

question: A company needs to retain application log files for a critical application for 10 years. The application team regularly accesses logs from the past month for troubleshooting, but logs older than 1 month are rarely accessed. The application generates more than 10 TB of logs per month. Which storage option meets these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

options.A: Store the logs in Amazon S3. Use AWS Backup to move logs more than 1 month old to S3 Glacier Deep Archive.
options.B: Store the logs in Amazon S3. Use S3 Lifecycle policies to move logs more than 1 month old to S3 Glacier Deep Archive.
options.C: Store the logs in Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Use AWS Backup to move logs more than 1 month old to S3 Glacier Deep Archive.
options.D: Store the logs in Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Use Amazon S3 Lifecycle policies to move logs more than 1 month old to S3 Glacier Deep Archive.

radar.signal: Archivage long + acces rare -> S3 Glacier Deep Archive ; transition auto -> S3 Lifecycle (natif, pas AWS Backup)

pieges.A: AWS Backup ne gere pas la transition S3->Glacier (mauvais outil pour du lifecycle S3)
pieges.C: CloudWatch Logs = stockage long tres couteux pour 10 To/mois
pieges.D: Idem CloudWatch Logs couteux + lifecycle ne s'applique pas ainsi

explication: Stocker dans S3 puis laisser une S3 Lifecycle policy basculer automatiquement les logs > 1 mois vers Glacier Deep Archive (le stockage le moins cher pour archivage 10 ans a acces rare). Lifecycle est natif et gratuit, contrairement a AWS Backup qui n'est pas concu pour ces transitions.

question: A company is planning to migrate a TCP-based application into the company VPC. The application is publicly accessible on a nonstandard TCP port through a hardware appliance in the company's data center. This public endpoint can process up to 3 million requests per second with low latency. The company requires the same level of performance for the new public endpoint in AWS. What should a solutions architect recommend to meet this requirement?

options.A: Deploy a Network Load Balancer (NLB). Configure the NLB to be publicly accessible over the TCP port that the application requires.
options.B: Deploy an Application Load Balancer (ALB). Configure the ALB to be publicly accessible over the TCP port that the application requires.
options.C: Deploy an Amazon CloudFront distribution that listens on the TCP port that the application requires. Use an Application Load Balancer as the origin.
options.D: Deploy an Amazon API Gateway API that is configured with the TCP port that the application requires. Configure AWS Lambda functions with provisioned concurrency to process the requests.

radar.signal: TCP/UDP niveau 4 + tres haut debit + faible latence -> Network Load Balancer

pieges.B: ALB = HTTP/HTTPS niveau 7, ne gere pas un port TCP arbitraire, moins performant
pieges.C: CloudFront = HTTP/S avec cache, pas du TCP brut
pieges.D: API Gateway/Lambda = HTTP, ne soutient pas ce debit L4

explication: Le Network Load Balancer opere au niveau 4 (TCP/UDP), gere les ports non standard, et soutient des millions de requetes/seconde a tres faible latence. C'est le seul choix compatible avec un endpoint TCP public ultra-performant.

question: A company runs its critical database on an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance. The company wants to migrate to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL with minimal downtime and data loss. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.A: Create a DB snapshot of the RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance to populate a new Aurora PostgreSQL DB cluster.
options.B: Create an Aurora read replica of the RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance. Promote the Aurora read replica to a new Aurora PostgreSQL DB cluster.
options.C: Use data import from Amazon S3 to migrate the database to an Aurora PostgreSQL DB cluster.
options.D: Use the pg-dump utility to back up the RDS for PostgreSQL database. Restore the backup to a new Aurora PostgreSQL DB cluster.

radar.signal: Migration RDS->Aurora meme moteur, downtime minimal -> creer un read replica Aurora puis le promouvoir

pieges.A: Snapshot = downtime + perte des ecritures posterieures au snapshot
pieges.C: Import S3 = complexe et avec interruption
pieges.D: pg_dump = manuel, downtime et risque de perte de donnees

explication: Creer un read replica Aurora de l'instance RDS PostgreSQL le synchronise en continu ; il suffit ensuite de le promouvoir en cluster Aurora autonome. Bascule quasi sans interruption ni perte de donnees, et peu d'operations manuelles.

question: A company stores multiple Amazon Machine Images (AMIs) in an AWS account to launch its Amazon EC2 instances. The AMIs contain critical data and configurations that are necessary for the company operations. The company wants to implement a solution that will recover accidentally deleted AMIs quickly and efficiently. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.A: Create Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) snapshots of the AMIs. Store the snapshots in a separate AWS account.
options.B: Copy all AMIs to another AWS account periodically.
options.C: Create a retention rule in Recycle Bin.
options.D: Upload the AMI to an Amazon S3 bucket that has Cross-Region Replication.

radar.signal: Recuperer des AMIs/snapshots supprimes par erreur -> regle de retention dans Recycle Bin

pieges.A: Snapshots EBS dans un autre compte = mise en place et gestion manuelles
pieges.B: Copie periodique inter-comptes = overhead eleve
pieges.D: Upload S3 + CRR = complexe et non concu pour l'undelete d'AMI

explication: Recycle Bin permet de definir une regle de retention sur les AMIs (et snapshots) : une AMI supprimee par erreur reste recuperable pendant la periode definie, sans aucune copie ni automatisation a maintenir. C'est le minimum d'overhead.

question: A company has 150 TB of archived image data stored on-premises that needs to be moved to the AWS Cloud within the next month. The company's current network connection allows up to 100 Mbps uploads for this purpose during the night only. What is the MOST cost-effective mechanism to move this data and meet the migration deadline?

options.A: Use AWS Snowmobile to ship the data to AWS.
options.B: Order multiple AWS Snowball devices to ship the data to AWS.
options.C: Enable Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration and securely upload the data.
options.D: Create an Amazon S3 VPC endpoint and establish a VPN to upload the data.

radar.signal: Gros volume + reseau insuffisant + deadline -> transfert physique. Pour ~150 To -> Snowball (env. 80 To/appareil, 2 appareils)

pieges.C: Transfer Acceleration depend du reseau 100 Mbps -> bien plus d'un mois
pieges.D: VPN sur 100 Mbps -> trop lent (>4 mois)
pieges.A: Snowmobile = echelle Petaoctet (100 Po), surdimensionne pour 150 To

alerte_cle: La cle du fichier indique A (Snowmobile), mais pour 150 To le bon choix standard est B (Snowball). Snowmobile ne se justifie qu'a l'echelle petaoctet.
explication: A 100 Mbps la nuit, transferer 150 To prend > 4 mois : le reseau est exclu. Il faut un transfert physique. 150 To correspond a environ 2 appareils Snowball (~80 To utiles chacun) : c'est la solution rentable et dans les delais. AWS Snowmobile est reserve aux migrations petaoctet (jusqu'a 100 Po) et serait surdimensionne/plus couteux ici.

question: A company has a static website that is hosted on Amazon CloudFront in front of Amazon S3. The static website uses a database backend. The company notices that the website does not reflect updates that have been made in the website's Git repository. The company checks the continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) pipeline between the Git repository and Amazon S3. The company verifies that the webhooks are configured properly and that the CI/CD pipeline is sending messages that indicate successful deployments. A solutions architect needs to implement a solution that displays the updates on the website. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Add an Application Load Balancer.
options.B: Add Amazon ElastiCache for Redis or Memcached to the database layer of the web application.
options.C: Invalidate the CloudFront cache.
options.D: Use AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) to validate the website's SSL certificate.

radar.signal: Contenu perime derriere CloudFront alors que le deploiement reussit -> invalider le cache CloudFront

pieges.A: ALB = repartition de charge, sans rapport avec le cache
pieges.B: ElastiCache = cache base de donnees, pas le CDN
pieges.D: ACM = certificat SSL, hors sujet

explication: Le pipeline pousse bien les fichiers vers S3, mais CloudFront sert encore la version en cache. Invalider le cache CloudFront (ou reduire le TTL) force la distribution a recuperer la version a jour depuis S3.

question: A company wants to migrate a Windows-based application from on premises to the AWS Cloud. The application has three tiers: an application tier, a business tier, and a database tier with Microsoft SQL Server. The company wants to use specific features of SQL Server such as native backups and Data Quality Services. The company also needs to share files for processing between the tiers. How should a solutions architect design the architecture to meet these requirements?

options.A: Host all three tiers on Amazon EC2 instances. Use Amazon FSx File Gateway for file sharing between the tiers.
options.B: Host all three tiers on Amazon EC2 instances. Use Amazon FSx for Windows File Server for file sharing between the tiers.
options.C: Host the application tier and the business tier on Amazon EC2 instances. Host the database tier on Amazon RDS. Use Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) for file sharing between the tiers.
options.D: Host the application tier and the business tier on Amazon EC2 instances. Host the database tier on Amazon RDS. Use a Provisioned IOPS SSD (io2) Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume for file sharing between the tiers.

radar.signal: Fonctions SQL Server non supportees par RDS (native backups, DQS) -> SQL sur EC2 ; partage de fichiers Windows/SMB -> FSx for Windows File Server

pieges.A: FSx File Gateway = passerelle on-prem vers le cloud, pas un partage inter-tiers
pieges.C: RDS ne supporte pas DQS/native backups ; EFS = NFS/Linux
pieges.D: EBS = volume attache a une seule instance, pas un partage multi-tiers

explication: Data Quality Services et les native backups SQL Server ne sont pas disponibles sur Amazon RDS : il faut heberger SQL Server sur EC2. Pour partager des fichiers entre tiers Windows (protocole SMB), Amazon FSx for Windows File Server est le service manage adapte.

question: A company is developing a real-time multiplayer game that uses UDP for communications between the client and servers in an Auto Scaling group. Spikes in demand are anticipated during the day, so the game server platform must adapt accordingly. Developers want to store gamer scores and other non-relational data in a database solution that will scale without intervention. Which solution should a solutions architect recommend?

options.A: Use Amazon Route 53 for traffic distribution and Amazon Aurora Serverless for data storage.
options.B: Use a Network Load Balancer for traffic distribution and Amazon DynamoDB on-demand for data storage.
options.C: Use a Network Load Balancer for traffic distribution and Amazon Aurora Global Database for data storage.
options.D: Use an Application Load Balancer for traffic distribution and Amazon DynamoDB global tables for data storage.

radar.signal: UDP -> Network Load Balancer (seul LB gerant UDP) ; NoSQL a scaling automatique sans gestion -> DynamoDB on-demand

pieges.A: Route 53 ne fait pas de repartition L4 UDP fine ; Aurora = relationnel
pieges.C: Aurora Global = relationnel
pieges.D: ALB = HTTP/HTTPS, pas UDP

explication: Un jeu multijoueur temps reel en UDP impose un Network Load Balancer (l'ALB ne gere pas UDP). Pour des donnees non relationnelles qui montent en charge lors des pics sans intervention, DynamoDB en mode on-demand s'adapte automatiquement.

question: A company hosts a frontend application that uses an Amazon API Gateway API backend that is integrated with AWS Lambda. When the API receives requests, the Lambda function loads many libraries. Then the Lambda function connects to an Amazon RDS database, processes the data, and returns the data to the frontend application. The company wants to ensure that response latency is as low as possible for all its users with the fewest number of changes to the company operations. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Establish a connection between the frontend application and the database to make queries faster by bypassing the API.
options.B: Configure provisioned concurrency for the Lambda function that handles the requests.
options.C: Cache the results of the queries in Amazon S3 for faster retrieval of similar datasets.
options.D: Increase the size of the database to increase the number of connections Lambda can establish at one time.

radar.signal: Latence due au demarrage a froid (chargement des libs) -> provisioned concurrency (instances pre-chauffees), sans refonte

pieges.A: Bypass de l'API = refonte majeure + faille de securite
pieges.C: Cache S3 ne regle pas le cold start
pieges.D: Agrandir la DB ne cible pas la cause (le demarrage Lambda)

explication: Le chargement de nombreuses librairies allonge le cold start de la Lambda. La provisioned concurrency maintient des environnements deja initialises, supprimant la latence de demarrage a froid, avec un minimum de changements operationnels.

question: A company collects and shares research data with the company's employees all over the world. The company wants to collect and store the data in an Amazon S3 bucket and process the data in the AWS Cloud. The company will share the data with the company's employees. The company needs a secure solution in the AWS Cloud that minimizes operational overhead. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Use an AWS Lambda function to create an S3 presigned URL. Instruct employees to use the URL.
options.B: Create an IAM user for each employee. Create an IAM policy for each employee to allow S3 access. Instruct employees to use the AWS Management Console.
options.C: Create an S3 File Gateway. Create a share for uploading and a share for downloading. Allow employees to mount shares on their local computers to use S3 File Gateway.
options.D: Configure AWS Transfer Family SFTP endpoints. Select the custom identity provider options. Use AWS Secrets Manager to manage the user credentials. Instruct employees to use Transfer Family.

declencheurs: store in S3 + share with employees worldwide
radar.signal: Partage de fichiers securise et manage sur S3 -> AWS Transfer Family (SFTP), IdP custom + Secrets Manager pour les identifiants

pieges.A: Presigned URL = ephemere et par objet, gestion manuelle
pieges.B: Un IAM user par employe = overhead eleve, non scalable
pieges.C: S3 File Gateway = appliance a deployer et maintenir

explication: AWS Transfer Family fournit des endpoints SFTP entierement manages au-dessus de S3. Avec un fournisseur d'identite personnalise et Secrets Manager pour les identifiants, on obtient un partage securise a l'echelle mondiale avec peu d'overhead operationnel.

question: A company is building a new furniture inventory application. The company has deployed the application on a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances across multiple Availability Zones. The EC2 instances run behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB) in their VPC. A solutions architect has observed that incoming traffic seems to favor one EC2 instance, resulting in latency for some requests. What should the solutions architect do to resolve this issue?

options.A: Disable session affinity (sticky sessions) on the ALB.
options.B: Replace the ALB with a Network Load Balancer.
options.C: Increase the number of EC2 instances in each Availability Zone.
options.D: Adjust the frequency of the health checks on the ALB's target group.

radar.signal: Trafic concentre sur une instance derriere un ALB -> sticky sessions activees -> les desactiver pour repartir

pieges.B: Remplacer par un NLB ne corrige pas l'affinite de session
pieges.C: Ajouter des instances ne resout pas le desequilibre
pieges.D: La frequence des health checks n'est pas la cause

explication: Quand l'ALB envoie tout vers une seule instance, c'est le symptome des sticky sessions (session affinity) qui collent les clients a une cible. Les desactiver retablit une repartition equilibree du trafic.

question: A company collects data from a large number of participants who use wearable devices. The company stores the data in an Amazon DynamoDB table and uses applications to analyze the data. The data workload is constant and predictable. The company wants to stay at or below its forecasted budget for DynamoDB. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

options.A: Use provisioned mode and DynamoDB Standard-Infrequent Access (DynamoDB Standard-IA). Reserve capacity for the forecasted workload.
options.B: Use provisioned mode. Specify the read capacity units (RCUs) and write capacity units (WCUs).
options.C: Use on-demand mode. Set the read capacity units (RCUs) and write capacity units (WCUs) high enough to accommodate changes in the workload.
options.D: Use on-demand mode. Specify the read capacity units (RCUs) and write capacity units (WCUs) with reserved capacity.

radar.signal: Charge previsible + budget -> mode provisioned avec capacite reservee (le moins cher) ; acces peu frequent -> Standard-IA

pieges.B: Provisioned sans reservation = moins optimal que la capacite reservee
pieges.C: On-demand = plus cher pour une charge previsible
pieges.D: On-demand ne se combine pas avec de la capacite reservee (incoherent)

explication: Pour une charge constante et previsible, le mode provisioned avec capacite reservee offre le tarif le plus bas et respecte le budget. La classe Standard-IA reduit encore le cout de stockage pour des donnees a acces peu frequent.

question: A company stores confidential data in an Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL database in the ap-southeast-3 Region. The database is encrypted with an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) customer managed key. The company was recently acquired and must securely share a backup of the database with the acquiring company's AWS account in ap-southeast-3. What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

options.A: Create a database snapshot. Copy the snapshot to a new unencrypted snapshot. Share the new snapshot with the acquiring company's AWS account.
options.B: Create a database snapshot. Add the acquiring company's AWS account to the KMS key policy. Share the snapshot with the acquiring company's AWS account.
options.C: Create a database snapshot that uses a different AWS managed KMS key. Add the acquiring company's AWS account to the KMS key alias. Share the snapshot with the acquiring company's AWS account.
options.D: Create a database snapshot. Download the database snapshot. Upload the database snapshot to an Amazon S3 bucket. Update the S3 bucket policy to allow access from the acquiring company's AWS account.

radar.signal: Partager un snapshot chiffre KMS -> ajouter le compte cible a la KMS key policy, puis partager le snapshot

pieges.A: Snapshot non chiffre = viole les exigences (donnees confidentielles)
pieges.C: Une cle AWS managed ne se partage pas ; un alias n'accorde pas de permissions
pieges.D: Download/upload S3 = non supporte pour un snapshot RDS et non securise

explication: Pour partager un snapshot chiffre avec une customer managed key, il faut autoriser le compte destinataire dans la policy de la cle KMS, puis partager le snapshot. Le compte cible peut alors le restaurer tout en gardant le chiffrement.

question: A company needs to provide customers with secure access to its data. The company processes customer data and stores the results in an Amazon S3 bucket. All the data is subject to strong regulations and security requirements. The data must be encrypted at rest. Each customer must be able to access only their data from their AWS account. Company employees must not be able to access the data. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Provision an AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) certificate for each customer. Encrypt the data client-side. In the private certificate policy, deny access to the certificate for all principals except an IAM role that the customer provides.
options.B: Provision a separate AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key for each customer. Encrypt the data server-side. In the S3 bucket policy, deny decryption of data for all principals except an IAM role that the customer provides.
options.C: Provision a separate AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key for each customer. Encrypt the data server-side. In each KMS key policy, deny decryption of data for all principals except an IAM role that the customer provides.
options.D: Provision an AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) certificate for each customer. Encrypt the data client-side. In the public certificate policy, deny access to the certificate for all principals except an IAM role that the customer provides.

radar.signal: Isolation par client + chiffrement au repos + exclure les employes -> une cle KMS par client, chiffrement server-side, deny du dechiffrement dans la KMS key policy sauf le role IAM du client

pieges.A: ACM = certificats TLS, pas du chiffrement de donnees au repos
pieges.D: Idem ACM (certificat public) : hors sujet pour le chiffrement au repos S3
pieges.B: Le deny dans la bucket policy est moins robuste que dans la key policy pour bloquer le dechiffrement par les employes

alerte_cle: La cle du fichier indique D (ACM), mais ACM sert aux certificats TLS et ne chiffre pas les donnees au repos. La reponse AWS standard est C.
explication: Il faut une cle KMS distincte par client et un chiffrement server-side. En placant le deny du dechiffrement dans la KMS key policy (sauf le role IAM fourni par le client), meme les employes de l'entreprise ne peuvent pas lire les donnees. La key policy est le levier canonique pour exclure les employes ; la bucket policy (B) est moins fiable, et ACM (A/D) ne concerne pas le chiffrement au repos.

question: A solutions architect creates a VPC that includes two public subnets and two private subnets. A corporate security mandate requires the solutions architect to launch all Amazon EC2 instances in a private subnet. However, when the solutions architect launches an EC2 instance that runs a web server on ports 80 and 443 in a private subnet, no external internet traffic can connect to the server. What should the solutions architect do to resolve this issue?

options.A: Attach the EC2 instance to an Auto Scaling group in a private subnet. Ensure that the DNS record for the website resolves to the Auto Scaling group identifier.
options.B: Provision an Internet-facing Application Load Balancer (ALB) in a public subnet. Add the EC2 instance to the target group that is associated with the ALB. Ensure that the DNS record for the website resolves to the ALB.
options.C: Launch a NAT gateway in a private subnet. Update the route table for the private subnets to add a default route to the NAT gateway. Attach public Elastic IP address to the NAT gateway.
options.D: Ensure that the security group that is attached to the EC2 instance allows HTTP traffic on port 80 and HTTPS traffic on port 443. Ensure that the DNS record for the website resolves to the public IP address of the EC2 instance.

declencheurs: mandate: all EC2 in private subnet
radar.signal: Instance web imposee en subnet prive mais accessible depuis Internet -> ALB internet-facing en subnet public, instance dans le target group

pieges.A: Le DNS ne resout pas vers un Auto Scaling group ; ne rend pas l'instance joignable
pieges.C: Un NAT gateway va dans un subnet PUBLIC et gere le trafic sortant, pas l'entrant
pieges.D: Une instance en subnet prive n'a pas d'IP publique -> contredit le mandat et ne fonctionne pas

alerte_cle: La cle du fichier indique D, mais D exige une IP publique sur l'instance, ce qui viole l'obligation de la garder en subnet prive. La reponse correcte est B.
explication: Le mandat impose de garder l'EC2 en subnet prive. Pour l'exposer a Internet sans lui donner d'IP publique, on place un Application Load Balancer internet-facing dans un subnet public et on ajoute l'instance au target group ; le DNS pointe vers l'ALB. L'option D est incoherente car une instance en subnet prive n'a pas d'IP publique routable.

question: A company previously migrated its data warehouse solution to AWS. The company also has an AWS Direct Connect connection. Corporate office users query the data warehouse using a visualization tool. The average size of a query returned by the data warehouse is 50 MB and each webpage sent by the visualization tool is approximately 500 KB. Result sets returned by the data warehouse are not cached. Which solution provides the LOWEST data transfer egress cost for the company?

options.A: Host the visualization tool on premises and query the data warehouse directly over the internet.
options.B: Host the visualization tool in the same AWS Region as the data warehouse. Access it over the internet.
options.C: Host the visualization tool on premises and query the data warehouse directly over a Direct Connect connection at a location in the same AWS Region.
options.D: Host the visualization tool in the same AWS Region as the data warehouse and access it over a Direct Connect connection at a location in the same Region.

radar.signal: Minimiser l'egress -> heberger l'outil dans la meme Region que l'entrepot ET sortir via Direct Connect (egress DX < egress Internet)

pieges.A: On-prem + Internet = gros egress Internet sur les 50 Mo par requete
pieges.B: Meme Region mais sortie Internet = egress Internet plus cher que DX
pieges.C: On-prem : l'outil telecharge 50 Mo/requete depuis AWS = egress eleve

explication: Le gros volume sort de l'entrepot (50 Mo/requete). En hebergeant l'outil de visualisation dans la meme Region, seules de petites pages (500 Ko) quittent AWS, et en passant par Direct Connect le tarif d'egress est inferieur a celui d'Internet. D minimise donc le cout de transfert sortant.

question: An online learning company is migrating to the AWS Cloud. The company maintains its student records in a PostgreSQL database. The company needs a solution in which its data is available and online across multiple AWS Regions at all times. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST amount of operational overhead?

options.A: Migrate the PostgreSQL database to a PostgreSQL cluster on Amazon EC2 instances.
options.B: Migrate the PostgreSQL database to an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance with the Multi-AZ feature turned on.
options.C: Migrate the PostgreSQL database to an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance. Create a read replica in another Region.
options.D: Migrate the PostgreSQL database to an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance. Set up DB snapshots to be copied to another Region.

declencheurs: available and online across multiple Regions at all times
radar.signal: Donnees en ligne dans plusieurs Regions en permanence -> RDS for PostgreSQL + read replica cross-Region

pieges.A: Cluster PostgreSQL sur EC2 = auto-gere, overhead maximal
pieges.B: Multi-AZ = haute dispo dans UNE seule Region, pas multi-Region
pieges.D: Snapshots copies vers une autre Region = pas 'online', restauration necessaire

explication: Multi-AZ ne couvre qu'une Region ; les snapshots ne sont pas 'en ligne'. Un read replica cross-Region d'une instance RDS for PostgreSQL garde les donnees disponibles et interrogeables dans plusieurs Regions en continu, avec un service manage donc peu d'overhead.

question: A company is deploying a two-tier web application in a VPC. The web tier is using an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group with public subnets that span multiple Availability Zones. The database tier consists of an Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance in separate private subnets. The web tier requires access to the database to retrieve product information. The web application is not working as intended. The web application reports that it cannot connect to the database. The database is confirmed to be up and running. All configurations for the network ACLs, security groups, and route tables are still in their default states. What should a solutions architect recommend to fix the application?

options.A: Add an explicit rule to the private subnet network ACL to allow traffic from the web tier's EC2 instances.
options.B: Add a route in the VPC route table to allow traffic between the web tier's EC2 instances and the database tier.
options.C: Deploy the web tier's EC2 instances and the database tier's RDS instance into two separate VPCs, and configure VPC peering.
options.D: Add an inbound rule to the security group of the database tier's RDS instance to allow traffic from the web tier's security group.

radar.signal: Connexion inter-tiers bloquee alors que tout est par defaut -> le SG de la base ne laisse pas entrer le trafic du tier web : ajouter une regle inbound depuis le SG web

pieges.A: Les NACL par defaut autorisent deja tout le trafic
pieges.B: Le routage intra-VPC est implicite, aucune route a ajouter
pieges.C: Deux VPC + peering = sur-ingenierie inutile pour un meme VPC

explication: Dans un meme VPC, le routage est implicite et les NACL par defaut autorisent tout. Les security groups, eux, refusent tout en entree par defaut. Il faut donc ajouter au SG de l'instance RDS une regle inbound (port 3306) autorisant le SG du tier web. Referencer le SG source plutot qu'une plage d'IP respecte le moindre privilege.

question: A company has a large dataset for its online advertising business stored in an Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance in a single Availability Zone. The company wants business reporting queries to run without impacting the write operations on the production DB instance. Which solution meets these requirements?

options.A: Deploy RDS read replicas to process the business reporting queries.
options.B: Scale out the DB instance horizontally by placing it behind an Elastic Load Balancer.
options.C: Scale up the DB instance to a larger instance type to handle write operations and queries.
options.D: Deploy the DB instance in multiple Availability Zones to process the business reporting queries.

radar.signal: Decharger les lectures/reporting sans impacter les ecritures -> RDS read replica

pieges.B: On ne met pas une base RDS derriere un ELB pour scaler
pieges.C: Scaler verticalement ne separe pas lectures et ecritures
pieges.D: Multi-AZ = haute dispo (standby passif), le standby ne sert pas les requetes

explication: Un read replica RDS recoit une copie asynchrone de la base et absorbe les requetes de reporting sans peser sur l'instance de production. Attention au piege classique : le standby Multi-AZ n'est PAS interrogeable (c'est une bascule de haute dispo, pas une repartition de lecture).

question: A company wants to restrict access to the content of its web application. The company needs to protect the content by using authorization techniques that are available on AWS. The company also wants to implement a serverless architecture for authorization and authentication that has low login latency. The solution must integrate with the web application and serve web content globally. The application currently has a small user base, but the company expects the application's user base to increase. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Configure Amazon Cognito for authentication. Implement Lambda@Edge for authorization. Configure Amazon CloudFront to serve the web application globally.
options.B: Configure AWS Directory Service for Microsoft Active Directory for authentication. Implement AWS Lambda for authorization. Use an Application Load Balancer to serve the web application globally.
options.C: Configure Amazon Cognito for authentication. Implement AWS Lambda for authorization. Use Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration to serve the web application globally.
options.D: Configure AWS Directory Service for Microsoft Active Directory for authentication. Implement Lambda@Edge for authorization. Use AWS Elastic Beanstalk to serve the web application globally.

radar.signal: Auth serverless + latence faible + global -> Cognito (authentification) + Lambda@Edge (autorisation au bord) + CloudFront (diffusion mondiale)

pieges.B: Directory Service (AD) n'est pas serverless ; ALB ne diffuse pas globalement
pieges.C: S3 Transfer Acceleration accelere les uploads, ne diffuse pas une app ; Lambda simple n'est pas au bord
pieges.D: AD non serverless ; Beanstalk n'est pas mondial

explication: Cognito fournit une authentification managee et scalable. Lambda@Edge execute l'autorisation au plus pres de l'utilisateur (faible latence de login), et CloudFront sert le contenu mondialement. Tout est serverless et suit la montee en charge sans gestion de serveurs.

question: A development team uses multiple AWS accounts for its development, staging, and production environments. Team members have been launching large Amazon EC2 instances that are underutilized. A solutions architect must prevent large instances from being launched in all accounts. How can the solutions architect meet this requirement with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.A: Update the IAM policies to deny the launch of large EC2 instances. Apply the policies to all users.
options.B: Define a resource in AWS Resource Access Manager that prevents the launch of large EC2 instances.
options.C: Create an IAM role in each account that denies the launch of large EC2 instances. Grant the developers IAM group access to the role.
options.D: Create an organization in AWS Organizations in the management account with the default policy. Create a service control policy (SCP) that denies the launch of large EC2 instances, and apply it to the AWS accounts.

declencheurs: prevent launching large instances in all accounts
radar.signal: Interdiction transverse a plusieurs comptes -> Service Control Policy (SCP) dans AWS Organizations

pieges.A: Des IAM policies a maintenir dans chaque compte/utilisateur = overhead eleve
pieges.B: RAM sert a partager des ressources, pas a interdire des lancements
pieges.C: Un role IAM par compte = gestion repetitive

explication: Une SCP appliquee via AWS Organizations pose un garde-fou de permissions maximales sur tous les comptes membres d'un coup. Une seule policy centrale interdit le lancement de grosses instances partout, avec un overhead minimal comparé a la gestion de policies compte par compte.

question: A company is designing a containerized application that will use Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS). The application needs to access a shared file system that is highly durable and can recover data to another AWS Region with a recovery point objective (RPO) of 8 hours. The file system needs to provide a mount target in each Availability Zone within a Region. A solutions architect wants to use AWS Backup to manage the replication to another Region. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Amazon FSx for Windows File Server with a Multi-AZ deployment.
options.B: Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP with a Multi-AZ deployment.
options.C: Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) with the Standard storage class.
options.D: Amazon FSx for OpenZFS.

radar.signal: Partage multi-AZ + replication cross-Region geree par AWS Backup -> FSx for NetApp ONTAP Multi-AZ

pieges.A: FSx for Windows = SMB/Windows, non adapte a des conteneurs Linux ECS ici
pieges.C: EFS ne se replique pas cross-Region via AWS Backup dans ce scenario
pieges.D: FSx for OpenZFS = mono-AZ, pas de mount target par AZ ni replication AWS Backup

explication: FSx for NetApp ONTAP en Multi-AZ offre un systeme de fichiers partage tres durable avec un mount target dans chaque AZ, et s'integre a AWS Backup pour repliquer vers une autre Region en respectant un RPO de 8 heures. C'est le seul choix cochant toutes les cases.

question: A company is expecting rapid growth in the near future. A solutions architect needs to configure existing users and grant permissions to new users on AWS. The solutions architect has decided to create IAM groups. The solutions architect will add the new users to IAM groups based on department. Which additional action is the MOST secure way to grant permissions to the new users?

options.A: Apply service control policies (SCPs) to manage access permissions.
options.B: Create IAM roles that have least privilege permissions. Attach the roles to the IAM groups.
options.C: Create an IAM policy that grants least privilege permissions. Attach the policy to the IAM groups.
options.D: Create IAM roles. Associate the roles with a permissions boundary that defines the maximum permissions.

radar.signal: Accorder des permissions a des groupes IAM -> attacher une IAM policy de moindre privilege aux groupes

pieges.A: Les SCP s'appliquent aux comptes d'une organisation, pas a des groupes d'utilisateurs
pieges.B: On n'attache pas un role IAM a un groupe (les roles s'assument, ils ne s'attachent pas aux groupes)
pieges.D: Un permissions boundary limite un maximum mais n'accorde pas les permissions

explication: Les permissions se distribuent en attachant une policy de moindre privilege aux groupes IAM : chaque nouvel utilisateur ajoute au groupe herite automatiquement des droits. Les roles ne s'attachent pas aux groupes (ils s'assument), et un permissions boundary ne fait que plafonner sans octroyer.

question: A social media company runs its application on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The ALB is the origin for an Amazon CloudFront distribution. The application has more than a billion images stored in an Amazon S3 bucket and processes thousands of images each second. The company wants to resize the images dynamically and serve appropriate formats to clients. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.A: Install an external image management library on an EC2 instance. Use the image management library to process the images.
options.B: Create a CloudFront origin request policy. Use the policy to automatically resize images and to serve the appropriate format based on the User-Agent HTTP header in the request.
options.C: Use a Lambda@Edge function with an external image management library. Associate the Lambda@Edge function with the CloudFront behavior that serves the images.
options.D: Create a CloudFront response headers policy. Use the policy to automatically resize images and to serve the appropriate format based on the User-Agent HTTP header in the request.

declencheurs: billions of images / thousands per second
radar.signal: Redimensionnement/transformation dynamique d'images au bord -> Lambda@Edge avec une librairie de traitement d'images sur le comportement CloudFront

pieges.A: Librairie sur une EC2 = a gerer/scaler, overhead eleve
pieges.B: Une origin request policy CloudFront ne redimensionne pas d'images
pieges.D: Une response headers policy ne transforme pas le contenu (elle ne fait que gerer des en-tetes)

alerte_cle: La cle du fichier indique D, mais une CloudFront response headers policy ne redimensionne pas d'images (elle ne manipule que des en-tetes). La reponse correcte est C (Lambda@Edge).
explication: Le redimensionnement dynamique et le choix de format doivent s'executer dans le traitement de la requete : Lambda@Edge, associe au comportement CloudFront qui sert les images, execute une librairie de traitement au plus pres du client. Les policies CloudFront (origin request/response headers) ne transforment pas le corps des images : ce sont des distracteurs.

question: A hospital needs to store patient records in an Amazon S3 bucket. The hospital's compliance team must ensure that all protected health information (PHI) is encrypted in transit and at rest. The compliance team must administer the encryption key for data at rest. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Create a public SSL/TLS certificate in AWS Certificate Manager (ACM). Associate the certificate with Amazon S3. Configure default encryption for each S3 bucket to use server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS). Assign the compliance team to manage the KMS keys.
options.B: Use the aws:SecureTransport condition on S3 bucket policies to allow only encrypted connections over HTTP (TLS). Configure default encryption for each S3 bucket to use server-side encryption with S3 managed encryption keys (SSE-S3). Assign the compliance team to manage the SSE-S3 keys.
options.C: Use the aws:SecureTransport condition on S3 bucket policies to allow only encrypted connections over HTTPS (TLS). Configure default encryption for each S3 bucket to use server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS). Assign the compliance team to manage the KMS keys.
options.D: Use the aws:SecureTransport condition on S3 bucket policies to allow only encrypted connections over HTTPS (TLS). Use Amazon Macie to protect the sensitive data that is stored in Amazon S3. Assign the compliance team to manage Macie.

declencheurs: PHI encrypted in transit AND at rest
radar.signal: Chiffrement en transit (HTTPS via aws:SecureTransport) + au repos avec cle administree par l'equipe -> SSE-KMS gere par l'equipe conformite

pieges.A: Un certificat ACM ne s'associe pas a S3 pour forcer le TLS
pieges.B: aws:SecureTransport concerne HTTPS (TLS) pas HTTP ; SSE-S3 n'est pas administrable par l'equipe
pieges.D: Macie decouvre les donnees sensibles, il ne chiffre pas au repos

explication: La condition aws:SecureTransport dans la bucket policy force les connexions HTTPS (chiffrement en transit). Pour le chiffrement au repos avec une cle que l'equipe conformite peut administrer, il faut SSE-KMS (les cles SSE-S3 ne sont pas gerables par le client). C repond aux deux exigences.

question: A company runs an on-premises application that is powered by a MySQL database. The company is migrating the application to AWS to increase the application's elasticity and availability. The current architecture shows heavy read activity on the database during times of normal operation. Every 4 hours, the company's development team pulls a full export of the production database to populate a database in the staging environment. During this period, users experience unacceptable application latency. The development team is unable to use the staging environment until the procedure completes. A solutions architect must recommend a replacement architecture that alleviates the application latency issue. The replacement architecture also must give the development team the ability to continue using the staging environment without delay. Which solution meets these requirements?

options.A: Use Amazon Aurora MySQL with Multi-AZ Aurora Replicas for production. Populate the staging database by implementing a backup and restore process that uses the mysqldump utility.
options.B: Use Amazon Aurora MySQL with Multi-AZ Aurora Replicas for production. Use database cloning to create the staging database on-demand.
options.C: Use Amazon RDS for MySQL with a Multi-AZ deployment and read replicas for production. Use the standby instance for the staging database.
options.D: Use Amazon RDS for MySQL with a Multi-AZ deployment and read replicas for production. Populate the staging database by implementing a backup and restore process that uses the mysqldump utility.

radar.signal: Rafraichir un environnement de staging sans impacter la prod -> Aurora MySQL + database cloning (copy-on-write, instantane, sans copie complete)

pieges.A: mysqldump = export complet couteux, reproduit le probleme de latence
pieges.C: Le standby Multi-AZ RDS n'est pas utilisable pour le staging
pieges.D: mysqldump sur RDS = meme charge lourde qu'aujourd'hui

explication: Le clonage de base Aurora cree une copie quasi instantanee via copy-on-write, sans lire/exporter tout le jeu de donnees : la production n'est pas sollicitee et l'equipe dev obtient un staging a la demande immediatement. Les approches mysqldump reproduiraient exactement la latence a resoudre.

question: A company is designing an application where users upload small files into Amazon S3. After a user uploads a file, the file requires one-time simple processing to transform the data and save the data in JSON format for later analysis. Each file must be processed as quickly as possible after it is uploaded. Demand will vary. On some days, users will upload a high number of files. On other days, users will upload a few files or no files. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.A: Configure Amazon EMR to read text files from Amazon S3. Run processing scripts to transform the data. Store the resulting JSON file in an Amazon Aurora DB cluster.
options.B: Configure Amazon S3 to send an event notification to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Use Amazon EC2 instances to read from the queue and process the data. Store the resulting JSON file in Amazon DynamoDB.
options.C: Configure Amazon S3 to send an event notification to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Use an AWS Lambda function to read from the queue and process the data. Store the resulting JSON file in Amazon DynamoDB.
options.D: Configure Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) to send an event to Amazon Kinesis Data Streams when a new file is uploaded. Use an AWS Lambda function to consume the event from the stream and process the data. Store the resulting JSON file in an Amazon Aurora DB cluster.

radar.signal: Traitement leger evenementiel a la charge variable -> S3 event -> SQS -> Lambda -> DynamoDB (serverless, decouple)

pieges.A: EMR = surdimensionne pour un petit traitement unitaire
pieges.B: EC2 a lire la file = serveurs a gerer et scaler
pieges.D: Kinesis + Aurora = trop lourd/complexe pour ce besoin simple

explication: Une notification d'evenement S3 vers SQS, consommee par une Lambda qui transforme et ecrit dans DynamoDB, donne une chaine entierement serverless : elle traite chaque fichier des l'upload, absorbe les pics et tombe a zero les jours creux, sans aucun serveur a administrer.

question: A company is running a highly sensitive application on Amazon EC2 backed by an Amazon RDS database. Compliance regulations mandate that all personally identifiable information (PII) be encrypted at rest. Which solution should a solutions architect recommend to meet this requirement with the LEAST amount of changes to the infrastructure?

options.A: Deploy AWS Certificate Manager to generate certificates. Use the certificate to encrypt the database volume.
options.B: Deploy AWS CloudHSM, generate encryption keys, and use the keys to encrypt database volumes.
options.C: Configure SSL encryption using AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) keys to encrypt database volumes.
options.D: Configure Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) encryption and Amazon RDS encryption with AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) keys to encrypt instance and database volumes.

radar.signal: Chiffrer au repos volumes EC2 et RDS avec le minimum de changement -> chiffrement EBS + chiffrement RDS via KMS

pieges.A: ACM = certificats TLS, ne chiffre pas un volume au repos
pieges.B: CloudHSM = surdimensionne et lourd a operer
pieges.C: SSL est du chiffrement en transit, pas au repos

explication: Le chiffrement au repos natif se fait en activant le chiffrement EBS (volumes EC2) et le chiffrement RDS, tous deux adosses a des cles KMS. C'est la solution avec le moins de changements d'infrastructure. ACM et SSL concernent le transit, et CloudHSM est disproportionne.

question: A company runs an AWS Lambda function in private subnets in a VPC. The subnets have a default route to the internet through an Amazon EC2 NAT instance. The Lambda function processes input data and saves its output as an object to Amazon S3. Intermittently, the Lambda function times out while trying to upload the object because of saturated traffic on the NAT instance's network. The company wants to access Amazon S3 without traversing the internet. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Replace the EC2 NAT instance with an AWS managed NAT gateway.
options.B: Increase the size of the EC2 NAT instance in the VPC to a network optimized instance type.
options.C: Provision a gateway endpoint for Amazon S3 in the VPC. Update the route tables of the subnets accordingly.
options.D: Provision a transit gateway. Place transit gateway attachments in the private subnets where the Lambda function is running.

radar.signal: Acceder a S3 sans passer par Internet/NAT -> gateway endpoint S3 + mise a jour des route tables

pieges.A: Un NAT gateway passe toujours par Internet et coute plus
pieges.B: Grossir la NAT instance ne supprime pas le trajet Internet
pieges.D: Transit gateway = interconnexion de VPC, hors sujet

explication: Un gateway endpoint pour S3 route le trafic vers S3 directement via le reseau AWS, en ajoutant une route dans les tables de routage des subnets. Le trafic S3 ne transite plus par la NAT instance saturee ni par Internet : plus de timeouts, et c'est gratuit.

question: A company runs an application on Amazon EC2 Linux instances across multiple Availability Zones. The application needs a storage layer that is highly available and Portable Operating System Interface (POSIX)-compliant. The storage layer must provide maximum data durability and must be shareable across the EC2 instances. The data in the storage layer will be accessed frequently for the first 30 days and will be accessed infrequently after that time. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

options.A: Use the Amazon S3 Standard storage class. Create an S3 Lifecycle policy to move infrequently accessed data to S3 Glacier.
options.B: Use the Amazon S3 Standard storage class. Create an S3 Lifecycle policy to move infrequently accessed data to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA).
options.C: Use the Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) Standard storage class. Create a lifecycle management policy to move infrequently accessed data to EFS Standard-Infrequent Access (EFS Standard-IA).
options.D: Use the Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) One Zone storage class. Create a lifecycle management policy to move infrequently accessed data to EFS One Zone-Infrequent Access (EFS One Zone-IA).

radar.signal: Partage POSIX multi-AZ, durabilite max -> EFS Standard + lifecycle vers EFS Standard-IA

pieges.A: S3 n'est pas POSIX ; Glacier n'est pas un systeme de fichiers montable
pieges.B: S3 n'est pas POSIX ni montable comme systeme de fichiers partage
pieges.D: EFS One Zone = une seule AZ -> durabilite/disponibilite moindres

explication: Le besoin POSIX + partage multi-AZ + durabilite maximale impose Amazon EFS en classe Standard (repartie sur plusieurs AZ). Une politique de cycle de vie bascule automatiquement les donnees non consultees vers EFS Standard-IA apres 30 jours, reduisant le cout. One Zone serait moins durable et moins disponible.

question: A solutions architect is creating a new VPC design. There are two public subnets for the load balancer, two private subnets for web servers, and two private subnets for MySQL. The web servers use only HTTPS. The solutions architect has already created a security group for the load balancer allowing port 443 from 0.0.0.0/0. Company policy requires that each resource has the least access required to be able to perform its tasks. Which additional configuration strategy should the solutions architect use to meet these requirements?

options.A: Create a security group for the web servers and allow port 443 from 0.0.0.0/0. Create a security group for the MySQL servers and allow port 3306 from the web servers' security group.
options.B: Create a network ACL for the web servers and allow port 443 from 0.0.0.0/0. Create a network ACL for the MySQL servers and allow port 3306 from the web servers' security group.
options.C: Create a security group for the web servers and allow port 443 from the load balancer. Create a security group for the MySQL servers and allow port 3306 from the web servers' security group.
options.D: Create a network ACL for the web servers and allow port 443 from the load balancer. Create a network ACL for the MySQL servers and allow port 3306 from the web servers' security group.

radar.signal: Moindre privilege par chainage de security groups -> web autorise 443 depuis le SG du LB, MySQL autorise 3306 depuis le SG web

pieges.A: 443 depuis 0.0.0.0/0 sur le web = trop ouvert, doit venir du LB seulement
pieges.B: Les NACL sont sans etat et ne referencent pas de security group
pieges.D: Idem : NACL ne peuvent pas referencer un security group source

explication: Le moindre privilege se realise en chainant les security groups par reference : le web n'accepte 443 que depuis le SG du load balancer, et MySQL n'accepte 3306 que depuis le SG du web. Les NACL sont sans etat et ne peuvent pas referencer un SG source, ce qui les disqualifie ici.

question: A company runs an application on several Amazon EC2 instances that store persistent data on an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. The company needs to replicate the data to another AWS Region by using an AWS managed service solution. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

options.A: Use the EFS-to-EFS backup solution to replicate the data to an EFS file system in another Region.
options.B: Run a nightly script to copy data from the EFS file system to an Amazon S3 bucket. Enable S3 Cross-Region Replication on the S3 bucket.
options.C: Create a VPC in another Region. Establish a cross-Region VPC peering. Run a nightly rsync to copy data from the original Region to the new Region.
options.D: Use AWS Backup to create a backup plan with a rule that takes a daily backup and replicates it to another Region. Assign the EFS file system resource to the backup plan.

radar.signal: Repliquer EFS cross-Region via un service manage -> AWS Backup (plan avec copie cross-Region)

pieges.A: La solution EFS-to-EFS backup est un ancien modele plus lourd/couteux
pieges.B: Script nocturne + S3 = auto-gere, pas un service manage
pieges.C: VPC peering + rsync = tres artisanal et couteux a maintenir

explication: AWS Backup gere nativement la sauvegarde d'EFS et la copie du backup vers une autre Region via un plan de sauvegarde. C'est un service entierement manage, sans scripts ni infrastructure a entretenir, donc l'option la plus rentable et la plus simple.

question: An ecommerce company is migrating its on-premises workload to the AWS Cloud. The workload currently consists of a web application and a backend Microsoft SQL database for storage. The company expects a high volume of customers during a promotional event. The new infrastructure in the AWS Cloud must be highly available and scalable. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST administrative overhead?

options.A: Migrate the web application to two Amazon EC2 instances across two Availability Zones behind an Application Load Balancer. Migrate the database to Amazon RDS for Microsoft SQL Server with read replicas in both Availability Zones.
options.B: Migrate the web application to an Amazon EC2 instance that runs in an Auto Scaling group across two Availability Zones behind an Application Load Balancer. Migrate the database to two EC2 instances across separate AWS Regions with database replication.
options.C: Migrate the web application to Amazon EC2 instances that run in an Auto Scaling group across two Availability Zones behind an Application Load Balancer. Migrate the database to Amazon RDS with Multi-AZ deployment.
options.D: Migrate the web application to three Amazon EC2 instances across three Availability Zones behind an Application Load Balancer. Migrate the database to three EC2 instances across three Availability Zones.

radar.signal: HA + scalable + peu d'admin -> web en Auto Scaling multi-AZ derriere ALB, base sur RDS Multi-AZ

pieges.A: Deux EC2 fixes = pas de scaling ; les read replicas ne sont pas de la HA
pieges.B: Base sur EC2 cross-Region = gestion manuelle lourde
pieges.D: Base sur 3 EC2 auto-gerees = overhead administratif eleve

explication: Un Auto Scaling group multi-AZ derriere un ALB rend le web hautement disponible et elastique pour absorber le pic promotionnel, tandis que RDS en Multi-AZ fournit une base geree et resiliente. C'est l'architecture avec le moins d'administration parmi les options.

question: A company has an on-premises volume backup solution that has reached its end of life. The company wants to use AWS as part of a new backup solution and wants to maintain local access to all the data while it is backed up on AWS. The company wants to ensure that the data backed up on AWS is automatically and securely transferred. Which solution meets these requirements?

options.A: Use AWS Snowball to migrate data out of the on-premises solution to Amazon S3. Configure on-premises systems to mount the Snowball S3 endpoint to provide local access to the data.
options.B: Use AWS Snowball Edge to migrate data out of the on-premises solution to Amazon S3. Use the Snowball Edge file interface to provide on-premises systems with local access to the data.
options.C: Use AWS Storage Gateway and configure a cached volume gateway. Run the Storage Gateway software appliance on premises and configure a percentage of data to cache locally. Mount the gateway storage volumes to provide local access to the data.
options.D: Use AWS Storage Gateway and configure a stored volume gateway. Run the Storage Gateway software appliance on premises and map the gateway storage volumes to on-premises storage. Mount the gateway storage volumes to provide local access to the data.

declencheurs: maintain local access to ALL data
radar.signal: Tout le jeu de donnees garde en local + sauvegarde vers AWS -> Storage Gateway en mode stored volume

pieges.A: Snowball = migration ponctuelle, on ne monte pas un endpoint S3 Snowball en continu
pieges.B: Snowball Edge = transfert ponctuel, pas une solution de backup continue
pieges.C: Le cached volume ne garde qu'une partie des donnees en local, pas tout

explication: Un stored volume gateway conserve l'integralite des donnees sur le stockage local (acces local a tout) et sauvegarde de maniere asynchrone et securisee des snapshots vers AWS. Le mode cached ne garderait qu'un sous-ensemble en local, ce qui ne satisfait pas l'exigence d'acces local a toutes les donnees.

question: An application that is hosted on Amazon EC2 instances needs to access an Amazon S3 bucket. Traffic must not traverse the internet. How should a solutions architect configure access to meet these requirements?

options.A: Create a private hosted zone by using Amazon Route 53.
options.B: Set up a gateway VPC endpoint for Amazon S3 in the VPC.
options.C: Configure the EC2 instances to use a NAT gateway to access the S3 bucket.
options.D: Establish an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection between the VPC and the S3 bucket.

radar.signal: Acces prive a S3 depuis un VPC -> gateway VPC endpoint pour S3

pieges.A: Une zone hebergee Route 53 gere du DNS, pas le chemin reseau vers S3
pieges.C: Un NAT gateway route justement via Internet
pieges.D: On n'etablit pas un VPN vers un bucket S3

explication: Le gateway VPC endpoint pour S3 ajoute une route privee vers S3 via le reseau AWS, sans passer par Internet et sans cout de transfert. Route 53 (DNS), NAT gateway (qui sort sur Internet) et VPN (inapplicable a S3) ne repondent pas au besoin.

question: A company hosts a multi-tier web application that uses an Amazon Aurora MySQL DB cluster for storage. The application tier is hosted on Amazon EC2 instances. The company IT security guidelines mandate that the database credentials be encrypted and rotated every 14 days. What should a solutions architect do to meet this requirement with the LEAST operational effort?

options.A: Create a new AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) encryption key. Use AWS Secrets Manager to create a new secret that uses the KMS key with the appropriate credentials. Associate the secret with the Aurora DB cluster. Configure a custom rotation period of 14 days.
options.B: Create two parameters in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store: one for the user name as a string parameter and one that uses the SecureString type for the password. Select AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) encryption for the password parameter, and load these parameters in the application tier. Implement an AWS Lambda function that rotates the password every 14 days.
options.C: Store a file that contains the credentials in an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) encrypted Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. Mount the EFS file system in all EC2 instances of the application tier. Restrict the access to the file on the file system so that the application can read the file and that only super users can modify the file. Implement an AWS Lambda function that rotates the key in Aurora every 14 days and writes new credentials into the file.
options.D: Store a file that contains the credentials in an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) encrypted Amazon S3 bucket that the application uses to load the credentials. Download the file to the application regularly to ensure that the correct credentials are used. Implement an AWS Lambda function that rotates the Aurora credentials every 14 days and uploads these credentials to the file in the S3 bucket.

declencheurs: database credentials encrypted and rotated every 14 days
radar.signal: Identifiants chiffres et rotation automatique -> AWS Secrets Manager (cle KMS + rotation planifiee) associe au cluster Aurora

pieges.B: Parameter Store SecureString + Lambda maison = rotation a coder/maintenir
pieges.C: Fichier sur EFS + Lambda = artisanal et lourd
pieges.D: Fichier sur S3 + Lambda + telechargement regulier = complexe et fragile

explication: AWS Secrets Manager stocke les identifiants chiffres par KMS et gere nativement la rotation automatique (ici tous les 14 jours) en s'integrant a Aurora. Les autres options exigent d'ecrire et de maintenir soi-meme la logique de rotation via Lambda, donc bien plus d'effort operationnel.

question: A company has deployed a web application on AWS. The company hosts the backend database on Amazon RDS for MySQL with a primary DB instance and five read replicas to support scaling needs. The read replicas must lag no more than 1 second behind the primary DB instance. The database routinely runs scheduled stored procedures. As traffic on the website increases, the replicas experience additional lag during periods of peak load. A solutions architect must reduce the replication lag as much as possible. The solutions architect must minimize changes to the application code and must minimize ongoing operational overhead. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Migrate the database to Amazon Aurora MySQL. Replace the read replicas with Aurora Replicas, and configure Aurora Auto Scaling. Replace the stored procedures with Aurora MySQL native functions.
options.B: Deploy an Amazon ElastiCache for Redis cluster in front of the database. Modify the application to check the cache before the application queries the database. Replace the stored procedures with AWS Lambda functions.
options.C: Migrate the database to a MySQL database that runs on Amazon EC2 instances. Choose large, compute optimized EC2 instances for all replica nodes. Maintain the stored procedures on the EC2 instances.
options.D: Migrate the database to Amazon DynamoDB. Provision a large number of read capacity units (RCUs) to support the required throughput, and configure on-demand capacity scaling. Replace the stored procedures with DynamoDB streams.

radar.signal: Reduire au maximum le lag de replication -> migrer vers Aurora MySQL (replication en quasi temps reel via stockage partage) + Aurora Auto Scaling

pieges.B: ElastiCache aide les lectures mais ne reduit pas le lag de replication et impose de reecrire l'app
pieges.C: MySQL auto-gere sur EC2 = overhead operationnel eleve
pieges.D: DynamoDB = refonte majeure du modele de donnees et du code

explication: Aurora MySQL partage un meme volume de stockage entre l'instance primaire et les Aurora Replicas, ce qui rend le lag de replication tres faible (quelques ms) meme en pic, avec Auto Scaling des replicas. La migration reste compatible MySQL, minimisant les changements de code face aux options DynamoDB ou EC2.

question: A company has an application that runs on Amazon EC2 instances in a private subnet. The application needs to process sensitive information from an Amazon S3 bucket. The application must not use the internet to connect to the S3 bucket. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Configure an internet gateway. Update the S3 bucket policy to allow access from the internet gateway. Update the application to use the new internet gateway.
options.B: Configure a VPN connection. Update the S3 bucket policy to allow access from the VPN connection. Update the application to use the new VPN connection.
options.C: Configure a NAT gateway. Update the S3 bucket policy to allow access from the NAT gateway. Update the application to use the new NAT gateway.
options.D: Configure a VPC endpoint. Update the S3 bucket policy to allow access from the VPC endpoint. Update the application to use the new VPC endpoint.

radar.signal: Acces prive a S3 sans Internet -> VPC endpoint (gateway) pour S3 + policy autorisant l'endpoint

pieges.A: Un internet gateway expose justement a Internet
pieges.B: Un VPN ne connecte pas a un service S3 regional
pieges.C: Un NAT gateway achemine le trafic via Internet

explication: Un VPC endpoint pour S3 permet aux instances d'un subnet prive d'atteindre S3 par le reseau interne AWS, sans jamais passer par Internet. La bucket policy peut restreindre l'acces a cet endpoint. Internet gateway, NAT gateway et VPN impliquent tous un chemin Internet ou sont inapplicables.

question: A company uses Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) to run a container application. The EKS cluster stores sensitive information in the Kubernetes secrets object. The company wants to ensure that the information is encrypted. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.A: Use the container application to encrypt the information by using AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS).
options.B: Enable secrets encryption in the EKS cluster by using AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS).
options.C: Implement an AWS Lambda function to encrypt the information by using AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS).
options.D: Use AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store to encrypt the information by using AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS).

radar.signal: Chiffrer les secrets Kubernetes sur EKS -> activer le chiffrement des secrets EKS (envelope encryption) avec KMS

pieges.A: Chiffrer dans l'app = code a ecrire et maintenir
pieges.C: Une Lambda de chiffrement = solution artisanale
pieges.D: Parameter Store deplace le probleme hors des secrets Kubernetes natifs

explication: EKS propose nativement le chiffrement enveloppe des objets Secret Kubernetes via une cle KMS : il suffit de l'activer sur le cluster. Aucune logique applicative ni service tiers a maintenir, d'ou l'overhead operationnel le plus faible.

question: A company has migrated a fleet of hundreds of on-premises virtual machines (VMs) to Amazon EC2 instances. The instances run a diverse fleet of Windows Server versions along with several Linux distributions. The company wants a solution that will automate inventory and updates of the operating systems. The company also needs a summary of common vulnerabilities of each instance for regular monthly reviews. What should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?

options.A: Set up AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager to manage all the EC2 instances. Configure AWS Security Hub to produce monthly reports.
options.B: Set up AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager to manage all the EC2 instances. Deploy Amazon Inspector, and configure monthly reports.
options.C: Set up AWS Shield Advanced, and configure monthly reports. Deploy AWS Config to automate patch installations on the EC2 instances.
options.D: Set up Amazon GuardDuty in the account to monitor all EC2 instances. Deploy AWS Config to automate patch installations on the EC2 instances.

radar.signal: Inventaire + patchs OS -> Systems Manager Patch Manager ; vulnerabilites (CVE) -> Amazon Inspector avec rapports mensuels

pieges.A: Security Hub agrege des findings mais ne scanne pas les vulnerabilites d'instance comme Inspector
pieges.C: Shield Advanced = protection DDoS, hors sujet
pieges.D: GuardDuty = detection de menaces, ne fait ni patch ni inventaire de vulnerabilites

explication: Systems Manager Patch Manager automatise l'inventaire et l'application des mises a jour sur les instances Windows et Linux. Amazon Inspector scanne en continu les vulnerabilites (CVE) et fournit les syntheses mensuelles demandees. Security Hub, Shield et GuardDuty ne couvrent pas ce couple inventaire+CVE.

question: A company hosts its application in the AWS Cloud. The application runs on Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group behind an Elastic Load Balancing (ELB) load balancer. The application connects to an Amazon DynamoDB table. For disaster recovery (DR) purposes, the company wants to ensure that the application is available from another AWS Region with minimal downtime. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST downtime?

options.A: Create an Auto Scaling group and an ELB in the DR Region. Configure the DynamoDB table as a global table. Configure DNS failover to point to the new DR Region's ELB.
options.B: Create an AWS CloudFormation template to create EC2 instances, ELBs, and DynamoDB tables to be launched when necessary. Configure DNS failover to point to the new DR Region's ELB.
options.C: Create an AWS CloudFormation template to create EC2 instances and an ELB to be launched when necessary. Configure the DynamoDB table as a global table. Configure DNS failover to point to the new DR Region's ELB.
options.D: Create an Auto Scaling group and an ELB in the DR Region. Configure the DynamoDB table as a global table. Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm with an evaluation period of 10 minutes to invoke an AWS Lambda function that updates Amazon Route 53 to point to the DR Region's ELB.

radar.signal: DR avec downtime minimal -> infra deja provisionnee dans la Region DR (ASG+ELB) + DynamoDB global table + bascule DNS (warm standby)

pieges.B: Creer l'infra via CloudFormation au moment du sinistre allonge le downtime
pieges.C: Provisionner EC2/ELB a la demande = plus de downtime qu'une infra deja prete
pieges.D: Attendre une alarme de 10 min + Lambda = downtime supplementaire evitable

explication: Pour minimiser le downtime, l'infrastructure de secours (Auto Scaling group + ELB) doit deja exister dans la Region DR, avec la table DynamoDB configuree en global table pour une replication multi-Region active. Un simple basculement DNS redirige alors le trafic quasi immediatement, contrairement aux options qui creent l'infra apres le sinistre.

question: A company is conducting an internal audit. The company wants to ensure that the data in an Amazon S3 bucket that is associated with the company AWS Lake Formation data lake does not contain sensitive customer or employee data. The company wants to discover personally identifiable information (PII) or financial information, including passport numbers and credit card numbers. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Configure AWS Audit Manager on the account. Select the Payment Card Industry Data Security Standards (PCI DSS) for auditing.
options.B: Configure Amazon S3 Inventory on the S3 bucket. Configure Amazon Athena to query the inventory.
options.C: Configure Amazon Macie to run a data discovery job that uses managed identifiers for the required data types.
options.D: Use Amazon S3 Select to run a report across the S3 bucket.

radar.signal: Decouvrir PII/donnees financieres dans S3 -> Amazon Macie avec identifiants manages

pieges.A: Audit Manager evalue la conformite (PCI DSS), il ne scanne pas le contenu pour trouver des PII
pieges.B: S3 Inventory + Athena listent/interrogent des metadonnees, pas la detection de PII
pieges.D: S3 Select interroge le contenu d'objets mais ne classifie pas les donnees sensibles

explication: Amazon Macie execute des jobs de decouverte de donnees en s'appuyant sur des identifiants manages pour de nombreux types sensibles (numeros de passeport, cartes de credit, etc.). C'est le service dedie a la detection de PII et d'informations financieres dans S3, contrairement a Audit Manager (conformite), S3 Inventory ou S3 Select.

question: A company uses on-premises servers to host its applications. The company is running out of storage capacity. The applications use both block storage and NFS storage. The company needs a high-performing solution that supports local caching without re-architecting its existing applications. Which combination of actions should a solutions architect take to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.A: Mount Amazon S3 as a file system to the on-premises servers.
options.B: Deploy an AWS Storage Gateway file gateway to replace NFS storage.
options.C: Deploy AWS Snowball Edge to provision NFS mounts to on-premises servers.
options.D: Deploy an AWS Storage Gateway volume gateway to replace the block storage.
options.E: Deploy Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) volumes and mount them to on-premises servers.

radar.signal: Etendre du stockage on-prem block + NFS avec cache local, sans changer l'app -> Storage Gateway file gateway (remplace NFS) + volume gateway (remplace le block)

pieges.A: Monter S3 comme systeme de fichiers n'est pas natif ni performant
pieges.C: Snowball Edge = transfert de donnees ponctuel, pas un cache continu
pieges.E: EFS ne se monte pas nativement sur des serveurs on-prem comme remplacement transparent

explication: Deux besoins distincts : le stockage NFS -> Storage Gateway file gateway, et le stockage block -> Storage Gateway volume gateway. Les deux offrent un cache local et s'adossent a S3 sans modifier les applications existantes. C'est pourquoi la reponse combine B et D.

question: A company deploys Amazon EC2 instances that run in a VPC. The EC2 instances load source data into Amazon S3 buckets so that the data can be processed in the future. According to compliance laws, the data must not be transmitted over the public internet. Servers in the company on-premises data center will consume the output from an application that runs on the EC2 instances. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Deploy an interface VPC endpoint for Amazon EC2. Create an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection between the company and the VPC.
options.B: Deploy a gateway VPC endpoint for Amazon S3. Set up an AWS Direct Connect connection between the on-premises network and the VPC.
options.C: Set up an AWS Transit Gateway connection from the VPC to the S3 buckets. Create an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection between the company and the VPC.
