options.D: Set up proxy EC2 instances that have routes to NAT gateways. Configure the proxy EC2 instances to fetch S3 data and feed the application instances.

radar.signal: S3 sans Internet -> gateway VPC endpoint S3 ; consommation on-prem privee -> AWS Direct Connect

pieges.A: Un interface endpoint pour EC2 ne concerne pas l'acces prive a S3
pieges.C: Transit Gateway ne fournit pas d'acces prive a S3 (service regional)
pieges.D: Des proxys via NAT gateway repassent par Internet

explication: Le gateway VPC endpoint garde le trafic vers S3 sur le reseau AWS (pas d'Internet public), conformement a la reglementation. Pour que le data center on-prem consomme la sortie sans passer par Internet, Direct Connect fournit une liaison privee dediee entre le site et le VPC.

question: A company has an application with a REST-based interface that allows data to be received in near-real time from a third-party vendor. Once received, the application processes and stores the data for further analysis. The application is running on Amazon EC2 instances. The third-party vendor has received many 503 Service Unavailable errors when sending data to the application. When the data volume spikes, the compute capacity reaches its maximum limit and the application is unable to process all requests. Which design should a solutions architect recommend to provide a more scalable solution?

options.A: Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to ingest the data. Process the data using AWS Lambda functions.
options.B: Use Amazon API Gateway on top of the existing application. Create a usage plan with a quota limit for the third-party vendor.
options.C: Use Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) to ingest the data. Put the EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer.
options.D: Repackage the application as a container. Deploy the application using Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) using the EC2 launch type with an Auto Scaling group.

radar.signal: Pics d'ingestion qui saturent le compute -> tampon Kinesis Data Streams + traitement Lambda (absorbe et scale)

pieges.B: API Gateway avec quota limite bride le vendeur au lieu de scaler
pieges.C: SNS est du pub/sub sans tampon durable comme Kinesis ; l'ASB aide mais moins elastique
pieges.D: ECS/EC2 en ASG scale mais reste limite par le compute EC2 face aux pics

explication: Les erreurs 503 viennent du compute sature pendant les pics. Kinesis Data Streams sert de tampon d'ingestion tres scalable qui decouple la reception du traitement ; des fonctions Lambda consomment le flux et montent en charge automatiquement. L'application ne rejette plus les requetes lors des pointes.

question: A company is migrating a Linux-based web server group to AWS. The web servers must access files in a shared file store for some content. The company must not make any changes to the application. What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

options.A: Create an Amazon S3 Standard bucket with access to the web servers.
options.B: Configure an Amazon CloudFront distribution with an Amazon S3 bucket as the origin.
options.C: Create an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. Mount the EFS file system on all web servers.
options.D: Configure a General Purpose SSD (gp3) Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume. Mount the EBS volume to all web servers.

radar.signal: Systeme de fichiers partage Linux (POSIX) sans changer l'app -> Amazon EFS monte sur tous les serveurs

pieges.A: S3 n'est pas un systeme de fichiers montable transparent (necessiterait des changements)
pieges.B: CloudFront+S3 sert du contenu web, ce n'est pas un partage de fichiers
pieges.D: Un volume EBS ne se partage pas simultanement entre plusieurs instances

explication: Amazon EFS fournit un systeme de fichiers partage POSIX que l'on monte sur tous les serveurs web Linux via NFS, sans modifier l'application. S3 imposerait de reecrire les acces, CloudFront ne partage pas de fichiers, et un volume EBS ne peut pas etre partage en ecriture par plusieurs instances.

question: A company has an AWS Lambda function that needs read access to an Amazon S3 bucket that is located in the same AWS account. Which solution will meet these requirements in the MOST secure manner?

options.A: Apply an S3 bucket policy that grants read access to the S3 bucket.
options.B: Apply an IAM role to the Lambda function. Apply an IAM policy to the role to grant read access to the S3 bucket.
options.C: Embed an access key and a secret key in the Lambda function's code to grant the required IAM permissions for read access to the S3 bucket.
options.D: Apply an IAM role to the Lambda function. Apply an IAM policy to the role to grant read access to all S3 buckets in the account.

declencheurs: Lambda needs read access to S3
radar.signal: Donner a une Lambda l'acces a S3 de facon securisee -> role IAM sur la Lambda avec une policy de moindre privilege sur CE bucket

pieges.A: Une bucket policy seule est moins ciblee que d'attacher l'autorisation au principal
pieges.C: Cles d'acces en dur dans le code = pratique interdite (fuite de secrets)
pieges.D: Accorder l'acces a TOUS les buckets viole le moindre privilege

explication: La bonne pratique consiste a attacher un role IAM d'execution a la Lambda, avec une policy accordant la lecture uniquement du bucket concerne. Cela evite tout secret en dur (C) et respecte le moindre privilege, contrairement a l'acces a tous les buckets (D).

question: A company hosts a web application on multiple Amazon EC2 instances. The EC2 instances are in an Auto Scaling group that scales in response to user demand. The company wants to optimize cost savings without making a long-term commitment. Which EC2 instance purchasing option should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?

options.A: Dedicated Instances only.
options.B: On-Demand Instances only.
options.C: A mix of On-Demand Instances and Spot Instances.
options.D: A mix of On-Demand Instances and Reserved Instances.

radar.signal: Reduire les couts sans engagement long -> melange On-Demand (base) + Spot (capacite supplementaire)

pieges.A: Dedicated Instances = les plus cheres
pieges.B: On-Demand seul ne fait aucune economie
pieges.D: Reserved Instances impliquent justement un engagement long terme

explication: Sans engagement long terme, les Reserved Instances sont exclues. Le meilleur compromis cout/disponibilite pour un Auto Scaling group est de couvrir la charge de base en On-Demand et d'ajouter de la capacite en Spot (jusqu'a 90% moins cher) pour les pics, l'app supportant les interruptions.

question: An entertainment company is using Amazon DynamoDB to store media metadata. The application is read intensive and experiencing delays. The company does not have staff to handle additional operational overhead and needs to improve the performance efficiency of DynamoDB without reconfiguring the application. What should a solutions architect recommend to meet this requirement?

options.A: Use Amazon ElastiCache for Redis.
options.B: Use Amazon DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX).
options.C: Replicate data by using DynamoDB global tables.
options.D: Use Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached with Auto Discovery enabled.

radar.signal: Accelerer des lectures DynamoDB sans changer l'app -> DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX), cache en memoire natif

pieges.A: ElastiCache Redis impose de reecrire l'app pour gerer le cache
pieges.C: Les global tables servent la replication multi-Region, pas la latence de lecture locale
pieges.D: ElastiCache Memcached impose aussi de modifier l'application

explication: DAX est un cache en memoire concu specifiquement pour DynamoDB : il s'intercale de facon quasi transparente (API compatible) et divise les temps de reponse en lecture par plusieurs ordres de grandeur, sans reecrire l'application ni gerer un cache externe comme ElastiCache.

question: A company infrastructure consists of Amazon EC2 instances and an Amazon RDS DB instance in a single AWS Region. The company wants to back up its data in a separate Region. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.A: Use AWS Backup to copy EC2 backups and RDS backups to the separate Region.
options.B: Use Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager (Amazon DLM) to copy EC2 backups and RDS backups to the separate Region.
options.C: Create Amazon Machine Images (AMIs) of the EC2 instances. Copy the AMIs to the separate Region. Create a read replica for the RDS DB instance in the separate Region.
options.D: Create Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) snapshots. Copy the EBS snapshots to the separate Region. Create RDS snapshots. Export the RDS snapshots to Amazon S3. Configure S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR) to the separate Region.

declencheurs: back up in a separate Region
radar.signal: Sauvegarde cross-Region de plusieurs services, sans effort -> AWS Backup (copie des backups EC2 et RDS vers l'autre Region)

pieges.B: DLM ne gere que les snapshots EBS/AMI, pas RDS de maniere unifiee
pieges.C: AMIs + read replica = manuel et melange sauvegarde et replication
pieges.D: Chaine EBS snapshots + export RDS vers S3 + CRR = beaucoup d'etapes a maintenir

explication: AWS Backup centralise et automatise la sauvegarde d'EC2 et de RDS et sait copier ces sauvegardes vers une autre Region depuis un plan unique. C'est nettement moins d'operations que d'assembler DLM, AMIs, exports RDS et replication S3 a la main.

question: A company hosts a data lake on Amazon S3. The data lake ingests data in Apache Parquet format from various data sources. The company uses multiple transformation steps to prepare the ingested data. The steps include filtering of anomalies, normalizing of date to standard date and time values, and generation of aggregates for analyses. The company must store the transformed data in S3 buckets that data analysts access. The company needs a prebuilt solution for data transformation that does not require code. The solution must provide data lineage and data profiling. The company needs to share the data transformation steps with employees throughout the company. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Configure an AWS Glue Studio visual canvas to transform the data. Share the transformation steps with employees by using AWS Glue jobs.
options.B: Configure Amazon EMR Serverless to transform the data. Share the transformation steps with employees by using EMR Serverless jobs.
options.C: Configure AWS Glue DataBrew to transform the data. Share the transformation steps with employees by using DataBrew recipes.
options.D: Create Amazon Athena tables for the data. Write Athena SQL queries to transform the data. Share the Athena SQL queries with employees.

radar.signal: Transformation sans code + lineage/profilage + partage des etapes -> AWS Glue DataBrew (recipes)

pieges.A: Glue Studio visuel genere du code (jobs Spark), moins no-code que DataBrew
pieges.B: EMR Serverless exige d'ecrire du code Spark
pieges.D: Athena impose d'ecrire du SQL

explication: AWS Glue DataBrew est l'outil no-code de preparation de donnees : il offre plus de 250 transformations pretes a l'emploi, le data lineage et le data profiling, et permet de partager les etapes sous forme de recipes reutilisables. Les autres options demandent d'ecrire du code Spark ou du SQL.

question: A solutions architect runs a web application on multiple Amazon EC2 instances that are in individual target groups behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). Users can reach the application through a public website. The solutions architect wants to allow engineers to use a development version of the website to access one specific development EC2 instance to test new features for the application. The solutions architect wants to use an Amazon Route 53 hosted zone to give the engineers access to the development instance. The solution must automatically route to the development instance even if the development instance is replaced. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Create an A Record for the development website that has the value set to the ALB. Create a listener rule on the ALB that forwards requests for the development website to the target group that contains the development instance.
options.B: Recreate the development instance with a public IP address. Create an A Record for the development website that has the value set to the public IP address of the development instance.
options.C: Create an A Record for the development website that has the value set to the ALB. Create a listener rule on the ALB to redirect requests for the development website to the public IP address of the development instance.
options.D: Place all the instances in the same target group. Create an A Record for the development website. Set the value to the ALB. Create a listener rule on the ALB that forwards requests for the development website to the target group.

radar.signal: Router un sous-domaine vers une instance de dev derriere un ALB, meme apres remplacement -> A record vers l'ALB + listener rule qui forwarde vers le target group de l'instance dev

pieges.B: Une IP publique fixe casse des que l'instance est remplacee
pieges.C: Un listener rule ne redirige pas vers une IP publique d'instance
pieges.D: Mettre toutes les instances dans le meme target group melange prod et dev

explication: On pointe le domaine de dev (A record) vers l'ALB, puis une listener rule route les requetes de ce host vers le target group contenant l'instance de dev. Comme le routage passe par le target group, remplacer l'instance ne casse rien, contrairement a un pointage direct sur une IP (B) qui devient invalide.

question: A solutions architect must provide an automated solution for a company compliance policy that states security groups cannot include a rule that allows SSH from 0.0.0.0/0. The company needs to be notified if there is any breach in the policy. A solution is needed as soon as possible. What should the solutions architect do to meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.A: Write an AWS Lambda script that monitors security groups for SSH being open to 0.0.0.0/0 addresses and creates a notification every time it finds one.
options.B: Enable the restricted-ssh AWS Config managed rule and generate an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) notification when a noncompliant rule is created.
options.C: Create an IAM role with permissions to globally open security groups and network ACLs. Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic to generate a notification every time the role is assumed by a user.
options.D: Configure a service control policy (SCP) that prevents non-administrative users from creating or editing security groups. Create a notification in the ticketing system when a user requests a rule that needs administrator permissions.

declencheurs: security group must not allow SSH from 0.0.0.0/0
radar.signal: Detecter automatiquement des SG non conformes + alerter, vite et sans code -> regle geree AWS Config restricted-ssh + notification SNS

pieges.A: Une Lambda maison = code a ecrire et maintenir
pieges.C: Un role + SNS sur assumption de role ne detecte pas les regles SG ouvertes
pieges.D: Une SCP bloque la creation mais ne detecte/notifie pas les violations existantes

explication: AWS Config fournit une regle geree prete a l'emploi, restricted-ssh, qui detecte tout security group autorisant SSH depuis 0.0.0.0/0. Couplee a une notification SNS sur non-conformite, elle repond au besoin immediatement, sans developper ni maintenir de script.

question: Use Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) with Amazon EC2 worker nodes. A company has deployed an application in an AWS account. The application consists of microservices that run on AWS Lambda and Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS). A separate team supports each microservice. The company has multiple AWS accounts and wants to give each team its own account for its microservices. A solutions architect needs to design a solution that will provide service-to-service communication over HTTPS (port 443). The solution also must provide a service registry for service discovery. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST administrative overhead?

options.A: Create an inspection VPC. Deploy an AWS Network Firewall firewall to the inspection VPC. Attach the inspection VPC to a new transit gateway. Route VPC traffic to the inspection VPC. Apply firewall rules to allow only HTTPS communication.
options.B: Create a VPC Lattice service network. Associate the microservices with the service network. Define HTTPS listeners for each service. Register microservice compute resources as targets. Identify VPCs that need to communicate with the services. Associate those VPCs with the service network.
options.C: Create a Network Load Balancer (NLB) with an HTTPS listener and target groups for each microservice. Create an AWS PrivateLink endpoint service for each microservice. Create an Interface VPC endpoint in each VPC that needs to consume that microservice.
options.D: Create peering connections between VPCs that contain microservices. Create a prefix list for each service that requires a connection to a client. Create route tables to route traffic to the appropriate VPC. Create security groups to allow only HTTPS communication.

radar.signal: Communication et decouverte inter-services multi-comptes/multi-VPC sans gerer le reseau -> Amazon VPC Lattice service network

pieges.A: Network Firewall + transit gateway = beaucoup d'infrastructure a operer
pieges.C: NLB + PrivateLink par microservice = lourd a maintenir a l'echelle
pieges.D: Peering + prefix lists + routes + SG = gestion reseau manuelle intense

explication: VPC Lattice fournit un reseau de services applicatif qui gere nativement la communication service-a-service en HTTPS, la decouverte via un registre de services, et l'association de VPC/comptes, le tout sans construire de peering, de PrivateLink ou de transit gateway. C'est l'option avec le moins d'administration.

question: A company is developing a new mobile app. The company must implement proper traffic filtering to protect its Application Load Balancer (ALB) against common application-level attacks, such as cross-site scripting or SQL injection. The company has minimal infrastructure and operational staff. The company needs to reduce its share of the responsibility in managing, updating, and securing servers for its AWS environment. What should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?

options.A: Configure AWS WAF rules and associate them with the ALB.
options.B: Deploy the application using Amazon S3 with public hosting enabled.
options.C: Deploy AWS Shield Advanced and add the ALB as a protected resource.
options.D: Create a new ALB that directs traffic to an Amazon EC2 instance running a third-party firewall, which then passes the traffic to the current ALB.

radar.signal: Filtrer les attaques applicatives (XSS/SQLi) sur un ALB, en managé -> AWS WAF associe a l'ALB

pieges.B: Heberger sur S3 ne filtre rien et change l'architecture
pieges.C: Shield Advanced protege des DDoS (couche reseau/transport), pas XSS/SQLi
pieges.D: Un pare-feu tiers sur EC2 = serveurs a gerer, contraire au besoin

explication: AWS WAF inspecte le trafic de couche 7 et bloque les attaques applicatives comme le cross-site scripting et l'injection SQL, via des regles (dont des regles managees). Associe a l'ALB, c'est un service entierement gere qui n'ajoute aucun serveur, contrairement a Shield Advanced (DDoS) ou a un pare-feu tiers sur EC2.

question: A company reporting system delivers hundreds of CSV files to an Amazon S3 bucket each day. The company must convert these files to Apache Parquet format and must store the files in a transformed data bucket. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST development effort?

options.A: Create an Amazon EMR cluster with Apache Spark installed. Write a Spark application to transform the data. Use EMR File System (EMRFS) to write files to the transformed data bucket.
options.B: Create an AWS Glue crawler to discover the data. Create an AWS Glue extract, transform, and load (ETL) job to transform the data. Specify the transformed data bucket in the output step.
options.C: Use AWS Batch to create a job definition with Bash syntax to transform the data and output the data to the transformed data bucket. Use the job definition to submit a job. Specify an array job as the job type.
options.D: Create an AWS Lambda function to transform the data and output the data to the transformed data bucket. Configure an event notification for the S3 bucket. Specify the Lambda function as the destination for the event notification.

radar.signal: Conversion CSV->Parquet declenchee a l'arrivee des fichiers avec peu de code -> Lambda sur notification d'evenement S3

pieges.A: Cluster EMR + application Spark = beaucoup de developpement et d'infra
pieges.B: Glue crawler + job ETL = plus de mise en place (alternative valable mais plus lourde ici)
pieges.C: AWS Batch + script Bash = a coder et orchestrer

explication: Une notification d'evenement S3 declenchant une Lambda de conversion (via AWS SDK for pandas / awswrangler, quelques lignes) traite chaque fichier des son depot, sans cluster ni orchestration. Note : AWS Glue (option B) est une alternative frequemment proposee ; ici la cle retient la Lambda evenementielle pour son faible effort de developpement.

question: A company is building an ecommerce web application on AWS. The application sends information about new orders to an Amazon API Gateway REST API to process. The company wants to ensure that orders are processed in the order that they are received. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Use an API Gateway integration to publish a message to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic when the application receives an order. Subscribe an AWS Lambda function to the topic to perform processing.
options.B: Use an API Gateway integration to send a message to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) FIFO queue when the application receives an order. Configure the SQS FIFO queue to invoke an AWS Lambda function for processing.
options.C: Use an API Gateway authorizer to block any requests while the application processes an order.
options.D: Use an API Gateway integration to send a message to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) standard queue when the application receives an order. Configure the SQS standard queue to invoke an AWS Lambda function for processing.

declencheurs: orders processed in the order received
radar.signal: Garantir l'ordre de traitement -> API Gateway vers une file SQS FIFO, qui declenche une Lambda

pieges.A: SNS ne garantit pas l'ordre de livraison
pieges.C: Bloquer les requetes via un authorizer ne traite pas la sequence
pieges.D: Une file SQS standard ne preserve pas l'ordre (best-effort)

explication: Seule une file SQS FIFO garantit que les messages sont traites dans l'ordre exact de reception (et sans doublon). API Gateway y depose chaque commande, puis une Lambda consomme la file en ordre. Les files standard (D) et SNS (A) ne preservent pas l'ordonnancement.

question: A company has an application that runs on Amazon EC2 instances and uses an Amazon Aurora database. The EC2 instances connect to the database by using user names and passwords that are stored locally in files. The company wants to minimize the operational overhead of credential management. What should a solutions architect do to accomplish this goal?

options.A: Use AWS Secrets Manager. Turn on automatic rotation.
options.B: Use AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store. Turn on automatic rotation.
options.C: Create an Amazon S3 bucket to store objects that are encrypted with an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) encryption key. Migrate the credential file to the S3 bucket. Point the application to the S3 bucket.
options.D: Create an encrypted Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume for each EC2 instance. Attach the new EBS volume to each EC2 instance. Migrate the credential file to the new EBS volume. Point the application to the new EBS volume.

declencheurs: minimize operational overhead of credential management
radar.signal: Gerer et faire tourner des identifiants de base avec peu d'effort -> AWS Secrets Manager + rotation automatique

pieges.B: Parameter Store n'a pas de rotation automatique native integree pour ce cas
pieges.C: Fichier chiffre sur S3 = gestion manuelle du cycle de vie
pieges.D: Fichier sur EBS chiffre = toujours de la gestion manuelle des identifiants

explication: AWS Secrets Manager stocke les identifiants de facon chiffree et gere nativement leur rotation automatique en s'integrant a Aurora. On supprime ainsi les fichiers locaux et la gestion manuelle. Parameter Store n'offre pas cette rotation automatique cle en main.

question: A company runs an ecommerce application on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. The instances run in an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones. The Auto Scaling group scales based on CPU utilization metrics. The ecommerce application stores the transaction data in a MySQL 8.0 database that is hosted on a large EC2 instance. The database performance degrades quickly as application load increases. The application handles more read requests than write transactions. The company wants a solution that will automatically scale the database to meet the demand of unpredictable read workloads while maintaining high availability. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Use Amazon Redshift with a single node for leader and compute functionality.
options.B: Use Amazon RDS with a Single-AZ deployment. Configure Amazon RDS to add reader instances in a different Availability Zone.
options.C: Use Amazon Aurora with a Multi-AZ deployment. Configure Aurora Auto Scaling with Aurora Replicas.
options.D: Use Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached with EC2 Spot Instances.

declencheurs: automatically scale for unpredictable read workloads
radar.signal: Montee en charge automatique des lectures + HA en MySQL -> Amazon Aurora Multi-AZ + Aurora Auto Scaling avec Aurora Replicas

pieges.A: Redshift = entrepot analytique, pas une base transactionnelle scalable en lecture
pieges.B: RDS Single-AZ n'est pas hautement disponible
pieges.D: ElastiCache Memcached + Spot ne remplace pas une base HA scalable

explication: Aurora (compatible MySQL) en Multi-AZ assure la haute disponibilite, et Aurora Auto Scaling ajoute/retire automatiquement des Aurora Replicas pour absorber des charges de lecture imprevisibles. C'est la seule option combinant scaling automatique des lectures et haute disponibilite.

question: A company recently migrated to AWS and wants to implement a solution to protect the traffic that flows in and out of the production VPC. The company had an inspection server in its on-premises data center. The inspection server performed specific operations such as traffic flow inspection and traffic filtering. The company wants to have the same functionalities in the AWS Cloud. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Use Amazon GuardDuty for traffic inspection and traffic filtering in the production VPC.
options.B: Use Traffic Mirroring to mirror traffic from the production VPC for traffic inspection and filtering.
options.C: Use AWS Network Firewall to create the required rules for traffic inspection and traffic filtering for the production VPC.
options.D: Use AWS Firewall Manager to create the required rules for traffic inspection and traffic filtering for the production VPC.

declencheurs: traffic flow inspection AND traffic filtering
radar.signal: Reproduire un serveur d'inspection (inspection + filtrage de flux) dans un VPC -> AWS Network Firewall

pieges.A: GuardDuty detecte des menaces via logs, il ne filtre pas le trafic en ligne
pieges.B: Traffic Mirroring copie le trafic pour analyse mais ne filtre pas
pieges.D: Firewall Manager gere/centralise des politiques (WAF, SG...), il n'inspecte pas lui-meme le trafic VPC

explication: AWS Network Firewall est un pare-feu reseau manage et avec etat qui realise a la fois l'inspection des flux et le filtrage du trafic entrant/sortant d'un VPC, exactement comme l'appliance d'inspection on-prem. GuardDuty et Traffic Mirroring analysent sans filtrer ; Firewall Manager ne fait qu'orchestrer des politiques.

question: A company runs an application using Amazon ECS. The application creates resized versions of an original image and then makes Amazon S3 API calls to store the resized images in Amazon S3. How can a solutions architect ensure that the application has permission to access Amazon S3?

options.A: Update the S3 role in AWS IAM to allow read/write access from Amazon ECS, and then relaunch the container.
options.B: Create an IAM role with S3 permissions, and then specify that role as the taskRoleArn in the task definition.
options.C: Create a security group that allows access from Amazon ECS to Amazon S3, and update the launch configuration used by the ECS cluster.
options.D: Create an IAM user with S3 permissions, and then relaunch the Amazon EC2 instances for the ECS cluster while logged in as this account.

radar.signal: Donner a des taches ECS l'acces a S3 -> role IAM specifie comme taskRoleArn dans la task definition

pieges.A: Modifier vaguement un 'role S3' n'accorde pas des permissions a la tache ECS
pieges.C: Un security group controle le reseau, pas les permissions IAM sur S3
pieges.D: Un IAM user avec cles = mauvaise pratique (secrets a gerer)

explication: Le mecanisme natif est le task IAM role : on cree un role avec les permissions S3 et on le declare comme taskRoleArn dans la task definition. Les conteneurs recoivent alors des identifiants temporaires automatiquement, sans cles en dur ni configuration reseau specifique.

question: A company has a Windows-based application that must be migrated to AWS. The application requires the use of a shared Windows file system attached to multiple Amazon EC2 Windows instances that are deployed across multiple Availability Zones. What should a solutions architect do to meet this requirement?

options.A: Configure AWS Storage Gateway in volume gateway mode. Mount the volume to each Windows instance.
options.B: Configure Amazon FSx for Windows File Server. Mount the Amazon FSx file system to each Windows instance.
options.C: Configure a file system by using Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS). Mount the EFS file system to each Windows instance.
options.D: Configure an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume with the required size. Attach each EC2 instance to the volume. Mount the file system within the volume to each Windows instance.

radar.signal: Partage de fichiers Windows (SMB) multi-AZ -> Amazon FSx for Windows File Server

pieges.A: Volume gateway = block iSCSI, pas un partage de fichiers Windows multi-instances
pieges.C: EFS = NFS/Linux, pas adapte a Windows/SMB
pieges.D: Un volume EBS ne se partage pas entre plusieurs instances

explication: Amazon FSx for Windows File Server fournit un systeme de fichiers Windows natif (protocole SMB, integration Active Directory) partageable simultanement par plusieurs instances EC2 Windows reparties sur plusieurs AZ. EFS (NFS/Linux) et EBS (mono-instance) ne conviennent pas.

question: A security team wants to limit access to specific services or actions in all of the teams' AWS accounts. All accounts belong to a large organization in AWS Organizations. The solution must be scalable and there must be a single point where permissions can be maintained. What should a solutions architect do to accomplish this?

options.A: Create an ACL to provide access to the services or actions.
options.B: Create a security group to allow accounts and attach it to user groups.
options.C: Create cross-account roles in each account to deny access to the services or actions.
options.D: Create a service control policy in the root organizational unit to deny access to the services or actions.

declencheurs: limit access to services/actions in all accounts
radar.signal: Restreindre des services/actions sur tous les comptes d'une organisation depuis un point unique -> Service Control Policy (SCP) sur l'OU racine

pieges.A: Une ACL ne gere pas des permissions de service a l'echelle d'une organisation
pieges.B: Un security group filtre du reseau, pas des actions AWS
pieges.C: Des roles cross-account dans chaque compte = gestion repartie, non centralisee

explication: Une SCP placee sur l'OU racine d'AWS Organizations s'applique a tous les comptes membres depuis un point de maintenance unique et evolue avec l'organisation. C'est le garde-fou centralise permettant de refuser des services ou actions partout a la fois.

question: A company is concerned about the security of its public web application due to recent web attacks. The application uses an Application Load Balancer (ALB). A solutions architect must reduce the risk of DDoS attacks against the application. What should the solutions architect do to meet this requirement?

options.A: Add an Amazon Inspector agent to the ALB.
options.B: Configure Amazon Macie to prevent attacks.
options.C: Enable AWS Shield Advanced to prevent attacks.
options.D: Configure Amazon GuardDuty to monitor the ALB.

radar.signal: Reduire le risque de DDoS -> AWS Shield Advanced (protection DDoS avancee + support)

pieges.A: Inspector scanne des vulnerabilites, pas de protection DDoS
pieges.B: Macie protege des donnees sensibles, hors sujet
pieges.D: GuardDuty detecte des menaces, il ne bloque pas les DDoS

explication: AWS Shield Advanced offre une protection DDoS renforcee pour les ressources exposees comme un ALB, avec detection/attenuation automatiques et acces a l'equipe de reponse DDoS. Inspector, Macie et GuardDuty ne traitent pas les attaques par deni de service.

question: A company web application is running on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. The company recently changed its policy, which now requires the application to be accessed from one specific country only. Which configuration will meet this requirement?

options.A: Configure the security group for the EC2 instances.
options.B: Configure the security group on the Application Load Balancer.
options.C: Configure AWS WAF on the Application Load Balancer in a VPC.
options.D: Configure the network ACL for the subnet that contains the EC2 instances.

declencheurs: access from one specific country only
radar.signal: Restreindre l'acces par pays (geo-restriction) sur un ALB -> AWS WAF avec regle geo match

pieges.A: Un security group filtre par IP/port, pas par pays
pieges.B: Idem pour le SG de l'ALB : pas de filtrage geographique
pieges.D: Une network ACL filtre par IP/plage, pas par pays

explication: AWS WAF associe a l'ALB permet une regle de geo match qui autorise (ou bloque) le trafic selon le pays d'origine. Les security groups et les NACL ne raisonnent qu'en adresses IP et ports, ils ne savent pas filtrer par geolocalisation.

question: A company that primarily runs its application servers on premises has decided to migrate to AWS. The company wants to minimize its need to scale its Internet Small Computer Systems Interface (iSCSI) storage on premises. The company wants only its recently accessed data to remain stored locally. Which AWS solution should the company use to meet these requirements?

options.A: Amazon S3 File Gateway
options.B: AWS Storage Gateway Tape Gateway
options.C: AWS Storage Gateway Volume Gateway stored volumes
options.D: AWS Storage Gateway Volume Gateway cached volumes

declencheurs: only recently accessed data stored locally
radar.signal: Stockage iSCSI (block) avec seulement les donnees recentes en local et le reste dans le cloud -> Storage Gateway Volume Gateway en mode cached volumes

pieges.A: S3 File Gateway expose du NFS/SMB, pas de l'iSCSI (mot-cle iSCSI = Volume Gateway)
pieges.B: Tape Gateway = sauvegarde type bandes virtuelles, pas du block a la demande
pieges.C: Stored volumes gardent TOUT en local (contraire au besoin de garder seulement le recent)

alerte_cle: La cle du fichier indique A (S3 File Gateway), mais File Gateway expose du NFS/SMB alors que l'enonce parle d'iSCSI. Le mot-cle iSCSI + 'seulement les donnees recentes en local' pointe vers D (Volume Gateway cached volumes).
explication: Le terme iSCSI impose un Volume Gateway (le File Gateway, lui, est NFS/SMB). En mode cached volumes, les donnees primaires resident dans S3 et seules les donnees recemment consultees sont mises en cache localement, ce qui limite le besoin de stockage iSCSI on-prem. Les stored volumes garderaient au contraire l'integralite en local.

question: A company has multiple AWS accounts that use consolidated billing. The company runs several active high performance Amazon RDS for Oracle On-Demand DB instances for 90 days. The company finance team has access to AWS Trusted Advisor in the consolidated billing account and all other AWS accounts. The finance team needs to use the appropriate AWS account to access the Trusted Advisor check recommendations for RDS. The finance team must review the appropriate Trusted Advisor check to reduce RDS costs. Which combination of steps should the finance team take to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.A: Use the Trusted Advisor recommendations from the account where the RDS instances are running.
options.B: Use the Trusted Advisor recommendations from the consolidated billing account to see all RDS instance checks at the same time.
options.C: Review the Trusted Advisor check for Amazon RDS Reserved Instance Optimization.
options.D: Review the Trusted Advisor check for Amazon RDS Idle DB Instances.
options.E: Review the Trusted Advisor check for Amazon Redshift Reserved Node Optimization.

radar.signal: Reduire les couts d'instances RDS actives en continu -> Trusted Advisor depuis le compte qui heberge les RDS (A) + check RDS Reserved Instance Optimization (C)

pieges.B: Le compte de facturation consolidee n'est pas le bon point pour ces checks au niveau des instances
pieges.D: Le check 'Idle DB Instances' vise les bases inactives, or ici elles sont actives/haute performance
pieges.E: Redshift Reserved Node est hors sujet (il s'agit de RDS)

explication: Pour des instances RDS actives en continu sur 90 jours, l'economie vient de l'achat de Reserved Instances : on consulte donc le check Trusted Advisor 'RDS Reserved Instance Optimization' (C), depuis le compte ou tournent les instances (A). Le check 'Idle DB Instances' (D) ne s'applique pas a des bases actives, et Redshift (E) n'a rien a voir.

question: A company has an on-premises server that uses an Oracle database to process and store customer information. The company wants to use an AWS database service to achieve higher availability and to improve application performance. The company also wants to offload reporting from its primary database system. Which solution will meet these requirements in the MOST operationally efficient way?

options.A: Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to create an Amazon RDS DB instance in multiple AWS Regions. Point the reporting functions toward a separate DB instance from the primary DB instance.
options.B: Use Amazon RDS in a Single-AZ deployment to create an Oracle database. Create a read replica in the same zone as the primary DB instance. Direct the reporting functions to the read replica.
options.C: Use Amazon RDS deployed in a Multi-AZ cluster deployment to create an Oracle database. Direct the reporting functions to use the reader instance in the cluster deployment.
options.D: Use Amazon RDS deployed in a Multi-AZ instance deployment to create an Amazon Aurora database. Direct the reporting functions to the reader instances.

radar.signal: HA + performance + decharger le reporting, avec efficacite -> Aurora en Multi-AZ, reporting dirige vers les reader instances

pieges.A: DMS multi-Region + DB separee = lourd et pas le plus efficace
pieges.B: Single-AZ = pas de haute disponibilite
pieges.C: RDS Oracle Multi-AZ cluster est valable mais Aurora offre de meilleurs readers/perf pour le reporting

explication: Aurora en Multi-AZ apporte la haute disponibilite et de meilleures performances, et ses reader instances permettent de decharger nativement les requetes de reporting du primaire. C'est la solution la plus efficace operationnellement parmi les options.

question: A company wants to build a web application on AWS. Client access requests to the website are not predictable and can be idle for a long time. Only customers who have paid a subscription fee can have the ability to sign in and use the web application. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively? (Choose three.)

options.A: Create an AWS Lambda function to retrieve user information from Amazon DynamoDB. Create an Amazon API Gateway endpoint to accept RESTful APIs. Send the API call to the Lambda function.
options.B: Create an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) service behind an Application Load Balancer to retrieve user information from Amazon RDS. Create an Amazon API Gateway endpoint to accept RESTful APIs. Send the API call to the Lambda function.
options.C: Create an Amazon Cognito user pool to authenticate users.
options.D: Create an Amazon Cognito identity pool to authenticate users.
options.E: Use AWS Amplify to serve the frontend web content with HTML, CSS, and JS. Use an integrated Amazon CloudFront configuration.
options.F: Use Amazon S3 static web hosting with PHP, CSS, and JS. Use Amazon CloudFront to serve the frontend web content.

radar.signal: Web serverless a trafic imprevisible + auth abonnes -> Lambda+API Gateway+DynamoDB (A) + Cognito user pool (C) + Amplify/CloudFront pour le front (E)

pieges.B: ECS+ALB+RDS = compute/base toujours actifs, pas rentable pour de longues periodes d'inactivite
pieges.D: Un identity pool federe des identites vers des roles AWS ; l'authentification de connexion se fait via un user pool
pieges.F: S3 static hosting ne sert pas du PHP (cote serveur)

explication: Pour un trafic imprevisible et souvent nul, le tout-serverless (API Gateway + Lambda + DynamoDB) ne coute rien au repos. Amazon Cognito user pool gere l'authentification des abonnes, et AWS Amplify avec CloudFront sert le frontend statique mondialement. Un identity pool (D) ne sert pas a la connexion, et ECS/RDS (B) tournent en continu.

question: A company is deploying a new application to Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) with an AWS Fargate cluster. The application needs a storage solution for data persistence. The solution must be highly available and fault tolerant. The solution also must be shared between multiple application containers. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.A: Create Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes in the same Availability Zones where EKS worker nodes are placed. Register the volumes in a StorageClass object on an EKS cluster. Use EBS Multi-Attach to share the data between containers.
options.B: Create an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. Register the file system in a StorageClass object on an EKS cluster. Use the same file system for all containers.
options.C: Create an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume. Register the volume in a StorageClass object on an EKS cluster. Use the same volume for all containers.
options.D: Create Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file systems in the same Availability Zones where EKS worker nodes are placed. Register the file systems in a StorageClass object on an EKS cluster. Create an AWS Lambda function to synchronize the data between file systems.

radar.signal: Stockage partage HA entre conteneurs EKS/Fargate -> un systeme de fichiers Amazon EFS via une StorageClass

pieges.A: EBS Multi-Attach = complexe et limite, pas concu pour du partage HA multi-AZ
pieges.C: Un volume EBS est mono-AZ et non partageable simplement entre conteneurs
pieges.D: Plusieurs EFS + Lambda de synchro = usine a gaz inutile

explication: Amazon EFS est un systeme de fichiers regional, redondant sur plusieurs AZ, montable simultanement par tous les conteneurs. Declare via une StorageClass sur EKS, il fournit un stockage partage, hautement disponible et tolerant aux pannes, sans gerer de volumes par AZ ni de synchronisation.

question: A company has an application that uses Docker containers in its local data center. The application runs on a container host that stores persistent data in a volume on the host. The container instances use the stored persistent data. The company wants to move the application to a fully managed service because the company does not want to manage any servers or storage infrastructure. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Use Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) with self-managed nodes. Create an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume attached to an Amazon EC2 instance. Use the EBS volume as a persistent volume mounted in the containers.
options.B: Use Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) with an AWS Fargate launch type. Create an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) volume. Add the EFS volume as a persistent storage volume mounted in the containers.
options.C: Use Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) with an AWS Fargate launch type. Create an Amazon S3 bucket. Map the S3 bucket as persistent storage volume mounted in the containers.
options.D: Use Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) with an Amazon EC2 launch type. Create an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) volume. Add the EFS volume as a persistent storage volume mounted in the containers.

declencheurs: no servers or storage infrastructure to manage
radar.signal: Conteneurs sans gerer de serveurs + stockage persistant partage -> ECS Fargate + volume EFS monte dans les conteneurs

pieges.A: EKS self-managed nodes + EBS/EC2 = serveurs a gerer
pieges.C: S3 ne se monte pas nativement comme volume persistant de conteneur
pieges.D: ECS launch type EC2 = on gere encore les instances EC2

explication: AWS Fargate execute les conteneurs sans gerer d'EC2 (serverless), et Amazon EFS fournit un stockage persistant partage entierement manage montable dans les conteneurs. Les options avec EC2/EKS self-managed imposent de gerer des serveurs, et S3 n'est pas un volume de fichiers montable.

question: As part of budget planning, management wants a report of AWS billed items listed by user. The data will be used to create department budgets. A solutions architect needs to determine the most efficient way to obtain this report information. Which solution meets these requirements?

options.A: Run a query with Amazon Athena to generate the report.
options.B: Create a report in Cost Explorer and download the report.
options.C: Access the bill details from the billing dashboard and download the bill.
options.D: Modify a cost budget in AWS Budgets to alert with Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES).

declencheurs: report of billed items by user
radar.signal: Rapport des couts ventiles (par utilisateur/tag) -> AWS Cost Explorer (creer et telecharger le rapport)

pieges.A: Athena sur les Cost and Usage Reports = plus de mise en place que Cost Explorer
pieges.C: La facture brute du dashboard n'est pas ventilee comme un rapport analytique
pieges.D: AWS Budgets alerte sur des seuils, il ne produit pas un rapport ventile

explication: Cost Explorer permet de generer directement des rapports de couts ventiles (par service, tag, compte...) et de les telecharger, ce qui est le moyen le plus efficace pour batir des budgets par departement. Athena imposerait de configurer les Cost and Usage Reports au prealable.

question: A company hosts its static website by using Amazon S3. The company wants to add a contact form to its webpage. The contact form will have dynamic server-side components for users to input their name, email address, phone number, and user message. The company anticipates that there will be fewer than 100 site visits each month. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

options.A: Host a dynamic contact form page in Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS). Set up Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES) to connect to any third-party email provider.
options.B: Create an Amazon API Gateway endpoint with an AWS Lambda backend that makes a call to Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES).
options.C: Convert the static webpage to dynamic by deploying Amazon Lightsail. Use client-side scripting to build the contact form. Integrate the form with Amazon WorkMail.
options.D: Create a t2 micro Amazon EC2 instance. Deploy a LAMP (Linux, Apache, MySQL, PHP/Perl/Python) stack to host the webpage. Use client-side scripting to build the contact form. Integrate the form with Amazon WorkMail.

radar.signal: Petit composant dynamique a tres faible trafic -> API Gateway + Lambda + SES (serverless, quasi gratuit au repos)

pieges.A: ECS = conteneur toujours actif, cher pour <100 visites
pieges.C: Lightsail = instance facturee en continu
pieges.D: EC2 t2.micro = serveur a payer et gerer en permanence

explication: Pour moins de 100 visites par mois, tout serveur permanent (ECS, Lightsail, EC2) est disproportionne. Un endpoint API Gateway declenchant une Lambda qui envoie l'email via SES ne coute pratiquement rien au repos et ne facture qu'a l'usage.

question: A company has an application that serves clients that are deployed in more than 20,000 retail storefront locations around the world. The application consists of backend web services that are exposed over HTTPS on port 443. The application is hosted on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The retail locations communicate with the web application over the public internet. The company allows each retail location to register the IP address that the retail location has been allocated by its local ISP. The company security team recommends to increase the security of the application endpoint by restricting access to only the IP addresses registered by the retail locations. What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

options.A: Associate an AWS WAF web ACL with the ALB. Use IP rule sets on the ALB to filter traffic. Update the IP addresses in the rule to include the registered IP addresses.
options.B: Deploy AWS Firewall Manager to manage the ALB. Configure firewall rules to restrict traffic to the ALB. Modify the firewall rules to include the registered IP addresses.
options.C: Store the IP addresses in an Amazon DynamoDB table. Configure an AWS Lambda authorization function on the ALB to validate that incoming requests are from the registered IP addresses.
options.D: Configure the network ACL on the subnet that contains the public interface of the ALB. Update the ingress rules on the network ACL with entries for each of the registered IP addresses.

declencheurs: restrict access to registered IP addresses
radar.signal: Autoriser seulement une liste d'IP sur un ALB -> AWS WAF web ACL avec IP set associe a l'ALB

pieges.B: Firewall Manager orchestre des politiques, il ne filtre pas lui-meme l'ALB par IP
pieges.C: Un authorizer Lambda 'sur l'ALB' via DynamoDB = complexe et non natif
pieges.D: Une network ACL a une limite de regles et ne monte pas a des milliers d'IP proprement

explication: AWS WAF associe a l'ALB permet de definir un IP set (liste d'adresses autorisees) et une regle qui bloque tout le reste. C'est la maniere native et scalable de restreindre l'acces aux IP enregistrees, la ou les NACL sont limitees en nombre de regles.

question: A company is building a data analysis platform on AWS by using AWS Lake Formation. The platform will ingest data from different sources such as Amazon S3 and Amazon RDS. The company needs a secure solution to prevent access to portions of the data that contain sensitive information. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.A: Create an IAM role that includes permissions to access Lake Formation tables.
options.B: Create data filters to implement row-level security and cell-level security.
options.C: Create an AWS Lambda function that removes sensitive information before Lake Formation ingests the data.
options.D: Create an AWS Lambda function that periodically queries and removes sensitive information from Lake Formation tables.

declencheurs: prevent access to portions of sensitive data
radar.signal: Masquer des portions de donnees dans Lake Formation -> data filters (securite au niveau ligne et cellule)

pieges.A: Un role IAM donne/refuse l'acces a des tables entieres, pas a des portions fines
pieges.C: Une Lambda de nettoyage a l'ingestion = a developper/maintenir et destructif
pieges.D: Une Lambda qui purge periodiquement les tables = fragile et couteuse en operations

explication: Lake Formation propose des data filters qui appliquent une securite au niveau des lignes et des cellules : on masque les portions sensibles sans supprimer de donnees ni ecrire de code. C'est bien plus simple que d'orchestrer des Lambda d'expurgation.

question: A company needs to store its accounting records in Amazon S3. The records must be immediately accessible for 1 year and then must be archived for an additional 9 years. No one at the company, including administrative users and root users, can be able to delete the records during the entire 10-year period. The records must be stored with maximum resiliency. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Store the records in S3 Glacier for the entire 10-year period. Use an access control policy to deny deletion of the records for a period of 10 years.
options.B: Store the records by using S3 Intelligent-Tiering. Use an IAM policy to deny deletion of the records. After 10 years, change the IAM policy to allow deletion.
options.C: Use an S3 Lifecycle policy to transition the records from S3 Standard to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 1 year. Use S3 Object Lock in compliance mode for a period of 10 years.
options.D: Use an S3 Lifecycle policy to transition the records from S3 Standard to S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA) after 1 year. Use S3 Object Lock in governance mode for a period of 10 years.

declencheurs: immediately accessible 1 year then archived 9 years
no one (even root) can delete for 10 years
radar.signal: Interdiction absolue de suppression (meme root) + archivage -> S3 Object Lock en mode compliance 10 ans + Lifecycle vers Glacier Deep Archive apres 1 an

pieges.A: Une access control policy peut etre modifiee/contournee par un admin
pieges.B: Une IAM policy modifiable n'empeche pas reellement la suppression (et One... n.a.)
pieges.D: Object Lock en mode governance peut etre outrepasse par un utilisateur privilegie ; One Zone-IA reduit la resilience

explication: Seul S3 Object Lock en mode compliance garantit qu'aucun utilisateur, y compris root, ne peut supprimer les objets avant la fin de la retention (10 ans). Une Lifecycle policy fait transiter les enregistrements vers Glacier Deep Archive apres 1 an. Le mode governance (D) peut etre outrepasse par un compte privilegie, et One Zone-IA reduit la resilience.

question: A company runs multiple Windows workloads on AWS. The company's employees use Windows file shares that are hosted on two Amazon EC2 instances. The file shares synchronize data between themselves and maintain duplicate copies. The company wants a highly available and durable storage solution that preserves how users currently access the files. What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

options.A: Migrate all the data to Amazon S3. Set up IAM authentication for users to access files.
options.B: Set up an Amazon S3 File Gateway. Mount the S3 File Gateway on the existing EC2 instances.
options.C: Extend the file share environment to Amazon FSx for Windows File Server with a Multi-AZ configuration. Migrate all the data to FSx for Windows File Server.
options.D: Extend the file share environment to Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) with a Multi-AZ configuration. Migrate all the data to Amazon EFS.

radar.signal: Remplacer des partages Windows auto-repliques par un service manage HA -> Amazon FSx for Windows File Server en Multi-AZ

pieges.A: S3 + IAM change completement la maniere d'acceder aux fichiers
pieges.B: S3 File Gateway n'est pas un partage Windows natif multi-instances HA
pieges.D: EFS = NFS/Linux, incompatible avec l'acces Windows/SMB actuel

explication: FSx for Windows File Server en Multi-AZ fournit un partage de fichiers Windows (SMB) manage, hautement disponible et durable, tout en preservant l'experience d'acces des utilisateurs. On supprime la synchronisation manuelle entre deux EC2. EFS (NFS) et S3 changeraient la facon d'acceder aux fichiers.

question: A solutions architect is creating an application. The application will run on Amazon EC2 instances in private subnets across multiple Availability Zones in a VPC. The EC2 instances will frequently access large files that contain confidential information. These files are stored in Amazon S3 buckets for processing. The solutions architect must optimize the network architecture to minimize data transfer costs. What should the solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

options.A: Create a gateway endpoint for Amazon S3 in the VPC. In the route tables for the private subnets, add an entry for the gateway endpoint.
options.B: Create a single NAT gateway in a public subnet. In the route tables for the private subnets, add a default route that points to the NAT gateway.
options.C: Create an AWS PrivateLink interface endpoint for Amazon S3 in the VPC. In the route tables for the private subnets, add an entry for the interface endpoint.
options.D: Create one NAT gateway for each Availability Zone in public subnets. In each of the route tables for the private subnets, add a default route that points to the NAT gateway in the same Availability Zone.

declencheurs: EC2 private subnets access large S3 files
radar.signal: Reduire le cout de transfert vers S3 depuis un VPC -> gateway endpoint S3 (gratuit) + route dans les tables des subnets prives

pieges.B: Un NAT gateway facture le transfert et le traitement des donnees
pieges.C: Un interface endpoint pour S3 est facture a l'heure et au Go (plus cher que le gateway endpoint ici)
pieges.D: Un NAT gateway par AZ = encore plus de couts de traitement

explication: Le gateway endpoint pour S3 est gratuit et route le trafic S3 directement via le reseau AWS, sans frais de NAT ni de sortie Internet. C'est la solution qui minimise le cout de transfert pour des instances de subnets prives qui lisent souvent de gros fichiers dans S3.

question: A company wants to relocate its on-premises MySQL database to AWS. The database accepts regular imports from a client-facing application, which causes a high volume of write operations. The company is concerned that the amount of traffic might be causing performance issues within the application. How should a solutions architect design the architecture on AWS?

options.A: Provision an Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance with Provisioned IOPS SSD storage. Monitor write operation metrics by using Amazon CloudWatch. Adjust the provisioned IOPS if necessary.
options.B: Provision an Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance with General Purpose SSD storage. Place an Amazon ElastiCache cluster in front of the DB instance. Configure the application to query ElastiCache instead.
options.C: Provision an Amazon DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility) instance with a memory optimized instance type. Monitor Amazon CloudWatch for performance-related issues. Change the instance class if necessary.
options.D: Provision an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system in General Purpose performance mode. Monitor Amazon CloudWatch for IOPS bottlenecks. Change to Provisioned Throughput performance mode if necessary.

radar.signal: Absorber un fort volume d'ecritures MySQL -> RDS for MySQL avec stockage Provisioned IOPS SSD (io1/io2) + surveillance CloudWatch

pieges.B: ElastiCache accelere les lectures, pas les ecritures intensives
pieges.C: DocumentDB (MongoDB) change de moteur, non pertinent pour un MySQL
pieges.D: EFS n'est pas une base de donnees relationnelle

explication: Un fort volume d'ecritures exige des IOPS elevees et constantes : RDS for MySQL avec stockage Provisioned IOPS SSD garantit ces performances, ajustables selon les metriques CloudWatch. ElastiCache n'aide que les lectures, et DocumentDB/EFS ne sont pas des bases MySQL.

question: An analytics company uses Amazon VPC to run its multi-tier services. The company wants to use RESTful APIs to offer a web analytics service to millions of users. Users must be verified by using an authentication service to access the APIs. Which solution will meet these requirements with the MOST operational efficiency?

options.A: Configure an Amazon Cognito user pool for user authentication. Implement Amazon API Gateway REST APIs with a Cognito authorizer.
options.B: Configure an Amazon Cognito identity pool for user authentication. Implement Amazon API Gateway HTTP APIs with a Cognito authorizer.
options.C: Configure an AWS Lambda function to handle user authentication. Implement Amazon API Gateway REST APIs with a Lambda authorizer.
options.D: Configure an IAM user to handle user authentication. Implement Amazon API Gateway HTTP APIs with an IAM authorizer.

radar.signal: Auth de millions d'utilisateurs devant des API REST, sans gerer de serveurs -> Cognito user pool + API Gateway REST avec un Cognito authorizer

pieges.B: Un identity pool federe des identites, il n'authentifie pas les connexions comme un user pool
pieges.C: Un Lambda authorizer = code d'auth a ecrire et maintenir
pieges.D: Un IAM user par utilisateur final ne passe pas a l'echelle de millions d'utilisateurs

explication: Un Cognito user pool gere l'authentification managee a grande echelle, et un Cognito authorizer sur les API Gateway REST valide les jetons sans code custom. C'est la solution la plus efficace : pas de serveur d'auth ni de logique a maintenir, contrairement au Lambda authorizer ou aux IAM users.

question: A company has a mobile app for customers. The app's data is sensitive and must be encrypted at rest. The company uses AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS). The company needs a solution that prevents the accidental deletion of KMS keys. The solution must use Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) to send an email notification to administrators when a user attempts to delete a KMS key. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.A: Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that reacts when a user tries to delete a KMS key. Configure an AWS Config rule that cancels any deletion of a KMS key. Add the AWS Config rule as a target of the EventBridge rule. Create an SNS topic that notifies the administrators.
options.B: Create an AWS Lambda function that has custom logic to prevent KMS key deletion. Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm that is activated when a user tries to delete a KMS key. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that invokes the Lambda function when the DeleteKey operation is performed. Create an SNS topic. Configure the EventBridge rule to publish an SNS message that notifies the administrators.
options.C: Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that reacts when the KMS DeleteKey operation is performed. Configure the rule to initiate an AWS Systems Manager Automation runbook. Configure the runbook to cancel the deletion of the KMS key. Create an SNS topic. Configure the EventBridge rule to publish an SNS message that notifies the administrators.
options.D: Create an AWS CloudTrail trail. Configure the trail to deliver logs to a new Amazon CloudWatch log group. Create a CloudWatch alarm based on the metric filter for the CloudWatch log group. Configure the alarm to use Amazon SNS to notify the administrators when the KMS DeleteKey operation is performed.

declencheurs: notify admins via SNS on delete attempt
radar.signal: Alerter sur une tentative de suppression de cle KMS, simplement -> CloudTrail -> CloudWatch Logs -> metric filter/alarm sur DeleteKey -> SNS

pieges.A: AWS Config ne 'target' pas une EventBridge rule pour annuler une suppression ainsi
pieges.B: Lambda custom + alarme + EventBridge = beaucoup de pieces a maintenir
pieges.C: Runbook Systems Manager pour annuler = plus complexe que necessaire

explication: La suppression d'une cle KMS passe deja par une periode d'attente obligatoire (jusqu'a 30 jours), laissant le temps de reagir. Le moyen le plus simple d'alerter est CloudTrail -> CloudWatch Logs avec un metric filter sur l'operation DeleteKey qui declenche une alarme et notifie via SNS, sans code custom ni orchestration.

question: A company has two VPCs that are located in the us-west-2 Region within the same AWS account. The company needs to allow network traffic between these VPCs. Approximately 500 GB of data transfer will occur between the VPCs each month. What is the MOST cost-effective solution to connect these VPCs?

options.A: Implement AWS Transit Gateway to connect the VPCs. Update the route tables of each VPC to use the transit gateway for inter-VPC communication.
options.B: Implement an AWS Site-to-Site VPN tunnel between the VPCs. Update the route tables of each VPC to use the VPN tunnel for inter-VPC communication.
options.C: Set up a VPC peering connection between the VPCs. Update the route tables of each VPC to use the VPC peering connection for inter-VPC communication.
options.D: Set up a 1 GB AWS Direct Connect connection between the VPCs. Update the route tables of each VPC to use the Direct Connect connection for inter-VPC communication.

radar.signal: Relier deux VPC d'un meme compte/Region a moindre cout -> VPC peering (pas de cout horaire, seulement le transfert)

pieges.A: Transit Gateway facture a l'heure + par attachment, superflu pour 2 VPC
pieges.B: Un VPN Site-to-Site entre VPC = complexe et facture a l'heure
pieges.D: Direct Connect sert a relier on-prem a AWS, pas deux VPC entre eux

explication: Le VPC peering n'a aucun cout horaire : on ne paie que le transfert de donnees. Pour deux VPC dans la meme Region et le meme compte avec 500 Go/mois, c'est nettement moins cher qu'un Transit Gateway ou un VPN factures a l'heure. Direct Connect est hors sujet (liaison on-prem).

question: A company hosts multiple applications on AWS for different product lines. The applications use different compute resources, including Amazon EC2 instances and Application Load Balancers. The applications run in different AWS accounts under the same organization in AWS Organizations across multiple AWS Regions. Teams for each product line have tagged each compute resource in the individual accounts. The company wants more details about the cost for each product line from the consolidated billing feature in Organizations. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.A: Select a specific AWS generated tag in the AWS Billing console.
options.B: Select a specific user-defined tag in the AWS Billing console.
options.C: Select a specific user-defined tag in the AWS Resource Groups console.
options.D: Activate the selected tag from each AWS account.
options.E: Activate the selected tag from the Organizations management account.

radar.signal: Ventiler les couts par tag dans la facturation consolidee -> selectionner le tag utilisateur dans la console Billing (B) + l'activer depuis le compte de gestion Organizations (E)

pieges.A: Un tag genere par AWS ne correspond pas aux tags metier definis par les equipes
pieges.C: La console Resource Groups ne pilote pas les cost allocation tags de facturation
pieges.D: L'activation des cost allocation tags se fait au niveau du compte de gestion, pas dans chaque compte

explication: Pour obtenir les couts par ligne de produit, il faut activer les cost allocation tags : on selectionne le tag user-defined dans la console Billing (B) et on l'active depuis le compte de gestion de l'organisation (E), ce qui l'applique a la facturation consolidee de tous les comptes.

question: A solutions architect is designing a VPC with public and private subnets. The VPC and subnets use IPv4 CIDR blocks. There is one public subnet and one private subnet in each of three Availability Zones (AZs) for high availability. An internet gateway is used to provide internet access for the public subnets. The private subnets require access to the internet to allow Amazon EC2 instances to download software updates. What should the solutions architect do to enable internet access for the private subnets?

options.A: Create three NAT gateways, one for each public subnet in each AZ. Create a private route table for each AZ that forwards non-VPC traffic to the NAT gateway in its AZ.
options.B: Create three NAT instances, one for each private subnet in each AZ. Create a private route table for each AZ that forwards non-VPC traffic to the NAT instance in its AZ.
options.C: Create a second internet gateway on one of the private subnets. Update the route table for the private subnets that forward non-VPC traffic to the private internet gateway.
options.D: Create an egress-only internet gateway on one of the public subnets. Update the route table for the private subnets that forward non-VPC traffic to the egress-only internet gateway.

declencheurs: private subnets need internet for updates
radar.signal: Acces Internet sortant HA pour subnets prives -> un NAT gateway par AZ + une route table privee par AZ pointant vers son NAT

pieges.B: Des NAT instances = a gerer/patcher soi-meme, moins disponibles qu'un NAT gateway
pieges.C: Un internet gateway ne se place pas dans un subnet prive et rend le subnet public
pieges.D: Un egress-only internet gateway est reserve a IPv6, pas a IPv4

explication: Pour un acces Internet sortant hautement disponible, on deploie un NAT gateway (manage) dans le subnet public de chaque AZ et on cree une route table privee par AZ dirigeant le trafic sortant vers le NAT de la meme AZ. Cela evite qu'une panne d'AZ coupe tout, et l'egress-only IGW (D) ne concerne que l'IPv6.

question: A company wants to migrate an on-premises data center to AWS. The data center hosts an SFTP server that stores its data on an NFS-based file system. The server holds 200 GB of data that needs to be transferred. The server must be hosted on an Amazon EC2 instance that uses an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. Which combination of steps should a solutions architect take to automate this task? (Choose two.)

options.A: Launch the EC2 instance into the same Availability Zone as the EFS file system.
options.B: Install an AWS DataSync agent in the on-premises data center.
options.C: Create a secondary Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume on the EC2 instance for the data.
options.D: Manually use an operating system copy command to push the data to the EC2 instance.
options.E: Use AWS DataSync to create a suitable location configuration for the on-premises SFTP server.

declencheurs: migrate on-prem NFS to EC2 with EFS
radar.signal: Transfert automatise on-prem -> EFS avec DataSync -> installer l'agent DataSync on-prem (B) + lancer l'EC2 dans la meme AZ que l'EFS (A)

pieges.C: Un volume EBS secondaire ne concerne pas le transfert vers EFS
pieges.D: Une copie manuelle par commande OS n'automatise rien
pieges.E: La location DataSync decrit un serveur SFTP, or la source est un partage NFS (formulation piege)

explication: AWS DataSync automatise le transfert : on installe son agent dans le data center (B) pour lire le partage NFS, et on lance l'instance EC2 dans la meme AZ que le systeme de fichiers EFS (A) pour un montage performant. L'option E est un piege car elle parle d'un serveur SFTP alors que la source est NFS, et la copie manuelle (D) n'automatise rien.

question: A company wants to move its application to a serverless solution. The serverless solution needs to analyze existing and new data by using SQL. The company stores the data in an Amazon S3 bucket. The data requires encryption and must be replicated to a different AWS Region. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.A: Create a new S3 bucket. Load the data into the new S3 bucket. Use S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR) to replicate encrypted objects to an S3 bucket in another Region. Use server-side encryption with AWS KMS multi-Region keys (SSE-KMS). Use Amazon Athena to query the data.
options.B: Create a new S3 bucket. Load the data into the new S3 bucket. Use S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR) to replicate encrypted objects to an S3 bucket in another Region. Use server-side encryption with AWS KMS multi-Region keys (SSE-KMS). Use Amazon RDS to query the data.
options.C: Load the data into the existing S3 bucket. Use S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR) to replicate encrypted objects to an S3 bucket in another Region. Use server-side encryption with Amazon S3 managed encryption keys (SSE-S3). Use Amazon Athena to query the data.
options.D: Load the data into the existing S3 bucket. Use S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR) to replicate encrypted objects to an S3 bucket in another Region. Use server-side encryption with Amazon S3 managed encryption keys (SSE-S3). Use Amazon RDS to query the data.

declencheurs: serverless SQL analysis of S3 data
radar.signal: SQL serverless sur S3 + chiffrement + replication cross-Region -> nouveau bucket, SSE-KMS multi-Region keys, S3 CRR, requetes via Amazon Athena

pieges.B: Amazon RDS n'est ni serverless au sens Athena ni fait pour interroger directement S3
pieges.C: SSE-S3 ne fournit pas de cles multi-Region pour un chiffrement coherent cross-Region
pieges.D: RDS + SSE-S3 cumulent les deux problemes ci-dessus

explication: Amazon Athena interroge directement les donnees S3 en SQL, sans serveur (serverless). SSE-KMS avec des cles multi-Region permet de conserver le chiffrement de facon coherente apres la replication S3 Cross-Region. RDS n'interroge pas S3 nativement, et SSE-S3 n'offre pas de cles multi-Region.

question: A company runs workloads on AWS. The company needs to connect to a service from an external provider. The service is hosted in the provider's VPC. According to the company security team, the connectivity must be private and must be restricted to the target service. The connection must be initiated only from the company's VPC. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Create a VPC peering connection between the company's VPC and the provider's VPC. Update the route table to connect to the target service.
options.B: Ask the provider to create a virtual private gateway in its VPC. Use AWS PrivateLink to connect to the target service.
options.C: Create a NAT gateway in a public subnet of the company's VPC. Update the route table to connect to the target service.
options.D: Ask the provider to create a VPC endpoint for the target service. Use AWS PrivateLink to connect to the target service.

declencheurs: connect to external provider's service in their VPC
radar.signal: Acces prive et unidirectionnel vers UN service d'un fournisseur -> le fournisseur cree un endpoint service, on consomme via AWS PrivateLink

pieges.A: VPC peering expose des reseaux entiers, pas un seul service, et n'est pas unidirectionnel
pieges.B: Un virtual private gateway sert au VPN, pas a exposer un service via PrivateLink
pieges.C: Un NAT gateway passe par Internet et n'est pas restreint au service cible

explication: AWS PrivateLink expose uniquement le service cible (pas tout le reseau) de facon privee, et la connexion est initiee depuis le VPC consommateur. Le fournisseur cree un VPC endpoint service pour son service, et l'entreprise cree un interface endpoint pour s'y connecter. VPC peering (A) exposerait des reseaux entiers de maniere bidirectionnelle.

question: A company has released a new version of its production application. The company's workload uses Amazon EC2, AWS Lambda, AWS Fargate, and Amazon SageMaker. The company wants to cost optimize the workload now that usage is at a steady state. The company wants to cover the most services with the fewest savings plans. Which combination of savings plans will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.A: Purchase an EC2 Instance Savings Plan for Amazon EC2 and SageMaker.
options.B: Purchase a Compute Savings Plan for Amazon EC2, Lambda, and SageMaker.
options.C: Purchase a SageMaker Savings Plan.
options.D: Purchase a Compute Savings Plan for Lambda, Fargate, and Amazon EC2.
options.E: Purchase an EC2 Instance Savings Plan for Amazon EC2 and Fargate.

declencheurs: cover most services with fewest savings plans
radar.signal: Couvrir 4 services avec le moins de plans -> Compute Savings Plan (couvre EC2+Lambda+Fargate) + SageMaker Savings Plan

pieges.A: Un EC2 Instance Savings Plan ne couvre ni Lambda, ni Fargate, ni SageMaker
pieges.B: Un Compute Savings Plan ne couvre PAS SageMaker (erreur classique)
pieges.E: Un EC2 Instance Savings Plan ne couvre pas SageMaker (ni Lambda)

alerte_cle: La cle du fichier indique BD, mais un Compute Savings Plan ne couvre pas SageMaker (l'option B est donc fausse). Le bon couple est CD : Compute Savings Plan (EC2+Lambda+Fargate) + SageMaker Savings Plan.
explication: Un Compute Savings Plan couvre EC2, Lambda ET Fargate (option D). SageMaker n'est couvert que par un SageMaker Savings Plan (option C). Deux plans suffisent donc a couvrir les quatre services. L'option B est un piege : elle pretend a tort qu'un Compute Savings Plan couvre SageMaker.

question: A company uses a Microsoft SQL Server database. The company's applications are connected to the database. The company wants to migrate to an Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL database with minimal changes to the application code. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.A: Use the AWS Schema Conversion Tool (AWS SCT) to rewrite the SQL queries in the applications.
options.B: Enable Babelfish on Aurora PostgreSQL to run the SQL queries from the applications.
options.C: Migrate the database schema and data by using the AWS Schema Conversion Tool (AWS SCT) and AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS).
options.D: Use Amazon RDS Proxy to connect the applications to Aurora PostgreSQL.
options.E: Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to rewrite the SQL queries in the applications.

radar.signal: Migrer SQL Server vers Aurora PostgreSQL sans toucher au code -> Babelfish (compatibilite T-SQL) + migration schema/donnees via SCT + DMS

pieges.A: Reecrire les requetes avec SCT change justement le code applicatif
pieges.D: RDS Proxy fait du pooling de connexions, il ne rend pas les requetes SQL Server compatibles
pieges.E: DMS migre des donnees, il ne reecrit pas les requetes de l'application

alerte_cle: La cle du fichier indique CD, mais RDS Proxy (D) ne concerne pas la compatibilite du code. Pour un 'minimal code change', c'est Babelfish (B). Le bon couple est BC : activer Babelfish + migrer schema/donnees avec SCT/DMS.
explication: Babelfish pour Aurora PostgreSQL comprend le T-SQL et le protocole SQL Server, permettant aux applications de tourner avec un minimum de changements de code (B). On migre par ailleurs le schema et les donnees avec SCT + DMS (C). RDS Proxy (D) ne fait que du pooling de connexions et n'aide pas la compatibilite applicative.
