question: A company has an on-premises business application that generates hundreds of files each day. These files are stored on an SMB file share and require a low-latency connection to the application servers. A new company policy states all application-generated files must be copied to AWS. There is already a VPN connection to AWS. The application development team does not have time to make the necessary code modifications to move the application to AWS. Which service should a solutions architect recommend to allow the application to copy files to AWS?

options.A: Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS)
options.B: Amazon FSx for Windows File Server
options.C: AWS Snowball
options.D: AWS Storage Gateway

radar.signal: Garder un acces local faible latence + copier vers AWS sans changer l'app -> AWS Storage Gateway (file gateway SMB)

pieges.A: EFS est un systeme de fichiers cloud, il ne fournit pas d'acces local faible latence on-prem
pieges.B: FSx for Windows est un partage cloud, meme limite pour l'acces local on-prem
pieges.C: Snowball = transfert ponctuel, pas une copie continue des nouveaux fichiers

explication: AWS Storage Gateway (mode file gateway) presente un partage SMB local a faible latence pour les serveurs applicatifs et copie automatiquement les fichiers vers S3, sans modifier l'application. EFS et FSx sont des systemes cloud, et Snowball ne fait qu'un transfert ponctuel.

question: A company has 15 employees. The company stores employee start dates in an Amazon DynamoDB table. The company wants to send an email message to each employee on the day of the employee's work anniversary. Which solution will meet these requirements with the MOST operational efficiency?

options.A: Create a script that scans the DynamoDB table and uses Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) to send email messages to employees when necessary. Use a cron job to run this script every day on an Amazon EC2 instance.
options.B: Create a script that scans the DynamoDB table and uses Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) to send email messages to employees when necessary. Use a cron job to run this script every day on an Amazon EC2 instance.
options.C: Create an AWS Lambda function that scans the DynamoDB table and uses Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) to send email messages to employees when necessary. Schedule this Lambda function to run every day.
options.D: Create an AWS Lambda function that scans the DynamoDB table and uses Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) to send email messages to employees when necessary. Schedule this Lambda function to run every day.

radar.signal: Tache quotidienne d'envoi d'emails -> Lambda planifiee qui scanne DynamoDB + Amazon SNS pour l'email

pieges.A: Un cron sur EC2 = serveur a gerer, moins efficace qu'une Lambda planifiee
pieges.B: SQS est une file de messages, pas un service d'envoi d'emails
pieges.D: Lambda planifiee est bon, mais SQS n'envoie pas d'emails

explication: Une fonction Lambda planifiee (EventBridge) qui scanne quotidiennement la table DynamoDB et envoie les emails via SNS est entierement serverless : aucun serveur a maintenir, contrairement au cron sur EC2. SQS est une file de messages et ne sert pas a envoyer des emails.

question: A company designed a stateless two-tier application that uses Amazon EC2 in a single Availability Zone and an Amazon RDS Multi-AZ DB instance. New company management wants to ensure the application is highly available. What should a solutions architect do to meet this requirement?

options.A: Configure the application to use Multi-AZ EC2 Auto Scaling and create an Application Load Balancer.
options.B: Configure the application to take snapshots of the EC2 instances and send them to a different AWS Region.
options.C: Configure the application to use Amazon Route 53 latency-based routing to feed requests to the application.
options.D: Configure Amazon Route 53 rules to handle incoming requests and create a Multi-AZ Application Load Balancer.

radar.signal: Rendre un tier EC2 mono-AZ hautement disponible -> Auto Scaling multi-AZ + Application Load Balancer

pieges.B: Des snapshots vers une autre Region servent au DR, pas a la HA active
pieges.C: Le routage latency-based de Route 53 ne rend pas un seul tier EC2 mono-AZ redondant
pieges.D: Un ALB seul sans Auto Scaling multi-AZ ne suffit pas a repartir/relancer les instances

explication: La base RDS est deja Multi-AZ ; il reste a rendre le tier EC2 redondant. Un Auto Scaling group reparti sur plusieurs AZ derriere un Application Load Balancer distribue le trafic et remplace automatiquement les instances defaillantes, rendant l'application stateless hautement disponible.

question: A company uses AWS Organizations. A member account has purchased a Compute Savings Plan. Because of changes in the workloads inside the member account, the account no longer receives the full benefit of the Compute Savings Plan commitment. The company uses less than 50% of its purchased compute power. What should the company do to optimize savings?

options.A: Turn on discount sharing from the Billing Preferences section of the account console in the member account that purchased the Compute Savings Plan.
options.B: Turn on discount sharing from the Billing Preferences section of the account console in the company Organizations management account.
options.C: Migrate additional compute workloads from another AWS account to the account that has the Compute Savings Plan.
options.D: Sell the excess Savings Plan commitment in the Reserved Instance Marketplace.

declencheurs: member account under-uses its Compute Savings Plan
radar.signal: Faire beneficier toute l'organisation d'un Savings Plan sous-utilise -> activer le partage des remises (discount sharing) depuis le compte de gestion

pieges.A: Le partage des remises s'active depuis le compte de gestion, pas depuis le compte membre
pieges.C: Deplacer des workloads = beaucoup d'effort et pas toujours possible
pieges.D: On ne revend pas un Compute Savings Plan sur le Reserved Instance Marketplace

explication: En activant le discount sharing depuis le compte de gestion d'AWS Organizations, la remise du Compute Savings Plan non consommee par le compte acheteur profite automatiquement aux autres comptes de l'organisation. C'est le levier natif, sans deplacer de workloads.

question: A company has a popular gaming platform running on AWS. The application is sensitive to latency because latency can impact the user experience and introduce unfair advantages to some players. The application is deployed in every AWS Region. It runs on Amazon EC2 instances that are part of Auto Scaling groups configured behind Application Load Balancers (ALBs). A solutions architect needs to implement a mechanism to monitor the health of the application and redirect traffic to healthy endpoints. Which solution meets these requirements?

options.A: Configure an accelerator in AWS Global Accelerator. Add a listener for the port that the application listens on, and attach it to a Regional endpoint in each Region. Add the ALB as the endpoint.
options.B: Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution and specify the ALB as the origin server. Configure the cache behavior to use origin cache headers. Use AWS Lambda functions to optimize the traffic.
options.C: Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution and specify Amazon S3 as the origin server. Configure the cache behavior to use origin cache headers. Use AWS Lambda functions to optimize the traffic.
options.D: Configure an Amazon DynamoDB database to serve as the data store for the application. Create a DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) cluster to act as an in-memory cache for DynamoDB hosting the application data.

declencheurs: monitor health + redirect to healthy endpoints
radar.signal: Router au plus vite vers l'endpoint regional sain, au niveau reseau -> AWS Global Accelerator (listener + endpoints regionaux = les ALB)

pieges.B: CloudFront (origine ALB) est optimise pour du contenu HTTP mis en cache, pas pour du routage TCP/UDP faible latence par sante regionale
pieges.C: CloudFront avec origine S3 ne sert pas l'application dynamique
pieges.D: DynamoDB/DAX est une couche de donnees, sans rapport avec le routage reseau

explication: AWS Global Accelerator utilise le reseau mondial d'AWS et des IP anycast pour diriger chaque joueur vers l'endpoint regional le plus proche et surtout sain, avec des bascules rapides en cas de defaillance. C'est la solution reseau faible latence adaptee a une app deployee dans chaque Region.

question: A company has one million users that use its mobile app. The company must analyze the data usage in near-real time. The company also must encrypt the data in near-real time and must store the data in a centralized location in Apache Parquet format for further processing. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.A: Create an Amazon Kinesis data stream to store the data in Amazon S3. Create an Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics application to analyze the data. Invoke an AWS Lambda function to send the data to the Kinesis Data Analytics application.
options.B: Create an Amazon Kinesis data stream to store the data in Amazon S3. Create an Amazon EMR cluster to analyze the data. Invoke an AWS Lambda function to send the data to the EMR cluster.
options.C: Create an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream to store the data in Amazon S3. Create an Amazon EMR cluster to analyze the data.
options.D: Create an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream to store the data in Amazon S3. Create an Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics application to analyze the data.

radar.signal: Ingestion managee vers S3 en Parquet + analyse temps quasi reel -> Kinesis Data Firehose (vers S3, conversion Parquet, chiffrement) + Kinesis Data Analytics

pieges.A: Data Streams + Lambda pour alimenter Data Analytics = plus de pieces a gerer que Firehose
pieges.B: EMR = cluster a gerer, plus d'overhead
pieges.C: Firehose est bon mais EMR pour l'analyse ajoute un cluster a operer

explication: Kinesis Data Firehose est entierement manage : il ingere le flux, chiffre, convertit en Parquet et depose dans S3 sans serveur. Kinesis Data Analytics analyse le flux en quasi temps reel. Cette combinaison sans cluster (contrairement a EMR) offre le moins d'overhead operationnel.

question: A company uses AWS Organizations to manage multiple AWS accounts for different departments. The management account has an Amazon S3 bucket that contains project reports. The company wants to limit access to this S3 bucket to only users of accounts within the organization in AWS Organizations. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST amount of operational overhead?

options.A: Add the aws:PrincipalOrgID global condition key with a reference to the organization ID to the S3 bucket policy.
options.B: Create an organizational unit (OU) for each department. Add the aws:PrincipalOrgPaths global condition key to the S3 bucket policy.
options.C: Use AWS CloudTrail to monitor the CreateAccount, InviteAccountToOrganization, LeaveOrganization, and RemoveAccountFromOrganization events. Update the S3 bucket policy accordingly.
options.D: Tag each user that needs access to the S3 bucket. Add the aws:PrincipalTag global condition key to the S3 bucket policy.

declencheurs: limit S3 bucket access to accounts within the organization
radar.signal: Restreindre un bucket aux comptes de l'organisation -> condition aws:PrincipalOrgID (avec l'org ID) dans la bucket policy

pieges.B: aws:PrincipalOrgPaths + OUs = plus complexe que necessaire pour 'toute l'organisation'
pieges.C: Surveiller des evenements CloudTrail et mettre a jour la policy = maintenance manuelle continue
pieges.D: Taguer chaque utilisateur = gestion fastidieuse a l'echelle

explication: La cle de condition globale aws:PrincipalOrgID, referencant l'ID de l'organisation dans la bucket policy, autorise d'un coup tous les principals des comptes de l'organisation et se met a jour automatiquement quand des comptes rejoignent/partent. C'est le minimum d'overhead.

question: An application runs on an Amazon EC2 instance in a VPC. The application processes logs that are stored in an Amazon S3 bucket. The EC2 instance needs to access the S3 bucket without connectivity to the internet. Which solution will provide private network connectivity to Amazon S3?

options.A: Create a gateway VPC endpoint to the S3 bucket.
options.B: Stream the logs to Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Export the logs to the S3 bucket.
options.C: Create an instance profile on Amazon EC2 to allow S3 access.
options.D: Create an Amazon API Gateway API with a private link to access the S3 endpoint.

radar.signal: Acces prive a S3 depuis un VPC -> gateway VPC endpoint pour S3

pieges.B: Passer par CloudWatch Logs puis exporter = detour inutile
pieges.C: Un instance profile donne des permissions IAM, pas un chemin reseau prive
pieges.D: API Gateway ne fournit pas un acces reseau prive a S3 ainsi

explication: Le gateway VPC endpoint pour S3 cree une route privee vers S3 via le reseau AWS, sans Internet. Un instance profile ne gere que les autorisations (le 'qui peut'), pas la connectivite reseau (le 'par ou'), qui est justement le besoin ici.

question: A company is hosting a web application on AWS using a single Amazon EC2 instance that stores user-uploaded documents in an Amazon EBS volume. For better scalability and availability, the company duplicated the architecture and created a second EC2 instance and EBS volume in another Availability Zone, placing both behind an Application Load Balancer. After completing this change, users reported that, each time they refreshed the website, they could see one subset of their documents or the other, but never all of the documents at the same time. What should a solutions architect propose to ensure users see all of their documents at once?

options.A: Copy the data so both EBS volumes contain all the documents.
options.B: Configure the Application Load Balancer to direct a user to the server with the documents.
options.C: Copy the data from both EBS volumes to Amazon EFS. Modify the application to save new documents to Amazon EFS.
options.D: Configure the Application Load Balancer to send the request to both servers. Return each document from the correct server.

declencheurs: documents on separate EBS per instance
users see one subset or the other
radar.signal: Donnees dupliquees/divergentes sur des EBS par instance -> stockage partage commun : Amazon EFS monte sur toutes les instances

pieges.A: Copier une fois ne resout pas les ecritures futures qui redivergent
pieges.B: Router vers 'le serveur avec les documents' n'a pas de sens (chaque serveur en a une partie)
pieges.D: Fusionner les reponses de deux serveurs = bricolage applicatif fragile

explication: Le probleme vient du stockage local par instance : chaque EBS ne contient qu'une partie des documents. En deplaçant les fichiers vers un systeme partage Amazon EFS monte par toutes les instances, tout le monde voit l'ensemble des documents quel que soit le serveur qui repond. Une simple copie unique (A) redivergerait des la prochaine ecriture.

question: A company's marketing data is uploaded from multiple sources to an Amazon S3 bucket. A series of data preparation jobs aggregate the data for reporting. The data preparation jobs need to run at regular intervals in parallel. A few jobs need to run in a specific order later. The company wants to remove the operational overhead of job error handling, retry logic, and state management. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Use an AWS Lambda function to process the data as soon as the data is uploaded to the S3 bucket. Invoke other Lambda functions at regularly scheduled intervals.
options.B: Use Amazon Athena to process the data. Use Amazon EventBridge Scheduler to invoke Athena on a regular interval.
options.C: Use AWS Glue DataBrew to process the data. Use an AWS Step Functions state machine to run the DataBrew data preparation jobs.
options.D: Use AWS Data Pipeline to process the data. Schedule Data Pipeline to process the data once at midnight.

declencheurs: data prep jobs in parallel + some in specific order
remove error handling / retry / state management overhead
radar.signal: Orchestrer des jobs (parallele + sequence) avec gestion d'etat/reprises deleguee -> AWS Step Functions pilotant des jobs Glue DataBrew

pieges.A: Des Lambda planifiees a la main ne gerent ni l'orchestration ni l'etat/reprise
pieges.B: Athena + EventBridge n'orchestre pas des dependances entre jobs
pieges.D: Data Pipeline (service en fin de vie) et une seule execution a minuit ne repondent pas au besoin parallele/ordonne

explication: AWS Step Functions gere nativement l'orchestration (execution parallele et sequences), les reprises sur erreur et l'etat, supprimant cet overhead du cote de l'equipe. Il pilote les jobs de preparation Glue DataBrew (no-code). Les Lambda planifiees ou Athena n'offrent pas cette gestion d'etat et de dependances.

question: A solutions architect is designing a payment processing application that runs on AWS Lambda in private subnets across multiple Availability Zones. The application uses multiple Lambda functions and processes millions of transactions each day. The architecture must ensure that the application does not process duplicate payments. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Use Lambda to retrieve all due payments. Publish the due payments to an Amazon S3 bucket. Configure the S3 bucket with an event notification to invoke another Lambda function to process the due payments.
options.B: Use Lambda to retrieve all due payments. Publish the due payments to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Configure another Lambda function to poll the SQS queue and to process the due payments.
options.C: Use Lambda to retrieve all due payments. Publish the due payments to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) FIFO queue. Configure another Lambda function to poll the FIFO queue and to process the due payments.
options.D: Use Lambda to retrieve all due payments. Store the due payments in an Amazon DynamoDB table. Configure streams on the DynamoDB table to invoke another Lambda function to process the due payments.

radar.signal: Eviter les paiements en double + traitement ordonne -> file SQS FIFO (deduplication + exactly-once processing)

pieges.A: S3 + event n'offre pas de deduplication de traitement
pieges.B: Une file SQS standard peut livrer des doublons (at-least-once)
pieges.D: DynamoDB Streams n'apporte pas la garantie de non-duplication de traitement des paiements

explication: Une file SQS FIFO garantit la deduplication et un traitement exactly-once dans l'ordre, ce qui empeche de traiter deux fois le meme paiement. Les files standard (B) sont at-least-once et peuvent donc dupliquer, ce qui est redhibitoire pour des paiements.

question: An application allows users at a company's headquarters to access product data. The product data is stored in an Amazon RDS MySQL DB instance. The operations team has isolated an application performance slowdown and wants to separate read traffic from write traffic. A solutions architect needs to optimize the application's performance quickly. What should the solutions architect recommend?

options.A: Change the existing database to a Multi-AZ deployment. Serve the read requests from the primary Availability Zone.
options.B: Change the existing database to a Multi-AZ deployment. Serve the read requests from the secondary Availability Zone.
options.C: Create read replicas for the database. Configure the read replicas with half of the compute and storage resources as the source database.
options.D: Create read replicas for the database. Configure the read replicas with the same compute and storage resources as the source database.

radar.signal: Separer lectures et ecritures -> read replicas RDS, dimensionnees comme la source pour eviter le retard de replication

pieges.A: Multi-AZ ne sert pas les lectures depuis le primaire pour decharger l'ecriture
pieges.B: Le standby Multi-AZ n'est pas interrogeable (piege classique)
pieges.C: Des replicas sous-dimensionnees (moitie des ressources) accumuleraient du lag

explication: Des read replicas RDS absorbent le trafic de lecture et soulagent le primaire pour les ecritures. Il faut les dimensionner comme la source (memes compute/stockage) afin qu'elles suivent le rythme et ne prennent pas de retard. Le standby Multi-AZ, lui, n'est jamais interrogeable.

question: A solutions architect needs to help a company optimize the cost of running an application on AWS. The application will use Amazon EC2 instances, AWS Fargate, and AWS Lambda for compute within the architecture. The EC2 instances will run the data ingestion layer of the application. EC2 usage will be sporadic and unpredictable. Workloads that run on EC2 instances can be interrupted at any time. The application front end will run on Fargate, and Lambda will serve the API layer. The frontend utilization and API layer utilization will be predictable over the course of the next year. Which combination of purchasing options will provide the MOST cost-effective solution for hosting this application? (Choose two.)

options.A: Use Spot Instances for the data ingestion layer.
options.B: Use On-Demand Instances for the data ingestion layer.
options.C: Purchase a 1-year Compute Savings Plan for the front end and API layer.
options.D: Purchase 1-year All Upfront Reserved Instances for the data ingestion layer.
options.E: Purchase a 1-year EC2 Instance Savings Plan for the front end and API layer.

declencheurs: Fargate + Lambda predictable over a year
radar.signal: Ingestion interruptible -> Spot ; front (Fargate) + API (Lambda) previsibles -> Compute Savings Plan 1 an

pieges.B: On-Demand pour l'ingestion = plus cher que Spot pour une charge interruptible
pieges.D: Reserved Instances pour une charge sporadique/interruptible = engagement mal adapte
pieges.E: Un EC2 Instance Savings Plan ne couvre ni Fargate ni Lambda

explication: La couche d'ingestion, sporadique et interruptible, est idealement couverte par des Spot Instances (A). Le frontend Fargate et l'API Lambda, a l'utilisation previsible sur un an, sont couverts par un Compute Savings Plan (C) qui, contrairement a un EC2 Instance Savings Plan, s'applique bien a Fargate et Lambda.

question: A company runs a web-based portal that provides users with global breaking news, local alerts, and weather updates. The portal delivers each user a personalized view by using a mixture of static and dynamic content. Content is served over HTTPS through an API server running on an Amazon EC2 instance behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The company wants the portal to provide this content to its users across the world as quickly as possible. How should a solutions architect design the application to ensure the LEAST amount of latency for all users?

options.A: Deploy the application stack in a single AWS Region. Use Amazon CloudFront to serve all static and dynamic content by specifying the ALB as an origin.
options.B: Deploy the application stack in two AWS Regions. Use an Amazon Route 53 latency routing policy to serve all content from the ALB in the closest Region.
options.C: Deploy the application stack in a single AWS Region. Use Amazon CloudFront to serve the static content. Serve the dynamic content directly from the ALB.
options.D: Deploy the application stack in two AWS Regions. Use an Amazon Route 53 geolocation routing policy to serve all content from the ALB in the closest Region.

radar.signal: Accelerer contenu statique ET dynamique mondialement -> CloudFront avec l'ALB en origine (le contenu dynamique transite aussi par le reseau edge d'AWS)

pieges.B: Deux Regions + routing latence = plus complexe et couteux qu'un CDN unique
pieges.C: Servir le dynamique directement depuis l'ALB laisse la latence internationale
pieges.D: Le geolocation routing choisit par pays, pas forcement la plus faible latence, et duplique l'infra

explication: CloudFront, avec l'ALB comme origine, accelere non seulement le contenu statique (mis en cache au bord) mais aussi le contenu dynamique, qui emprunte le reseau backbone d'AWS jusqu'a l'origine. On reduit ainsi la latence pour tous les utilisateurs sans dupliquer l'architecture dans plusieurs Regions.

question: A company that runs its application on AWS uses an Amazon Aurora DB cluster as its database. During peak usage hours when multiple users access and read the data, the monitoring system shows degradation of database performance for the write queries. The company wants to increase the scalability of the application to meet peak usage demands. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

options.A: Create a second Aurora DB cluster. Configure a copy job to replicate the users' data to the new database. Update the application to use the second database to read the data.
options.B: Create an Amazon DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) cluster in front of the existing Aurora DB cluster. Update the application to use the DAX cluster for read-only queries. Write data directly to the Aurora DB cluster.
options.C: Create an Aurora read replica in the existing Aurora DB cluster. Update the application to use the replica endpoint for read-only queries and to use the cluster endpoint for write queries.
options.D: Create an Amazon Redshift cluster. Copy the users' data to the Redshift cluster. Update the application to connect to the Redshift cluster and to perform read-only queries on the Redshift cluster.

radar.signal: Decharger les lectures d'Aurora a moindre cout -> Aurora read replica (endpoint reader pour les lectures, cluster endpoint pour les ecritures)

pieges.A: Un second cluster + job de copie = couteux et complexe
pieges.B: DAX est un cache pour DynamoDB, pas pour Aurora
pieges.D: Redshift est un entrepot analytique, surdimensionne et couteux pour ce besoin transactionnel

explication: Ajouter une Aurora read replica et diriger les requetes de lecture vers le reader endpoint (tout en ecrivant via le cluster endpoint) soulage le primaire pendant les pics, a faible cout. DAX ne fonctionne qu'avec DynamoDB, et Redshift serait disproportionne.

question: A company near-real-time streaming application is running on AWS. As the data is ingested, a job runs on the data and takes 30 minutes to complete. The workload frequently experiences high latency due to large amounts of incoming data. A solutions architect needs to design a scalable and serverless solution to enhance performance. Which combination of steps should the solutions architect take? (Choose two.)

options.A: Use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to ingest the data.
options.B: Use AWS Lambda with AWS Step Functions to process the data.
options.C: Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to ingest the data.
options.D: Use Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group to process the data.
options.E: Use AWS Fargate with Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) to process the data.

radar.signal: Ingestion + traitement serverless scalables -> Kinesis Data Firehose (ingestion) + Lambda orchestre par Step Functions (traitement)

pieges.C: DMS sert a migrer des bases, pas a ingerer un flux temps reel
pieges.D: EC2 en Auto Scaling n'est pas serverless
pieges.E: Fargate est serverless (alternative valable pour un job long) mais la cle retient Lambda + Step Functions

explication: Kinesis Data Firehose ingere le flux de facon scalable et managee (A), et AWS Step Functions orchestre des fonctions Lambda pour le traitement serverless en decoupant le workflow (B). Note : comme une Lambda est limitee a 15 min, un job reellement monolithique de 30 min plaiderait pour Fargate (E) ; c'est le point a verifier selon la formulation exacte.

question: A company is designing a shared storage solution for a gaming application that is hosted in the AWS Cloud. The company needs the ability to use SMB clients to access data. The solution must be fully managed. Which AWS solution meets these requirements?

options.A: Create an AWS DataSync task that shares the data as a mountable file system. Mount the file system to the application server.
options.B: Create an Amazon EC2 Windows instance. Install and configure a Windows file share role on the instance. Connect the application server to the file share.
options.C: Create an Amazon FSx for Windows File Server file system. Attach the file system to the origin server. Connect the application server to the file system.
options.D: Create an Amazon S3 bucket. Assign an IAM role to the application to grant access to the S3 bucket. Mount the S3 bucket to the application server.

radar.signal: Partage de fichiers SMB entierement manage -> Amazon FSx for Windows File Server

pieges.A: DataSync transfere des donnees, ce n'est pas un partage de fichiers SMB persistant
pieges.B: Un serveur de fichiers Windows sur EC2 = a gerer soi-meme (pas fully managed)
pieges.D: S3 n'est pas un partage SMB montable nativement

explication: Amazon FSx for Windows File Server offre un partage de fichiers SMB natif et entierement manage, exactement ce que demande l'enonce. Un serveur de fichiers sur EC2 imposerait de gerer l'OS et le service, et S3 n'expose pas de partage SMB.

question: A company wants to run an in-memory database for a latency-sensitive application that runs on Amazon EC2 instances. The application processes more than 100,000 transactions each minute and requires high network throughput. A solutions architect needs to provide a cost-effective network design that minimizes data transfer charges. Which solution meets these requirements?

options.A: Launch all EC2 instances in the same Availability Zone within the same AWS Region. Specify a placement group with cluster strategy when launching EC2 instances.
options.B: Launch all EC2 instances in different Availability Zones within the same AWS Region. Specify a placement group with partition strategy when launching EC2 instances.
options.C: Deploy an Auto Scaling group to launch EC2 instances in different Availability Zones based on a network utilization target.
options.D: Deploy an Auto Scaling group with a step scaling policy to launch EC2 instances in different Availability Zones.

radar.signal: Haut debit reseau + zero cout de transfert inter-AZ -> toutes les EC2 dans la meme AZ + placement group en strategie cluster

pieges.B: Repartir sur plusieurs AZ genere des frais de transfert inter-AZ
pieges.C: Auto Scaling multi-AZ ajoute du transfert inter-AZ facture
pieges.D: Idem : instances dans differentes AZ = couts de transfert

explication: Un placement group en strategie cluster regroupe les instances au plus pres pour un debit reseau maximal et une latence minimale. Les placer dans la meme AZ evite tout frais de transfert inter-AZ. Repartir sur plusieurs AZ ameliorerait la resilience mais couterait en transfert, contraire a l'objectif.

question: A company is planning to run a group of Amazon EC2 instances that connect to an Amazon Aurora database. The company has built an AWS CloudFormation template to deploy the EC2 instances and the Aurora DB cluster. The company wants to allow the instances to authenticate to the database in a secure way. The company does not want to maintain static database credentials. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational effort?

options.A: Create a database user with a user name and password. Add parameters for the database user name and password to the CloudFormation template. Pass the parameters to the EC2 instances when the instances are launched.
options.B: Create a database user with a user name and password. Store the user name and password in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store. Configure the EC2 instances to retrieve the database credentials from Parameter Store.
options.C: Configure the DB cluster to use IAM database authentication. Create a database user to use with IAM authentication. Associate a role with the EC2 instances to allow applications on the instances to access the database.
options.D: Configure the DB cluster to use IAM database authentication with an IAM user. Create a database user that has a name that matches the IAM user. Associate the IAM user with the EC2 instances to allow applications on the instances to access the database.

radar.signal: Auth a la base sans identifiants statiques -> IAM database authentication + role IAM sur les EC2

pieges.A: Passer user/password en parametres = identifiants statiques (ce qu'on veut eviter)
pieges.B: Parameter Store stocke encore des identifiants statiques a gerer
pieges.D: L'authentification IAM DB se fait via un role sur l'EC2, pas en associant un IAM user aux instances

explication: L'authentification IAM a la base Aurora supprime les mots de passe statiques : les instances obtiennent des jetons temporaires grace a un role IAM associe aux EC2. C'est le moindre effort operationnel et le plus sur. Les options A et B conservent des identifiants statiques a gerer.

question: A company wants to configure its Amazon CloudFront distribution to use SSL/TLS certificates. The company does not want to use the default domain name for the distribution. Instead, the company wants to use a different domain name for the distribution. Which solution will deploy the certificate without incurring any additional costs?

options.A: Request an Amazon issued private certificate from AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) in the us-east-1 Region.
options.B: Request an Amazon issued private certificate from AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) in the us-west-1 Region.
options.C: Request an Amazon issued public certificate from AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) in the us-east-1 Region.
options.D: Request an Amazon issued public certificate from AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) in the us-west-1 Region.

radar.signal: Certificat gratuit pour un domaine custom sur CloudFront -> certificat public ACM dans us-east-1 (region obligatoire pour CloudFront)

pieges.A: Un certificat prive ACM est payant (CA privee)
pieges.B: Prive = payant, et mauvaise region
pieges.D: Public gratuit mais CloudFront exige la region us-east-1, pas us-west-1

explication: Les certificats publics ACM sont gratuits. CloudFront impose que le certificat soit demande dans la region us-east-1 (N. Virginia). Un certificat prive ACM, lui, engendre des couts de CA privee. La bonne reponse est donc un certificat public dans us-east-1.

question: A company serves a dynamic website from a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The website needs to support multiple languages to serve customers around the world. The website's architecture is running in the us-west-1 Region and is exhibiting high request latency for users that are located in other parts of the world. The website needs to serve requests quickly and efficiently regardless of a user's location. However, the company does not want to recreate the existing architecture across multiple Regions. What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

options.A: Replace the existing architecture with a website that is served from an Amazon S3 bucket. Configure an Amazon CloudFront distribution with the S3 bucket as the origin. Set the cache behavior settings to cache based on the Accept-Language request header.
options.B: Configure an Amazon CloudFront distribution with the ALB as the origin. Set the cache behavior settings to cache based on the Accept-Language request header.
options.C: Create an Amazon API Gateway API that is integrated with the ALB. Configure the API to use the HTTP Integration type. Set up an API Gateway stage to enable the API cache based on the Accept-Language request header.
options.D: Launch an EC2 instance in each additional Region and configure NGINX to act as a cache server for that Region. Put all the EC2 instances and the ALB behind an Amazon Route 53 record set with a geolocation routing policy.

declencheurs: do not recreate architecture in multiple Regions
radar.signal: Reduire la latence mondiale sans dupliquer l'infra + varier par langue -> CloudFront avec origine ALB, cache base sur l'en-tete Accept-Language

pieges.A: Servir depuis S3 impose de refaire un site statique (l'app est dynamique)
pieges.C: API Gateway devant l'ALB = detour complexe, pas concu pour ce cache CDN mondial
pieges.D: Des serveurs NGINX par Region = recreer de l'infra, ce que l'entreprise refuse

explication: CloudFront, avec l'ALB en origine, rapproche le contenu des utilisateurs du monde entier sans recreer l'architecture ailleurs. En mettant en cache selon l'en-tete Accept-Language, on sert la bonne version linguistique. C'est la solution la plus simple qui reduit la latence globale.

question: A rapidly growing ecommerce company is running its workloads in a single AWS Region. A solutions architect must create a disaster recovery (DR) strategy that includes a different AWS Region. The company wants its database to be up to date in the DR Region with the least possible latency. The remaining infrastructure in the DR Region needs to run at reduced capacity and must be able to scale up if necessary. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LOWEST recovery time objective (RTO)?

options.A: Use an Amazon Aurora global database with a pilot light deployment.
options.B: Use an Amazon Aurora global database with a warm standby deployment.
options.C: Use an Amazon RDS Multi-AZ DB instance with a pilot light deployment.
options.D: Use an Amazon RDS Multi-AZ DB instance with a warm standby deployment.

declencheurs: database up to date with least latency
radar.signal: RTO le plus bas + base repliquee cross-Region a faible latence + infra deja active reduite -> Aurora global database + deploiement warm standby

pieges.A: Le pilot light garde l'infra quasi eteinte -> RTO plus eleve que le warm standby
pieges.C: RDS Multi-AZ ne couvre qu'une Region (pas de DR cross-Region)
pieges.D: RDS Multi-AZ n'offre pas de replication cross-Region a faible latence comme l'Aurora global database

explication: Une Aurora global database replique vers l'autre Region avec une latence tres faible (typiquement < 1 s). Un deploiement warm standby maintient une infrastructure deja active a capacite reduite, prete a monter en charge : c'est ce qui donne le RTO le plus bas. Le pilot light aurait un RTO plus long, et RDS Multi-AZ n'est pas cross-Region.

question: A company runs a microservice-based serverless web application. The application must be able to retrieve data from multiple Amazon DynamoDB tables. A solutions architect needs to give the application the ability to retrieve the data with no impact on the baseline performance of the application. Which solution will meet these requirements in the MOST operationally efficient way?

options.A: AWS AppSync pipeline resolvers.
options.B: Amazon CloudFront with Lambda@Edge functions.
options.C: Edge-optimized Amazon API Gateway with AWS Lambda functions.
options.D: Amazon Athena Federated Query with a DynamoDB connector.

declencheurs: retrieve data from multiple DynamoDB tables
radar.signal: Agreger plusieurs tables DynamoDB en un appel, en serverless manage -> AWS AppSync pipeline resolvers

pieges.B: CloudFront + Lambda@Edge sert du contenu au bord, pas l'agregation multi-tables
pieges.C: API Gateway + Lambda impose d'ecrire/maintenir la logique d'agregation
pieges.D: Athena Federated Query est fait pour de l'analytique, pas pour des lectures applicatives a faible latence

explication: Les pipeline resolvers d'AWS AppSync enchainent plusieurs operations (ici sur plusieurs tables DynamoDB) dans une seule requete GraphQL managee, sans code serveur a maintenir ni impact sur la performance de base. C'est l'option la plus efficace operationnellement pour composer des lectures multi-tables.

question: A company wants to analyze and troubleshoot Access Denied errors and Unauthorized errors that are related to IAM permissions. The company has AWS CloudTrail turned on. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST effort?

options.A: Use AWS Glue and write custom scripts to query CloudTrail logs for the errors.
options.B: Use AWS Batch and write custom scripts to query CloudTrail logs for the errors.
options.C: Search CloudTrail logs with Amazon Athena queries to identify the errors.
options.D: Search CloudTrail logs with Amazon QuickSight. Create a dashboard to identify the errors.

radar.signal: Interroger des logs CloudTrail avec le moins d'effort -> requetes Amazon Athena sur les logs CloudTrail

pieges.A: Glue + scripts custom = developpement inutile
pieges.B: AWS Batch + scripts custom = encore plus lourd
pieges.D: QuickSight sert a visualiser, pas a interroger directement, et demande une mise en place

explication: Amazon Athena interroge directement les logs CloudTrail en SQL, sans infrastructure ni scripts a developper : quelques requetes suffisent a isoler les erreurs Access Denied et Unauthorized. Glue, Batch et QuickSight demanderaient bien plus d'effort de mise en place.

question: A company application runs on Amazon EC2 instances that are in multiple Availability Zones. The application needs to ingest real-time data from third-party applications. The company needs a data ingestion solution that places the ingested raw data in an Amazon S3 bucket. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Create Amazon Kinesis data streams for data ingestion. Create Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery streams to consume the Kinesis data streams. Specify the S3 bucket as the destination of the delivery streams.
options.B: Create database migration tasks in AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS). Specify replication instances of the EC2 instances as the source endpoints. Specify the S3 bucket as the target endpoint. Set the migration type to migrate existing data and replicate ongoing changes.
options.C: Create and configure AWS DataSync agents on the EC2 instances. Configure DataSync tasks to transfer data from the EC2 instances to the S3 bucket.
options.D: Create an AWS Direct Connect connection to the application for data ingestion. Create Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery streams to consume direct PUT operations from the application. Specify the S3 bucket as the destination of the delivery streams.

declencheurs: ingest real-time data from third parties
radar.signal: Ingestion temps reel puis depot du brut dans S3 -> Kinesis Data Streams + Kinesis Data Firehose vers le bucket S3

pieges.B: DMS migre des bases, il n'ingere pas un flux temps reel de tiers
pieges.C: DataSync transfere des fichiers, pas un flux temps reel
pieges.D: Direct Connect (liaison privee dediee) est inutile pour ingerer depuis des applications tierces publiques

explication: Kinesis Data Streams capte le flux temps reel, et Kinesis Data Firehose le consomme pour deposer les donnees brutes dans S3, le tout manage. DMS et DataSync ne traitent pas un flux temps reel, et Direct Connect n'a pas lieu d'etre pour des sources tierces.

question: A company application is receiving data from multiple data sources. The size of the data varies and is expected to increase over time. The current maximum size is 700 KB. The data volume and data size continue to grow as more data sources are added. The company decides to use Amazon DynamoDB as the primary database for the application. A solutions architect needs to identify a solution that handles the large data sizes. Which solution will meet these requirements in the MOST operationally efficient way?

options.A: Create an AWS Lambda function to filter the data that exceeds DynamoDB item size limits. Store the larger data in an Amazon DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility) database.
options.B: Store the large data as objects in an Amazon S3 bucket. In a DynamoDB table, create an item that has an attribute that points to the S3 URL of the data.
options.C: Split all incoming large data into a collection of items that have the same partition key. Write the data to a DynamoDB table in a single operation by using the BatchWriteItem API operation.
options.D: Create an AWS Lambda function that uses gzip compression to compress the large objects as they are written to a DynamoDB table.

radar.signal: Objets depassant la limite d'item DynamoDB (400 KB) -> stocker le gros dans S3 et garder un pointeur (URL S3) dans l'item DynamoDB

pieges.A: Ajouter DocumentDB pour les gros objets = deuxieme base a gerer
pieges.C: Decouper en plusieurs items avec BatchWriteItem = complexe et fragile
pieges.D: La compression gzip ne suffit pas quand la donnee depasse durablement 400 KB

explication: Un item DynamoDB est limite a 400 KB, or les donnees atteignent 700 KB et grossissent. Le pattern recommande est de stocker l'objet volumineux dans S3 et de conserver dans DynamoDB un attribut pointant vers l'URL S3. C'est simple, scalable et evite d'ajouter une seconde base.

question: A company collects and processes data from a vendor. The vendor stores its data in an Amazon RDS for MySQL database in the vendor's own AWS account. The company VPC does not have an internet gateway, an AWS Direct Connect connection, or an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection. The company needs to access the data that is in the vendor database. Which solution will meet this requirement?

options.A: Instruct the vendor to sign up for the AWS Hosted Connection Direct Connect Program. Use VPC peering to connect the company's VPC and the vendor's VPC.
options.B: Configure a client VPN connection between the company's VPC and the vendor's VPC. Use VPC peering to connect the company VPC and the vendor's VPC.
options.C: Instruct the vendor to create a Network Load Balancer (NLB). Place the NLB in front of the Amazon RDS for MySQL database. Use AWS PrivateLink to integrate the company's VPC and the vendor's VPC.
options.D: Use AWS Transit Gateway to integrate the company's VPC and the vendor's VPC. Use VPC peering to connect the company's VPC and the vendor's VPC.

declencheurs: access vendor's RDS in vendor's account
no IGW, no Direct Connect, no VPN
private cross-account access to one service
radar.signal: Acceder de facon privee a UN service d'un autre compte, sans Internet -> le fournisseur place un NLB devant RDS et l'expose via AWS PrivateLink (interface endpoint cote entreprise)

pieges.A: Le 'Direct Connect Hosted Connection Program' sert a relier de l'on-prem, pas deux VPC ; formulation hors sujet
pieges.B: Un client VPN + peering est complexe et non adapte a l'exposition d'un seul service
pieges.D: Transit Gateway + peering = sur-ingenierie pour acceder a un unique service RDS

alerte_cle: La cle du fichier indique A, mais A melange un 'Direct Connect Program' hors sujet (l'on-prem, pas du VPC-a-VPC). Le motif attendu pour exposer un seul service entre comptes sans Internet est AWS PrivateLink : la reponse est C.
explication: AWS PrivateLink est concu pour exposer un service unique entre comptes/VPC de facon privee, sans Internet ni VPN. Le fournisseur place un Network Load Balancer devant sa base RDS et cree un endpoint service ; l'entreprise cree un interface endpoint pour s'y connecter. Direct Connect (A) concerne la connectivite on-prem et n'a pas de sens ici.

question: A company wants to set up Amazon Managed Grafana as its visualization tool. The company wants to visualize data from its Amazon RDS database as one data source. The company needs a secure solution that will not expose the data over the internet. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Create an Amazon Managed Grafana workspace without a VPC. Create a public endpoint for the RDS database. Configure the public endpoint as a data source in Amazon Managed Grafana.
options.B: Create an Amazon Managed Grafana workspace in a VPC. Create a private endpoint for the RDS database. Configure the private endpoint as a data source in Amazon Managed Grafana.
options.C: Create an Amazon Managed Grafana workspace without a VPC. Create an AWS PrivateLink endpoint to establish a connection between Amazon Managed Grafana and Amazon RDS. Set up Amazon RDS as a data source in Amazon Managed Grafana.
options.D: Create an Amazon Managed Grafana workspace in a VPC. Create a public endpoint for the RDS database. Configure the public endpoint as a data source in Amazon Managed Grafana.

declencheurs: secure, not exposed over the internet
radar.signal: Connexion privee entre Managed Grafana et RDS -> workspace Grafana dans un VPC + endpoint prive vers RDS

pieges.A: Workspace sans VPC + endpoint RDS public = exposition sur Internet
pieges.C: PrivateLink entre Managed Grafana et RDS n'est pas le montage standard ; le workspace doit etre dans un VPC
pieges.D: Un endpoint RDS public expose la base sur Internet, meme si le workspace est dans un VPC

explication: En creant le workspace Amazon Managed Grafana dans un VPC et en utilisant un endpoint prive vers la base RDS, le trafic reste sur le reseau prive AWS sans jamais passer par Internet. Toute option reposant sur un endpoint RDS public (A, D) exposerait la base sur Internet.

question: A company security team requests that network traffic be captured in VPC Flow Logs. The logs will be frequently accessed for 90 days and then accessed intermittently. What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements when configuring the logs?

options.A: Use Amazon CloudWatch as the target. Set the CloudWatch log group with an expiration of 90 days.
options.B: Use Amazon Kinesis as the target. Configure the Kinesis stream to always retain the logs for 90 days.
options.C: Use AWS CloudTrail as the target. Configure CloudTrail to save to an Amazon S3 bucket, and enable S3 Intelligent-Tiering.
options.D: Use Amazon S3 as the target. Enable an S3 Lifecycle policy to transition the logs to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) after 90 days.

radar.signal: Garder les logs longtemps avec un cout reduit apres 90 jours -> S3 comme cible + S3 Lifecycle vers Standard-IA apres 90 jours

pieges.A: Une expiration a 90 jours sur CloudWatch SUPPRIME les logs, empechant l'acces intermittent ensuite
pieges.B: Kinesis est un flux, pas un stockage long terme economique
pieges.C: Les Flow Logs ne ciblent pas CloudTrail (services distincts)

alerte_cle: La cle du fichier indique A, mais A configure une expiration a 90 jours qui SUPPRIME les logs, alors que l'enonce demande un acces intermittent apres 90 jours. La bonne reponse est D (S3 + Lifecycle vers Standard-IA).
explication: L'enonce veut conserver les logs au-dela de 90 jours pour un acces occasionnel. En ciblant Amazon S3 et en appliquant une Lifecycle policy qui bascule vers S3 Standard-IA apres 90 jours, on garde les donnees accessibles a moindre cout. L'option A programme une expiration (suppression) a 90 jours, ce qui contredit le besoin.

question: An Amazon EC2 instance is located in a private subnet in a new VPC. This subnet does not have outbound internet access, but the EC2 instance needs the ability to download monthly security updates from an outside vendor. What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

options.A: Create an internet gateway, and attach it to the VPC. Configure the private subnet route table to use the internet gateway as the default route.
options.B: Create a NAT gateway, and place it in a public subnet. Configure the private subnet route table to use the NAT gateway as the default route.
options.C: Create a NAT instance, and place it in the same subnet where the EC2 instance is located. Configure the private subnet route table to use the NAT instance as the default route.
options.D: Create an internet gateway, and attach it to the VPC. Create a NAT instance, and place it in the same subnet where the EC2 instance is located. Configure the private subnet route table to use the internet gateway as the default route.

radar.signal: Acces Internet sortant seulement depuis un subnet prive -> NAT gateway dans un subnet public + route par defaut vers le NAT

pieges.A: Un internet gateway sur le subnet prive le rendrait public (et exposerait l'instance)
pieges.C: Une NAT instance DANS le subnet prive n'a pas d'acces Internet elle-meme (elle doit etre en subnet public)
pieges.D: Un IGW + NAT instance dans le subnet prive est incoherent

explication: Un NAT gateway place dans un subnet public permet aux instances d'un subnet prive d'initier des connexions sortantes (telechargement des mises a jour) sans etre joignables depuis Internet. La route par defaut du subnet prive pointe vers le NAT. Placer un IGW ou un NAT dans le subnet prive romprait l'isolation ou ne fonctionnerait pas.

question: A company stores its data on premises. The amount of data is growing beyond the company's available capacity. The company wants to migrate its data from the on-premises location to an Amazon S3 bucket. The company needs a solution that will automatically validate the integrity of the data after the transfer. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Order an AWS Snowball Edge device. Configure the Snowball Edge device to perform the online data transfer to an S3 bucket.
options.B: Deploy an AWS DataSync agent on premises. Configure the DataSync agent to perform the online data transfer to an S3 bucket.
options.C: Create an Amazon S3 File Gateway on premises. Configure the S3 File Gateway to perform the online data transfer to an S3 bucket.
options.D: Configure an accelerator in Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration on premises. Configure the accelerator to perform the online data transfer to an S3 bucket.

radar.signal: Transfert en ligne vers S3 avec verification d'integrite automatique -> agent AWS DataSync on-prem

pieges.A: Snowball Edge = transfert hors ligne par appareil, pas 'online'
pieges.C: S3 File Gateway expose un partage, il n'est pas concu pour une migration validee
pieges.D: S3 Transfer Acceleration accelere l'upload mais ne valide pas l'integrite automatiquement

explication: AWS DataSync realise le transfert en ligne vers S3 et verifie automatiquement l'integrite des donnees a l'arrivee (checksums), avec chiffrement en transit. Snowball est hors ligne, et Transfer Acceleration/File Gateway n'offrent pas cette validation d'integrite integree.

question: A company wants to migrate two DNS servers to AWS. The servers host a total of approximately 200 zones and receive 1 million requests each day on average. The company wants to maximize availability while minimizing the operational overhead that is related to the management of the two servers. What should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?

options.A: Create 200 new hosted zones in the Amazon Route 53 console. Import zone files.
options.B: Launch a single large Amazon EC2 instance. Import zone files. Configure Amazon CloudWatch alarms and notifications to alert the company about any downtime.
options.C: Migrate the servers to AWS by using AWS Server Migration Service (AWS SMS). Configure Amazon CloudWatch alarms and notifications to alert the company about any downtime.
options.D: Launch an Amazon EC2 instance in an Auto Scaling group across two Availability Zones. Import zone files. Set the desired capacity to 1 and the maximum capacity to 3 for the Auto Scaling group. Configure scaling alarms to scale based on CPU utilization.

radar.signal: DNS manage, hautement disponible, sans serveurs a gerer -> Amazon Route 53 (creer les hosted zones, importer les zone files)

pieges.B: Un unique EC2 = point de defaillance unique, pas hautement disponible
pieges.C: Migrer les serveurs (SMS) laisse des EC2 a gerer
pieges.D: EC2 en Auto Scaling pour du DNS = infrastructure a maintenir inutilement

explication: Amazon Route 53 est un service DNS manage, hautement disponible et scalable par conception. Creer les 200 hosted zones et importer les zone files supprime toute gestion de serveurs, contrairement aux options basees sur EC2 qui laissent de l'infrastructure a exploiter.

question: A company wants to improve its ability to clone large amounts of production data into a test environment in the same AWS Region. The data is stored in Amazon EC2 instances on Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes. Modifications to the cloned data must not affect the production environment. The software that accesses this data requires consistently high I/O performance. A solutions architect needs to minimize the time that is required to clone the production data into the test environment. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Take EBS snapshots of the production EBS volumes. Restore the snapshots onto EC2 instance store volumes in the test environment.
options.B: Configure the production EBS volumes to use the EBS Multi-Attach feature. Take EBS snapshots of the production EBS volumes. Attach the production EBS volumes to the EC2 instances in the test environment.
options.C: Take EBS snapshots of the production EBS volumes. Create and initialize new EBS volumes. Attach the new EBS volumes to EC2 instances in the test environment before restoring the volumes from the production EBS snapshots.
options.D: Take EBS snapshots of the production EBS volumes. Turn on the EBS fast snapshot restore feature on the EBS snapshots. Restore the snapshots into new EBS volumes. Attach the new EBS volumes to EC2 instances in the test environment.

declencheurs: clone large production data to test
radar.signal: Cloner vite avec de bonnes I/O des le depart -> snapshots EBS + Fast Snapshot Restore, restaures dans de nouveaux volumes isoles

pieges.A: Instance store = ephemere, perd les donnees a l'arret
pieges.B: Multi-Attach partage le meme volume -> les modifs de test impacteraient la prod
pieges.C: Restaurer sans FSR subit l'initialisation lente (I/O degradees au debut)

explication: Un volume EBS restaure depuis un snapshot est normalement lent au demarrage (les blocs se chargent a la demande depuis S3). Fast Snapshot Restore supprime cette latence d'initialisation, donnant des I/O pleines immediatement. On restaure dans de nouveaux volumes isoles, si bien que les modifications de test n'affectent pas la production.

question: An ecommerce company wants to launch a one-deal-a-day website on AWS. Each day will feature exactly one product on sale for a period of 24 hours. The company wants to be able to handle millions of requests each hour with millisecond latency during peak hours. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.A: Use Amazon S3 to host the full website in different S3 buckets. Add Amazon CloudFront distributions. Set the S3 buckets as origins for the distributions. Store the order data in Amazon S3.
options.B: Deploy the full website on Amazon EC2 instances that run in Auto Scaling groups across multiple Availability Zones. Add an Application Load Balancer (ALB) to distribute the website traffic. Add another ALB for the backend APIs. Store the data in Amazon RDS for MySQL.
options.C: Migrate the full application to run in containers. Host the containers on Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS). Use the Kubernetes Cluster Autoscaler to increase and decrease the number of pods to process bursts in traffic. Store the data in Amazon RDS for MySQL.
options.D: Use an Amazon S3 bucket to host the website's static content. Deploy an Amazon CloudFront distribution. Set the S3 bucket as the origin. Use Amazon API Gateway and AWS Lambda functions for the backend APIs. Store the data in Amazon DynamoDB.

radar.signal: Site a fort trafic, faible latence, sans serveur a gerer -> S3+CloudFront (statique) + API Gateway+Lambda (backend) + DynamoDB

pieges.A: S3 seul ne gere pas le backend/commande dynamique proprement
pieges.B: EC2 en Auto Scaling + RDS = serveurs et base a gerer
pieges.C: EKS = orchestration a operer, plus d'overhead

explication: L'architecture entierement serverless (S3 + CloudFront pour le statique, API Gateway + Lambda pour les API, DynamoDB pour les donnees) encaisse des millions de requetes a la milliseconde et scale automatiquement, sans serveurs ni base a administrer. Les options EC2/EKS imposent de gerer de l'infrastructure.

question: A company has a highly dynamic batch processing job that uses many Amazon EC2 instances to complete it. The job is stateless in nature, can be started and stopped at any given time with no negative impact, and typically takes upwards of 60 minutes total to complete. The company has asked a solutions architect to design a scalable and cost-effective solution that meets the requirements of the job. What should the solutions architect recommend?

options.A: Implement EC2 Spot Instances.
options.B: Purchase EC2 Reserved Instances.
options.C: Implement EC2 On-Demand Instances.
options.D: Implement the processing on AWS Lambda.

radar.signal: Traitement batch stateless et interruptible -> EC2 Spot Instances (jusqu'a 90% moins cher)

pieges.B: Reserved Instances = engagement long, inadapte a un batch intermittent
pieges.C: On-Demand = bien plus cher que Spot pour une charge interruptible
pieges.D: Lambda est limite a 15 min, or le job dure ~60 min

explication: Un job batch stateless qui tolere d'etre interrompu et relance est le cas d'usage type des Spot Instances, qui offrent le meilleur cout. Lambda est exclu car sa duree max est de 15 minutes alors que le job dure environ 60 minutes.

question: A company runs its two-tier ecommerce website on AWS. The web tier consists of a load balancer that sends traffic to Amazon EC2 instances. The database tier uses an Amazon RDS DB instance. The EC2 instances and the RDS DB instance should not be exposed to the public internet. The EC2 instances require internet access to complete payment processing of orders through a third-party web service. The application must be highly available. Which combination of configuration options will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.A: Use an Auto Scaling group to launch the EC2 instances in private subnets. Deploy an RDS Multi-AZ DB instance in private subnets.
options.B: Configure a VPC with two private subnets and two NAT gateways across two Availability Zones. Deploy an Application Load Balancer in the private subnets.
options.C: Use an Auto Scaling group to launch the EC2 instances in public subnets across two Availability Zones. Deploy an RDS Multi-AZ DB instance in private subnets.
options.D: Configure a VPC with one public subnet, one private subnet, and two NAT gateways across two Availability Zones. Deploy an Application Load Balancer in the public subnet.
options.E: Configure a VPC with two public subnets, two private subnets, and two NAT gateways across two Availability Zones. Deploy an Application Load Balancer in the public subnets.

declencheurs: EC2 need internet for payment (third party)
radar.signal: Web/BD prives + sortie Internet HA + ALB public -> ASG EC2 en subnets prives + RDS Multi-AZ prive (A) ET VPC 2 public/2 prives/2 NAT + ALB dans les subnets publics (E)

pieges.B: Un ALB dans des subnets prives ne peut pas recevoir le trafic public
pieges.C: Des EC2 en subnets publics les exposent a Internet (interdit)
pieges.D: Un seul subnet public/prive ne fournit pas la haute disponibilite multi-AZ

explication: Les instances EC2 vont dans des subnets prives (Auto Scaling) avec une base RDS Multi-AZ egalement privee (A), et l'infrastructure comporte 2 subnets publics/2 prives et un NAT gateway par AZ, avec l'ALB place dans les subnets publics (E). L'ALB doit etre public pour recevoir le trafic, tandis que les NAT permettent la sortie vers le service de paiement sans exposer les EC2.

question: A company is building a mobile app on AWS. The company wants to expand its reach to millions of users. The company needs to build a platform so that authorized users can watch the company's content on their mobile devices. What should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?

options.A: Publish content to a public Amazon S3 bucket. Use AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) keys to stream content.
options.B: Set up IPsec VPN between the mobile app and the AWS environment to stream content.
options.C: Use Amazon CloudFront. Provide signed URLs to stream content.
options.D: Set up AWS Client VPN between the mobile app and the AWS environment to stream content.

radar.signal: Diffuser du contenu a des utilisateurs autorises a grande echelle -> Amazon CloudFront avec des signed URLs

pieges.A: Un bucket S3 public expose le contenu a tous (pas 'autorises')
pieges.B: Un VPN IPsec ne passe pas a l'echelle de millions d'utilisateurs mobiles
pieges.D: Client VPN idem : inadapte a la diffusion grand public

explication: CloudFront diffuse le contenu mondialement avec faible latence, et les signed URLs (ou signed cookies) restreignent l'acces aux seuls utilisateurs autorises et pour une duree limitee. Les solutions VPN ne s'adaptent pas a des millions d'utilisateurs, et un bucket public ne controle pas l'autorisation.

question: A company has an on-premises MySQL database used by the global sales team with infrequent access patterns. The sales team requires the database to have minimal downtime. A database administrator wants to migrate this database to AWS without selecting a particular instance type in anticipation of more users in the future. Which service should a solutions architect recommend?

options.A: Amazon Aurora MySQL
options.B: Amazon Aurora Serverless for MySQL
options.C: Amazon Redshift Spectrum
options.D: Amazon RDS for MySQL

radar.signal: Base MySQL a acces irregulier, sans dimensionner d'instance, qui scale seule -> Amazon Aurora Serverless for MySQL

pieges.A: Aurora MySQL provisionne impose de choisir un type d'instance
pieges.C: Redshift Spectrum = analytique sur S3, pas une base transactionnelle MySQL
pieges.D: RDS for MySQL impose aussi de selectionner une classe d'instance

explication: Aurora Serverless for MySQL ajuste automatiquement la capacite selon la charge, sans qu'on ait a choisir ni gerer un type d'instance, ce qui convient a un acces irregulier et a une croissance future incertaine. Les options provisionnees (Aurora, RDS) exigent de dimensionner une instance.

question: A company runs a website that stores images of historical events. Website users need the ability to search and view images based on the year that the event in the image occurred. On average, users request each image only once or twice a year. The company wants a highly available solution to store and deliver the images to users. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

options.A: Store images in Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS). Use a web server that runs on Amazon EC2.
options.B: Store images in Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS). Use a web server that runs on Amazon EC2.
options.C: Store images in Amazon S3 Standard. Use S3 Standard to directly deliver images by using a static website.
options.D: Store images in Amazon S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA). Use S3 Standard-IA to directly deliver images by using a static website.

declencheurs: images accessed once or twice a year
radar.signal: Stocker/diffuser des images a acces rare -> Amazon S3 (site statique), classe adaptee a l'acces peu frequent

pieges.A: EBS + EC2 = serveur a gerer et volume non partage, plus cher
pieges.B: EFS + EC2 = serveur a gerer, surdimensionne pour de simples images
pieges.D: S3 Standard-IA est concu pour l'acces peu frequent (souvent plus economique ici)

explication: Heberger et servir les images directement depuis Amazon S3 (site statique) supprime tout serveur, avec une haute disponibilite native. Nuance : la cle retient S3 Standard (C), mais pour un acces reellement une a deux fois par an, S3 Standard-IA (D) est generalement plus economique (stockage ~2x moins cher, frais de recuperation negligeables a cette frequence) tout en offrant la meme disponibilite. Verifie la formulation attendue.

question: A company has multiple AWS accounts in an organization in AWS Organizations that different business units use. The company has multiple offices around the world. The company needs to update security group rules to allow new office CIDR ranges or to remove old CIDR ranges across the organization. The company wants to centralize the management of security group rules to minimize the administrative overhead that updating CIDR ranges requires. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

options.A: Create VPC security groups in the organization management account. Update the security groups when a CIDR range update is necessary.
options.B: Create a VPC customer managed prefix list that contains the list of CIDRs. Use AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM) to share the prefix list across the organization. Use the prefix list in the security groups across the organization.
options.C: Create an AWS managed prefix list. Use an AWS Security Hub policy to enforce the security group update across the organization. Use an AWS Lambda function to update the prefix list automatically when the CIDR ranges change.
options.D: Create security groups in a central administrative AWS account. Create an AWS Firewall Manager common security group policy for the whole organization. Select the previously created security groups as primary groups in the policy.

declencheurs: update SG rules for office CIDRs org-wide
radar.signal: Centraliser des plages CIDR reutilisees dans des SG a travers l'organisation -> customer managed prefix list partagee via AWS RAM

pieges.A: Des SG dans le compte de gestion ne se propagent pas aux autres comptes
pieges.C: AWS managed prefix list (non modifiable) + Security Hub + Lambda = complexe et inadapte
pieges.D: Firewall Manager fonctionne mais est plus lourd/couteux qu'une prefix list partagee

explication: Une customer managed prefix list regroupe les CIDR des bureaux en une seule liste. Partagee via AWS RAM a toute l'organisation et referencee dans les security groups, elle permet de mettre a jour les plages en un seul endroit : les SG qui l'utilisent sont automatiquement a jour. C'est la solution la plus economique et la moins administrative.

question: A company runs a container application on a Kubernetes cluster in the company's data center. The application uses Advanced Message Queuing Protocol (AMQP) to communicate with a message queue. The data center cannot scale fast enough to meet the company's expanding business needs. The company wants to migrate the workloads to AWS. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.A: Migrate the container application to Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS). Use Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) to retrieve the messages.
options.B: Migrate the container application to Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS). Use Amazon MQ to retrieve the messages.
options.C: Use highly available Amazon EC2 instances to run the application. Use Amazon MQ to retrieve the messages.
options.D: Use AWS Lambda functions to run the application. Use Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) to retrieve the messages.

radar.signal: Migrer des conteneurs + messagerie manages avec le moins d'overhead -> Amazon ECS + Amazon SQS (serverless)

pieges.B: EKS + Amazon MQ preserve l'AMQP mais EKS et un broker MQ sont plus lourds a operer
pieges.C: EC2 + Amazon MQ = serveurs et broker a gerer
pieges.D: Lambda convient mal a un service conteneurise long

explication: La cle retient ECS + SQS car SQS est une file entierement managee (aucun broker a exploiter) et ECS demande moins d'operations qu'EKS, d'ou le plus faible overhead au quotidien. A noter : cela suppose d'adapter l'application de l'AMQP vers l'API SQS ; si l'on veut conserver strictement l'AMQP sans toucher au code, Amazon MQ (options B/C) serait le choix, au prix d'un broker a gerer.

question: An online gaming company hosts its platform on Amazon EC2 instances behind Network Load Balancers (NLBs) across multiple AWS Regions. The NLBs can route requests to targets over the internet. The company wants to improve the customer playing experience by reducing end-to-end load time for its global customer base. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Create Application Load Balancers (ALBs) in each Region to replace the existing NLBs. Register the existing EC2 instances as targets for the ALBs in each Region.
options.B: Configure Amazon Route 53 to route equally weighted traffic to the NLBs in each Region.
options.C: Create additional NLBs and EC2 instances in other Regions where the company has large customer bases.
options.D: Create a standard accelerator in AWS Global Accelerator. Configure the existing NLBs as target endpoints.

radar.signal: Reduire la latence mondiale devant des NLB multi-Region -> AWS Global Accelerator (standard) avec les NLB en endpoints

pieges.A: Remplacer les NLB par des ALB ne reduit pas la latence reseau internationale
pieges.B: Route 53 en poids egaux ignore la proximite/latence des utilisateurs
pieges.C: Ajouter des NLB/EC2 par Region = infrastructure supplementaire sans reseau accelere

explication: AWS Global Accelerator route le trafic via le backbone mondial d'AWS depuis des points de presence proches des utilisateurs, reduisant la latence de bout en bout. Les NLB existants deviennent des endpoints de l'accelerateur, sans recreer d'infrastructure. Route 53 en poids egaux n'optimise pas la proximite.

question: A company recently launched Linux-based application instances on Amazon EC2 in a private subnet and launched a Linux-based bastion host on an Amazon EC2 instance in a public subnet of a VPC. A solutions architect needs to connect from the on-premises network, through the company internet connection, to the bastion host, and to the application servers. The solutions architect must make sure that the security groups of all the EC2 instances will allow that access. Which combination of steps should the solutions architect take to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.A: Replace the current security group of the bastion host with one that only allows inbound access from the application instances.
options.B: Replace the current security group of the bastion host with one that only allows inbound access from the internal IP range for the company.
options.C: Replace the current security group of the bastion host with one that only allows inbound access from the external IP range for the company.
options.D: Replace the current security group of the application instances with one that allows inbound SSH access from only the private IP address of the bastion host.
options.E: Replace the current security group of the application instances with one that allows inbound SSH access from only the public IP address of the bastion host.

declencheurs: connect from on-premises to bastion (public subnet) then to app instances (private)
radar.signal: Chaine d'acces SSH via bastion -> SG du bastion autorise l'entree depuis la plage IP externe de l'entreprise (C) + SG des app instances autorise SSH depuis l'IP privee du bastion (D)

pieges.A: Autoriser le bastion seulement depuis les app instances empeche l'entree depuis l'on-prem
pieges.B: L'on-prem arrive avec l'IP externe (publique) de l'entreprise, pas une IP interne
pieges.E: Depuis le meme VPC, le bastion joint les app instances via son IP privee, pas publique

explication: Depuis l'on-prem, le trafic atteint le bastion avec l'IP publique (externe) de l'entreprise : le SG du bastion doit donc autoriser cette plage externe (C). Ensuite, le bastion se connecte aux serveurs applicatifs prives au sein du VPC via son IP privee : le SG des app instances autorise SSH depuis l'IP privee du bastion (D).

question: A solutions architect is designing a two-tier web application. The application consists of a public-facing web tier hosted on Amazon EC2 in public subnets. The database tier consists of Microsoft SQL Server running on Amazon EC2 in a private subnet. Security is a high priority for the company. How should security groups be configured in this situation? (Choose two.)

options.A: Configure the security group for the web tier to allow inbound traffic on port 443 from 0.0.0.0/0.
options.B: Configure the security group for the web tier to allow outbound traffic on port 443 from 0.0.0.0/0.
options.C: Configure the security group for the database tier to allow inbound traffic on port 1433 from the security group for the web tier.
options.D: Configure the security group for the database tier to allow outbound traffic on ports 443 and 1433 to the security group for the web tier.
options.E: Configure the security group for the database tier to allow inbound traffic on ports 443 and 1433 from the security group for the web tier.

radar.signal: SG en moindre privilege -> web autorise l'entree 443 depuis 0.0.0.0/0 (A) + DB autorise l'entree 1433 depuis le SG du web (C)

pieges.B: Restreindre le trafic sortant du web en 443 n'est pas le besoin (les SG sont statefull)
pieges.D: Un SG raisonne sur le trafic entrant reference par SG ; regle 'sortante vers le web' mal formulee
pieges.E: Ouvrir 443 en entree sur la DB est inutile et elargit la surface d'attaque

explication: Le tier web public accepte le HTTPS entrant de tout Internet (443 depuis 0.0.0.0/0 -> A). Le tier base de donnees n'accepte que le port SQL Server (1433) et uniquement depuis le security group du tier web (C), en referencant le SG source. Cela applique le moindre privilege : la DB n'est joignable que par le web, sur le seul port necessaire.

question: A package delivery company has an application that uses Amazon EC2 instances and an Amazon Aurora MySQL DB cluster. As the application becomes more popular, EC2 instance usage increases only slightly. DB cluster usage increases at a much faster rate. The company adds a read replica, which reduces the DB cluster usage for a short period of time. However, the load continues to increase. The operations that cause the increase in DB cluster usage are all repeated read statements that are related to delivery details. The company needs to alleviate the effect of repeated reads on the DB cluster. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

options.A: Implement an Amazon ElastiCache for Redis cluster between the application and the DB cluster.
options.B: Add an additional read replica to the DB cluster.
options.C: Configure Aurora Auto Scaling for the Aurora read replicas.
options.D: Modify the DB cluster to have multiple write instances.

declencheurs: Aurora read replica helped briefly then load grew
radar.signal: Soulager des lectures repetees identiques -> cache en memoire Amazon ElastiCache for Redis devant la base

pieges.B: Une replica de plus traite plus de lectures mais ne cache pas les lectures repetees (cout qui grimpe)
pieges.C: Aurora Auto Scaling ajoute des replicas (compute facture), moins economique qu'un cache
pieges.D: Plusieurs instances d'ecriture ne resolvent pas un probleme de lecture

explication: Comme il s'agit de lectures repetees identiques, un cache en memoire ElastiCache for Redis sert ces resultats sans retoucher la base, ce qui est plus economique que d'empiler des read replicas ou d'activer l'Auto Scaling (qui facturent du compute supplementaire).

question: A company has an application that uses an Amazon DynamoDB table for storage. A solutions architect discovers that many requests to the table are not returning the latest data. The company's users have not reported any other issues with database performance. Latency is in an acceptable range. Which design change should the solutions architect recommend?

options.A: Add read replicas to the table.
options.B: Use a global secondary index (GSI).
