options.C: Create an FSx for ONTAP instance in the secondary Region. Use NetApp SnapMirror to replicate data from the primary Region to the secondary Region.
options.D: Create an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) volume. Migrate the current data to the volume. Replicate the volume to the secondary Region.

radar.signal: DR multi-protocole pour ONTAP -> FSx for ONTAP dans la Region secondaire + replication NetApp SnapMirror

pieges.A: Copier vers S3 perd l'acces natif CIFS/NFS
pieges.B: AWS Backup + recreation d'instance = plus d'etapes et de gestion que SnapMirror
pieges.D: EFS ne supporte pas le protocole SMB/CIFS et impose une migration

explication: NetApp SnapMirror replique nativement et en continu les donnees d'un FSx for ONTAP vers un autre FSx for ONTAP dans la Region secondaire, en conservant l'acces via les memes protocoles CIFS et NFS. C'est la solution DR avec le moins d'overhead, contrairement au passage par S3 ou EFS.

question: A solutions architect is using Amazon S3 to design the storage architecture of a new digital media application. The media files must be resilient to the loss of an Availability Zone. Some files are accessed frequently while other files are rarely accessed in an unpredictable pattern. The solutions architect must minimize the costs of storing and retrieving the media files. Which storage option meets these requirements?

options.A: S3 Standard
options.B: S3 Intelligent-Tiering
options.C: S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA)
options.D: S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA)

declencheurs: resilient to loss of an AZ
some frequent, some rare, unpredictable pattern
radar.signal: Multi-AZ + pattern d'acces imprevisible + minimiser stockage/recuperation -> S3 Intelligent-Tiering

pieges.A: S3 Standard ne minimise pas le cout pour les objets rarement consultes
pieges.C: Standard-IA facture la recuperation (mauvais si acces imprevisible)
pieges.D: One Zone-IA n'est pas resilient a la perte d'une AZ

explication: S3 Intelligent-Tiering stocke les donnees sur plusieurs AZ (resilient) et deplace automatiquement les objets entre paliers frequent/infrequent selon l'usage reel, sans frais de recuperation. C'est ideal quand certains fichiers sont chauds et d'autres froids de facon imprevisible. One Zone-IA (D) ne survivrait pas a la perte d'une AZ.

question: A company is storing backup files by using Amazon S3 Standard storage. The files are accessed frequently for 1 month. However, the files are not accessed after 1 month. The company must keep the files indefinitely. Which storage solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

options.A: Configure S3 Intelligent-Tiering to automatically migrate objects.
options.B: Create an S3 Lifecycle configuration to transition objects from S3 Standard to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 1 month.
options.C: Create an S3 Lifecycle configuration to transition objects from S3 Standard to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) after 1 month.
options.D: Create an S3 Lifecycle configuration to transition objects from S3 Standard to S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA) after 1 month.

declencheurs: frequent for 1 month then never accessed
radar.signal: Plus jamais consulte apres 1 mois + conservation indefinie -> Lifecycle vers S3 Glacier Deep Archive apres 1 mois

pieges.A: Intelligent-Tiering coute plus que Deep Archive quand on sait que l'acces cesse totalement
pieges.C: Standard-IA reste bien plus cher que Deep Archive pour de l'archivage indefini
pieges.D: One Zone-IA est moins durable et plus cher que Deep Archive

explication: Puisque les fichiers ne sont plus consultes apres un mois mais doivent etre conserves indefiniment, une Lifecycle policy qui les bascule vers S3 Glacier Deep Archive (le stockage le moins cher) est la plus economique. Standard-IA et One Zone-IA restent bien plus chers pour de l'archivage long.

question: A company has stored 10 TB of log files in Apache Parquet format in an Amazon S3 bucket. The company occasionally needs to use SQL to analyze the log files. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

options.A: Create an Amazon Aurora MySQL database. Migrate the data from the S3 bucket into Aurora by using AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS). Issue SQL statements to the Aurora database.
options.B: Create an Amazon Redshift cluster. Use Redshift Spectrum to run SQL statements directly on the data in the S3 bucket.
options.C: Create an AWS Glue crawler to store and retrieve table metadata from the S3 bucket. Use Amazon Athena to run SQL statements directly on the data in the S3 bucket.
options.D: Create an Amazon EMR cluster. Use Apache Spark SQL to run SQL statements directly on the data in the S3 bucket.

radar.signal: SQL occasionnel sur des donnees S3, sans infra permanente -> Glue crawler (schema) + Amazon Athena (serverless, a la requete)

pieges.A: Migrer vers Aurora via DMS = base a payer en continu
pieges.B: Un cluster Redshift tourne (et coute) en permanence, meme pour un usage occasionnel
pieges.D: Un cluster EMR persistant est couteux pour des requetes ponctuelles

explication: Amazon Athena interroge directement les fichiers Parquet dans S3 en SQL, sans serveur, et ne facture qu'a la requete : parfait pour un usage occasionnel. Un crawler Glue fournit le schema. Redshift et EMR imposeraient des clusters factures en continu.

question: A company needs a solution to prevent AWS CloudFormation stacks from deploying AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) resources that include an inline policy with ** in the statement. The solution must also prohibit deployment of Amazon EC2 instances with public IP addresses. The company has AWS Control Tower enabled in its organization in AWS Organizations. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Use AWS Control Tower proactive controls to block deployment of EC2 instances with public IP addresses and inline policies with elevated access or "**".
options.B: Use AWS Control Tower detective controls to block deployment of EC2 instances with public IP addresses and inline policies with elevated access or "**".
options.C: Use AWS Config to create rules for EC2 and IAM compliance. Configure the rules to run an AWS Systems Manager Session Manager automation to delete a resource when it is not compliant.
options.D: Use a service control policy (SCP) to block actions for the EC2 instances and IAM resources if the actions lead to noncompliance.

declencheurs: prevent CloudFormation from deploying non-compliant resources
radar.signal: Bloquer des ressources non conformes AVANT provisionnement via CloudFormation (Control Tower) -> proactive controls

pieges.B: Les detective controls detectent apres coup, ils ne bloquent pas le deploiement
pieges.C: AWS Config detecte/remedie apres creation, il n'empeche pas le deploiement
pieges.D: Une SCP bloque des actions d'API mais ne peut pas inspecter le contenu (ex: '**' dans une inline policy) au deploiement CloudFormation

alerte_cle: La cle du fichier indique D (SCP), mais une SCP ne peut pas inspecter des proprietes fines comme '**' dans une inline policy ou une IP publique au deploiement CloudFormation. Les proactive controls d'AWS Control Tower (hooks CloudFormation) sont concus pour bloquer ces ressources avant provisionnement : reponse A.
explication: Les proactive controls d'AWS Control Tower s'appuient sur des hooks CloudFormation qui evaluent les ressources contre des regles AVANT leur provisionnement et bloquent les non conformes (inline policy avec '**', EC2 avec IP publique). Les detective controls et AWS Config n'agissent qu'apres coup, et une SCP ne sait pas inspecter ces proprietes de contenu.

question: A company needs to store contract documents. A contract lasts for 5 years. During the 5-year period, the company must ensure that the documents cannot be overwritten or deleted. The company needs to encrypt the documents at rest and rotate the encryption keys automatically every year. Which combination of steps should a solutions architect take to meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead? (Choose two.)

options.A: Store the documents in Amazon S3. Use S3 Object Lock in governance mode.
options.B: Store the documents in Amazon S3. Use S3 Object Lock in compliance mode.
options.C: Use server-side encryption with Amazon S3 managed encryption keys (SSE-S3). Configure key rotation.
options.D: Use server-side encryption with AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) customer managed keys. Configure key rotation.
options.E: Use server-side encryption with AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) customer provided (imported) keys. Configure key rotation.

declencheurs: documents cannot be overwritten or deleted for 5 years
radar.signal: Immuabilite reglementaire + rotation annuelle automatique -> S3 Object Lock en mode compliance (B) + SSE-KMS avec cle customer managed et rotation activee (D)

pieges.A: Le mode governance peut etre outrepasse par un utilisateur privilegie
pieges.C: SSE-S3 ne permet pas une rotation annuelle configurable des cles comme KMS
pieges.E: Des cles importees (customer provided) ne beneficient pas de la rotation automatique KMS

explication: S3 Object Lock en mode compliance garantit qu'aucun utilisateur, meme root, ne peut ecraser ou supprimer les documents pendant les 5 ans (B). Le chiffrement au repos avec une cle KMS customer managed permet d'activer la rotation automatique annuelle des cles (D). SSE-S3 et les cles importees n'offrent pas cette rotation configurable.

question: A company has a web application that is based on Java and PHP. The company plans to move the application from on premises to AWS. The company needs the ability to test new site features frequently. The company also needs a highly available and managed solution that requires minimum operational overhead. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Create an Amazon S3 bucket. Enable static web hosting on the S3 bucket. Upload the static content to the S3 bucket. Use AWS Lambda to process all dynamic content.
options.B: Deploy the web application to an AWS Elastic Beanstalk environment. Use URL swapping to switch between multiple Elastic Beanstalk environments for feature testing.
options.C: Deploy the web application to Amazon EC2 instances that are configured with Java and PHP. Use Auto Scaling groups and an Application Load Balancer to manage the website's availability.
options.D: Containerize the web application. Deploy the web application to Amazon EC2 instances. Use the AWS Load Balancer Controller to dynamically route traffic between containers that contain the new site features for testing.

radar.signal: App web manageee, HA, avec tests de features -> AWS Elastic Beanstalk + URL swapping entre environnements

pieges.A: S3 static + Lambda ne convient pas a une app Java/PHP complete
pieges.C: EC2 + ASG + ALB a construire soi-meme = plus d'overhead qu'Elastic Beanstalk
pieges.D: Conteneuriser + gerer les EC2 et le routage = plus d'effort operationnel

explication: AWS Elastic Beanstalk gere l'infrastructure d'une application Java/PHP hautement disponible avec un minimum d'overhead. L'URL swapping (swap CNAME) entre deux environnements permet de tester de nouvelles fonctionnalites puis de basculer sans interruption, ideal pour des tests frequents.

question: A manufacturing company runs its report generation application on AWS. The application generates each report in about 20 minutes. The application is built as a monolith that runs on a single Amazon EC2 instance. The application requires frequent updates to its tightly coupled modules. The application becomes complex to maintain as the company adds new features. Each time the company patches a software module, the application experiences downtime. Report generation must restart from the beginning after any interruptions. The company wants to redesign the application so that the application can be flexible, scalable, and gradually improved. The company wants to minimize application downtime. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Run the application on AWS Lambda as a single function with maximum provisioned concurrency.
options.B: Run the application on Amazon EC2 Spot Instances as microservices with a Spot Fleet default allocation strategy.
options.C: Run the application on Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) as microservices with service auto scaling.
options.D: Run the application on AWS Elastic Beanstalk as a single application environment with an all-at-once deployment strategy.

declencheurs: tightly coupled modules, frequent patches cause downtime
radar.signal: Decoupler le monolithe en services independants deployables sans downtime -> microservices sur Amazon ECS avec service auto scaling

pieges.A: Lambda en fonction unique reste monolithique et limite a 15 min
pieges.B: Les Spot Instances peuvent etre interrompues, or la generation doit repartir de zero
pieges.D: Elastic Beanstalk en app unique + deploiement all-at-once = downtime a chaque mise a jour

explication: Decouper l'application en microservices conteneurises sur Amazon ECS permet de patcher/ameliorer chaque module independamment, sans interrompre l'ensemble, et de scaler service par service. Cela reduit le downtime et rend l'application flexible, contrairement au monolithe (Lambda unique, Beanstalk all-at-once) ou aux Spot interruptibles.

question: A company wants to rearchitect a large-scale web application to a serverless microservices architecture. The application uses Amazon EC2 instances and is written in Python. The company selected one component of the web application to test as a microservice. The component supports hundreds of requests each second. The company wants to create and test the microservice on an AWS solution that supports Python. The solution must also scale automatically and require minimal infrastructure and minimal operational support. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Use a Spot Fleet with auto scaling of EC2 instances that run the most recent Amazon Linux operating system.
options.B: Use an AWS Elastic Beanstalk web server environment that has high availability configured.
options.C: Use Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS). Launch Auto Scaling groups of self-managed EC2 instances.
options.D: Use an AWS Lambda function that runs custom developed code.

radar.signal: Microservice Python serverless a montee en charge automatique -> AWS Lambda avec code custom

pieges.A: Un Spot Fleet d'EC2 n'est pas serverless et demande de la gestion
pieges.B: Elastic Beanstalk gere des serveurs (moins 'minimal infrastructure' que Lambda)
pieges.C: EKS avec noeuds EC2 autogeres = beaucoup d'infrastructure a operer

explication: AWS Lambda execute du code Python, scale automatiquement avec le nombre de requetes et ne demande aucune infrastructure a gerer. C'est la brique serverless ideale pour tester un composant en microservice avec un support operationnel minimal, contrairement aux options basees sur EC2/EKS.

question: A company has deployed a multiplayer game for mobile devices. The game requires live location tracking of players based on latitude and longitude. The data store for the game must support rapid updates and retrieval of locations. The game uses an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance with read replicas to store the location data. During peak usage periods, the database is unable to maintain the performance that is needed for reading and writing updates. The game's user base is increasing rapidly. What should a solutions architect do to improve the performance of the data tier?

options.A: Take a snapshot of the existing DB instance. Restore the snapshot with Multi-AZ enabled.
options.B: Migrate from Amazon RDS to Amazon OpenSearch Service with OpenSearch Dashboards.
options.C: Deploy Amazon DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) in front of the existing DB instance. Modify the game to use DAX.
options.D: Deploy an Amazon ElastiCache for Redis cluster in front of the existing DB instance. Modify the game to use Redis.

declencheurs: RDS PostgreSQL + read replicas can't keep up
radar.signal: Acceler les ecritures/lectures rapides de positions -> cache en memoire Amazon ElastiCache for Redis devant la base

pieges.A: Multi-AZ ameliore la disponibilite, pas le debit lecture/ecriture
pieges.B: Migrer vers OpenSearch change de moteur et ne cible pas le besoin transactionnel de positions
pieges.C: DAX accelere DynamoDB uniquement, pas une base RDS PostgreSQL

explication: Un cluster ElastiCache for Redis en memoire absorbe les mises a jour et lectures tres frequentes de positions, soulageant la base PostgreSQL saturee, et Redis gere nativement les donnees geospatiales. DAX (C) ne fonctionne qu'avec DynamoDB, et Multi-AZ n'ameliore pas le debit.

question: A company stores critical data in Amazon DynamoDB tables in the company's AWS account. An IT administrator accidentally deleted a DynamoDB table. The deletion caused a significant loss of data and disrupted the company operations. The company wants to prevent this type of disruption in the future. Which solution will meet this requirement with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.A: Configure a trail in AWS CloudTrail. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule for delete actions. Create an AWS Lambda function to automatically restore deleted DynamoDB tables.
options.B: Create a backup and restore plan for the DynamoDB tables. Recover the DynamoDB tables manually.
options.C: Configure deletion protection on the DynamoDB tables.
options.D: Enable point-in-time recovery on the DynamoDB tables.

declencheurs: admin accidentally deleted a DynamoDB table
radar.signal: Empecher la suppression accidentelle d'une table DynamoDB -> activer la deletion protection sur les tables

pieges.A: CloudTrail + EventBridge + Lambda de restauration = solution complexe a construire
pieges.B: Un plan de backup/restore manuel repare apres coup, il n'empeche pas la suppression
pieges.D: Le point-in-time recovery aide a restaurer, mais n'empeche pas la suppression de la table

explication: La deletion protection de DynamoDB empeche purement et simplement la suppression d'une table tant qu'elle est activee, ce qui bloque l'erreur a la source avec le moins d'overhead. Le PITR et les backups servent a restaurer apres coup, mais ne previennent pas la suppression.

question: A media company hosts its website on AWS. The website application's architecture includes a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB) and a database that is hosted on Amazon Aurora. The company's cybersecurity team reports that the application is vulnerable to SQL injection. How should the company resolve this issue?

options.A: Use AWS WAF in front of the ALB. Associate the appropriate web ACLs with AWS WAF.
options.B: Create an ALB listener rule to reply to SQL injections with a fixed response.
options.C: Subscribe to AWS Shield Advanced to block all SQL injection attempts automatically.
options.D: Set up Amazon Inspector to block all SQL injection attempts automatically.

radar.signal: Bloquer les injections SQL (couche 7) -> AWS WAF devant l'ALB avec les web ACL appropriees

pieges.B: Une listener rule a reponse fixe ne detecte pas les injections SQL
pieges.C: Shield Advanced protege des DDoS, pas des injections SQL
pieges.D: Inspector scanne des vulnerabilites, il ne bloque pas le trafic

explication: AWS WAF inspecte le trafic applicatif et bloque les tentatives d'injection SQL grace a des regles managees (SQLi). Associe a l'ALB, il resout la vulnerabilite. Shield (DDoS) et Inspector (vulnerabilites) ne filtrent pas ce type d'attaque applicative.

question: A company has an Amazon S3 data lake that is governed by AWS Lake Formation. The company wants to create a visualization in Amazon QuickSight by joining the data in the data lake with operational data that is stored in an Amazon Aurora MySQL database. The company wants to enforce column-level authorization so that the company's marketing team can access only a subset of columns in the database. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.A: Use Amazon EMR to ingest the data directly from the database to the QuickSight SPICE engine. Include only the required columns.
options.B: Use AWS Glue Studio to ingest the data from the database to the S3 data lake. Attach an IAM policy to the QuickSight users to enforce column-level access control. Use Amazon S3 as the data source in QuickSight.
options.C: Use AWS Glue Elastic Views to create a materialized view for the database in Amazon S3. Create an S3 bucket policy to enforce column-level access control for the QuickSight users. Use Amazon S3 as the data source in QuickSight.
options.D: Use a Lake Formation blueprint to ingest the data from the database to the S3 data lake. Use Lake Formation to enforce column-level access control for the QuickSight users. Use Amazon Athena as the data source in QuickSight.

declencheurs: join with Aurora MySQL data in QuickSight
radar.signal: Autorisation au niveau colonne sur des donnees ingerees dans le lac -> Lake Formation blueprint pour ingerer + controle colonne via Lake Formation + Athena comme source QuickSight

pieges.A: EMR vers SPICE n'applique pas de controle d'acces colonne gere
pieges.B: Une IAM policy sur les utilisateurs QuickSight n'offre pas un controle colonne aussi fin/gere que Lake Formation
pieges.C: Glue Elastic Views + bucket policy ne fait pas de controle au niveau colonne

explication: Un blueprint Lake Formation ingere les donnees Aurora dans le lac S3, et Lake Formation applique nativement des permissions au niveau colonne pour les utilisateurs QuickSight (via Athena comme source). C'est le moyen le plus simple d'imposer que le marketing ne voie qu'un sous-ensemble de colonnes.

question: A company has hundreds of Amazon EC2 Linux-based instances in the AWS Cloud. Systems administrators have used shared SSH keys to manage the instances. After a recent audit, the company security team is mandating the removal of all shared keys. A solutions architect must design a solution that provides secure access to the EC2 instances. Which solution will meet this requirement with the LEAST amount of administrative overhead?

options.A: Use AWS Systems Manager Session Manager to connect to the EC2 instances.
options.B: Use AWS Security Token Service (AWS STS) to generate one-time SSH keys on demand.
options.C: Allow shared SSH access to a set of bastion instances. Configure all other instances to allow only SSH access from the bastion instances.
options.D: Use an Amazon Cognito custom authorizer to authenticate users. Invoke an AWS Lambda function to generate a temporary SSH key.

radar.signal: Supprimer les cles SSH partagees et acceder de facon sure -> AWS Systems Manager Session Manager

pieges.B: Generer des cles SSH a la demande via STS = mecanisme custom a batir
pieges.C: Des bastions avec cles partagees reintroduisent le probleme des cles
pieges.D: Cognito + Lambda pour generer des cles SSH = solution complexe a maintenir

explication: AWS Systems Manager Session Manager donne un acces securise aux instances sans aucune cle SSH ni port ouvert : on peut donc supprimer toutes les cles partagees. L'acces est controle par IAM et journalise, avec le moins d'administration, contrairement aux solutions de generation de cles a la demande.

question: A company is using a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances to ingest data from on-premises data sources. The data is in JSON format and ingestion rates can be as high as 1 MB/s. When an EC2 instance is rebooted, the data in-flight is lost. The company's data science team wants to query ingested data in near-real time. Which solution provides near-real-time data querying that is scalable with minimal data loss?

options.A: Publish data to Amazon Kinesis Data Streams. Use Kinesis Data Analytics to query the data.
options.B: Publish data to Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose with Amazon Redshift as the destination. Use Amazon Redshift to query the data.
options.C: Store ingested data in an EC2 instance store. Publish data to Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose with Amazon S3 as the destination. Use Amazon Athena to query the data.
options.D: Store ingested data in an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume. Publish data to Amazon ElastiCache for Redis. Subscribe to the Redis channel to query the data.

radar.signal: Ingestion durable temps reel + requetes proches du temps reel -> publier vers Kinesis Data Streams + interroger avec Kinesis Data Analytics

pieges.B: Firehose vers Redshift ajoute une base a gerer et n'est pas aussi 'near-real-time query' que Data Analytics
pieges.C: Stocker dans l'instance store perd les donnees au reboot (le probleme meme)
pieges.D: EBS + ElastiCache pub/sub n'est pas une solution d'ingestion durable et scalable

explication: En publiant directement vers Kinesis Data Streams, les donnees ne dependent plus du disque local des EC2 (donc pas de perte au reboot) et le flux est scalable. Kinesis Data Analytics interroge ce flux en quasi temps reel. Stocker dans l'instance store (C) reproduirait la perte de donnees.

question: What should a solutions architect do to ensure that all objects uploaded to an Amazon S3 bucket are encrypted?

options.A: Update the bucket policy to deny if the PutObject does not have an s3:x-amz-acl header set.
options.B: Update the bucket policy to deny if the PutObject does not have an s3:x-amz-acl header set to private.
options.C: Update the bucket policy to deny if the PutObject does not have an aws:SecureTransport header set to true.
options.D: Update the bucket policy to deny if the PutObject does not have an x-amz-server-side-encryption header set.

declencheurs: ensure all objects uploaded to S3 are encrypted
radar.signal: Forcer le chiffrement a l'upload -> bucket policy qui refuse PutObject sans l'en-tete x-amz-server-side-encryption

pieges.A: s3:x-amz-acl concerne les ACL, pas le chiffrement
pieges.B: s3:x-amz-acl=private gere l'ACL, pas le chiffrement
pieges.C: aws:SecureTransport force le HTTPS (transit), pas le chiffrement au repos

explication: Une bucket policy qui refuse toute operation PutObject ne portant pas l'en-tete x-amz-server-side-encryption garantit que seuls des objets chiffres cote serveur sont acceptes. Les en-tetes d'ACL (A/B) ou aws:SecureTransport (transit, C) ne concernent pas le chiffrement au repos.

question: A company has a business system that generates hundreds of reports each day. The business system saves the reports to a network share in CSV format. The company needs to store this data in the AWS Cloud in near-real time for analysis. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST administrative overhead?

options.A: Use AWS DataSync to transfer the files to Amazon S3. Create a scheduled task that runs at the end of each day.
options.B: Create an Amazon S3 File Gateway. Update the business system to use a new network share from the S3 File Gateway.
options.C: Use AWS DataSync to transfer the files to Amazon S3. Create an application that uses the DataSync API in the automation workflow.
options.D: Deploy an AWS Transfer for SFTP endpoint. Create a script that checks for new files on the network share and uploads the new files by using SFTP.

declencheurs: hundreds of CSV reports to a network share daily
store in AWS in near-real time
radar.signal: Ingestion continue d'un partage reseau vers S3 sans script -> Amazon S3 File Gateway (le systeme ecrit sur un nouveau partage)

pieges.A: DataSync planifie en fin de journee n'est pas du near-real-time
pieges.C: DataSync + application d'automatisation = du developpement a maintenir
pieges.D: Transfer for SFTP + script de detection de fichiers = solution custom lourde

explication: Un Amazon S3 File Gateway expose un partage reseau que le systeme metier utilise directement ; les fichiers ecrits sont automatiquement televerses vers S3 en continu (quasi temps reel), sans script ni tache planifiee. DataSync planifie serait par lots, et les autres options exigent du developpement.

question: A company is storing petabytes of data in Amazon S3 Standard. The data is stored in multiple S3 buckets and is accessed with varying frequency. The company does not know access patterns for all the data. The company needs to implement a solution for each S3 bucket to optimize the cost of S3 usage. Which solution will meet these requirements with the MOST operational efficiency?

options.A: Create an S3 Lifecycle configuration with a rule to transition the objects in the S3 bucket to S3 Intelligent-Tiering.
options.B: Use the S3 storage class analysis tool to determine the correct tier for each object in the S3 bucket. Move each object to the identified storage tier.
options.C: Create an S3 Lifecycle configuration with a rule to transition the objects in the S3 bucket to S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval.
options.D: Create an S3 Lifecycle configuration with a rule to transition the objects in the S3 bucket to S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA).

radar.signal: Optimiser le cout sans connaitre les patterns, automatiquement -> Lifecycle vers S3 Intelligent-Tiering

pieges.B: Storage class analysis + deplacement manuel = beaucoup d'operations
pieges.C: Glacier Instant Retrieval suppose un acces rare connu (pas le cas ici)
pieges.D: One Zone-IA est moins durable et suppose un acces peu frequent connu

explication: Une Lifecycle rule vers S3 Intelligent-Tiering laisse S3 deplacer automatiquement chaque objet entre paliers selon son usage reel, sans frais de recuperation ni analyse manuelle. C'est la solution la plus efficace operationnellement quand les patterns d'acces sont inconnus et variables.

question: A gaming company wants to launch a new internet-facing application in multiple AWS Regions. The application will use the TCP and UDP protocols for communication. The company needs to provide high availability and minimum latency for global users. Which combination of actions should a solutions architect take to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.A: Create internal Network Load Balancers in front of the application in each Region.
options.B: Create external Application Load Balancers in front of the application in each Region.
options.C: Create an AWS Global Accelerator accelerator to route traffic to the load balancers in each Region.
options.D: Configure Amazon Route 53 to use a geolocation routing policy to distribute the traffic.
options.E: Configure Amazon CloudFront to handle the traffic and route requests to the application in each Region.

radar.signal: TCP+UDP multi-Region a faible latence -> Network Load Balancers (TCP/UDP) dans chaque Region (A) + AWS Global Accelerator routant vers ces LB (C)

pieges.B: Un ALB ne gere que HTTP/HTTPS, pas TCP/UDP brut
pieges.D: Route 53 geolocation route par pays, pas au plus bas en latence ni avec bascule reseau
pieges.E: CloudFront est pour le HTTP(S), pas pour TCP/UDP

explication: Le trafic TCP et UDP impose des Network Load Balancers dans chaque Region (A). AWS Global Accelerator (C), place devant, fournit des IP statiques anycast et route chaque utilisateur via le backbone AWS vers la Region la plus proche/saine, assurant haute disponibilite et latence minimale. ALB et CloudFront sont limites au HTTP(S).

question: A city has deployed a web application running on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The application's users have reported sporadic performance, which appears to be related to DDoS attacks originating from random IP addresses. The city needs a solution that requires minimal configuration changes and provides an audit trail for the DDoS sources. Which solution meets these requirements?

options.A: Enable an AWS WAF web ACL on the ALB, and configure rules to block traffic from unknown sources.
options.B: Subscribe to Amazon Inspector. Engage the AWS DDoS Response Team (DRT) to integrate mitigating controls into the service.
options.C: Subscribe to AWS Shield Advanced. Engage the AWS DDoS Response Team (DRT) to integrate mitigating controls into the service.
options.D: Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution for the application, and set the ALB as the origin. Enable an AWS WAF web ACL on the distribution and configure rules to block traffic from unknown sources.

radar.signal: Attenuation DDoS manageee + traçabilite, peu de config -> AWS Shield Advanced + AWS DDoS Response Team (DRT)

pieges.A: Bloquer manuellement des IP 'inconnues' via WAF n'est pas fiable face a des IP aleatoires et demande de la config
pieges.B: Inspector scanne des vulnerabilites, il ne fait pas d'attenuation DDoS
pieges.D: CloudFront + WAF avec regles a maintenir = plus de configuration

explication: AWS Shield Advanced fournit une detection/attenuation DDoS manageee, des rapports et une piste d'audit des attaques, avec l'appui de la DDoS Response Team, le tout avec peu de changements de configuration. Bloquer des IP aleatoires via WAF serait laborieux et peu fiable.

question: A company serves its website by using an Auto Scaling group of Amazon EC2 instances in a single AWS Region. The website does not require a database. The company is expanding, and the company's engineering team deploys the website to a second Region. The company wants to distribute traffic across both Regions to accommodate growth and for disaster recovery purposes. The solution should not serve traffic from a Region in which the website is unhealthy. Which policy or resource should the company use to meet these requirements?

options.A: An Amazon Route 53 simple routing policy.
options.B: An Amazon Route 53 multivalue answer routing policy.
options.C: An Application Load Balancer in one Region with a target group that specifies the EC2 instance IDs from both Regions.
options.D: An Application Load Balancer in one Region with a target group that specifies the IP addresses of the EC2 instances from both Regions.

declencheurs: do not serve from an unhealthy Region
radar.signal: Repartir entre Regions avec verification de sante -> Route 53 multivalue answer routing policy + health checks

pieges.A: La simple routing policy ne gere pas les health checks pour ecarter une Region malade
pieges.C: Un target group d'ALB ne reference pas des instances par ID cross-Region
pieges.D: Un ALB ne cible pas des IP d'instances situees dans une autre Region

explication: La multivalue answer routing policy de Route 53 renvoie plusieurs enregistrements et, associee a des health checks, n'inclut que les endpoints sains : le trafic n'est donc pas dirige vers une Region defaillante. Un ALB reste regional et ne peut pas cibler des instances d'une autre Region.

question: A company runs its applications on Amazon EC2 instances that are backed by Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS). The EC2 instances run the most recent Amazon Linux release. The applications are experiencing availability issues when the company's employees store and retrieve files that are 25 GB or larger. The company needs a solution that does not require the company to transfer files between EC2 instances. The files must be available across many EC2 instances and across multiple Availability Zones. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Migrate all the files to an Amazon S3 bucket. Instruct the employees to access the files from the S3 bucket.
options.B: Take a snapshot of the existing EBS volume. Mount the snapshot as an EBS volume across the EC2 instances. Instruct the employees to access the files from the EC2 instances.
options.C: Mount an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system across all the EC2 instances. Instruct the employees to access the files from the EC2 instances.
options.D: Create an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) from the EC2 instances. Configure new EC2 instances from the AMI that use an instance store volume. Instruct the employees to access the files from the EC2 instances.

declencheurs: available across many EC2 and multiple AZ
radar.signal: Fichiers partages entre instances et AZ, sans copie -> Amazon EFS monte sur toutes les EC2

pieges.A: S3 change la methode d'acces aux fichiers (pas un montage transparent)
pieges.B: Un volume EBS/snapshot ne se partage pas simultanement entre plusieurs instances/AZ
pieges.D: L'instance store est ephemere et local a chaque instance

explication: Amazon EFS fournit un systeme de fichiers partage, monte simultanement par de nombreuses instances reparties sur plusieurs AZ, sans transferer les fichiers entre instances. Les employes accedent aux memes fichiers volumineux depuis n'importe quelle instance, ce qu'EBS (mono-instance) ou l'instance store ne permettent pas.

question: A company is deploying an application that processes streaming data in near-real time. The company plans to use Amazon EC2 instances for the workload. The network architecture must be configurable to provide the lowest possible latency between nodes. Which combination of network solutions will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.A: Enable and configure enhanced networking on each EC2 instance.
options.B: Group the EC2 instances in separate accounts.
options.C: Run the EC2 instances in a cluster placement group.
options.D: Attach multiple elastic network interfaces to each EC2 instance.
options.E: Use Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) optimized instance types.

radar.signal: Latence minimale entre noeuds EC2 -> enhanced networking (A) + cluster placement group (C)

pieges.B: Repartir les instances dans des comptes separes n'a aucun effet sur la latence
pieges.D: Ajouter des ENI n'ameliore pas la latence entre noeuds
pieges.E: EBS-optimized concerne le debit vers le stockage, pas la latence reseau inter-noeuds

explication: Un cluster placement group regroupe les instances au plus pres physiquement pour minimiser la latence reseau (C), et l'enhanced networking (SR-IOV/ENA) reduit encore la latence et augmente le debit paquets (A). Les ENI multiples ou EBS-optimized ne reduisent pas la latence inter-noeuds.

question: A financial services company wants to shut down two data centers and migrate more than 100 TB of data to AWS. The data has an intricate directory structure with millions of small files stored in deep hierarchies of subfolders. Most of the data is unstructured, and the company file storage consists of SMB-based storage types from multiple vendors. The company does not want to change its applications to access the data after migration. What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.A: Use AWS Direct Connect to migrate the data to Amazon S3.
options.B: Use AWS DataSync to migrate the data to Amazon FSx for Lustre.
options.C: Use AWS DataSync to migrate the data to Amazon FSx for Windows File Server.
options.D: Use AWS Direct Connect to migrate the data from on-premises file storage to an AWS Storage Gateway volume gateway.

declencheurs: 100+ TB, millions of small files, deep folders
radar.signal: Migrer du SMB vers un partage SMB manage sans changer les apps -> AWS DataSync vers Amazon FSx for Windows File Server

pieges.A: S3 n'est pas un partage SMB : les applications devraient changer
pieges.B: FSx for Lustre cible le HPC/Linux, pas des partages SMB Windows
pieges.D: Storage Gateway volume gateway (block iSCSI) ne remplace pas un partage SMB

explication: AWS DataSync transfere efficacement des millions de petits fichiers vers Amazon FSx for Windows File Server, un partage SMB manage. Les applications continuent d'acceder aux donnees en SMB sans modification. S3 (non SMB) ou FSx for Lustre (Linux/HPC) imposeraient des changements.

question: A company hosts a data lake on AWS. The data lake consists of data in Amazon S3 and Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL. The company needs a reporting solution that provides data visualization and includes all the data sources within the data lake. Only the company's management team should have full access to all the visualizations. The rest of the company should have only limited access. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Create an analysis in Amazon QuickSight. Connect all the data sources and create new datasets. Publish dashboards to visualize the data. Share the dashboards with the appropriate IAM roles.
options.B: Create an analysis in Amazon QuickSight. Connect all the data sources and create new datasets. Publish dashboards to visualize the data. Share the dashboards with the appropriate users and groups.
options.C: Create an AWS Glue table and crawler for the data in Amazon S3. Create an AWS Glue extract, transform, and load (ETL) job to produce reports. Publish the reports to Amazon S3. Use S3 bucket policies to limit access to the reports.
options.D: Create an AWS Glue table and crawler for the data in Amazon S3. Use Amazon Athena Federated Query to access data within Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL. Generate reports by using Amazon Athena. Publish the reports to Amazon S3. Use S3 bucket policies to limit access to the reports.

declencheurs: data in S3 AND RDS PostgreSQL
management full access, rest limited access
radar.signal: Visualisation multi-sources avec acces differencie -> Amazon QuickSight, dashboards partages avec les utilisateurs et groupes appropries

pieges.A: QuickSight partage avec des utilisateurs/groupes QuickSight, pas avec des IAM roles
pieges.C: Glue ETL + rapports S3 = pas de visualisation interactive ni de partage fin
pieges.D: Athena Federated + rapports S3 = plus complexe et sans visualisation manageee

explication: Amazon QuickSight se connecte a la fois a S3 et a RDS PostgreSQL, cree des datasets et des dashboards de visualisation, puis les partage avec les utilisateurs et groupes QuickSight (acces complet pour la direction, limite pour le reste). Le partage QuickSight se fait par utilisateurs/groupes, pas par IAM roles.

question: A company is implementing a new business application. The application runs on two Amazon EC2 instances and uses an Amazon S3 bucket for document storage. A solutions architect needs to ensure that the EC2 instances can access the S3 bucket. What should the solutions architect do to meet this requirement?

options.A: Create an IAM role that grants access to the S3 bucket. Attach the role to the EC2 instances.
options.B: Create an IAM policy that grants access to the S3 bucket. Attach the policy to the EC2 instances.
options.C: Create an IAM group that grants access to the S3 bucket. Attach the group to the EC2 instances.
options.D: Create an IAM user that grants access to the S3 bucket. Attach the user account to the EC2 instances.

radar.signal: Donner a des EC2 l'acces a S3 -> role IAM accordant l'acces, attache aux instances

pieges.B: On n'attache pas une policy directement a une instance EC2 (elle s'attache a un role)
pieges.C: Un IAM group regroupe des utilisateurs, il ne s'attache pas a une instance
pieges.D: On n'attache pas un IAM user a une instance

explication: Le mecanisme correct est un role IAM (via instance profile) attache aux instances EC2 : elles obtiennent des identifiants temporaires pour acceder au bucket, sans cles statiques. Une policy s'attache a un role/utilisateur/groupe, pas directement a une instance.

question: A company has created an image analysis application in which users can upload photos and add photo frames to their images. The users upload images and metadata to indicate which photo frames they want to add to their images. The application uses a single Amazon EC2 instance and Amazon DynamoDB to store the metadata. The application is becoming more popular, and the number of users is increasing. The company expects the number of concurrent users to vary significantly depending on the time of day and day of week. The company must ensure that the application can scale to meet the needs of the growing user base. Which solution meets these requirements?

options.A: Use AWS Lambda to process the photos. Store the photos and metadata in DynamoDB.
options.B: Use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to process the photos and to store the photos and metadata.
options.C: Use AWS Lambda to process the photos. Store the photos in Amazon S3. Retain DynamoDB to store the metadata.
options.D: Increase the number of EC2 instances to three. Use Provisioned IOPS SSD (io2) Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes to store the photos and metadata.

declencheurs: photo app on single EC2 + DynamoDB
users increasing, concurrency varies a lot
radar.signal: Traitement scalable + stockage adapte -> AWS Lambda pour traiter, photos dans Amazon S3, metadonnees dans DynamoDB

pieges.A: Stocker des photos (objets binaires volumineux) dans DynamoDB est inadapte (limite 400 KB/item)
pieges.B: Kinesis Data Firehose n'est pas fait pour traiter/stocker des photos
pieges.D: Passer a 3 EC2 + EBS ne scale pas dynamiquement selon une charge tres variable

explication: AWS Lambda traite les photos et scale automatiquement avec la concurrence variable. Les images (objets volumineux) vont dans S3, tandis que DynamoDB conserve les metadonnees. Stocker des photos dans DynamoDB (A) est impossible au-dela de 400 KB, et ajouter des EC2 fixes (D) ne suit pas une charge fluctuante.

question: A medical records company is hosting an application on Amazon EC2 instances. The application processes customer data files that are stored on Amazon S3. The EC2 instances are hosted in public subnets. The EC2 instances access Amazon S3 over the internet, but they do not require any other network access. A new requirement mandates that the network traffic for file transfers take a private route and not be sent over the internet. Which change to the network architecture should a solutions architect recommend to meet this requirement?

options.A: Create a NAT gateway. Configure the route table for the public subnets to send traffic to Amazon S3 through the NAT gateway.
options.B: Configure the security group for the EC2 instances to restrict outbound traffic so that only traffic to the S3 prefix list is permitted.
options.C: Move the EC2 instances to private subnets. Create a VPC endpoint for Amazon S3, and link the endpoint to the route table for the private subnets.
options.D: Remove the internet gateway from the VPC. Set up an AWS Direct Connect connection, and route traffic to Amazon S3 over the Direct Connect connection.

declencheurs: EC2 access S3 over internet currently
traffic must take a private route
radar.signal: Rendre l'acces S3 prive -> deplacer les EC2 en subnets prives + VPC endpoint pour S3, route dans les tables prives

pieges.A: Un NAT gateway achemine toujours le trafic via Internet
pieges.B: Restreindre le SG au prefix list S3 ne rend pas le chemin prive (toujours via Internet)
pieges.D: Direct Connect relie l'on-prem a AWS, sans rapport avec l'acces prive a S3 depuis un VPC

explication: En placant les instances en subnets prives et en creant un VPC gateway endpoint pour S3 (route ajoutee dans les tables prives), le trafic vers S3 emprunte le reseau AWS et non Internet. Un NAT gateway ou un internet gateway laisseraient le trafic passer par Internet.

question: A solutions architect needs to implement a solution to reduce a company's storage costs. All the company data is in the Amazon S3 Standard storage class. The company must keep all data for at least 25 years. Data from the most recent 2 years must be highly available and immediately retrievable. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Set up an S3 Lifecycle policy to transition objects to S3 Glacier Deep Archive immediately.
options.B: Set up an S3 Lifecycle policy to transition objects to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 2 years.
options.C: Use S3 Intelligent-Tiering. Activate the archiving option to ensure that data is archived in S3 Glacier Deep Archive.
options.D: Set up an S3 Lifecycle policy to transition objects to S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA) immediately and to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 2 years.

declencheurs: recent 2 years highly available and immediate
radar.signal: Acces immediat 2 ans puis archivage long -> Lifecycle qui bascule vers S3 Glacier Deep Archive apres 2 ans

pieges.A: Transition immediate vers Deep Archive empeche l'acces immediat des 2 premieres annees
pieges.C: Intelligent-Tiering coute plus qu'une transition directe vers Deep Archive apres 2 ans
pieges.D: One Zone-IA immediat reduit la durabilite/disponibilite exigee sur les 2 ans recents

explication: Les donnees des 2 dernieres annees doivent rester en S3 Standard (hautement disponibles, immediates). Une Lifecycle policy les bascule ensuite vers S3 Glacier Deep Archive (le plus economique) pour le reste des 25 ans. Une transition immediate (A) casserait l'exigence d'acces immediat recent.

question: A media company is evaluating the possibility of moving its systems to the AWS Cloud. The company needs at least 10 TB of storage with the maximum possible I/O performance for video processing, 300 TB of very durable storage for storing media content, and 900 TB of storage to meet requirements for archival media that is not in use anymore. Which set of services should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?

options.A: Amazon EBS for maximum performance, Amazon S3 for durable data storage, and Amazon S3 Glacier for archival storage.
options.B: Amazon EBS for maximum performance, Amazon EFS for durable data storage, and Amazon S3 Glacier for archival storage.
options.C: Amazon EC2 instance store for maximum performance, Amazon EFS for durable data storage, and Amazon S3 for archival storage.
options.D: Amazon EC2 instance store for maximum performance, Amazon S3 for durable data storage, and Amazon S3 Glacier for archival storage.

declencheurs: 10 TB max I/O performance for video
radar.signal: Perf max -> Amazon EBS ; stockage durable -> Amazon S3 ; archivage -> Amazon S3 Glacier

pieges.B: EFS n'est pas le plus durable/economique pour 300 To de contenu media (S3 l'est)
pieges.C: L'instance store est ephemere ; EFS/S3 mal repartis
pieges.D: L'instance store perd les donnees a l'arret (pas fiable pour la performance persistante)

explication: Amazon EBS (ex. io2) offre les IOPS maximales pour le traitement video (10 To), Amazon S3 fournit un stockage tres durable et economique pour les 300 To de media, et S3 Glacier archive les 900 To inutilises a bas cout. L'instance store est ephemere et EFS n'est pas le choix le plus durable/economique ici.

question: A company wants to run applications in containers in the AWS Cloud. These applications are stateless and can tolerate disruptions within the underlying infrastructure. The company needs a solution that minimizes cost and operational overhead. What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

options.A: Use Spot Instances in an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group to run the application containers.
options.B: Use Spot Instances in an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) managed node group.
options.C: Use On-Demand Instances in an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group to run the application containers.
options.D: Use On-Demand Instances in an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) managed node group.

radar.signal: Conteneurs stateless interruptibles au moindre cout/overhead -> Spot Instances dans un EC2 Auto Scaling group

pieges.B: EKS ajoute la gestion d'un plan de controle Kubernetes (plus d'overhead)
pieges.C: On-Demand coute plus cher que Spot pour une charge tolerant les interruptions
pieges.D: On-Demand + EKS cumule cout eleve et overhead Kubernetes

explication: Des conteneurs stateless tolerant les interruptions sont ideaux pour des Spot Instances (jusqu'a 90% moins cher) dans un EC2 Auto Scaling group (ECS), plus simple a operer qu'EKS. On minimise ainsi a la fois le cout et l'overhead operationnel.

question: A company has hired an external vendor to perform work in the company's AWS account. The vendor uses an automated tool that is hosted in an AWS account that the vendor owns. The vendor does not have IAM access to the company's AWS account. The company needs to grant the vendor access to the company's AWS account. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST securely?

options.A: Create an IAM role in the company's account to delegate access to the vendor's IAM role. Attach the appropriate IAM policies to the role for the permissions that the vendor requires.
options.B: Create an IAM user in the company account with a password that meets the password complexity requirements. Attach the appropriate IAM policies to the user for the permissions that the vendor requires.
options.C: Create an IAM group in the company's account. Add the automated tool IAM user from the vendor account to the group. Attach the appropriate IAM policies to the group for the permissions that the vendor requires.
options.D: Create an IAM user in the company account that has a permission boundary that allows the vendor's account. Attach the appropriate IAM policies to the user for the permissions that the vendor requires.

declencheurs: external vendor tool in vendor's AWS account
no IAM access to company account
radar.signal: Acces cross-account securise -> role IAM dans le compte de l'entreprise deleguant au role IAM du prestataire

pieges.B: Un IAM user + mot de passe = identifiants a gerer (moins sur)
pieges.C: On ne peut pas ajouter l'IAM user d'un autre compte a un groupe local
pieges.D: Un permission boundary ne remplace pas la relation de confiance cross-account

explication: Le modele le plus sur est un role IAM dans le compte de l'entreprise, avec une relation de confiance vers le role/compte du prestataire et les permissions requises. L'outil du prestataire assume ce role et recoit des identifiants temporaires, sans creer d'utilisateur ni de cles statiques.

question: A company wants to run its experimental workloads in the AWS Cloud. The company has a budget for cloud spending. The company's CFO is concerned about cloud spending accountability for each department. The CFO wants to receive notification when the spending threshold reaches 60% of the budget. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Use cost allocation tags on AWS resources to label owners. Create usage budgets in AWS Budgets. Add an alert threshold to receive notification when spending exceeds 60% of the budget.
options.B: Use AWS Cost Explorer forecasts to determine resource owners. Use AWS Cost Anomaly Detection to create alert threshold notifications when spending exceeds 60% of the budget.
options.C: Use cost allocation tags on AWS resources to label owners. Use AWS Support API on AWS Trusted Advisor to create alert threshold notifications when spending exceeds 60% of the budget.
options.D: Use AWS Cost Explorer forecasts to determine resource owners. Create usage budgets in AWS Budgets. Add an alert threshold to receive notification when spending exceeds 60% of the budget.

radar.signal: Responsabiliser par departement + alerte a 60% -> cost allocation tags (proprietaires) + AWS Budgets avec seuil d'alerte a 60%

pieges.B: Cost Explorer/Anomaly Detection detecte des anomalies, il ne fixe pas un seuil de budget a 60%
pieges.C: Trusted Advisor ne cree pas d'alertes de seuil budgetaire par departement
pieges.D: Cost Explorer forecasts ne 'determine' pas les proprietaires ; ce sont les tags qui le font

explication: Les cost allocation tags identifient le departement proprietaire de chaque ressource, et AWS Budgets cree des budgets d'usage par departement avec une alerte declenchee a 60% du budget. Cost Anomaly Detection ou Trusted Advisor ne repondent pas a une notification de seuil budgetaire.

question: A company hosts an application on multiple Amazon EC2 instances. The application processes messages from an Amazon SQS queue, writes to an Amazon RDS table, and deletes the message from the queue. Occasional duplicate records are found in the RDS table. The SQS queue does not contain any duplicate messages. What should a solutions architect do to ensure messages are being processed once only?

options.A: Use the CreateQueue API call to create a new queue.
options.B: Use the AddPermission API call to add appropriate permissions.
options.C: Use the ReceiveMessage API call to set an appropriate wait time.
options.D: Use the ChangeMessageVisibility API call to increase the visibility timeout.

declencheurs: process SQS message, write to RDS, delete message
radar.signal: Doublons dus a un traitement plus long que le visibility timeout -> augmenter le visibility timeout via ChangeMessageVisibility

pieges.A: Creer une nouvelle file ne change rien au probleme de timeout
pieges.B: AddPermission gere les autorisations, pas la duplication
pieges.C: Le wait time (long polling) concerne la reception, pas la reapparition prematuree du message

explication: Les doublons viennent du fait que le traitement (ecriture RDS) depasse le visibility timeout : le message redevient visible et est traite une seconde fois avant sa suppression. Augmenter le visibility timeout (ChangeMessageVisibility) laisse le temps de finir le traitement et de supprimer le message une seule fois.

question: A solutions architect is designing a new hybrid architecture to extend a company's on-premises infrastructure to AWS. The company requires a highly available connection with consistent low latency to an AWS Region. The company needs to minimize costs and is willing to accept slower traffic if the primary connection fails. What should the solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

options.A: Provision an AWS Direct Connect connection to a Region. Provision a VPN connection as a backup if the primary Direct Connect connection fails.
options.B: Provision a VPN tunnel connection to a Region for private connectivity. Provision a second VPN tunnel for private connectivity and as a backup if the primary VPN connection fails.
options.C: Provision an AWS Direct Connect connection to a Region. Provision a second Direct Connect connection to the same Region as a backup if the primary Direct Connect connection fails.
options.D: Provision an AWS Direct Connect connection to a Region. Use the Direct Connect failover attribute from the AWS CLI to automatically create a backup connection if the primary Direct Connect connection fails.

radar.signal: Faible latence stable + backup economique acceptant une degradation -> Direct Connect en principal + VPN en secours

pieges.B: Deux VPN n'offrent pas la latence stable de Direct Connect
pieges.C: Un second Direct Connect en backup est plus couteux qu'un VPN de secours
pieges.D: Il n'existe pas d'attribut CLI 'failover Direct Connect' creant automatiquement un backup

explication: Direct Connect fournit une liaison privee a faible latence constante. Comme l'entreprise accepte un trafic plus lent en cas de panne, un VPN sur Internet en secours est bien moins cher qu'un second Direct Connect. C'est la combinaison HA la plus economique respectant les contraintes.

question: A company is using a centralized AWS account to store log data in various Amazon S3 buckets. A solutions architect needs to ensure that the data is encrypted at rest before the data is uploaded to the S3 buckets. The data also must be encrypted in transit. Which solution meets these requirements?

options.A: Use client-side encryption to encrypt the data that is being uploaded to the S3 buckets.
options.B: Use server-side encryption to encrypt the data that is being uploaded to the S3 buckets.
options.C: Create bucket policies that require the use of server-side encryption with S3 managed encryption keys (SSE-S3) for S3 uploads.
options.D: Enable the security option to encrypt the S3 buckets through the use of a default AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key.

radar.signal: Donnees chiffrees AVANT l'upload -> chiffrement cote client (client-side encryption)

pieges.B: Le server-side encryption chiffre a l'arrivee, pas avant l'upload
pieges.C: SSE-S3 impose est aussi cote serveur (apres reception)
pieges.D: Une cle KMS par defaut reste du chiffrement cote serveur

explication: L'exigence 'chiffre au repos AVANT l'upload' impose un chiffrement cote client : les donnees sont chiffrees par l'application avant d'etre envoyees, et le transit se fait en HTTPS. Le server-side encryption (B, C, D) ne chiffre qu'une fois les donnees arrivees dans S3.

question: A solutions architect observes that a nightly batch processing job is automatically scaled up for 1 hour before the desired Amazon EC2 capacity is reached. The peak capacity is the same every night and the batch jobs always start at 1 AM. The solutions architect needs to find a cost-effective solution that will allow for the desired EC2 capacity to be reached quickly and allow the Auto Scaling group to scale down after the batch jobs are complete. What should the solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

options.A: Increase the minimum capacity for the Auto Scaling group.
options.B: Increase the maximum capacity for the Auto Scaling group.
options.C: Configure scheduled scaling to scale up to the desired compute level.
options.D: Change the scaling policy to add more EC2 instances during each scaling operation.

declencheurs: reach capacity quickly then scale down
radar.signal: Charge previsible a heure fixe -> scheduled scaling pour atteindre la capacite juste avant 1h du matin

pieges.A: Augmenter la capacite minimale garde des instances actives toute la journee (cout inutile)
pieges.B: Augmenter la capacite maximale n'accelere pas la montee a l'heure voulue
pieges.D: Ajouter plus d'instances par operation reste reactif, pas anticipe

explication: Comme le pic est previsible et se produit chaque nuit a 1h, le scheduled scaling provisionne la capacite desiree juste avant l'heure, evitant l'heure de montee reactive. L'Auto Scaling group redescend ensuite apres les jobs. Augmenter le minimum (A) garderait des instances actives (et facturees) en permanence.

question: A company runs a shopping application that uses Amazon DynamoDB to store customer information. In case of data corruption, a solutions architect needs to design a solution that meets a recovery point objective (RPO) of 15 minutes and a recovery time objective (RTO) of 1 hour. What should the solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?

options.A: Configure DynamoDB global tables. For RPO recovery, point the application to a different AWS Region.
options.B: Configure DynamoDB point-in-time recovery. For RPO recovery, restore to the desired point in time.
options.C: Export the DynamoDB data to Amazon S3 Glacier on a daily basis. For RPO recovery, import the data from S3 Glacier to DynamoDB.
options.D: Schedule Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) snapshots for the DynamoDB table every 15 minutes. For RPO recovery, restore the DynamoDB table by using the EBS snapshot.

radar.signal: Restaurer une table DynamoDB a un instant precis apres corruption -> point-in-time recovery (PITR)

pieges.A: Les global tables repliquent la corruption vers les autres Regions
pieges.C: Un export quotidien vers Glacier donne un RPO de 24h (> 15 min)
pieges.D: Les snapshots EBS ne s'appliquent pas a DynamoDB (service manage)

explication: Le point-in-time recovery de DynamoDB permet de restaurer la table a n'importe quel instant des 35 derniers jours, a la seconde pres, ce qui couvre un RPO de 15 minutes et un RTO d'une heure. Les global tables repliqueraient la corruption, et un export quotidien ne tiendrait pas le RPO.

question: A company runs a photo processing application that needs to frequently upload and download pictures from Amazon S3 buckets that are located in the same AWS Region. A solutions architect has noticed an increased cost in data transfer fees and needs to implement a solution to reduce these costs. How can the solutions architect meet this requirement?

options.A: Deploy Amazon API Gateway into a public subnet and adjust the route table to route S3 calls through it.
options.B: Deploy a NAT gateway into a public subnet and attach an endpoint policy that allows access to the S3 buckets.
options.C: Deploy the application into a public subnet and allow it to route through an internet gateway to access the S3 buckets.
options.D: Deploy an S3 VPC gateway endpoint into the VPC and attach an endpoint policy that allows access to the S3 buckets.

declencheurs: frequent upload/download to S3 same Region
radar.signal: Reduire les frais de transfert vers S3 depuis un VPC -> S3 VPC gateway endpoint (gratuit) + endpoint policy

pieges.A: API Gateway ne route pas les appels S3 pour reduire les frais de transfert
pieges.B: Un NAT gateway facture le traitement et le transfert des donnees
pieges.C: Passer par un internet gateway maintient des frais de transfert de donnees

explication: Un S3 VPC gateway endpoint est gratuit et route le trafic vers S3 directement par le reseau AWS, supprimant les frais de transfert lies au NAT gateway ou a la sortie Internet. Une endpoint policy restreint l'acces aux buckets voulus.

question: A company hosts a marketing website in an on-premises data center. The website consists of static documents and runs on a single server. An administrator updates the website content infrequently and uses an SFTP client to upload new documents. The company decides to host its website on AWS and to use Amazon CloudFront. The company solutions architect creates a CloudFront distribution. The solutions architect must design the most cost-effective and resilient architecture for website hosting to serve as the CloudFront origin. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Create a virtual server by using Amazon Lightsail. Configure the web server in the Lightsail instance. Upload website content by using an SFTP client.
options.B: Create an AWS Auto Scaling group for Amazon EC2 instances. Use an Application Load Balancer. Upload website content by using an SFTP client.
options.C: Create a private Amazon S3 bucket. Use an S3 bucket policy to allow access from a CloudFront origin access identity (OAI). Upload website content by using the AWS CLI.
options.D: Create a public Amazon S3 bucket. Configure AWS Transfer for SFTP. Configure the S3 bucket for website hosting. Upload website content by using the SFTP client.

radar.signal: Origine statique economique et resiliente pour CloudFront -> bucket S3 prive + OAI (bucket policy) + upload via AWS CLI

pieges.A: Lightsail = instance facturee en continu pour du statique
pieges.B: ASG EC2 + ALB = infrastructure couteuse et superflue pour un site statique
pieges.D: Un bucket public + Transfer for SFTP est moins securise et plus complexe que l'upload CLI

explication: Un bucket S3 prive comme origine de CloudFront, accessible seulement via une Origin Access Identity, est l'hebergement statique le plus economique et le plus resilient (durabilite S3, aucune instance a gerer). L'administrateur televerse le contenu occasionnel via la CLI. EC2/Lightsail seraient couteux et fragiles pour du statique.

question: A company wants to manage Amazon Machine Images (AMIs). The company currently copies AMIs to the same AWS Region where the AMIs were created. The company needs to design an application that captures AWS API calls and sends alerts whenever the Amazon EC2 CreateImage API operation is called within the company account. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.A: Create an AWS Lambda function to query AWS CloudTrail logs and to send an alert when a CreateImage API call is detected.
options.B: Configure AWS CloudTrail with an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) notification that occurs when updated logs are sent to Amazon S3. Use Amazon Athena to create a new table and to query on CreateImage when an API call is detected.
options.C: Create an Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) rule for the CreateImage API call. Configure the target as an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic to send an alert when a CreateImage API call is detected.
options.D: Configure an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) FIFO queue as a target for AWS CloudTrail logs. Create an AWS Lambda function to send an alert to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic when a CreateImage API call is detected.

radar.signal: Alerter sur un appel d'API precis -> regle Amazon EventBridge sur CreateImage, cible SNS

pieges.A: Une Lambda qui interroge CloudTrail = code a ecrire et a planifier
pieges.B: CloudTrail + SNS sur logs S3 + Athena = plusieurs composants a configurer
pieges.D: SQS FIFO + Lambda + SNS = chaine plus complexe que necessaire

explication: Une regle Amazon EventBridge qui reagit a l'appel d'API CreateImage et cible un topic SNS envoie l'alerte immediatement, sans code ni infrastructure a maintenir. Les autres options ajoutent des Lambda, Athena ou des files a configurer et exploiter.

question: A news company that has reporters all over the world is hosting its broadcast system on AWS. The reporters send live broadcasts to the broadcast system. The reporters use software on their phones to send live streams through the Real Time Messaging Protocol (RTMP). A solutions architect must design a solution that gives the reporters the ability to send the highest quality streams. The solution must provide accelerated TCP connections back to the broadcast system. What should the solutions architect use to meet these requirements?

options.A: Amazon CloudFront
options.B: AWS Global Accelerator
options.C: AWS Client VPN
options.D: Amazon EC2 instances and AWS Elastic IP addresses

declencheurs: reporters worldwide send RTMP live streams
accelerated TCP connections back to system
radar.signal: Accelerer des connexions TCP mondiales vers un systeme -> AWS Global Accelerator

pieges.A: CloudFront est un CDN de diffusion sortante (HTTP), pas d'acceleration TCP entrante RTMP
pieges.C: Un Client VPN ne fournit pas d'acceleration reseau
pieges.D: Des EC2 + Elastic IP n'accelerent pas le transport TCP mondial

explication: AWS Global Accelerator achemine les connexions TCP des reporters via le backbone AWS depuis le point de presence le plus proche, accelerant et fiabilisant le transport RTMP (base TCP) vers le systeme de diffusion. CloudFront sert a diffuser du contenu, pas a accelerer des flux entrants.

question: A company uses Amazon EC2 instances and Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) to run its self-managed database. The company has 350 TB of data spread across all EBS volumes. The company takes daily EBS snapshots and keeps the snapshots for 1 month. The daily change rate is 5% of the EBS volumes. Because of new regulations, the company needs to keep the monthly snapshots for 7 years. The company needs to change its backup strategy to comply with the new regulations and to ensure that data is available with minimal administrative effort. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

options.A: Keep the daily snapshot in the EBS snapshot standard tier for 1 month. Copy the monthly snapshot to Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive with a 7-year retention period.
options.B: Continue with the current EBS snapshot policy. Add a new policy to move the monthly snapshot to Amazon EBS Snapshots Archive with a 7-year retention period.
options.C: Keep the daily snapshot in the EBS snapshot standard tier for 1 month. Keep the monthly snapshot in the standard tier for 7 years. Use incremental snapshots.
options.D: Keep the daily snapshot in the EBS snapshot standard tier. Use EBS direct APIs to take snapshots of all the EBS volumes every month. Store the snapshots in an Amazon S3 bucket in the Infrequent Access tier for 7 years.

radar.signal: Conserver des snapshots mensuels 7 ans a bas cout -> garder la politique EBS actuelle + politique deplacant le snapshot mensuel vers EBS Snapshots Archive (retention 7 ans)

pieges.A: Copier vers Glacier Deep Archive n'est pas le mecanisme natif d'archivage des snapshots EBS
pieges.C: Garder les mensuels en tier standard 7 ans coute bien plus cher
pieges.D: Les EBS direct APIs vers S3 IA = solution custom et couteuse en effort

explication: Amazon EBS Snapshots Archive est un tier d'archivage a bas cout concu pour les snapshots rarement restaures conserves longtemps. En gardant la politique quotidienne actuelle et en ajoutant une regle qui deplace le snapshot mensuel vers l'Archive avec 7 ans de retention, on repond a la reglementation au meilleur cout et avec un minimum d'effort.

question: A company wants to ingest customer payment data into the company data lake in Amazon S3. The company receives payment data every minute on average. The company wants to analyze the payment data in real time. Then the company wants to ingest the data into the data lake. Which solution will meet these requirements with the MOST operational efficiency?

options.A: Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to ingest data. Use AWS Lambda to analyze the data in real time.
options.B: Use AWS Glue to ingest data. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics to analyze the data in real time.
options.C: Use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to ingest data. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics to analyze the data in real time.
options.D: Use Amazon API Gateway to ingest data. Use AWS Lambda to analyze the data in real time.

declencheurs: ingest payment data into S3 data lake
radar.signal: Ingestion temps reel + analyse immediate -> Amazon Kinesis Data Streams + AWS Lambda pour analyser en temps reel

pieges.B: AWS Glue est un ETL par lots, pas une ingestion temps reel
pieges.C: Firehose est proche du temps reel (buffering) mais moins reactif que Data Streams + Lambda pour de l'analyse a la seconde
pieges.D: API Gateway n'est pas un service d'ingestion de flux

explication: Kinesis Data Streams capte le flux de paiements en temps reel, et une fonction Lambda l'analyse a la volee avant depot dans le lac S3. C'est la combinaison la plus efficace pour de l'analyse temps reel, la ou Glue (batch) ou Firehose (buffering) seraient moins reactifs.

question: A company runs a website that uses a content management system (CMS) on Amazon EC2. The CMS runs on a single EC2 instance and uses an Amazon Aurora MySQL Multi-AZ DB instance for the data tier. Website images are stored on an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume that is mounted inside the EC2 instance. Which combination of actions should a solutions architect take to improve the performance and resilience of the website? (Choose two.)

options.A: Move the website images into an Amazon S3 bucket that is mounted on every EC2 instance.
options.B: Share the website images by using an NFS share from the primary EC2 instance. Mount this share on the other EC2 instances.
options.C: Move the website images onto an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system that is mounted on every EC2 instance.
options.D: Create an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) from the existing EC2 instance. Use the AMI to provision new instances behind an Application Load Balancer as part of an Auto Scaling group. Configure the Auto Scaling group to maintain a minimum of two instances. Configure an accelerator in AWS Global Accelerator for the website.
options.E: Create an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) from the existing EC2 instance. Use the AMI to provision new instances behind an Application Load Balancer as part of an Auto Scaling group. Configure the Auto Scaling group to maintain a minimum of two instances. Configure an Amazon CloudFront distribution for the website.

declencheurs: images on EBS mounted in the instance
radar.signal: Rendre le CMS resilient/performant -> images sur Amazon EFS partage (C) + AMI/ASG multi-instances derriere un ALB + CloudFront (E)

pieges.A: On ne 'monte' pas nativement un bucket S3 sur chaque EC2 comme un systeme de fichiers
pieges.B: Un partage NFS depuis l'instance primaire recree un point de defaillance unique
pieges.D: Global Accelerator convient a TCP/UDP, pas a l'acceleration de contenu web comme CloudFront

explication: Deplacer les images vers Amazon EFS les rend accessibles a toutes les instances sans point unique (C). Creer une AMI pour lancer plusieurs instances via un Auto Scaling group derriere un ALB, avec CloudFront devant (E), ajoute haute disponibilite et performance. Global Accelerator (D) n'est pas adapte a du contenu web, contrairement a CloudFront.

question: A company is migrating applications to AWS. The applications are deployed in different accounts. The company manages the accounts centrally by using AWS Organizations. The company security team needs a single sign-on (SSO) solution across all the company accounts. The company must continue managing the users and groups in its on-premises self-managed Microsoft Active Directory. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Enable AWS Single Sign-On (AWS SSO) from the AWS SSO console. Create a one-way forest trust or a one-way domain trust to connect the company self-managed Microsoft Active Directory with AWS SSO by using AWS Directory Service for Microsoft Active Directory.
options.B: Enable AWS Single Sign-On (AWS SSO) from the AWS SSO console. Create a two-way forest trust to connect the company self-managed Microsoft Active Directory with AWS SSO by using AWS Directory Service for Microsoft Active Directory.
options.C: Use AWS Directory Service. Create a two-way trust relationship with the company self-managed Microsoft Active Directory.
options.D: Deploy an identity provider (IdP) on premises. Enable AWS Single Sign-On (AWS SSO) from the AWS SSO console.

declencheurs: keep managing users/groups in on-prem self-managed AD
radar.signal: SSO multi-comptes en conservant l'AD on-prem -> AWS SSO (IAM Identity Center) + trust unidirectionnelle vers l'AD via AWS Managed Microsoft AD

pieges.B: Une two-way forest trust n'est pas necessaire (une one-way suffit et est plus sure)
pieges.C: Directory Service seul, sans AWS SSO, ne fournit pas le SSO multi-comptes
pieges.D: Deployer un IdP on-prem ajoute de l'infrastructure alors que l'AD existe deja

explication: AWS SSO (IAM Identity Center) fournit le SSO sur tous les comptes de l'organisation. En connectant l'Active Directory auto-gere via AWS Directory Service for Microsoft AD avec une trust unidirectionnelle (forest ou domain), l'entreprise continue de gerer ses utilisateurs/groupes on-prem. Une trust bidirectionnelle serait inutile et moins sure.

question: A company provides a Voice over Internet Protocol (VoIP) service that uses UDP connections. The service consists of Amazon EC2 instances that run in an Auto Scaling group. The company has deployments across multiple AWS Regions. The company needs to route users to the Region with the lowest latency. The company also needs automated failover between Regions. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Deploy a Network Load Balancer (NLB) and an associated target group. Associate the target group with the Auto Scaling group. Use the NLB as an AWS Global Accelerator endpoint in each Region.
options.B: Deploy an Application Load Balancer (ALB) and an associated target group. Associate the target group with the Auto Scaling group. Use the ALB as an AWS Global Accelerator endpoint in each Region.
options.C: Deploy a Network Load Balancer (NLB) and an associated target group. Associate the target group with the Auto Scaling group. Create an Amazon Route 53 latency record that points to aliases for each NLB. Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution that uses the latency record as an origin.
options.D: Deploy an Application Load Balancer (ALB) and an associated target group. Associate the target group with the Auto Scaling group.
