Create an Amazon Route 53 weighted record that points to aliases for each ALB. Deploy an Amazon CloudFront distribution that uses the weighted record as an origin.

radar.signal: UDP multi-Region a faible latence + bascule automatique -> Network Load Balancer par Region comme endpoints d'AWS Global Accelerator

pieges.B: Un ALB ne gere pas l'UDP
pieges.C: CloudFront (HTTP) ne convient pas a l'UDP, et Route 53 n'a pas la bascule reseau de Global Accelerator
pieges.D: ALB + Route 53 weighted ne gere ni l'UDP ni le routage par latence avec bascule reseau

explication: Le trafic UDP impose des Network Load Balancers. En les enregistrant comme endpoints d'AWS Global Accelerator, les utilisateurs sont diriges vers la Region la plus proche via le backbone AWS, avec une bascule automatique et rapide vers une Region saine en cas de panne. ALB et CloudFront ne gerent pas l'UDP.

question: A research laboratory needs to process approximately 8 TB of data. The laboratory requires sub-millisecond latencies and a minimum throughput of 6 GBps for the storage subsystem. Hundreds of Amazon EC2 instances that run Amazon Linux will distribute and process the data. Which solution will meet the performance requirements?

options.A: Create an Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP file system. Set each volume's tiering policy to ALL. Import the raw data into the file system. Mount the file system on the EC2 instances.
options.B: Create an Amazon S3 bucket to store the raw data. Create an Amazon FSx for Lustre file system that uses persistent SSD storage. Select the option to import data from and export data to Amazon S3. Mount the file system on the EC2 instances.
options.C: Create an Amazon S3 bucket to store the raw data. Create an Amazon FSx for Lustre file system that uses persistent HDD storage. Select the option to import data from and export data to Amazon S3. Mount the file system on the EC2 instances.
options.D: Create an Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP file system. Set each volume's tiering policy to NONE. Import the raw data into the file system. Mount the file system on the EC2 instances.

radar.signal: Debit massif + latence sub-milliseconde pour du calcul distribue Linux -> Amazon FSx for Lustre avec stockage SSD persistant (integre a S3)

pieges.A: FSx for NetApp ONTAP avec tiering ALL deplace les donnees vers un tier lent (latence accrue)
pieges.C: FSx for Lustre en HDD n'atteint pas la latence sub-milliseconde ni 6 GBps
pieges.D: FSx for ONTAP n'est pas optimise pour ce niveau de debit HPC comme Lustre

explication: Amazon FSx for Lustre est le systeme de fichiers hautes performances (HPC) d'AWS : en stockage SSD persistant, il offre des latences sub-milliseconde et un debit de plusieurs Go/s, monte par des centaines d'instances Linux. Le HDD (C) ou ONTAP avec tiering (A) ne tiennent pas ces exigences.

question: A company needs to migrate a legacy application from an on-premises data center to the AWS Cloud because of hardware capacity constraints. The application runs 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. The application database storage continues to grow over time. What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

options.A: Migrate the application layer to Amazon EC2 Spot Instances. Migrate the data storage layer to Amazon S3.
options.B: Migrate the application layer to Amazon EC2 Reserved Instances. Migrate the data storage layer to Amazon RDS On-Demand Instances.
options.C: Migrate the application layer to Amazon EC2 Reserved Instances. Migrate the data storage layer to Amazon Aurora Reserved Instances.
options.D: Migrate the application layer to Amazon EC2 On-Demand Instances. Migrate the data storage layer to Amazon RDS Reserved Instances.

radar.signal: Charge continue previsible + stockage croissant -> EC2 Reserved Instances + Aurora (Reserved Instances) dont le stockage grandit automatiquement

pieges.A: Spot peut etre interrompu (inadapte a une app 24/7) ; S3 n'est pas une base relationnelle
pieges.B: RDS On-Demand coute plus cher qu'un engagement Reserved pour du 24/7
pieges.D: EC2 On-Demand coute plus cher que Reserved pour une charge permanente

explication: Pour une application qui tourne 24/7, des Reserved Instances (EC2 et Aurora) offrent la meilleure economie sur une charge previsible. Aurora gere automatiquement la croissance du stockage. Spot (interruptible) et On-Demand (plus cher) ne conviennent pas a ce profil continu.

question: A company wants to provide users with access to AWS resources. The company has 1,500 users and manages their access to on-premises resources through Active Directory user groups on the corporate network. However, the company does not want users to have to maintain another identity to access the resources. A solutions architect must manage user access to the AWS resources while preserving access to the on-premises resources. What should the solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

options.A: Create an IAM user for each user in the company. Attach the appropriate policies to each user.
options.B: Use Amazon Cognito with an Active Directory user pool. Create roles with the appropriate policies attached.
options.C: Define cross-account roles with the appropriate policies attached. Map the roles to the Active Directory groups.
options.D: Configure Security Assertion Markup Language (SAML) 2.0-based federation. Create roles with the appropriate policies attached. Map the roles to the Active Directory groups.

declencheurs: access AWS while keeping on-prem access
radar.signal: Federer l'AD existant vers AWS sans nouvelle identite -> federation SAML 2.0 + roles IAM mappes aux groupes AD

pieges.A: Creer un IAM user par utilisateur = seconde identite a maintenir
pieges.B: Cognito cible des utilisateurs applicatifs (web/mobile), pas l'acces console/ressources par des employes AD
pieges.C: Des cross-account roles ne federent pas l'authentification depuis l'AD

explication: La federation SAML 2.0 laisse les utilisateurs s'authentifier avec leurs identites Active Directory existantes ; des roles IAM mappes aux groupes AD accordent les permissions AWS. Aucune seconde identite n'est creee, et l'acces on-prem est preserve. Cognito et les IAM users ne repondent pas a ce besoin de federation d'employes.

question: A company is hosting a website behind multiple Application Load Balancers. The company has different distribution rights for its content around the world. A solutions architect needs to ensure that users are served the correct content without violating distribution rights. Which configuration should the solutions architect choose to meet these requirements?

options.A: Configure Amazon CloudFront with AWS WAF.
options.B: Configure Application Load Balancers with AWS WAF.
options.C: Configure Amazon Route 53 with a geolocation policy.
options.D: Configure Amazon Route 53 with a geoproximity routing policy.

declencheurs: different distribution rights around the world
radar.signal: Servir un contenu selon le pays de l'utilisateur -> Amazon Route 53 avec une geolocation routing policy

pieges.A: CloudFront + WAF filtre/protege mais ne route pas le contenu par droits geographiques ainsi
pieges.B: WAF sur les ALB ne gere pas le routage par pays vers le bon contenu
pieges.D: Le geoproximity route selon la proximite geographique, pas selon les droits de diffusion par pays

explication: La geolocation routing policy de Route 53 dirige chaque utilisateur vers l'endpoint correspondant a son pays/continent, ce qui permet de servir le contenu conforme aux droits de diffusion locaux. Le geoproximity (D) optimise la distance, pas le respect des droits par pays.

question: A company has a large workload that runs every Friday evening. The workload runs on Amazon EC2 instances that are in two Availability Zones in the us-east-1 Region. Normally, the company must run no more than two instances at all times. However, the company wants to scale up to six instances each Friday to handle a regular repeating increased workload. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.A: Create a reminder in Amazon EventBridge to scale the instances.
options.B: Create an Auto Scaling group that has a scheduled action.
options.C: Create an Auto Scaling group that uses manual scaling.
options.D: Create an Auto Scaling group that uses automatic scaling.

radar.signal: Montee previsible a heure/jour fixe -> Auto Scaling group avec une scheduled action

pieges.A: Un rappel EventBridge n'ajuste pas la capacite automatiquement
pieges.C: Le scaling manuel impose une intervention chaque vendredi
pieges.D: Le scaling automatique reagit aux metriques, moins precis qu'une action planifiee pour un pic connu

explication: Le pic etant previsible (chaque vendredi soir), une scheduled action sur l'Auto Scaling group porte la capacite a six instances a l'horaire voulu puis revient a deux ensuite, sans intervention. C'est le moins d'overhead, contrairement au scaling manuel ou a un simple rappel.

question: A company is creating a REST API. The company has strict requirements for the use of TLS. The company requires TLSv1.3 on the API endpoints. The company also requires a specific public third-party certificate authority (CA) to sign the TLS certificate. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Use a local machine to create a certificate that is signed by the third-party CA. Import the certificate into AWS Certificate Manager (ACM). Create an HTTP API in Amazon API Gateway with a custom domain. Configure the custom domain to use the certificate.
options.B: Create a certificate in AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) that is signed by the third-party CA. Create an HTTP API in Amazon API Gateway with a custom domain. Configure the custom domain to use the certificate.
options.C: Use AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) to create a certificate that is signed by the third-party CA. Import the certificate into AWS Certificate Manager (ACM). Create an AWS Lambda function with a Lambda function URL. Configure the Lambda function URL to use the certificate.
options.D: Create a certificate in AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) that is signed by the third-party CA. Create an AWS Lambda function with a Lambda function URL. Configure the Lambda function URL to use the certificate.

declencheurs: certificate signed by a specific third-party CA
radar.signal: Certificat signe par une CA tierce sur API Gateway -> creer/signer le certificat chez la CA, l'importer dans ACM, l'utiliser sur un custom domain API Gateway

pieges.B: ACM ne peut pas emettre un certificat signe par une CA tierce (il faut l'importer)
pieges.C: Une Lambda function URL n'est pas la bonne cible pour une REST API avec custom domain, et ACM n'emet pas via une CA tierce
pieges.D: Idem : ACM ne signe pas via une CA tierce et la function URL n'est pas adaptee

explication: ACM ne peut pas emettre un certificat signe par une autorite de certification tierce specifique : il faut creer le certificat aupres de cette CA, puis l'importer dans ACM. On l'associe ensuite a un custom domain d'Amazon API Gateway, qui supporte TLSv1.3.

question: A company is planning to store data on Amazon RDS DB instances. The company must encrypt the data at rest. What should a solutions architect do to meet this requirement?

options.A: Create a key in AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS). Enable encryption for the DB instances.
options.B: Create an encryption key. Store the key in AWS Secrets Manager. Use the key to encrypt the DB instances.
options.C: Generate a certificate in AWS Certificate Manager (ACM). Enable SSL/TLS on the DB instances by using the certificate.
options.D: Generate a certificate in AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM). Enable SSL/TLS on the DB instances by using the certificate.

radar.signal: Chiffrement au repos RDS -> creer une cle AWS KMS et activer le chiffrement des DB instances

pieges.B: Secrets Manager stocke des secrets, il ne chiffre pas le stockage d'une DB
pieges.C: ACM/SSL concernent le chiffrement en transit, pas au repos
pieges.D: IAM ne genere pas de certificats pour chiffrer le stockage au repos

explication: Le chiffrement au repos d'RDS s'active a la creation de l'instance en s'appuyant sur une cle AWS KMS. Secrets Manager (secrets), ACM et IAM (certificats/en transit) ne fournissent pas le chiffrement du stockage au repos.

question: A company must migrate 20 TB of data from a data center to the AWS Cloud within 30 days. The company's network bandwidth is limited to 15 Mbps and cannot exceed 70% utilization. What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

options.A: Use AWS Snowball.
options.B: Use AWS DataSync.
options.C: Use a secure VPN connection.
options.D: Use Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration.

radar.signal: Volume trop gros pour le reseau disponible dans les delais -> AWS Snowball (transfert physique)

pieges.B: DataSync depend du reseau (10,5 Mbps effectifs) -> bien plus de 30 jours
pieges.C: Un VPN passe par le meme lien reseau limite
pieges.D: Transfer Acceleration reste limite par la bande passante disponible

explication: A 15 Mbps plafonnes a 70% (soit ~10,5 Mbps), transferer 20 To prendrait des mois, bien au-dela des 30 jours. AWS Snowball realise un transfert physique qui contourne la limite reseau et respecte le delai. DataSync, VPN et Transfer Acceleration restent bornes par la bande passante.

question: A company is implementing a shared storage solution for a gaming application that is hosted in an on-premises data center. The company needs the ability to use Lustre clients to access data. The solution must be fully managed. Which solution meets these requirements?

options.A: Create an AWS Storage Gateway file gateway. Create a file share that uses the required client protocol. Connect the application server to the file share.
options.B: Create an Amazon EC2 Windows instance. Install and configure a Windows file share role on the instance. Connect the application server to the file share.
options.C: Create an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system, and configure it to support Lustre. Attach the file system to the origin server. Connect the application server to the file system.
options.D: Create an Amazon FSx for Lustre file system. Attach the file system to the origin server. Connect the application server to the file system.

radar.signal: Acces via clients Lustre, entierement manage -> Amazon FSx for Lustre

pieges.A: Un file gateway Storage Gateway n'expose pas de systeme de fichiers Lustre
pieges.B: Un serveur de fichiers sur EC2 n'est pas manage et ne parle pas Lustre
pieges.C: EFS ne supporte pas le protocole Lustre

explication: Amazon FSx for Lustre est le systeme de fichiers manage compatible avec les clients Lustre, adapte aux charges hautes performances. EFS (NFS) ne parle pas Lustre, et un serveur de fichiers EC2 ne serait pas entierement manage.

question: A company containerized application runs on an Amazon EC2 instance. The application needs to download security certificates before it can communicate with other business applications. The company wants a highly secure solution to encrypt and decrypt the certificates in near real time. The solution also needs to store data in highly available storage after the data is encrypted. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.A: Create AWS Secrets Manager secrets for encrypted certificates. Manually update the certificates as needed. Control access to the data by using fine-grained IAM access.
options.B: Create an AWS Lambda function that uses the Python cryptography library to receive and perform encryption operations. Store the function in an Amazon S3 bucket.
options.C: Create an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) customer managed key. Allow the EC2 role to use the KMS key for encryption operations. Store the encrypted data on Amazon S3.
options.D: Create an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) customer managed key. Allow the EC2 role to use the KMS key for encryption operations. Store the encrypted data on Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes.

declencheurs: encrypt/decrypt certificates in near real time
store encrypted data in highly available storage
radar.signal: Chiffrer/dechiffrer via un service manage + stockage HA -> cle KMS customer managed (role EC2 autorise) + donnees chiffrees sur Amazon S3

pieges.A: Secrets Manager avec mise a jour manuelle des certificats = plus d'operations
pieges.B: Une Lambda avec une librairie crypto custom = code a maintenir
pieges.D: EBS est moins hautement disponible/durable que S3 pour ces donnees

explication: AWS KMS realise les operations de chiffrement/dechiffrement de facon manageee et securisee ; on autorise le role de l'EC2 a utiliser la cle customer managed, et on stocke les donnees chiffrees sur Amazon S3 (hautement disponible et durable). S3 est preferable a EBS pour la disponibilite, et KMS evite le code crypto custom.

question: A company runs its workloads on Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS). The container images that the ECS task definition uses need to be scanned for Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs). New container images that are created also need to be scanned. Which solution will meet these requirements with the FEWEST changes to the workloads?

options.A: Use Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) as a private image repository to store the container images. Specify scan on push filters for the ECR basic scan.
options.B: Store the container images in an Amazon S3 bucket. Use Amazon Macie to scan the images. Use an S3 Event Notification to initiate a Macie scan for every event with an s3:ObjectCreated:Put event type.
options.C: Deploy the workloads to Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS). Use Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) as a private image repository. Specify scan on push filters for the ECR enhanced scan.
options.D: Store the container images in an Amazon S3 bucket that has versioning enabled. Configure an S3 Event Notification for s3:ObjectCreated:* events to invoke an AWS Lambda function. Configure the Lambda function to initiate an Amazon Inspector scan.

declencheurs: ECS container images scanned for CVEs
radar.signal: Scanner les images ECS avec le moins de changement -> Amazon ECR comme registre prive + scan on push (basic scan)

pieges.B: S3 + Macie ne scanne pas des images de conteneur pour des CVE
pieges.C: Migrer vers EKS = beaucoup de changements aux workloads
pieges.D: S3 + Lambda + Inspector = solution custom plus complexe

explication: En stockant les images dans Amazon ECR (registre prive natif d'ECS) et en activant le scan on push, chaque image poussee est automatiquement analysee pour les CVE, y compris les nouvelles. C'est le changement minimal, sans migrer vers EKS ni batir un pipeline S3/Lambda/Inspector.

question: A company uses an AWS Batch job to run its end-of-day sales process. The company needs a serverless solution that will invoke a third-party reporting application when the AWS Batch job is successful. The reporting application has an HTTP API interface that uses username and password authentication. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Configure an Amazon EventBridge rule to match incoming AWS Batch job SUCCEEDED events. Configure the third-party API as an EventBridge API destination with a username and password. Set the API destination as the EventBridge rule target.
options.B: Configure Amazon EventBridge Scheduler to match incoming AWS Batch job SUCCEEDED events. Configure an AWS Lambda function to invoke the third-party API by using a username and password. Set the Lambda function as the EventBridge rule target.
options.C: Configure an AWS Batch job to publish job SUCCEEDED events to an Amazon API Gateway REST API. Configure an HTTP proxy integration on the API Gateway REST API to invoke the third-party API by using a username and password.
options.D: Configure an AWS Batch job to publish job SUCCEEDED events to an Amazon API Gateway REST API. Configure a proxy integration on the API Gateway REST API to an AWS Lambda function. Configure the Lambda function to invoke the third-party API by using a username and password.

declencheurs: invoke third-party HTTP API with username/password
radar.signal: Reagir a un evenement Batch et appeler une API HTTP authentifiee, sans code -> regle EventBridge + EventBridge API destination (username/password)

pieges.B: EventBridge Scheduler declenche sur horaire, pas sur des evenements ; ajouter une Lambda = plus de code
pieges.C: Batch ne 'publie' pas d'evenements vers une REST API Gateway ainsi
pieges.D: API Gateway + Lambda = chaine custom superflue face aux API destinations

explication: Une regle Amazon EventBridge filtre les evenements AWS Batch 'SUCCEEDED' et cible une EventBridge API destination configuree avec l'API tierce et une authentification username/password. C'est entierement serverless et sans code custom, contrairement aux options avec Lambda ou API Gateway.

question: A company is deploying an application in three AWS Regions using an Application Load Balancer. Amazon Route 53 will be used to distribute traffic between these Regions. Which Route 53 configuration should a solutions architect use to provide the MOST high-performing experience?

options.A: Create an A record with a latency policy.
options.B: Create an A record with a geolocation policy.
options.C: Create a CNAME record with a failover policy.
options.D: Create a CNAME record with a geoproximity policy.

radar.signal: Diriger vers la Region la plus rapide -> A record avec latency routing policy

pieges.B: La geolocation route par pays, pas selon la latence reelle
pieges.C: Failover est pour la reprise, pas la performance ; et un alias vers un ALB se fait via un A record
pieges.D: Geoproximity optimise la distance geographique, pas forcement la latence mesuree

explication: Une latency routing policy (A record alias vers chaque ALB) dirige chaque utilisateur vers la Region offrant la latence la plus faible, ce qui maximise la performance. La geolocation/geoproximity raisonnent en pays/distance, pas en latence mesuree.

question: A company has a web application that includes an embedded NoSQL database. The application runs on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The instances run in an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group in a single Availability Zone. A recent increase in traffic requires the application to be highly available and for the database to be eventually consistent. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.A: Replace the ALB with a Network Load Balancer. Maintain the embedded NoSQL database with its replication service on the EC2 instances.
options.B: Replace the ALB with a Network Load Balancer. Migrate the embedded NoSQL database to Amazon DynamoDB by using AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS).
options.C: Modify the Auto Scaling group to use EC2 instances across three Availability Zones. Maintain the embedded NoSQL database with its replication service on the EC2 instances.
options.D: Modify the Auto Scaling group to use EC2 instances across three Availability Zones. Migrate the embedded NoSQL database to Amazon DynamoDB by using AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS).

declencheurs: embedded NoSQL DB on EC2 with its own replication
radar.signal: Rendre l'ensemble HA sans reecrire/migrer la base -> Auto Scaling group sur trois AZ, en gardant la base NoSQL embarquee et son service de replication

pieges.A: Remplacer l'ALB par un NLB n'apporte pas la haute disponibilite multi-AZ de la base
pieges.B: Migrer vers DynamoDB via DMS = beaucoup plus d'effort
pieges.D: Migrer vers DynamoDB (D) ajoute aussi un effort important de migration

explication: En etendant l'Auto Scaling group sur trois Availability Zones tout en conservant la base NoSQL embarquee et son propre service de replication (coherence a terme), on obtient la haute disponibilite avec le moins d'effort. Migrer vers DynamoDB via DMS imposerait bien plus de changements.

question: A company has an application that places hundreds of .csv files into an Amazon S3 bucket every hour. The files are 1 GB in size. Each time a file is uploaded, the company needs to convert the file to Apache Parquet format and place the output file into an S3 bucket. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.A: Create an AWS Lambda function to download the .csv files, convert the files to Parquet format, and place the output files in an S3 bucket. Invoke the Lambda function for each S3 PUT event.
options.B: Create an Apache Spark job to read the .csv files, convert the files to Parquet format, and place the output files in an S3 bucket. Create an AWS Lambda function for each S3 PUT event to invoke the Spark job.
options.C: Create an AWS Glue table and an AWS Glue crawler for the S3 bucket where the application places the .csv files. Schedule an AWS Lambda function to periodically use Amazon Athena to query the AWS Glue table, convert the query results into Parquet format, and place the output files into an S3 bucket.
options.D: Create an AWS Glue extract, transform, and load (ETL) job to convert the .csv files to Parquet format and place the output files into an S3 bucket. Create an AWS Lambda function for each S3 PUT event to invoke the ETL job.

declencheurs: convert to Parquet on each upload
radar.signal: Conversion CSV->Parquet declenchee a chaque depot, sans infra -> Lambda invoquee sur chaque evenement S3 PUT

pieges.B: Un job Spark declenche par Lambda = infrastructure Spark a gerer
pieges.C: Glue crawler + Athena periodique = plus complexe et pas par fichier
pieges.D: Un job Glue ETL invoque a chaque PUT = plus lourd qu'une simple Lambda

explication: Une fonction Lambda declenchee par chaque evenement S3 PUT telecharge le CSV, le convertit en Parquet et depose la sortie dans S3, sans serveur ni cluster a gerer. C'est l'option au plus faible overhead face aux jobs Spark ou Glue a orchestrer.

question: A company is implementing new data retention policies for all databases that run on Amazon RDS DB instances. The company must retain daily backups for a minimum period of 2 years. The backups must be consistent and restorable. Which solution should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?

options.A: Create a backup vault in AWS Backup to retain RDS backups. Create a new backup plan with a daily schedule and an expiration period of 2 years after creation. Assign the RDS DB instances to the backup plan.
options.B: Configure a backup window for the RDS DB instances for daily snapshots. Assign a snapshot retention policy of 2 years to each RDS DB instance. Use Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager (Amazon DLM) to schedule snapshot deletions.
options.C: Configure database transaction logs to be automatically backed up to Amazon CloudWatch Logs with an expiration period of 2 years.
options.D: Configure an AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) replication task. Deploy a replication instance, and configure a change data capture (CDC) task to stream database changes to Amazon S3 as the target. Configure S3 Lifecycle policies to delete the snapshots after 2 years.

radar.signal: Sauvegardes RDS coherentes conservees 2 ans, managees -> AWS Backup (vault + plan quotidien, expiration 2 ans)

pieges.B: Une retention de snapshots de 2 ans + DLM (qui ne gere pas RDS) est bancale
pieges.C: Les transaction logs vers CloudWatch Logs ne sont pas des backups restaurables
pieges.D: DMS + CDC vers S3 n'est pas une sauvegarde coherente et restaurable de la base

explication: AWS Backup gere des sauvegardes RDS coherentes et restaurables via un backup plan quotidien avec une retention (expiration) de 2 ans, stockees dans un backup vault. DLM ne gere pas RDS, les logs CloudWatch ne sont pas restaurables comme une base, et DMS n'est pas un outil de sauvegarde.

question: A company maintains a searchable repository of items on its website. The data is stored in an Amazon RDS for MySQL database table that contains more than 10 million rows. The database has 2 TB of General Purpose SSD storage. There are millions of updates against this data every day through the company's website. The company has noticed that some insert operations are taking 10 seconds or longer. The company has determined that the database storage performance is the problem. Which solution addresses this performance issue?

options.A: Change the storage type to Provisioned IOPS SSD.
options.B: Change the DB instance to a memory optimized instance class.
options.C: Change the DB instance to a burstable performance instance class.
options.D: Enable Multi-AZ RDS read replicas with MySQL native asynchronous replication.

declencheurs: RDS MySQL, millions of daily updates
radar.signal: Probleme d'IOPS de stockage sous forte charge d'ecriture -> passer au stockage Provisioned IOPS SSD

pieges.B: Une instance memory optimized n'adresse pas un goulot d'IOPS de stockage
pieges.C: Une instance burstable est encore moins performante en I/O soutenues
pieges.D: Des read replicas soulagent les lectures, pas la lenteur des inserts (ecritures)

explication: Le probleme identifie est la performance du stockage sous une charge d'ecritures intense. Le stockage Provisioned IOPS SSD (io1/io2) garantit des IOPS eleves et constants, resolvant la lenteur des inserts. Changer la classe d'instance ou ajouter des read replicas ne corrige pas un goulot d'IOPS d'ecriture.

question: A company has thousands of edge devices that collectively generate 1 TB of status alerts each day. Each alert is approximately 2 KB in size. A solutions architect needs to implement a solution to ingest and store the alerts for future analysis. The company wants a highly available solution. However, the company needs to minimize costs and does not want to manage additional infrastructure. Additionally, the company wants to keep 14 days of data available for immediate analysis and archive any data older than 14 days. What is the MOST operationally efficient solution that meets these requirements?

options.A: Create an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream to ingest the alerts. Configure the Kinesis Data Firehose stream to deliver the alerts to an Amazon S3 bucket. Set up an S3 Lifecycle configuration to transition data to Amazon S3 Glacier after 14 days.
options.B: Launch Amazon EC2 instances across two Availability Zones and place them behind an Elastic Load Balancer to ingest the alerts. Create a script on the EC2 instances that will store the alerts in an Amazon S3 bucket. Set up an S3 Lifecycle configuration to transition data to Amazon S3 Glacier after 14 days.
options.C: Create an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream to ingest the alerts. Configure the Kinesis Data Firehose stream to deliver the alerts to an Amazon OpenSearch Service (Amazon Elasticsearch Service) cluster. Set up the Amazon OpenSearch Service (Amazon Elasticsearch Service) cluster to take manual snapshots every day and delete data from the cluster that is older than 14 days.
options.D: Create an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) standard queue to ingest the alerts, and set the message retention period to 14 days. Configure consumers to poll the SQS queue, check the age of the message, and analyze the message data as needed. If the message is 14 days old, the consumer should copy the message to an Amazon S3 bucket and delete the message from the SQS queue.

declencheurs: minimize cost, no infrastructure to manage
radar.signal: Ingestion manageee + archivage automatique -> Kinesis Data Firehose vers S3 + Lifecycle vers Glacier apres 14 jours

pieges.B: EC2 + ELB + script = infrastructure a gerer
pieges.C: Un cluster OpenSearch + snapshots manuels = plus d'operations et de cout
pieges.D: SQS + consommateurs qui gerent l'age des messages = logique custom lourde

explication: Kinesis Data Firehose ingere les alertes de facon manageee et hautement disponible, sans serveur, et les depose dans S3. Une Lifecycle policy bascule les donnees vers S3 Glacier apres 14 jours pour l'archivage. C'est l'option la plus efficace, sans cluster OpenSearch ni EC2 a exploiter.

question: A company hosts an application on Amazon EC2 On-Demand Instances in an Auto Scaling group. Application peak hours occur at the same time each day. Application users report slow application performance at the start of peak hours. The application performs normally 23 hours after peak hours begin. The company wants to ensure that the application works properly at the start of peak hours. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Configure an Application Load Balancer to distribute traffic properly to the instances.
options.B: Configure a dynamic scaling policy for the Auto Scaling group to launch new instances based on memory utilization.
options.C: Configure a dynamic scaling policy for the Auto Scaling group to launch new instances based on CPU utilization.
options.D: Configure a scheduled scaling policy for the Auto Scaling group to launch new instances before peak hours.

declencheurs: peak hours same time each day
ensure ready at start of peak
radar.signal: Pic previsible a heure fixe -> scheduled scaling qui lance les instances AVANT le debut du pic

pieges.A: Un ALB repartit le trafic mais ne provisionne pas la capacite a l'avance
pieges.B: Le dynamic scaling sur la memoire reagit apres coup (lenteur au demarrage du pic)
pieges.C: Le dynamic scaling sur le CPU reagit aussi trop tard au debut du pic

explication: La lenteur survient car le scaling reactif prend du temps a rattraper le pic. Comme le pic est previsible et quotidien, une scheduled scaling policy provisionne les instances juste avant l'heure de pointe, garantissant la capacite des le debut du pic.

question: A company runs applications on AWS that connect to the company's Amazon RDS database. The applications scale on weekends and at peak times of the year. The company wants to scale the database more effectively for its applications that connect to the database. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.A: Use Amazon DynamoDB with connection pooling with a target group configuration for the database. Change the applications to use the DynamoDB endpoint.
options.B: Use Amazon RDS Proxy with a target group for the database. Change the applications to use the RDS Proxy endpoint.
options.C: Use a custom proxy that runs on Amazon EC2 as an intermediary to the database. Change the applications to use the custom proxy endpoint.
options.D: Use an AWS Lambda function to provide connection pooling with a target group configuration for the database. Change the applications to use the Lambda function.

radar.signal: Gerer efficacement les connexions a une base qui scale -> Amazon RDS Proxy (pooling de connexions manage)

pieges.A: DynamoDB n'est pas un 'pool de connexions' pour RDS ; migration inadaptee
pieges.C: Un proxy custom sur EC2 = infrastructure a gerer
pieges.D: Une Lambda de pooling custom = solution a developper et maintenir

explication: Amazon RDS Proxy mutualise et reutilise les connexions a la base, ce qui absorbe les montees en charge (week-ends, pics) sans epuiser les connexions, en tant que service manage. Les applications pointent vers l'endpoint RDS Proxy. Un proxy custom sur EC2 ou une Lambda demanderaient bien plus d'operations.

question: A company web application that is hosted in the AWS Cloud recently increased in popularity. The web application currently exists on a single Amazon EC2 instance in a single public subnet. The web application has not been able to meet the demand of the increased web traffic. The company needs a solution that will provide high availability and scalability to meet the increased user demand without rewriting the web application. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.A: Replace the EC2 instance with a larger compute optimized instance.
options.B: Configure Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling with multiple Availability Zones in private subnets.
options.C: Configure a NAT gateway in a public subnet to handle web requests.
options.D: Replace the EC2 instance with a larger memory optimized instance.
options.E: Configure an Application Load Balancer in a public subnet to distribute web traffic.

declencheurs: single EC2 in a public subnet
radar.signal: Rendre l'app HA et scalable sans la reecrire -> EC2 Auto Scaling multi-AZ en subnets prives (B) + Application Load Balancer en subnet public (E)

pieges.A: Une instance plus grosse (scale-up) ne fournit ni HA ni scalabilite horizontale
pieges.C: Un NAT gateway gere la sortie Internet, il ne repartit pas le trafic web entrant
pieges.D: Une instance memory optimized plus grosse ne resout ni HA ni scaling

explication: Un Application Load Balancer dans un subnet public (E) repartit le trafic vers un Auto Scaling group d'instances reparties sur plusieurs AZ en subnets prives (B). On obtient haute disponibilite et scalabilite horizontale sans reecrire l'application. Agrandir l'instance (A/D) ne fait que du scale-up vertical sans redondance.

question: A company has AWS Lambda functions that use environment variables. The company does not want its developers to see environment variables in plaintext. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Deploy code to Amazon EC2 instances instead of using Lambda functions.
options.B: Configure SSL encryption on the Lambda functions to use AWS CloudHSM to store and encrypt the environment variables.
options.C: Create a certificate in AWS Certificate Manager (ACM). Configure the Lambda functions to use the certificate to encrypt the environment variables.
options.D: Create an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key. Enable encryption helpers on the Lambda functions to use the KMS key to store and encrypt the environment variables.

declencheurs: developers must not see them in plaintext
radar.signal: Chiffrer les variables d'environnement Lambda -> cle AWS KMS + encryption helpers de Lambda

pieges.A: Deployer sur EC2 ne repond pas au besoin (et abandonne Lambda)
pieges.B: CloudHSM + SSL n'est pas le mecanisme de chiffrement des variables d'environnement Lambda
pieges.C: Un certificat ACM chiffre du TLS, pas des variables d'environnement

explication: Lambda propose des encryption helpers qui chiffrent les variables d'environnement avec une cle KMS : elles ne sont plus visibles en clair dans la console pour les developpeurs sans permission de dechiffrement. ACM (TLS) et CloudHSM/SSL ne sont pas concus pour cela.

question: A company applications use Apache Hadoop and Apache Spark to process data on premises. The existing infrastructure is not scalable and is complex to manage. A solutions architect must design a scalable solution that reduces operational complexity. The solution must keep the data processing on premises. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Use AWS Site-to-Site VPN to access the on-premises Hadoop Distributed File System (HDFS) data and application. Use an Amazon EMR cluster to process the data.
options.B: Use AWS DataSync to connect to the on-premises Hadoop Distributed File System (HDFS) cluster. Create an Amazon EMR cluster to process the data.
options.C: Migrate the Apache Hadoop application and the Apache Spark application to Amazon EMR clusters on AWS Outposts. Use the EMR clusters to process the data.
options.D: Use an AWS Snowball device to migrate the data to an Amazon S3 bucket. Create an Amazon EMR cluster to process the data.

radar.signal: Traitement Hadoop/Spark manage tout en restant on-prem -> Amazon EMR sur AWS Outposts

pieges.A: EMR dans le cloud + VPN traite les donnees dans AWS, pas on-prem
pieges.B: DataSync + EMR cloud deplace/traite dans AWS, pas on-prem
pieges.D: Snowball + EMR cloud migre les donnees vers AWS (traitement dans le cloud)

explication: AWS Outposts apporte l'infrastructure et les services AWS (dont Amazon EMR) dans le data center de l'entreprise. Migrer Hadoop/Spark vers des clusters EMR sur Outposts rend le traitement scalable et manage tout en gardant les donnees et le calcul sur site, ce que les options cloud+VPN/Snowball ne font pas.

question: A company is migrating a large amount of data from on-premises storage to AWS. Windows, Mac, and Linux based Amazon EC2 instances in the same AWS Region will access the data by using SMB and NFS storage protocols. The company will access a portion of the data routinely. The company will access the remaining data infrequently. The company needs to design a solution to host the data. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.A: Create an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) volume that uses EFS Intelligent-Tiering. Use AWS DataSync to migrate the data to the EFS volume.
options.B: Create an Amazon FSx for ONTAP instance. Create an FSx for ONTAP file system with a root volume that uses the auto tiering policy. Migrate the data to the FSx for ONTAP volume.
options.C: Create an Amazon S3 bucket that uses S3 Intelligent-Tiering. Migrate the data to the S3 bucket by using an AWS Storage Gateway Amazon S3 File Gateway.
options.D: Create an Amazon FSx for OpenZFS file system. Migrate the data to the new volume.

radar.signal: Multi-protocole SMB/NFS + tiering automatique frequent/rare -> Amazon FSx for ONTAP avec auto tiering policy

pieges.A: EFS ne supporte pas SMB (Windows)
pieges.C: S3 File Gateway n'expose pas nativement NFS+SMB multi-OS comme un systeme de fichiers unique
pieges.D: FSx for OpenZFS ne fait pas le multi-protocole SMB+NFS avec auto tiering comme ONTAP

explication: Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP expose a la fois SMB et NFS (donc Windows, Mac et Linux) et sa politique d'auto tiering bascule automatiquement les donnees peu consultees vers un tier moins cher. C'est la solution multi-protocole avec le moins d'overhead ; EFS (NFS uniquement) et OpenZFS ne conviennent pas.

question: A solutions architect needs to copy files from an Amazon S3 bucket to an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system and another S3 bucket. The files must be copied continuously. New files are added to the original S3 bucket consistently. The copied files should be overwritten if the source file changes. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.A: Create an AWS DataSync location for both the destination S3 bucket and the EFS file system. Create a task for the destination S3 bucket and the EFS file system. Set the transfer mode to transfer only data that has changed.
options.B: Create an AWS Lambda function. Mount the file system to the function. Set up an S3 event notification to invoke the function when files are created and changed in Amazon S3. Configure the function to copy files to the file system and the destination S3 bucket.
options.C: Create an AWS DataSync location for both the destination S3 bucket and the EFS file system. Create a task for the destination S3 bucket and the EFS file system. Set the transfer mode to transfer all data.
options.D: Launch an Amazon EC2 instance in the same VPC as the file system. Mount the file system. Create a script to routinely synchronize all objects that changed in the origin S3 bucket to the destination S3 bucket and the mounted file system.

declencheurs: copy S3 -> EFS and another S3 bucket
radar.signal: Copie continue geree avec detection des changements -> AWS DataSync (locations S3/EFS + tache, transfert des donnees modifiees seulement)

pieges.B: Une Lambda montant EFS + evenements S3 = code a ecrire et maintenir
pieges.C: Transferer TOUTES les donnees a chaque fois est inefficace
pieges.D: Un EC2 + script de synchro = infrastructure et code a gerer

explication: AWS DataSync copie de facon manageee entre S3 et EFS (et vers un autre bucket) et, en mode 'transfert des seules donnees modifiees', ne recopie que ce qui a change en ecrasant les fichiers mis a jour. C'est le moins d'overhead, sans Lambda ni EC2 a maintenir.

question: A company uses Amazon EC2 instances and stores data on Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes. The company must ensure that all data is encrypted at rest by using AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS). The company must be able to control rotation of the encryption keys. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.A: Create a customer managed key. Use the key to encrypt the EBS volumes.
options.B: Use an AWS managed key to encrypt the EBS volumes. Use the key to configure automatic key rotation.
options.C: Create an external KMS key with imported key material. Use the key to encrypt the EBS volumes.
options.D: Use an AWS owned key to encrypt the EBS volumes.

declencheurs: encrypt EBS at rest with KMS
radar.signal: Chiffrement EBS avec controle de la rotation -> customer managed key KMS

pieges.B: Une AWS managed key ne laisse pas controler la rotation
pieges.C: Une cle avec key material importe ne beneficie pas de la rotation automatique et ajoute de la gestion
pieges.D: Une AWS owned key n'est ni visible ni controlable par le client

explication: Une customer managed key KMS permet de chiffrer les volumes EBS tout en donnant le controle de la rotation (activation de la rotation automatique annuelle ou rotation a la demande). Les cles AWS managed/owned ne laissent pas ce controle, et une cle importee ajoute de l'administration sans rotation automatique.

question: A company regularly uploads GB-sized files to Amazon S3. After the company uploads the files, the company uses a fleet of Amazon EC2 Spot Instances to transcode the file format. The company needs to scale throughput when the company uploads data from the on-premises data center to Amazon S3 and when the company downloads data from Amazon S3 to the EC2 instances. Which solutions will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.A: Use the S3 bucket access point instead of accessing the S3 bucket directly.
options.B: Upload the files into multiple S3 buckets.
options.C: Use S3 multipart uploads.
options.D: Fetch multiple byte-ranges of an object in parallel.
options.E: Add a random prefix to each object when uploading the files.

declencheurs: scale throughput on upload to S3 and download from S3
radar.signal: Augmenter le debit vers/depuis S3 -> multipart uploads a l'envoi (C) + fetch de plusieurs byte-ranges en parallele au telechargement (D)

pieges.A: Un S3 access point ne change pas le debit de transfert
pieges.B: Uploader dans plusieurs buckets ne parallelise pas un meme gros fichier
pieges.E: Le prefixe aleatoire n'est plus necessaire (S3 scale par prefixe automatiquement) et ne change pas le debit d'un objet

explication: Pour de gros fichiers, les multipart uploads envoient plusieurs parties en parallele (montee en debit a l'upload), et le fetch de plusieurs byte-ranges en parallele accelere le telechargement. Ce sont les deux mecanismes natifs de parallelisation S3 pour scaler le debit.

question: A solutions architect is designing a shared storage solution for a web application that is deployed across multiple Availability Zones. The web application runs on Amazon EC2 instances that are in an Auto Scaling group. The company plans to make frequent changes to the content. The solution must have strong consistency in returning the new content as soon as the changes occur. Which solutions meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.A: Use AWS Storage Gateway Volume Gateway Internet Small Computer Systems Interface (iSCSI) block storage that is mounted to the individual EC2 instances.
options.B: Create an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. Mount the EFS file system on the individual EC2 instances.
options.C: Create a shared Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume. Mount the EBS volume on the individual EC2 instances.
options.D: Use AWS DataSync to perform continuous synchronization of data between EC2 hosts in the Auto Scaling group.
options.E: Create an Amazon S3 bucket to store the web content. Set the metadata for the Cache-Control header to no-cache. Use Amazon CloudFront to deliver the content.

radar.signal: Stockage partage a coherence forte immediate -> Amazon EFS monte sur les instances (B) ou S3 + Cache-Control no-cache + CloudFront (E)

pieges.A: Un volume iSCSI n'est pas un partage multi-instances/multi-AZ coherent
pieges.C: Un volume EBS ne se partage pas entre plusieurs instances/AZ
pieges.D: DataSync fait de la synchro periodique, pas une coherence forte immediate

explication: Amazon EFS fournit un systeme de fichiers partage multi-AZ a coherence forte, monte par toutes les instances (B). Alternativement, S3 (coherence forte en lecture-apres-ecriture) avec Cache-Control no-cache et CloudFront sert immediatement le nouveau contenu (E). EBS/iSCSI ne se partagent pas, et DataSync n'est que periodique.

question: A company is migrating five on-premises applications to VPCs in the AWS Cloud. Each application is currently deployed in isolated virtual networks on premises and should be deployed similarly in the AWS Cloud. The applications need to reach a shared services VPC. All the applications must be able to communicate with each other. If the migration is successful, the company will repeat the migration process for more than 100 applications. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST administrative overhead?

options.A: Deploy software VPN tunnels between the application VPCs and the shared services VPC. Add routes between the application VPCs in their subnets to the shared services VPC.
options.B: Deploy VPC peering connections between the application VPCs and the shared services VPC. Add routes between the application VPCs in their subnets to the shared services VPC through the peering connection.
options.C: Deploy an AWS Direct Connect connection between the application VPCs and the shared services VPC. Add routes from the application VPCs in their subnets to the shared services VPC and the applications VPCs. Add routes from the shared services VPC subnets to the applications VPCs.
options.D: Deploy a transit gateway with associations between the transit gateway and the application VPCs and the shared services VPC. Add routes between the application VPCs in their subnets and the application VPCs to the shared services VPC through the transit gateway.

radar.signal: Interconnecter de nombreux VPC de facon scalable -> AWS Transit Gateway avec attachments

pieges.A: Des tunnels VPN logiciels entre VPC = complexe et non scalable
pieges.B: Le VPC peering ne scale pas (maillage complet ingerable a 100+ VPC)
pieges.C: Direct Connect relie de l'on-prem, il n'interconnecte pas des VPC entre eux

explication: AWS Transit Gateway agit comme un hub central : chaque VPC (applications et shared services) s'y rattache par un attachment, et le routage permet a tous de communiquer. C'est la solution qui scale a plus de 100 VPC avec le moins d'administration, la ou le peering imposerait un maillage ingerable.

question: A company wants to use Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) to run its on-premises application in a hybrid environment. The application currently runs on containers on premises. The company needs a single container solution that can scale in an on-premises, hybrid, or cloud environment. The company must run new application containers in the AWS Cloud and must use a load balancer for HTTP traffic. Which combination of actions will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.A: Set up an ECS cluster that uses the AWS Fargate launch type for the cloud application containers. Use an Amazon ECS Anywhere external launch type for the on-premises application containers.
options.B: Set up an Application Load Balancer for cloud ECS services.
options.C: Set up a Network Load Balancer for cloud ECS services.
options.D: Set up an ECS cluster that uses the AWS Fargate launch type. Use Fargate for the cloud application containers and the on-premises application containers.
options.E: Set up an ECS cluster that uses the Amazon EC2 launch type for the cloud application containers. Use Amazon ECS Anywhere with an AWS Fargate launch type for the on-premises application containers.

radar.signal: ECS uniforme cloud + on-prem + HTTP -> cluster ECS Fargate (cloud) et ECS Anywhere external (on-prem) (A) + Application Load Balancer pour le HTTP (B)

pieges.C: Un Network Load Balancer n'est pas fait pour le trafic HTTP applicatif (L7)
pieges.D: Fargate ne s'execute pas on-premises (impossible pour les conteneurs sur site)
pieges.E: ECS Anywhere n'utilise pas un 'Fargate launch type' on-prem (c'est le external launch type)

explication: ECS unifie la gestion : Fargate execute les conteneurs dans le cloud et ECS Anywhere (external launch type) gere ceux qui restent on-premises (A). Pour le trafic HTTP, un Application Load Balancer (niveau 7) est adapte (B). Fargate ne tourne pas on-prem, et le NLB (L4) ne convient pas au HTTP applicatif.

question: A company is preparing to store confidential data in Amazon S3. For compliance reasons, the data must be encrypted at rest. Encryption key usage must be logged for auditing purposes. Keys must be rotated every year. Which solution meets these requirements and is the MOST operationally efficient?

options.A: Server-side encryption with customer-provided keys (SSE-C).
options.B: Server-side encryption with Amazon S3 managed keys (SSE-S3).
options.C: Server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS) with manual rotation.
options.D: Server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS) with automatic rotation.

radar.signal: Chiffrement au repos + audit d'usage des cles + rotation annuelle automatique -> SSE-KMS avec rotation automatique

pieges.A: SSE-C impose de gerer et fournir soi-meme les cles (pas d'audit/rotation KMS)
pieges.B: SSE-S3 ne journalise pas l'usage des cles ni ne permet une rotation configurable
pieges.C: SSE-KMS avec rotation manuelle ajoute une operation annuelle inutile

explication: SSE-KMS chiffre au repos, journalise l'usage des cles dans CloudTrail (audit) et prend en charge la rotation automatique annuelle des cles. Avec la rotation automatique activee, c'est la solution la plus efficace : SSE-S3 n'audite pas l'usage, SSE-C impose de gerer les cles, et la rotation manuelle ajoute du travail.

question: A bicycle sharing company is developing a multi-tier architecture to track the location of its bicycles during peak operating hours. The company wants to use these data points in its existing analytics platform. A solutions architect must determine the most viable multi-tier option to support this architecture. The data points must be accessible from the REST API. Which action meets these requirements for storing and retrieving location data?

options.A: Use Amazon Athena with Amazon S3.
options.B: Use Amazon API Gateway with AWS Lambda.
options.C: Use Amazon QuickSight with Amazon Redshift.
options.D: Use Amazon API Gateway with Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics.

declencheurs: data points accessible from a REST API
radar.signal: Exposer/stocker des points de localisation via une REST API serverless -> Amazon API Gateway + AWS Lambda

pieges.A: Athena + S3 sert a l'analyse ad hoc, pas a une API de stockage/recuperation temps reel
pieges.C: QuickSight + Redshift = visualisation/analytique, pas une REST API
pieges.D: Kinesis Data Analytics traite un flux, il n'expose pas une REST API de recuperation

explication: Amazon API Gateway expose la REST API demandee et AWS Lambda traite le stockage et la recuperation des points de localisation (par ex. vers une base), le tout serverless. Athena/QuickSight/Redshift servent a l'analyse et Kinesis Data Analytics au flux, pas a exposer une API de recuperation de donnees.

question: An ecommerce company is running a multi-tier application on AWS. The front-end and backend tiers both run on Amazon EC2, and the database runs on Amazon RDS for MySQL. The backend tier communicates with the RDS instance. There are frequent calls to return identical datasets from the database that are causing performance slowdowns. Which action should be taken to improve the performance of the backend?

options.A: Implement Amazon SNS to store the database calls.
options.B: Implement Amazon ElastiCache to cache the large datasets.
options.C: Implement an RDS for MySQL read replica to cache database calls.
options.D: Implement Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to stream the calls to the database.

radar.signal: Servir des jeux de donnees identiques et frequents sans retaper la base -> Amazon ElastiCache

pieges.A: SNS est un service de notification, il ne cache pas des donnees
pieges.C: Un read replica traite plus de lectures mais ne cache pas les resultats identiques (moins efficace qu'un cache)
pieges.D: Kinesis Data Firehose streame des donnees, il n'accelere pas des lectures repetees

explication: Comme les memes jeux de donnees sont demandes de facon repetee, un cache en memoire Amazon ElastiCache sert ces resultats sans solliciter la base a chaque appel, eliminant le goulot. Un read replica repartirait les lectures mais sans la rapidite ni l'economie d'un cache pour des donnees identiques.

question: A new employee has joined a company as a deployment engineer. The deployment engineer will be using AWS CloudFormation templates to create multiple AWS resources. A solutions architect wants the deployment engineer to perform job activities while following the principle of least privilege. Which combination of actions should the solutions architect take to accomplish this goal? (Choose two.)

options.A: Have the deployment engineer use AWS account root user credentials for performing AWS CloudFormation stack operations.
options.B: Create a new IAM user for the deployment engineer and add the IAM user to a group that has the PowerUsers IAM policy attached.
options.C: Create a new IAM user for the deployment engineer and add the IAM user to a group that has the AdministratorAccess IAM policy attached.
options.D: Create a new IAM user for the deployment engineer and add the IAM user to a group that has an IAM policy that allows AWS CloudFormation actions only.
options.E: Create an IAM role for the deployment engineer to explicitly define the permissions specific to the AWS CloudFormation stack and launch stacks using that IAM role.

radar.signal: Moindre privilege pour du CloudFormation -> IAM user dans un groupe avec une policy limitee aux actions CloudFormation (D) + role IAM aux permissions specifiques pour lancer les stacks (E)

pieges.A: Utiliser le root est l'oppose du moindre privilege
pieges.B: PowerUsers accorde bien trop de permissions
pieges.C: AdministratorAccess = acces complet, contraire au moindre privilege

explication: Le moindre privilege consiste a donner a l'ingenieur un IAM user dans un groupe autorisant uniquement les actions CloudFormation (D), et a definir un role IAM aux permissions precises pour les ressources des stacks, que l'on utilise pour lancer les stacks (E). Root, PowerUsers ou AdministratorAccess accordent trop de droits.

question: A company uses Amazon API Gateway to run a private gateway with two REST APIs in the same VPC. The BuyStock RESTful web service calls the CheckFunds RESTful web service to ensure that enough funds are available before a stock can be purchased. The company has noticed in the VPC flow logs that the BuyStock RESTful web service calls the CheckFunds RESTful web service over the internet instead of through the VPC. A solutions architect must implement a solution so that the APIs communicate through the VPC. Which solution will meet these requirements with the FEWEST changes to the code?

options.A: Add an X-API-Key header in the HTTP header for authorization.
options.B: Use an interface endpoint.
options.C: Use a gateway endpoint.
options.D: Add an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue between the two REST APIs.

declencheurs: private API Gateway, two REST APIs same VPC
calls go over the internet instead of the VPC
radar.signal: Faire communiquer des API privees via le VPC -> interface endpoint (PrivateLink) pour API Gateway

pieges.A: Un header X-API-Key gere l'autorisation, pas le chemin reseau
pieges.C: Un gateway endpoint ne sert qu'a S3/DynamoDB, pas a API Gateway
pieges.D: Ajouter une file SQS change l'architecture et le code

explication: Un interface endpoint (AWS PrivateLink) pour API Gateway permet aux appels de rester dans le VPC au lieu de sortir sur Internet, avec un minimum de changements de code. Les gateway endpoints ne concernent que S3/DynamoDB, et une file SQS modifierait l'architecture.

question: A company hosts a multiplayer gaming application on AWS. The company wants the application to read data with sub-millisecond latency and run one-time queries on historical data. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.A: Use Amazon RDS for data that is frequently accessed. Run a periodic custom script to export the data to an Amazon S3 bucket.
options.B: Store the data directly in an Amazon S3 bucket. Implement an S3 Lifecycle policy to move older data to S3 Glacier Deep Archive for long-term storage. Run one-time queries on the data in Amazon S3 by using Amazon Athena.
options.C: Use Amazon DynamoDB with DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) for data that is frequently accessed. Export the data to an Amazon S3 bucket by using DynamoDB table export. Run one-time queries on the data in Amazon S3 by using Amazon Athena.
options.D: Use Amazon DynamoDB for data that is frequently accessed. Turn on streaming to Amazon Kinesis Data Streams. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to read the data from Kinesis Data Streams. Store the records in an Amazon S3 bucket.

radar.signal: Lectures ultra rapides + requetes ad hoc sur l'historique -> DynamoDB + DAX (donnees chaudes) + export vers S3 + Athena pour les requetes ponctuelles

pieges.A: RDS + script d'export custom = plus d'operations et pas sub-milliseconde
pieges.B: S3 seul ne fournit pas des lectures sub-milliseconde
pieges.D: DynamoDB + Kinesis + Firehose = pipeline plus complexe pour de simples requetes ad hoc

explication: DynamoDB avec DAX fournit des lectures en memoire sub-milliseconde pour les donnees chaudes. L'export natif de la table vers S3, interroge par Amazon Athena, couvre les requetes ponctuelles sur l'historique, sans pipeline complexe (Kinesis) ni script custom (RDS).

question: A company is creating an application. The company stores data from tests of the application in multiple on-premises locations. The company needs to connect the on-premises locations to VPCs in an AWS Region in the AWS Cloud. The number of accounts and VPCs will increase during the next year. The network architecture must simplify the administration of new connections and must provide the ability to scale. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST administrative overhead?

options.A: Create a peering connection between the VPCs. Create a VPN connection between the VPCs and the on-premises locations.
options.B: Launch an Amazon EC2 instance. On the instance, include VPN software that uses a VPN connection to connect all VPCs and on-premises locations.
options.C: Create a transit gateway. Create VPC attachments for the VPC connections. Create VPN attachments for the on-premises connections.
options.D: Create an AWS Direct Connect connection between the on-premises locations and a central VPC. Connect the central VPC to other VPCs by using peering connections.

declencheurs: number of accounts and VPCs will grow
radar.signal: Interconnexion scalable on-prem + multi-VPC -> AWS Transit Gateway (VPC attachments + VPN attachments)

pieges.A: Peering + VPN par paire = maillage ingerable a mesure que ca grandit
pieges.B: Un EC2 avec logiciel VPN = point de defaillance et gestion manuelle
pieges.D: Direct Connect vers un VPC central + peering ne simplifie pas la croissance des connexions

explication: AWS Transit Gateway centralise la connectivite : des VPC attachments pour les VPC et des VPN attachments pour les sites on-prem. A mesure que les comptes et VPC se multiplient, il suffit d'ajouter des attachments, ce qui simplifie l'administration et scale, contrairement a un maillage de peering/VPN.

question: A company that uses AWS needs a solution to predict the resources needed for manufacturing processes each month. The solution must use historical values that are currently stored in an Amazon S3 bucket. The company has no machine learning (ML) experience and wants to use a managed service for the training and predictions. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.A: Deploy an Amazon SageMaker model. Create a SageMaker endpoint for inference.
options.B: Use Amazon SageMaker to train a model by using the historical data in the S3 bucket.
options.C: Configure an AWS Lambda function with a function URL that uses Amazon SageMaker endpoints to create predictions based on the inputs.
options.D: Configure an AWS Lambda function with a function URL that uses an Amazon Forecast predictor to create a prediction based on the inputs.
options.E: Train an Amazon Forecast predictor by using the historical data in the S3 bucket.

declencheurs: managed service for training and predictions
radar.signal: Prevision sans expertise ML, manageee -> entrainer un predictor Amazon Forecast sur les donnees S3 (E) + Lambda function URL utilisant ce predictor Forecast (D)

pieges.A: SageMaker exige des competences ML pour construire/deployer un modele
pieges.B: SageMaker demande aussi une expertise ML (contraire a l'enonce)
pieges.C: Utiliser des endpoints SageMaker suppose un modele SageMaker (expertise ML)

explication: Amazon Forecast est un service de prevision manage qui ne demande pas d'expertise ML : on entraine un predictor a partir des donnees historiques dans S3 (E), puis une Lambda (function URL) l'appelle pour generer des previsions (D). SageMaker impliquerait de construire et gerer un modele, ce que la compagnie ne sait pas faire.

question: A company needs to provide its employees with secure access to confidential and sensitive files. The company wants to ensure that the files can be accessed only by authorized users. The files must be downloaded securely to the employees' devices. The files are stored in an on-premises Windows file server. However, due to an increase in remote usage, the file server is running out of capacity. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Migrate the file server to an Amazon EC2 instance in a public subnet. Configure the security group to limit inbound traffic to the employees' IP addresses.
options.B: Migrate the files to an Amazon FSx for Windows File Server file system. Integrate the Amazon FSx file system with the on-premises Active Directory. Configure AWS Client VPN.
options.C: Migrate the files to Amazon S3, and create a private VPC endpoint. Create a signed URL to allow download.
options.D: Migrate the files to Amazon S3, and create a public VPC endpoint. Allow employees to sign on with AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On).

declencheurs: on-prem Windows file server out of capacity
radar.signal: Migrer un partage Windows securise accessible a distance -> FSx for Windows File Server + integration Active Directory + AWS Client VPN

pieges.A: Un EC2 en subnet public expose le serveur de fichiers
pieges.C: S3 + signed URL change la maniere d'acceder aux fichiers (pas un partage Windows natif)
pieges.D: Un VPC endpoint public + SSO ne fournit pas un partage de fichiers Windows securise et prive

explication: Amazon FSx for Windows File Server remplace le serveur de fichiers a court de capacite, integre a l'Active Directory pour n'autoriser que les utilisateurs habilites (permissions NTFS). AWS Client VPN offre aux employes distants un acces prive et securise pour telecharger les fichiers, sans exposer le partage sur Internet.

question: A company application runs on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The instances run in an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones. On the first day of every month at midnight, the application becomes much slower when the month-end financial calculation batch runs. This causes the CPU utilization of the EC2 instances to immediately peak to 100%, which disrupts the application. What should a solutions architect recommend to ensure the application is able to handle the workload and avoid downtime?

options.A: Configure an Amazon CloudFront distribution in front of the ALB.
options.B: Configure an EC2 Auto Scaling simple scaling policy based on CPU utilization.
options.C: Configure an EC2 Auto Scaling scheduled scaling policy based on the monthly schedule.
options.D: Configure Amazon ElastiCache to remove some of the workload from the EC2 instances.

declencheurs: month-end batch at midnight first day of month
radar.signal: Pic previsible a date fixe (debut de mois) -> scheduled scaling policy calee sur le planning mensuel

pieges.A: CloudFront ne resout pas un pic CPU du batch backend
pieges.B: Le simple scaling sur CPU reagit apres coup (le pic est deja a 100%)
pieges.D: ElastiCache ne soulage pas un calcul batch CPU-intensif

explication: Le pic est previsible (minuit, premier jour du mois). Une scheduled scaling policy provisionne des instances supplementaires juste avant ce moment, evitant que le CPU sature a 100% et cause du downtime. Un scaling reactif au CPU (B) interviendrait trop tard.

question: A company has an online gaming application that has TCP and UDP multiplayer gaming capabilities. The company uses Amazon Route 53 to point the application traffic to multiple Network Load Balancers (NLBs) in different AWS Regions. The company needs to improve application performance and decrease latency for the online game in preparation for user growth. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Add an Amazon CloudFront distribution in front of the NLBs. Increase the Cache-Control max-age parameter.
options.B: Replace the NLBs with Application Load Balancers (ALBs). Configure Route 53 to use latency-based routing.
options.C: Add AWS Global Accelerator in front of the NLBs. Configure a Global Accelerator endpoint to use the correct listener ports.
options.D: Add an Amazon API Gateway endpoint behind the NLBs. Enable API caching. Override method caching for the different stages.

declencheurs: Route 53 to multiple NLBs in Regions
radar.signal: Accelerer du TCP/UDP multi-Region -> AWS Global Accelerator devant les NLB (ports d'ecoute corrects)

pieges.A: CloudFront (HTTP + cache) ne convient pas a du trafic de jeu TCP/UDP
pieges.B: Les ALB ne gerent pas l'UDP ; le latency routing DNS reste moins performant que Global Accelerator
pieges.D: API Gateway + cache ne s'applique pas a du trafic de jeu TCP/UDP

explication: AWS Global Accelerator place devant les Network Load Balancers achemine le trafic TCP et UDP via le backbone AWS depuis le point de presence le plus proche, reduisant la latence et ameliorant la performance a grande echelle. CloudFront et API Gateway sont pour le HTTP, et les ALB ne gerent pas l'UDP.

question: A company needs to integrate with a third-party data feed. The data feed sends a webhook to notify an external service when new data is ready for consumption. A developer wrote an AWS Lambda function to retrieve data when the company receives a webhook callback. The developer must make the Lambda function available for the third party to call. Which solution will meet these requirements with the MOST operational efficiency?

options.A: Create a function URL for the Lambda function. Provide the Lambda function URL to the third party for the webhook.
options.B: Deploy an Application Load Balancer (ALB) in front of the Lambda function. Provide the ALB URL to the third party for the webhook.
options.C: Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Attach the topic to the Lambda function. Provide the public hostname of the SNS topic to the third party for the webhook.
options.D: Create an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Attach the queue to the Lambda function. Provide the public hostname of the SQS queue to the third party for the webhook.

declencheurs: make Lambda callable by the third party
radar.signal: Exposer une Lambda a un webhook tiers simplement -> creer une function URL et la fournir au tiers

pieges.B: Un ALB devant la Lambda = infrastructure superflue pour un simple webhook
pieges.C: SNS n'expose pas un 'hostname public' a appeler par un webhook
pieges.D: SQS n'expose pas non plus un endpoint HTTP a appeler par un webhook

explication: Une function URL fournit a la fonction Lambda un endpoint HTTPS dedie que le tiers peut appeler directement depuis son webhook, sans infrastructure additionnelle. Un ALB serait superflu, et SNS/SQS n'exposent pas un endpoint HTTP appelable par un webhook.

question: A company needs a solution to enforce data encryption at rest on Amazon EC2 instances. The solution must automatically identify noncompliant resources and enforce compliance policies on findings. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST administrative overhead?

options.A: Use an IAM policy that allows users to create only encrypted Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes. Use AWS Config and AWS Systems Manager to automate the detection and remediation of unencrypted EBS volumes.
options.B: Use AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) to manage access to encrypted Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes. Use AWS Lambda and Amazon EventBridge to automate the detection and remediation of unencrypted EBS volumes.
options.C: Use Amazon Macie to detect unencrypted Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes. Use AWS Systems Manager Automation rules to automatically encrypt existing and new EBS volumes.
options.D: Use Amazon Inspector to detect unencrypted Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes. Use AWS Systems Manager Automation rules to automatically encrypt existing and new EBS volumes.

radar.signal: Prevenir + detecter + remedier le non-chiffrement EBS -> IAM policy n'autorisant que des volumes EBS chiffres + AWS Config + Systems Manager pour la remediation automatique

pieges.B: KMS gere les cles, il ne detecte pas les volumes non conformes
pieges.C: Macie analyse des donnees S3, pas le chiffrement des volumes EBS
pieges.D: Inspector scanne des vulnerabilites, il ne detecte pas des EBS non chiffres

explication: Une IAM policy qui n'autorise que la creation de volumes EBS chiffres previent la non-conformite a la source. AWS Config detecte les volumes non chiffres existants et declenche une remediation automatique via Systems Manager. Macie (S3) et Inspector (vulnerabilites) ne detectent pas le chiffrement des volumes EBS.

question: A company is migrating its multi-tier on-premises application to AWS. The application consists of a single-node MySQL database and a multi-node web tier. The company must minimize changes to the application during the migration. The company wants to improve application resiliency after the migration. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.A: Migrate the web tier to Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer.
options.B: Migrate the database to Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group behind a Network Load Balancer.
options.C: Migrate the database to an Amazon RDS Multi-AZ deployment.
options.D: Migrate the web tier to an AWS Lambda function.
options.E: Migrate the database to an Amazon DynamoDB table.

radar.signal: Ameliorer la resilience avec peu de changements -> web tier en Auto Scaling derriere un ALB (A) + base sur Amazon RDS Multi-AZ (C)

pieges.B: Mettre une base MySQL sur EC2 derriere un NLB n'est pas une base manageee resiliente
pieges.D: Passer le web tier en Lambda = reecriture importante
pieges.E: Migrer vers DynamoDB change le modele de donnees (contraire a 'minimize changes')

explication: On migre le web tier vers des EC2 en Auto Scaling derriere un Application Load Balancer (A) et la base MySQL vers Amazon RDS Multi-AZ (C), ce qui ameliore la resilience avec des changements minimes (RDS reste MySQL). Lambda ou DynamoDB imposeraient de reecrire l'application ou le modele de donnees.

question: A company is developing a new machine learning (ML) model solution on AWS. The models are developed as independent microservices that fetch approximately 1 GB of model data from Amazon S3 at startup and load the data into memory. Users access the models through an asynchronous API. Users can send a request or a batch of requests and specify where the results should be sent. The company provides models to hundreds of users. The usage patterns for the models are irregular. Some models could be unused for days or weeks. Other models could receive batches of thousands of requests at a time. Which design should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?

options.A: Direct the requests from the API to a Network Load Balancer (NLB). Deploy the models as AWS Lambda functions that are invoked by the NLB.
options.B: Direct the requests from the API to an Application Load Balancer (ALB). Deploy the models as Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) services that read from an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Use AWS App Mesh to scale the instances of the ECS cluster based on the SQS queue size.
options.C: Direct the requests from the API into an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Deploy the models as AWS Lambda functions that are invoked by SQS events. Use AWS Auto Scaling to increase the number of vCPUs for the Lambda functions based on the SQS queue size.
options.D: Direct the requests from the API into an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Deploy the models as Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) services that read from the queue. Enable AWS Auto Scaling on Amazon ECS for both the cluster and copies of the service based on the queue size.

declencheurs: ML microservices load 1 GB at startup
irregular usage (idle days or thousands of requests)
radar.signal: Traitement asynchrone elastique de modeles lourds -> requetes vers une file SQS + modeles en services ECS lisant la file + Auto Scaling ECS (cluster et service) selon la taille de la file

pieges.A: NLB + Lambda : charger 1 Go en memoire a chaque invocation est mal adapte a Lambda
pieges.B: App Mesh sert au maillage de services, pas au scaling selon une file SQS
pieges.C: On ne 'scale pas les vCPU d'une Lambda via Auto Scaling', et 1 Go en memoire convient mal a Lambda

explication: Une file SQS decouple l'API asynchrone du traitement et absorbe les rafales. Des services Amazon ECS chargent le modele de 1 Go en memoire et consomment la file ; l'Auto Scaling d'ECS (cluster + service) ajuste la capacite selon la profondeur de la file, y compris a zero quand un modele est inutilise. Lambda convient mal au chargement de 1 Go a chaque invocation.

question: A company has deployed its newest product on AWS. The product runs in an Auto Scaling group behind a Network Load Balancer. The company stores the product objects in an Amazon S3 bucket. The company recently experienced malicious attacks against its systems. The company needs a solution that continuously monitors for malicious activity in the AWS account, workloads, and access patterns to the S3 bucket. The solution must also report suspicious activity and display the information on a dashboard. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Configure Amazon Macie to monitor and report findings to AWS Config.
