options.B: Configure Amazon Inspector to monitor and report findings to AWS CloudTrail.
options.C: Configure Amazon GuardDuty to monitor and report findings to AWS Security Hub.
options.D: Configure AWS Config to monitor and report findings to Amazon EventBridge.

declencheurs: continuously monitor malicious activity in account/workloads/S3 access patterns
radar.signal: Detection continue de menaces + tableau de bord centralise -> Amazon GuardDuty avec envoi des findings vers AWS Security Hub

pieges.A: Macie detecte des donnees sensibles, pas l'activite malveillante du compte
pieges.B: Inspector scanne des vulnerabilites, il ne surveille pas les patterns d'acces malveillants
pieges.D: AWS Config verifie la conformite, il ne detecte pas les menaces

explication: Amazon GuardDuty surveille en continu le compte, les workloads et les patterns d'acces (dont S3) pour detecter les activites malveillantes. En envoyant ses findings a AWS Security Hub, on obtient les rapports et le tableau de bord centralise demandes. Macie (donnees sensibles), Inspector (vulnerabilites) et Config (conformite) ne couvrent pas la detection de menaces.

question: A company wants to migrate an on-premises data center to AWS. The data center hosts a storage server that stores data in an NFS-based file system. The storage server holds 200 GB of data. The company needs to migrate the data without interruption to existing services. Multiple resources in AWS must be able to access the data by using the NFS protocol. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively? (Choose two.)

options.A: Create an Amazon FSx for Lustre file system.
options.B: Create an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system.
options.C: Create an Amazon S3 bucket to receive the data.
options.D: Manually use an operating system copy command to push the data into the AWS destination.
options.E: Install an AWS DataSync agent in the on-premises data center. Use a DataSync task between the on-premises location and AWS.

declencheurs: multiple AWS resources access via NFS
radar.signal: Cible NFS partagee + migration manageee -> Amazon EFS (B) + agent AWS DataSync avec une tache on-prem->AWS (E)

pieges.A: FSx for Lustre cible le HPC, plus cher et non necessaire ici
pieges.C: S3 n'est pas un systeme de fichiers NFS montable par plusieurs ressources
pieges.D: Une copie manuelle par commande OS n'automatise pas la migration

explication: Amazon EFS fournit la cible NFS partagee accessible par plusieurs ressources AWS (B). Un agent AWS DataSync avec une tache transfere les 200 Go depuis l'on-prem vers EFS de facon manageee et sans interrompre les services (E). FSx for Lustre serait surdimensionne et S3 n'est pas un systeme de fichiers NFS.

question: An Amazon EC2 administrator created the following policy associated with an IAM group containing several users: { "Version": "2012-10-17", "Statement": [ { "Effect": "Allow", "Action": "ec2:TerminateInstances", "Resource": "*", "Condition": { "IpAddress": { "aws:SourceIp": "10.100.100.0/24" } } }, { "Effect": "Deny", "Action": "ec2:*", "Resource": "*", "Condition": { "StringNotEquals": { "ec2:Region": "us-east-1" } } } ] } What is the effect of this policy?

options.A: Users can terminate an EC2 instance in any AWS Region except us-east-1.
options.B: Users can terminate an EC2 instance with the IP address 10.100.100. in the us-east-1 Region.
options.C: Users can terminate an EC2 instance in the us-east-1 Region when the users' source IP is 10.100.100.254.
options.D: Users cannot terminate an EC2 instance in the us-east-1 Region when the users' source IP is 10.100.100.254.

declencheurs: Deny all ec2 if region != us-east-1
radar.signal: Combiner Allow (terminer si IP source dans le /24) et Deny (tout ec2 hors us-east-1) -> terminer en us-east-1 seulement, et seulement si l'IP source est dans 10.100.100.0/24 (ex. .254)

pieges.A: Le Deny bloque toutes les Regions sauf us-east-1 (donc pas 'n'importe quelle Region')
pieges.B: '10.100.100.' n'est pas une adresse valide ; la condition porte sur l'IP source, pas l'IP de l'instance
pieges.D: L'IP .254 appartient a 10.100.100.0/24, donc l'action est autorisee (pas interdite)

explication: Le premier statement autorise ec2:TerminateInstances si l'IP source de l'utilisateur est dans 10.100.100.0/24. Le second refuse toute action ec2 en dehors d'us-east-1. Resultat : les utilisateurs peuvent terminer une instance en us-east-1 uniquement lorsque leur IP source appartient a 10.100.100.0/24 (ce qui inclut 10.100.100.254).

question: A company wants to provide data scientists with near real-time read-only access to the company's production Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL database. The database is currently configured as a Single-AZ database. The data scientists use complex queries that will not affect the production database. The company needs a solution that is highly available. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

options.A: Scale the existing production database in a maintenance window to provide enough power for the data scientists.
options.B: Change the setup from a Single-AZ to a Multi-AZ instance deployment with a larger secondary standby instance. Provide the data scientists access to the secondary instance.
options.C: Change the setup from a Single-AZ to a Multi-AZ instance deployment. Provide two additional read replicas for the data scientists.
options.D: Change the setup from a Single-AZ to a Multi-AZ cluster deployment with two readable standby instances. Provide read endpoints to the data scientists.

radar.signal: Lectures HA sans impacter la prod -> RDS Multi-AZ cluster deployment avec deux standby lisibles + read endpoints

pieges.A: Scaler la prod existante ne fournit pas de HA ni d'isolation des requetes
pieges.B: Le standby Multi-AZ instance n'est pas lisible (piege classique)
pieges.C: Multi-AZ instance + deux read replicas coute plus cher qu'un Multi-AZ cluster a standby lisibles

explication: Un deploiement RDS Multi-AZ en mode cluster fournit deux instances standby LISIBLES et hautement disponibles. En donnant aux data scientists les read endpoints, ils executent leurs requetes complexes sans impacter la production, de facon economique. Le standby d'un Multi-AZ 'instance' (B) n'est pas interrogeable.

question: A company runs a three-tier web application in the AWS Cloud that operates across three Availability Zones. The application architecture has an Application Load Balancer, an Amazon EC2 web server that hosts user session states, and a MySQL database that runs on an EC2 instance. The company expects sudden increases in application traffic. The company wants to be able to scale to meet future application capacity demands and to ensure high availability across all three Availability Zones. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Migrate the MySQL database to Amazon RDS for MySQL with a Multi-AZ DB cluster deployment. Use Amazon ElastiCache for Redis with high availability to store session data and to cache reads. Migrate the web server to an Auto Scaling group that is in three Availability Zones.
options.B: Migrate the MySQL database to Amazon RDS for MySQL with a Multi-AZ DB cluster deployment. Use Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached with high availability to store session data and to cache reads. Migrate the web server to an Auto Scaling group that is in three Availability Zones.
options.C: Migrate the MySQL database to Amazon DynamoDB. Use DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) to cache reads. Store the session data in DynamoDB. Migrate the web server to an Auto Scaling group that is in three Availability Zones.
options.D: Migrate the MySQL database to Amazon RDS for MySQL in a single Availability Zone. Use Amazon ElastiCache for Redis with high availability to store session data and to cache reads. Migrate the web server to an Auto Scaling group that is in three Availability Zones.

radar.signal: HA + scaling 3 AZ -> RDS MySQL Multi-AZ cluster + ElastiCache for Redis (sessions + cache, HA) + web en Auto Scaling sur 3 AZ

pieges.B: ElastiCache Memcached ne fait pas de replication/HA native comme Redis
pieges.C: Migrer MySQL vers DynamoDB change le modele de donnees relationnel
pieges.D: RDS en Single-AZ ne fournit pas la haute disponibilite

explication: On externalise l'etat de session vers ElastiCache for Redis (qui supporte la replication et la haute disponibilite, contrairement a Memcached), on rend la base HA via RDS MySQL Multi-AZ, et on place le web dans un Auto Scaling group sur trois AZ. L'application devient scalable et hautement disponible sans changer le modele relationnel.

question: An international company has a subdomain for each country that the company operates in. The subdomains are formatted as example.com, country1.example.com, and country2.example.com. The company's workloads are behind an Application Load Balancer. The company wants to encrypt the website data that is in transit. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.A: Use the AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) console to request a public certificate for the apex top domain example.com and a wildcard certificate for *.example.com.
options.B: Use the AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) console to request a private certificate for the apex top domain example.com and a wildcard certificate for *.example.com.
options.C: Use the AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) console to request a public and private certificate for the apex top domain example.com.
options.D: Validate domain ownership by email address.
options.E: Validate domain ownership for the domain by adding the required DNS records to the DNS provider.

radar.signal: Certificat TLS couvrant l'apex et les sous-domaines -> certificat public ACM pour example.com + wildcard *.example.com (A) + validation par enregistrements DNS (E)

pieges.B: Un certificat prive ACM n'est pas approprie pour un site public (et est payant)
pieges.C: Demander 'public et prive' pour le seul apex ne couvre pas les sous-domaines
pieges.D: La validation par email est moins automatisable/fiable que la validation DNS

explication: Pour chiffrer en transit, on demande un certificat public ACM couvrant l'apex example.com et un wildcard *.example.com (A), associe a l'ALB. La validation de propriete se fait en ajoutant les enregistrements DNS requis (E), plus automatisable que l'email. Un certificat prive (B) ne convient pas a un site public.

question: A company is required to use cryptographic keys in its on-premises key manager. The key manager is outside of the AWS Cloud because of regulatory and compliance requirements. The company wants to manage encryption and decryption by using cryptographic keys that are retained outside of the AWS Cloud and that support a variety of external key managers from different vendors. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.A: Use AWS CloudHSM key store backed by a CloudHSM cluster.
options.B: Use an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) external key store backed by an external key manager.
options.C: Use the default AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) managed key store.
options.D: Use a custom key store backed by an AWS CloudHSM cluster.

declencheurs: support various external key managers from different vendors
radar.signal: Cles conservees hors d'AWS, multi-fournisseurs -> AWS KMS external key store (XKS) adosse a un external key manager

pieges.A: CloudHSM key store garde les cles dans AWS (CloudHSM), pas chez un gestionnaire externe tiers
pieges.C: Le key store KMS par defaut garde les cles dans AWS
pieges.D: Un custom key store adosse a CloudHSM reste dans AWS

explication: L'AWS KMS external key store (XKS) permet de conserver le materiel des cles dans un gestionnaire de cles externe, hors du cloud AWS, tout en utilisant l'API KMS. Il supporte differents gestionnaires de cles de multiples fournisseurs, repondant a l'exigence reglementaire avec un overhead reduit. CloudHSM garde les cles dans AWS.

question: A company wants to migrate its web applications from on premises to AWS. The company is located close to the eu-central-1 Region. Because of regulations, the company cannot launch some of its applications in eu-central-1. The company wants to achieve single-digit millisecond latency. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Deploy the applications in eu-central-1. Extend the company's VPC from eu-central-1 to an edge location in Amazon CloudFront.
options.B: Deploy the applications in AWS Local Zones by extending the company's VPC from eu-central-1 to the chosen Local Zone.
options.C: Deploy the applications in eu-central-1. Extend the company's VPC from eu-central-1 to the regional edge caches in Amazon CloudFront.
options.D: Deploy the applications in AWS Wavelength Zones by extending the company's VPC from eu-central-1 to the chosen Wavelength Zone.

declencheurs: cannot launch some apps in eu-central-1
radar.signal: Latence a un chiffre en millisecondes hors de la Region -> AWS Local Zones (extension du VPC eu-central-1)

pieges.A: Etendre le VPC vers un edge CloudFront n'est pas possible (CloudFront diffuse du contenu)
pieges.C: Les regional edge caches CloudFront ne recoivent pas des applications VPC
pieges.D: Wavelength cible la 5G/mobile edge, pas ce cas d'usage general

explication: Les AWS Local Zones rapprochent le calcul des utilisateurs, hors de la Region principale, pour une latence a un chiffre en millisecondes. En etendant le VPC eu-central-1 vers une Local Zone, la compagnie deploie les applications qu'elle ne peut pas placer dans eu-central-1. Wavelength vise les reseaux 5G, un autre cas d'usage.

question: A company ecommerce website has unpredictable traffic and uses AWS Lambda functions to directly access a private Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance. The company wants to maintain predictable database performance and ensure that the Lambda invocations do not overload the database with too many connections. What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

options.A: Point the client driver at an RDS custom endpoint. Deploy the Lambda functions inside a VPC.
options.B: Point the client driver at an RDS proxy endpoint. Deploy the Lambda functions inside a VPC.
options.C: Point the client driver at an RDS custom endpoint. Deploy the Lambda functions outside a VPC.
options.D: Point the client driver at an RDS proxy endpoint. Deploy the Lambda functions outside a VPC.

radar.signal: Eviter la surcharge de connexions RDS depuis Lambda -> pointer le driver vers un RDS Proxy endpoint + Lambda dans le VPC

pieges.A: Un custom endpoint ne mutualise pas les connexions comme RDS Proxy
pieges.C: Un custom endpoint + Lambda hors VPC n'atteint pas une base privee ni ne gere le pooling
pieges.D: RDS Proxy est bon mais la Lambda doit etre DANS le VPC pour joindre une base privee

explication: RDS Proxy mutualise les connexions, evitant que des invocations Lambda imprevisibles n'ouvrent trop de connexions et ne saturent la base. On pointe le driver vers l'endpoint RDS Proxy, et la Lambda doit etre deployee dans le VPC pour atteindre la base RDS privee.

question: A gaming company has a web application that displays scores. The application runs on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. The application stores data in an Amazon RDS for MySQL database. Users are starting to experience long delays and interruptions that are caused by database read performance. The company wants to improve the user experience while minimizing changes to the application's architecture. What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

options.A: Use Amazon ElastiCache in front of the database.
options.B: Use RDS Proxy between the application and the database.
options.C: Migrate the application from EC2 instances to AWS Lambda.
options.D: Migrate the database from Amazon RDS for MySQL to Amazon DynamoDB.

declencheurs: RDS MySQL read performance causing delays
improve UX with minimal architecture changes
radar.signal: Ameliorer les lectures avec un minimum de changements -> Amazon ElastiCache devant la base

pieges.B: RDS Proxy gere les connexions, il ne cache pas les lectures
pieges.C: Migrer vers Lambda est un changement d'architecture important
pieges.D: Migrer vers DynamoDB change le modele de donnees (beaucoup de changements)

explication: Un cache en memoire Amazon ElastiCache place devant la base sert les lectures frequentes (scores) sans solliciter RDS a chaque requete, ameliorant la latence avec un minimum de changements a l'architecture. RDS Proxy ne cache pas, et migrer vers Lambda/DynamoDB serait bien plus intrusif.

question: An ecommerce company has noticed performance degradation of its Amazon RDS based web application. The performance degradation is attributed to an increase in the number of read-only SQL queries triggered by business analysts. A solutions architect needs to solve the problem with minimal changes to the existing web application. What should the solutions architect recommend?

options.A: Export the data to Amazon DynamoDB and have the business analysts run their queries.
options.B: Load the data into Amazon ElastiCache and have the business analysts run their queries.
options.C: Create a read replica of the primary database and have the business analysts run their queries.
options.D: Copy the data into an Amazon Redshift cluster and have the business analysts run their queries.

declencheurs: RDS performance degraded by read-only queries from analysts
minimal changes to the web application
radar.signal: Isoler les lectures analytiques du primaire -> creer un read replica RDS pour les analystes

pieges.A: Exporter vers DynamoDB change le modele et l'usage
pieges.B: ElastiCache aide des lectures repetees, pas des requetes analytiques variees des analystes
pieges.D: Copier vers Redshift ajoute un entrepot a gerer et alimenter

explication: Un read replica RDS absorbe les requetes en lecture des analystes sans peser sur la base primaire, avec un impact minimal sur l'application (les analystes pointent vers le replica). Redshift ou DynamoDB imposeraient des changements plus lourds, et ElastiCache ne convient pas a des requetes analytiques variees.

question: A company built an application with Docker containers and needs to run the application in the AWS Cloud. The company wants to use a managed service to host the application. The solution must scale in and out appropriately according to demand on the individual container services. The solution also must not result in additional operational overhead or infrastructure to manage. Which solutions will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.A: Use Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) with AWS Fargate.
options.B: Use Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) with AWS Fargate.
options.C: Provision an Amazon API Gateway API. Connect the API to AWS Lambda to run the containers.
options.D: Use Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) with Amazon EC2 worker nodes.
options.E: Use Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) with Amazon EC2 worker nodes.

declencheurs: no additional operational overhead or infrastructure
radar.signal: Conteneurs manages sans infrastructure a gerer -> ECS avec Fargate (A) ou EKS avec Fargate (B)

pieges.C: API Gateway + Lambda ne fait pas tourner des conteneurs Docker ainsi
pieges.D: ECS avec des worker nodes EC2 = instances a gerer
pieges.E: EKS avec des worker nodes EC2 = instances a gerer

explication: AWS Fargate execute les conteneurs sans gerer d'instances : ECS avec Fargate (A) ou EKS avec Fargate (B) hebergent l'application, scalent selon la demande de chaque service et n'ajoutent aucune infrastructure. Les variantes avec worker nodes EC2 imposent de gerer des serveurs.

question: An ecommerce company is running a seasonal online sale. The company hosts its website on Amazon EC2 instances spanning multiple Availability Zones. The company wants its website to manage sudden traffic increases during the sale. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

options.A: Create an Auto Scaling group that is large enough to handle peak traffic load. Stop half of the Amazon EC2 instances. Configure the Auto Scaling group to use the stopped instances to scale out when traffic increases.
options.B: Create an Auto Scaling group for the website. Set the minimum size of the Auto Scaling group so that it can handle high traffic volumes without the need to scale out.
options.C: Use Amazon CloudFront and Amazon ElastiCache to cache dynamic content with an Auto Scaling group set as the origin. Configure the Auto Scaling group with the instances necessary to populate CloudFront and ElastiCache. Scale in after the cache is fully populated.
options.D: Configure an Auto Scaling group to scale out as traffic increases. Create a launch template to start new instances from a preconfigured Amazon Machine Image (AMI).

radar.signal: Absorber des pics soudains a moindre cout -> Auto Scaling group qui scale out + launch template a partir d'une AMI preconfiguree

pieges.A: Des instances 'stoppees' ne servent pas de reserve de scaling (l'ASG lance de nouvelles instances)
pieges.B: Dimensionner le minimum pour le pic paie la capacite max en permanence
pieges.C: CloudFront + ElastiCache pour du 'contenu dynamique' + ASG origine = complexe et pas le plus economique

explication: Un Auto Scaling group qui monte en charge a la demande, avec un launch template base sur une AMI preconfiguree pour demarrer vite de nouvelles instances, absorbe les pics saisonniers en ne payant que la capacite reellement utilisee. Dimensionner le minimum au pic (B) couterait cher en permanence.

question: A company is developing software that uses a PostgreSQL database schema. The company needs to configure multiple development environments and databases for the company's developers. On average, each development environment is used for half of the 8-hour workday. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

options.A: Configure each development environment with its own Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL database.
options.B: Configure each development environment with its own Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL Single-AZ DB instances.
options.C: Configure each development environment with its own Amazon Aurora On-Demand PostgreSQL-Compatible database.
options.D: Configure each development environment with its own Amazon S3 bucket by using Amazon S3 Object Select.

radar.signal: Bases de dev utilisees quelques heures/jour -> Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL Single-AZ (que l'on peut arreter hors usage)

pieges.A: Aurora PostgreSQL est plus cher qu'RDS Single-AZ pour du dev
pieges.C: Aurora On-Demand reste plus couteux qu'RDS Single-AZ ici
pieges.D: S3 Object Select n'est pas une base de donnees PostgreSQL

explication: Pour des environnements de developpement utilises seulement la moitie de la journee, des instances Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL Single-AZ (que l'on peut arreter quand elles ne servent pas) sont les plus economiques. Aurora coute davantage, et S3 Object Select n'est pas une base PostgreSQL.

question: A company uses AWS Organizations with resources tagged by account. The company also uses AWS Backup to back up its AWS infrastructure resources. The company needs to back up all AWS resources. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.A: Use AWS Config to identify all untagged resources. Tag the identified resources programmatically. Use tags in the backup plan.
options.B: Use AWS Config to identify all resources that are not running. Add those resources to the backup vault.
options.C: Require all AWS account owners to review their resources to identify the resources that need to be backed up.
options.D: Use Amazon Inspector to identify all noncompliant resources.

radar.signal: Inclure les ressources non tagguees dans les backups par tag -> AWS Config identifie les non-tagguees, on les tague par programme, puis on utilise les tags dans le backup plan

pieges.B: AWS Config n'identifie pas 'les ressources non demarrees' pour du backup pertinent
pieges.C: Demander a chaque proprietaire de revoir = beaucoup d'overhead manuel
pieges.D: Amazon Inspector detecte des vulnerabilites, pas des ressources non tagguees

explication: Comme AWS Backup selectionne les ressources par tag, il faut d'abord taguer celles qui ne le sont pas. AWS Config identifie les ressources non tagguees, qu'on tague ensuite par programme, puis le backup plan base sur les tags couvre l'ensemble. C'est automatisable et a faible overhead.

question: A company has a mobile chat application with a data store based in Amazon DynamoDB. Users would like new messages to be read with as little latency as possible. A solutions architect needs to design an optimal solution that requires minimal application changes. Which method should the solutions architect select?

options.A: Configure Amazon DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) for the new messages table. Update the code to use the DAX endpoint.
options.B: Add DynamoDB read replicas to handle the increased read load. Update the application to point to the read endpoint for the read replicas.
options.C: Double the number of read capacity units for the new messages table in DynamoDB. Continue to use the existing DynamoDB endpoint.
options.D: Add an Amazon ElastiCache for Redis cache to the application stack. Update the application to point to the Redis cache endpoint instead of DynamoDB.

declencheurs: read new messages with as little latency as possible
radar.signal: Lectures DynamoDB ultra rapides avec peu de changements -> DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX), pointer le code vers l'endpoint DAX

pieges.B: DynamoDB n'a pas de 'read replicas' a ajouter comme une base relationnelle
pieges.C: Doubler les RCU ameliore le debit, pas la latence en memoire de DAX
pieges.D: ElastiCache Redis exige plus de changements applicatifs que DAX (API compatible)

explication: DAX est un cache en memoire natif de DynamoDB : il divise fortement la latence de lecture et ne demande qu'a pointer le code vers l'endpoint DAX (API compatible). ElastiCache imposerait plus de changements, augmenter les RCU n'apporte pas la latence en memoire, et DynamoDB n'a pas de read replicas a ajouter.

question: A company hosts a website on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The website serves static content. Website traffic is increasing, and the company is concerned about a potential increase in cost. Which solution should they implement?

options.A: Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution to cache static files at edge locations.
options.B: Create an Amazon ElastiCache cluster. Connect the ALB to the ElastiCache cluster to serve cached files.
options.C: Create an AWS WAF web ACL and associate it with the ALB. Add a rule to the web ACL to cache static files.
options.D: Create a second ALB in an alternative AWS Region. Route user traffic to the closest Region to minimize data transfer costs.

radar.signal: Reduire le cout en cachant du statique -> CloudFront pour mettre en cache les fichiers statiques aux points de presence

pieges.B: ElastiCache cache des donnees applicatives, pas des fichiers web statiques via l'ALB
pieges.C: AWS WAF filtre les attaques, il ne cache pas de contenu
pieges.D: Un second ALB dans une autre Region ajoute du cout, il ne cache pas le statique

explication: CloudFront met en cache les fichiers statiques aux points de presence : la majorite des requetes est servie depuis le cache, ce qui reduit la charge (et le cout) sur les EC2/ALB tout en accelerant la diffusion. WAF (securite) et ElastiCache (cache de donnees) ne cachent pas du contenu web statique.

question: A company has multiple VPCs across AWS Regions to support and run workloads that are isolated from workloads in other Regions. Because of a recent application launch requirement, the company VPCs must communicate with all other VPCs across all Regions. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST amount of administrative effort?

options.A: Use VPC peering to manage VPC communication in a single Region. Use VPC peering across Regions to manage VPC communications.
options.B: Use AWS Direct Connect gateways across all Regions to connect VPCs across regions and manage VPC communications.
options.C: Use AWS Transit Gateway to manage VPC communication in a single Region and Transit Gateway peering across Regions to manage VPC communications.
options.D: Use AWS PrivateLink across all Regions to connect VPCs across Regions and manage VPC communications.

declencheurs: must communicate with all VPCs across all Regions
radar.signal: Interconnexion inter-Regions de nombreux VPC -> AWS Transit Gateway par Region + Transit Gateway peering entre Regions

pieges.A: Le VPC peering ne scale pas (maillage complet intra et inter-Region)
pieges.B: Direct Connect gateway sert a relier de l'on-prem, pas a interconnecter des VPC entre eux
pieges.D: PrivateLink expose des services, il n'interconnecte pas des reseaux VPC complets

explication: Un Transit Gateway centralise la connectivite des VPC d'une Region, et le Transit Gateway peering relie ces hubs entre Regions. Tous les VPC communiquent alors via les hubs, avec bien moins d'administration qu'un maillage de peering. PrivateLink (services) et Direct Connect (on-prem) ne repondent pas au besoin d'interconnexion de reseaux.

question: A company runs applications on Amazon EC2 instances in one AWS Region. The company wants to back up the EC2 instances to a second Region. The company also wants to provision EC2 resources in the second Region and manage the EC2 instances centrally from one AWS account. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

options.A: Create a disaster recovery (DR) plan that has a similar number of EC2 instances in the second Region. Configure data replication.
options.B: Create point-in-time Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) snapshots of the EC2 instances. Copy the snapshots to the second Region periodically.
options.C: Create a backup plan by using AWS Backup. Configure cross-Region backup to the second Region for the EC2 instances.
options.D: Deploy a similar number of EC2 instances in the second Region. Use AWS DataSync to transfer the data from the source Region to the second Region.

declencheurs: back up EC2 to a second Region
radar.signal: Backup cross-Region manage et central -> AWS Backup avec backup plan et copie cross-Region

pieges.A: Un DR avec un nombre similaire d'instances actives = couteux
pieges.B: Copier des snapshots EBS periodiquement = plus manuel qu'AWS Backup
pieges.D: Deployer autant d'instances + DataSync = couteux et non centralise pour du backup

explication: AWS Backup gere de facon centralisee la sauvegarde des instances EC2 et sa copie vers une seconde Region via un backup plan, a faible cout et sans maintenir d'infrastructure active dupliquee. Copier des snapshots a la main (B) ou deployer des instances miroir (A/D) serait plus couteux ou plus manuel.

question: A company that uses AWS is building an application to transfer data to a product manufacturer. The company has its own identity provider (IdP). The company wants the IdP to authenticate application users while the users use the application to transfer data. The company must use Applicability Statement 2 (AS2) protocol. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Use AWS DataSync to transfer the data. Create an AWS Lambda function for IdP authentication.
options.B: Use Amazon AppFlow flows to transfer the data. Create an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) task for IdP authentication.
options.C: Use AWS Transfer Family to transfer the data. Create an AWS Lambda function for IdP authentication.
options.D: Use AWS Storage Gateway to transfer the data. Create an Amazon Cognito identity pool for IdP authentication.

radar.signal: Transfert de fichiers via AS2 avec authentification par IdP -> AWS Transfer Family + Lambda pour l'authentification IdP

pieges.A: DataSync ne supporte pas le protocole AS2
pieges.B: AppFlow integre des SaaS, il ne fait pas de l'AS2
pieges.D: Storage Gateway n'est pas un service de transfert AS2, et un identity pool Cognito n'est pas l'IdP demande

explication: AWS Transfer Family prend en charge le protocole AS2 pour echanger des fichiers avec des partenaires, et une fonction Lambda peut integrer l'IdP de l'entreprise comme fournisseur d'identite custom pour authentifier les utilisateurs. DataSync/AppFlow/Storage Gateway ne supportent pas l'AS2.

question: A company solutions architect is designing an AWS multi-account solution that uses AWS Organizations. The solutions architect has organized the company's accounts into organizational units (OUs). The solutions architect needs a solution that will identify any changes to the OU hierarchy. The solution also needs to notify the company's operations team of any changes. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.A: Provision the AWS accounts by using AWS Control Tower. Use account drift notifications to identify the changes to the OU hierarchy.
options.B: Provision the AWS accounts by using AWS Control Tower. Use AWS Config aggregated rules to identify the changes to the OU hierarchy.
options.C: Use AWS Service Catalog to create accounts in Organizations. Use an AWS CloudTrail organization trail to identify the changes to the OU hierarchy.
options.D: Use AWS CloudFormation templates to create accounts in Organizations. Use the drift detection operation on a Stack to identify the changes to the OU hierarchy.

declencheurs: identify changes to the OU hierarchy
radar.signal: Detecter les derives de la hierarchie d'OU -> AWS Control Tower + notifications de drift de compte

pieges.B: AWS Config aggregated rules ne suivent pas nativement la hierarchie des OU
pieges.C: Service Catalog + CloudTrail trail = plus de configuration pour parser les evenements
pieges.D: CloudFormation + drift detection ne suit pas la hierarchie des OU d'Organizations

explication: AWS Control Tower detecte automatiquement les derives (drift) par rapport a la structure attendue, y compris les changements de hierarchie d'OU, et notifie l'equipe. En provisionnant les comptes via Control Tower et en utilisant les notifications de drift, on obtient la solution avec le moins d'overhead.

question: A company website handles millions of requests each day, and the number of requests continues to increase. A solutions architect needs to improve the response time of the web application. The solutions architect determines that the application needs to decrease latency when retrieving product details from the Amazon DynamoDB table. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST amount of operational overhead?

options.A: Set up a DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) cluster. Route all read requests through DAX.
options.B: Set up Amazon ElastiCache for Redis between the DynamoDB table and the web application. Route all read requests through Redis.
options.C: Set up Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached between the DynamoDB table and the web application. Route all read requests through Memcached.
options.D: Set up Amazon DynamoDB Streams on the table, and have AWS Lambda read from the table and populate Amazon ElastiCache. Route all read requests through ElastiCache.

declencheurs: decrease latency retrieving product details from DynamoDB
radar.signal: Reduire la latence de lecture DynamoDB avec peu d'overhead -> cluster DAX, router les lectures via DAX

pieges.B: ElastiCache Redis impose plus de changements et de gestion que DAX pour DynamoDB
pieges.C: ElastiCache Memcached idem : cache externe a gerer et code a adapter
pieges.D: DynamoDB Streams + Lambda + ElastiCache = pipeline complexe a maintenir

explication: DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) est un cache en memoire natif de DynamoDB : router les lectures via DAX reduit la latence (microsecondes) avec un minimum d'overhead, sans batir un pipeline (Streams/Lambda/ElastiCache) ni gerer un cache externe comme ElastiCache.

question: A company runs its ecommerce application on AWS. Every new order is published as a message in a RabbitMQ queue that runs on an Amazon EC2 instance in a single Availability Zone. These messages are processed by a different application that runs on a separate EC2 instance. This application stores the details in a PostgreSQL database on another EC2 instance. All the EC2 instances are in the same Availability Zone. The company needs to redesign its architecture to provide the highest availability with the least operational overhead. What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

options.A: Migrate the queue to a redundant pair (active/standby) of RabbitMQ instances on Amazon MQ. Create a Multi-AZ Auto Scaling group for EC2 instances that host the application. Create another Multi-AZ Auto Scaling group for EC2 instances that host the PostgreSQL database.
options.B: Migrate the queue to a redundant pair (active/standby) of RabbitMQ instances on Amazon MQ. Create a Multi-AZ Auto Scaling group for EC2 instances that host the application. Migrate the database to run on a Multi-AZ deployment of Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL.
options.C: Create a Multi-AZ Auto Scaling group for EC2 instances that host the RabbitMQ queue. Create another Multi-AZ Auto Scaling group for EC2 instances that host the application. Migrate the database to run on a Multi-AZ deployment of Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL.
options.D: Create a Multi-AZ Auto Scaling group for EC2 instances that host the RabbitMQ queue. Create another Multi-AZ Auto Scaling group for EC2 instances that host the application. Create a third Multi-AZ Auto Scaling group for EC2 instances that host the PostgreSQL database.

declencheurs: RabbitMQ + app + PostgreSQL all on EC2 in a single AZ
radar.signal: Rendre chaque tier HA et manage -> Amazon MQ RabbitMQ actif/standby + Auto Scaling Multi-AZ pour l'app + RDS for PostgreSQL Multi-AZ

pieges.A: Mettre PostgreSQL dans un Auto Scaling group d'EC2 n'est pas une base manageee HA
pieges.C: RabbitMQ auto-gere sur EC2 en ASG = plus d'overhead qu'Amazon MQ
pieges.D: Tout garder sur EC2 (queue + app + base) maximise l'overhead operationnel

explication: On migre la file vers Amazon MQ (RabbitMQ manage en paire actif/standby), l'application vers un Auto Scaling group Multi-AZ, et la base vers Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL Multi-AZ. Chaque tier devient hautement disponible et manage. Garder PostgreSQL sur EC2 (A) ou RabbitMQ auto-gere (C/D) ajouterait de l'overhead.

question: A reporting team receives files each day in an Amazon S3 bucket. The reporting team manually reviews and copies the files from this initial S3 bucket to an analysis S3 bucket each day at the same time to use with Amazon QuickSight. Additional teams are starting to send more files in larger sizes to the initial S3 bucket. The reporting team wants to move the files automatically to the analysis S3 bucket as the files enter the initial S3 bucket. The reporting team also wants to use AWS Lambda functions to run pattern-matching code on the copied data. In addition, the reporting team wants to send the data files to a pipeline in Amazon SageMaker Pipelines. What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.A: Create a Lambda function to copy the files to the analysis S3 bucket. Create an S3 event notification for the analysis S3 bucket. Configure Lambda and SageMaker Pipelines as destinations of the event notification. Configure s3:ObjectCreated:Put as the event type.
options.B: Create a Lambda function to copy the files to the analysis S3 bucket. Configure the analysis S3 bucket to send event notifications to Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events). Configure an ObjectCreated rule in EventBridge (CloudWatch Events). Configure Lambda and SageMaker Pipelines as targets for the rule.
options.C: Configure S3 replication between the S3 buckets. Create an S3 event notification for the analysis S3 bucket. Configure Lambda and SageMaker Pipelines as destinations of the event notification. Configure s3:ObjectCreated:Put as the event type.
options.D: Configure S3 replication between the S3 buckets. Configure the analysis S3 bucket to send event notifications to Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events). Configure an ObjectCreated rule in EventBridge (CloudWatch Events). Configure Lambda and SageMaker Pipelines as targets for the rule.

declencheurs: auto-copy files from initial to analysis bucket
radar.signal: Copie auto + declenchement multi-cibles (Lambda + SageMaker Pipelines) -> S3 replication entre buckets + regle EventBridge ObjectCreated ciblant Lambda et SageMaker Pipelines

pieges.A: Une Lambda de copie + notifications S3 = plus de code, et les notifications S3 ne ciblent pas SageMaker Pipelines
pieges.B: Une Lambda de copie custom ajoute de l'overhead face a la replication S3 native
pieges.C: Les S3 event notifications ne peuvent pas cibler SageMaker Pipelines (il faut EventBridge)

explication: La replication S3 copie automatiquement les fichiers vers le bucket d'analyse sans code. En envoyant les evenements a Amazon EventBridge, une regle ObjectCreated peut cibler a la fois une Lambda et SageMaker Pipelines (ce que les S3 event notifications ne permettent pas). C'est la solution au plus faible overhead.

question: A company runs an application in the AWS Cloud that generates sensitive archival data files. The company wants to rearchitect the application's data storage. The company wants to encrypt the data files and to ensure that third parties do not have access to the data before the data is encrypted and sent to AWS. The company has already created an Amazon S3 bucket. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Configure the S3 bucket to use client-side encryption with an Amazon S3 managed encryption key. Configure the application to use the S3 bucket to store the archival files.
options.B: Configure the S3 bucket to use server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS). Configure the application to use the S3 bucket to store the archival files.
options.C: Configure the S3 bucket to use dual-layer server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS). Configure the application to use the S3 bucket to store the archival files.
options.D: Configure the application to use client-side encryption with a key stored in AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS). Configure the application to store the archival files in the S3 bucket.

declencheurs: third parties must not access before it is encrypted and sent to AWS
radar.signal: Chiffrer AVANT l'envoi, cle geree -> chiffrement cote client par l'application avec une cle stockee dans AWS KMS

pieges.A: Le client-side encryption avec une cle S3 managed n'existe pas ainsi (SSE-S3 est cote serveur)
pieges.B: SSE-KMS chiffre cote serveur, apres reception par AWS
pieges.C: Le dual-layer SSE-KMS reste du chiffrement cote serveur

explication: Pour garantir qu'aucun tiers n'accede aux donnees avant leur chiffrement et leur envoi a AWS, l'application doit chiffrer cote client, avec une cle stockee dans AWS KMS, puis deposer les fichiers deja chiffres dans S3. Le chiffrement cote serveur (SSE-KMS, dual-layer) n'intervient qu'une fois les donnees arrivees dans AWS.

question: A company uses Amazon RDS with default backup settings for its database. The company needs to make a daily backup of the database to meet regulatory requirements. The company must retain the backup for 30 days. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.A: Write an AWS Lambda function to create an RDS snapshot every day.
options.B: Modify the RDS database to have a retention period of 30 days for automated backups.
options.C: Use AWS Systems Manager Maintenance Windows to modify the RDS backup retention period.
options.D: Create a manual snapshot every day by using the AWS CLI. Modify the RDS backup retention period.

radar.signal: Backup quotidien conserve 30 jours, natif -> regler la periode de retention des automated backups d'RDS a 30 jours

pieges.A: Une Lambda de snapshot quotidien = code a ecrire et maintenir
pieges.C: Les Maintenance Windows ne servent pas a fixer la retention des backups
pieges.D: Des snapshots manuels quotidiens via CLI = operation recurrente a gerer

explication: Les automated backups d'RDS realisent deja des sauvegardes quotidiennes ; il suffit de porter leur periode de retention a 30 jours. C'est natif et sans code, contrairement a une Lambda ou a des snapshots manuels quotidiens qui ajouteraient de l'overhead.

question: A solutions architect is using an AWS CloudFormation template to deploy a three-tier web application. The web application consists of a web tier and an application tier that stores and retrieves user data in Amazon DynamoDB tables. The web and application tiers are hosted on Amazon EC2 instances, and the database tier is not publicly accessible. The application EC2 instances need to access the DynamoDB tables without exposing API credentials in the template. What should the solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

options.A: Create an IAM role to read the DynamoDB tables. Associate the role with the application instances by referencing an instance profile.
options.B: Create an IAM role that has the required permissions to read and write from the DynamoDB tables. Add the role to the EC2 instance profile, and associate the instance profile with the application instances.
options.C: Use the parameter section in the AWS CloudFormation template to have the user input access and secret keys from an already-created IAM user that has the required permissions to read and write from the DynamoDB tables.
options.D: Create an IAM user in the AWS CloudFormation template that has the required permissions to read and write from the DynamoDB tables. Use the GetAtt function to retrieve the access and secret keys, and pass them to the application instances through the user data.

declencheurs: without exposing API credentials in the template
radar.signal: Acces sans identifiants en dur -> role IAM avec permissions read/write DynamoDB via un instance profile associe aux instances

pieges.A: Le role ne donne que la lecture, or il faut aussi ecrire (store)
pieges.C: Saisir access/secret keys en parametre expose des identifiants
pieges.D: Creer un IAM user et passer les cles via user data expose des secrets

explication: Un role IAM avec les permissions de lecture ET d'ecriture sur DynamoDB, attache aux instances via un instance profile, leur fournit des identifiants temporaires sans exposer de cles dans le template. L'option A n'accorde que la lecture, alors que l'application doit aussi ecrire.

question: A solutions architect manages an analytics application. The application stores large amounts of semistructured data in an Amazon S3 bucket. The solutions architect wants to use parallel data processing to process the data more quickly. The solutions architect also wants to use information that is stored in an Amazon Redshift database to enrich the data. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Use Amazon Athena to process the S3 data. Use AWS Glue with the Amazon Redshift data to enrich the S3 data.
options.B: Use Amazon EMR to process the S3 data. Use Amazon EMR with the Amazon Redshift data to enrich the S3 data.
options.C: Use Amazon EMR to process the S3 data. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to move the S3 data into Amazon Redshift so that the data can be enriched.
options.D: Use AWS Glue to process the S3 data. Use AWS Lake Formation with the Amazon Redshift data to enrich the S3 data.

radar.signal: Traitement parallele massif + enrichissement Redshift -> Amazon EMR pour traiter S3 et joindre les donnees Redshift

pieges.A: Athena est du SQL serverless, pas du traitement parallele distribue custom ; le montage Glue ici est bancal
pieges.C: Kinesis Data Streams sert au flux temps reel, pas a deplacer des donnees S3 vers Redshift pour enrichir
pieges.D: Glue + Lake Formation n'est pas centre sur le traitement parallele massif demande

explication: Amazon EMR (Spark/Hadoop) traite en parallele de gros volumes de donnees semi-structurees de S3 et peut lire les donnees Amazon Redshift pour enrichir le resultat. C'est la solution adaptee au traitement parallele distribue avec enrichissement, la ou Athena/Glue ne fournissent pas ce parallelisme custom.

question: A company has a Microsoft .NET application that runs on an on-premises Windows Server. The application stores data by using an Oracle Database Standard Edition server. The company is planning a migration to AWS and wants to minimize development changes while moving the application. The AWS application environment should be highly available. Which combination of actions should the company take to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.A: Refactor the application as serverless with AWS Lambda functions running .NET Core.
options.B: Rehost the application in AWS Elastic Beanstalk with the .NET platform in a Multi-AZ deployment.
options.C: Replatform the application to run on Amazon EC2 with the Amazon Linux Amazon Machine Image (AMI).
options.D: Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to migrate from the Oracle database to Amazon DynamoDB in a Multi-AZ deployment.
options.E: Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to migrate from the Oracle database to Oracle on Amazon RDS in a Multi-AZ deployment.

radar.signal: Rehost .NET sans reecrire + base Oracle manageee HA -> Elastic Beanstalk .NET Multi-AZ (B) + DMS vers Oracle sur Amazon RDS Multi-AZ (E)

pieges.A: Refactorer en Lambda .NET Core = changements de developpement importants
pieges.C: Replatform vers Amazon Linux impose de porter une app .NET Windows
pieges.D: Migrer Oracle vers DynamoDB change le modele relationnel (beaucoup de changements)

explication: AWS Elastic Beanstalk avec la plateforme .NET en Multi-AZ rehberge l'application sans reecriture, hautement disponible (B). AWS DMS migre la base Oracle vers Oracle sur Amazon RDS en Multi-AZ, en conservant le moteur (E). Lambda .NET Core ou DynamoDB imposeraient des changements de code majeurs.

question: A company runs a containerized application on a Kubernetes cluster in an on-premises data center. The company is using a MongoDB database for data storage. The company wants to migrate some of these environments to AWS, but no code changes or deployment method changes are possible at this time. The company needs a solution that minimizes operational overhead. Which solution meets these requirements?

options.A: Use Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) with Amazon EC2 worker nodes for compute and MongoDB on EC2 for data storage.
options.B: Use Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) with AWS Fargate for compute and Amazon DynamoDB for data storage.
options.C: Use Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) with Amazon EC2 worker nodes for compute and Amazon DynamoDB for data storage.
options.D: Use Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) with AWS Fargate for compute and Amazon DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility) for data storage.

declencheurs: no code or deployment method changes
radar.signal: Garder Kubernetes + MongoDB sans changer le code -> Amazon EKS + AWS Fargate + Amazon DocumentDB (compatible MongoDB)

pieges.A: ECS change la methode de deploiement (pas Kubernetes) et MongoDB sur EC2 = a gerer
pieges.B: ECS + DynamoDB change la methode de deploiement ET le modele de donnees
pieges.C: EKS avec worker nodes EC2 = infra a gerer ; DynamoDB n'est pas compatible MongoDB

explication: Pour conserver Kubernetes (aucun changement de methode de deploiement), on migre vers Amazon EKS ; AWS Fargate supprime la gestion des noeuds. Amazon DocumentDB, compatible avec MongoDB, remplace la base sans changement de code applicatif. C'est le minimum d'overhead sans toucher au code.

question: A company is building an ecommerce application and needs to store sensitive customer information. The company needs to give customers the ability to complete purchase transactions on the website. The company also needs to ensure that sensitive customer data is protected, even from database administrators. Which solution meets these requirements?

options.A: Store sensitive data in an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume. Use EBS encryption to encrypt the data. Use an IAM instance role to restrict access.
options.B: Store sensitive data in Amazon RDS for MySQL. Use AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) client-side encryption to encrypt the data.
options.C: Store sensitive data in Amazon S3. Use AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) server-side encryption to encrypt the data. Use S3 bucket policies to restrict access.
options.D: Store sensitive data in Amazon FSx for Windows Server. Mount the file share on application servers. Use Windows file permissions to restrict access.

radar.signal: Proteger les donnees meme des DBA -> RDS for MySQL + chiffrement cote client avec AWS KMS

pieges.A: Le chiffrement EBS protege le volume mais un DBA peut lire les donnees dechiffrees dans la base
pieges.C: SSE cote serveur laisse les donnees lisibles par ceux qui accedent a la base/au bucket
pieges.D: Des permissions Windows n'empechent pas un admin de lire les donnees en clair

explication: Avec un chiffrement cote client (AWS KMS), les donnees sont chiffrees par l'application avant d'entrer dans RDS : meme un administrateur de base ne voit que du chiffre, car il ne possede pas la cle de dechiffrement. Le chiffrement au repos cote serveur (EBS/SSE) laisserait les donnees lisibles par qui accede a la base.

question: A company has an on-premises MySQL database that handles transactional data. The company is migrating the database to the AWS Cloud. The migrated database must maintain compatibility with the company applications that use the database. The migrated database also must scale automatically during periods of increased demand. Which migration solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Use native MySQL tools to migrate the database to Amazon RDS for MySQL. Configure elastic storage scaling.
options.B: Migrate the database to Amazon Redshift by using the mysqldump utility. Turn on Auto Scaling for the Amazon Redshift cluster.
options.C: Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to migrate the database to Amazon Aurora. Turn on Aurora Auto Scaling.
options.D: Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to migrate the database to Amazon DynamoDB. Configure an Auto Scaling policy.

radar.signal: MySQL compatible + scaling automatique -> DMS vers Amazon Aurora (MySQL-compatible) + Aurora Auto Scaling

pieges.A: RDS for MySQL + elastic storage scaling ne scale que le stockage, pas le calcul de lecture automatiquement
pieges.B: Redshift est un entrepot analytique, pas compatible avec des apps transactionnelles MySQL
pieges.D: DynamoDB n'est pas compatible MySQL (changement de modele)

explication: Amazon Aurora est compatible MySQL, ce qui preserve la compatibilite avec les applications, et Aurora Auto Scaling ajoute automatiquement des replicas pendant les pics. AWS DMS realise la migration. Redshift (analytique) et DynamoDB (NoSQL) ne sont pas compatibles avec des applications MySQL transactionnelles.

question: A company has separate AWS accounts for its finance, data analytics, and development departments. Because of costs and security concerns, the company wants to control which services each AWS account can use. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.A: Use AWS Systems Manager templates to control which AWS services each department can use.
options.B: Create organizational units (OUs) for each department in AWS Organizations. Attach service control policies (SCPs) to the OUs.
options.C: Use AWS CloudFormation to automatically provision only the AWS services that each department can use.
options.D: Set up a list of products in AWS Service Catalog in the AWS accounts to manage and control the usage of specific AWS services.

declencheurs: control which services each account can use
radar.signal: Restreindre les services par compte/departement -> OUs dans AWS Organizations + Service Control Policies (SCP)

pieges.A: Les templates Systems Manager ne controlent pas quels services un compte peut utiliser
pieges.C: CloudFormation provisionne, il ne restreint pas l'usage des services
pieges.D: Service Catalog controle des produits approuves, pas globalement les services autorises par compte

explication: En organisant les comptes en OUs dans AWS Organizations et en attachant des Service Control Policies, on definit centralement quels services chaque departement peut utiliser. C'est le garde-fou natif avec le moins d'overhead, la ou Systems Manager/CloudFormation/Service Catalog ne restreignent pas l'usage des services.

question: A company has created a multi-tier application for its ecommerce website. The website uses an Application Load Balancer that resides in the public subnets, a web tier in the public subnets, and a MySQL cluster hosted on Amazon EC2 instances in the private subnets. The MySQL database needs to retrieve product catalog and pricing information that is hosted on the internet by a third-party provider. A solutions architect must devise a strategy that maximizes security without increasing operational overhead. What should the solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

options.A: Deploy a NAT instance in the VPC. Route all the internet-based traffic through the NAT instance.
options.B: Deploy a NAT gateway in the public subnets. Modify the private subnet route table to direct all internet-bound traffic to the NAT gateway.
options.C: Configure an internet gateway and attach it to the VPC. Modify the private subnet route table to direct internet-bound traffic to the internet gateway.
options.D: Configure a virtual private gateway and attach it to the VPC. Modify the private subnet route table to direct internet-bound traffic to the virtual private gateway.

declencheurs: MySQL in private subnet must reach a third-party internet provider
radar.signal: Sortie Internet securisee depuis un subnet prive, managee -> NAT gateway dans un subnet public + route par defaut du subnet prive vers le NAT

pieges.A: Une NAT instance = a gerer/patcher soi-meme (plus d'overhead qu'un NAT gateway)
pieges.C: Un internet gateway rendrait le subnet prive public (moins securise)
pieges.D: Un virtual private gateway sert au VPN, pas a la sortie Internet

explication: Un NAT gateway (manage) dans un subnet public permet a la base en subnet prive d'initier des connexions sortantes vers le fournisseur tiers, sans etre joignable depuis Internet. Contrairement a une NAT instance (a gerer), il n'ajoute pas d'overhead, et un internet gateway exposerait la base.

question: A company has users all around the world accessing its HTTP-based application deployed on Amazon EC2 instances in multiple AWS Regions. The company wants to improve the availability and performance of the application. The company also wants to protect the application against common web exploits that may affect availability, compromise security, or consume excessive resources. Static IP addresses are required. What should a solutions architect recommend to accomplish this?

options.A: Put the EC2 instances behind Network Load Balancers (NLBs) in each Region. Deploy AWS WAF on the NLBs. Create an accelerator using AWS Global Accelerator and register the NLBs as endpoints.
options.B: Put the EC2 instances behind Application Load Balancers (ALBs) in each Region. Deploy AWS WAF on the ALBs. Create an accelerator using AWS Global Accelerator and register the ALBs as endpoints.
options.C: Put the EC2 instances behind Network Load Balancers (NLBs) in each Region. Deploy AWS WAF on the NLBs. Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution with an origin that uses Amazon Route 53 latency-based routing to route requests to the NLBs.
options.D: Put the EC2 instances behind Application Load Balancers (ALBs) in each Region. Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution with an origin that uses Amazon Route 53 latency-based routing to route requests to the ALBs. Deploy AWS WAF on the CloudFront distribution.

radar.signal: HTTP + WAF + IP statiques mondial -> ALB par Region + AWS WAF sur les ALB + AWS Global Accelerator avec les ALB en endpoints

pieges.A: AWS WAF ne s'associe pas a un NLB (couche 4)
pieges.C: CloudFront ne fournit pas d'IP statiques d'entree comme Global Accelerator
pieges.D: CloudFront + Route 53 ne fournit pas les IP statiques exigees

explication: Comme l'application est en HTTP, on utilise des Application Load Balancers, seuls compatibles avec AWS WAF (protection contre les exploits web). AWS Global Accelerator, avec les ALB en endpoints, ameliore performance et disponibilite mondiales tout en fournissant les adresses IP statiques exigees. WAF ne s'attache pas a un NLB.

question: A company data platform uses an Amazon Aurora MySQL database. The database has multiple read replicas and multiple DB instances across different Availability Zones. Users have recently reported errors from the database that indicate that there are too many connections. The company wants to reduce the failover time by 20% when a read replica is promoted to primary writer. Which solution will meet this requirement?

options.A: Switch from Aurora to Amazon RDS with Multi-AZ cluster deployment.
options.B: Use Amazon RDS Proxy in front of the Aurora database.
options.C: Switch to Amazon DynamoDB with DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) for read connections.
options.D: Switch to Amazon Redshift with relocation capability.

declencheurs: reduce failover time by 20% when a replica is promoted
radar.signal: Trop de connexions + failover plus rapide -> Amazon RDS Proxy devant Aurora

pieges.A: Passer d'Aurora a RDS Multi-AZ n'accelere pas le failover ni ne gere les connexions
pieges.C: DynamoDB/DAX change le modele de donnees
pieges.D: Redshift est un entrepot analytique, hors sujet

explication: RDS Proxy mutualise les connexions (resolvant les erreurs 'too many connections') et, en gerant le pool de connexions, reduit le temps de bascule lors de la promotion d'un replica en primaire. C'est la solution qui traite a la fois la saturation des connexions et l'objectif de failover plus rapide.

question: A financial services company launched a new application that uses an Amazon RDS for MySQL database. The company uses the application to track stock market trends. The company needs to operate the application for only 2 hours at the end of each week. The company needs to optimize the cost of running the database. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

options.A: Migrate the existing RDS for MySQL database to an Aurora Serverless v2 MySQL database cluster.
options.B: Migrate the existing RDS for MySQL database to an Aurora MySQL database cluster.
options.C: Migrate the existing RDS for MySQL database to an Amazon EC2 instance that runs MySQL. Purchase an instance reservation for the EC2 instance.
options.D: Migrate the existing RDS for MySQL database to an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster that uses MySQL container images to run tasks.

declencheurs: app runs only 2 hours at end of each week
radar.signal: Base utilisee tres ponctuellement -> Aurora Serverless v2 (MySQL) qui ajuste/reduit la capacite quand inutilisee

pieges.B: Aurora provisionne facture en continu meme inutilise
pieges.C: EC2 MySQL reserve facture en permanence
pieges.D: ECS avec des conteneurs MySQL = gestion et cout continus

explication: Comme la base ne sert que 2 heures par semaine, Aurora Serverless v2 ajuste automatiquement la capacite a la charge et la reduit quand l'application est inactive, minimisant le cout. Les options provisionnees (Aurora, EC2 reserve, ECS) facturent des ressources en continu.

question: A company deploys its applications on Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) behind an Application Load Balancer in an AWS Region. The application needs to store data in a PostgreSQL database engine. The company wants the data in the database to be highly available. The company also needs increased capacity for read workloads. Which solution will meet these requirements with the MOST operational efficiency?

options.A: Create an Amazon DynamoDB database table configured with global tables.
options.B: Create an Amazon RDS database with Multi-AZ deployments.
options.C: Create an Amazon RDS database with Multi-AZ DB cluster deployment.
options.D: Create an Amazon RDS database configured with cross-Region read replicas.

radar.signal: HA + lectures accrues en PostgreSQL manage -> Amazon RDS Multi-AZ DB cluster deployment (standby lisibles)

pieges.A: DynamoDB n'est pas PostgreSQL (changement de modele)
pieges.B: Un Multi-AZ 'instance' standard offre la HA mais son standby n'est pas lisible
pieges.D: Des cross-Region read replicas ajoutent de la complexite cross-Region non demandee

explication: Le mode Multi-AZ DB cluster d'Amazon RDS fournit la haute disponibilite ET des instances standby lisibles, ce qui augmente la capacite de lecture sans ajouter de composants. Le Multi-AZ 'instance' (B) a un standby non lisible, et DynamoDB n'est pas PostgreSQL.

question: A company is building a new dynamic ordering website. The company wants to minimize server maintenance and patching. The website must be highly available and must scale read and write capacity as quickly as possible to meet changes in user demand. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Host static content in Amazon S3. Host dynamic content by using Amazon API Gateway and AWS Lambda. Use Amazon DynamoDB with on-demand capacity for the database. Configure Amazon CloudFront to deliver the website content.
options.B: Host static content in Amazon S3. Host dynamic content by using Amazon API Gateway and AWS Lambda. Use Amazon Aurora with Aurora Auto Scaling for the database. Configure Amazon CloudFront to deliver the website content.
options.C: Host all the website content on Amazon EC2 instances. Create an Auto Scaling group to scale the EC2 instances. Use an Application Load Balancer to distribute traffic. Use Amazon DynamoDB with provisioned write capacity for the database.
options.D: Host all the website content on Amazon EC2 instances. Create an Auto Scaling group to scale the EC2 instances. Use an Application Load Balancer to distribute traffic. Use Amazon Aurora with Aurora Auto Scaling for the database.

declencheurs: scale read AND write as quickly as possible
radar.signal: Serverless + scaling instantane lecture/ecriture -> S3 (statique) + API Gateway/Lambda (dynamique) + DynamoDB on-demand + CloudFront

pieges.B: Aurora Auto Scaling ajoute surtout des replicas de lecture, moins immediat que DynamoDB on-demand pour l'ecriture
pieges.C: EC2 + DynamoDB provisioned = serveurs a gerer et ecriture non elastique instantanee
pieges.D: EC2 + Aurora = serveurs a maintenir et scaling moins immediat

explication: Une architecture entierement serverless (S3 + API Gateway/Lambda + DynamoDB on-demand + CloudFront) supprime la maintenance de serveurs et scale instantanement en lecture comme en ecriture grace au mode on-demand de DynamoDB. Aurora Auto Scaling (B) est surtout oriente lectures et moins immediat pour l'ecriture.

question: A company has an AWS account used for software engineering. The AWS account has access to the company's on-premises data center through a pair of AWS Direct Connect connections. All non-VPC traffic routes to the virtual private gateway. A development team recently created an AWS Lambda function through the console. The development team needs to allow the function to access a database that runs in a private subnet in the company's data center. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Configure the Lambda function to run in the VPC with the appropriate security group.
options.B: Set up a VPN connection from AWS to the data center. Route the traffic from the Lambda function through the VPN.
options.C: Update the route tables in the VPC to allow the Lambda function to access the on-premises data center through Direct Connect.
options.D: Create an Elastic IP address. Configure the Lambda function to send traffic through the Elastic IP address without an elastic network interface.

declencheurs: Lambda must access on-prem DB in private subnet
account has Direct Connect + virtual private gateway
radar.signal: Faire passer le trafic Lambda par le VPC/DX -> configurer la Lambda dans le VPC avec le security group approprie

pieges.B: Un VPN est inutile : Direct Connect existe deja
pieges.C: Modifier des route tables ne suffit pas si la Lambda n'est pas dans le VPC
pieges.D: Une Elastic IP sans ENI ne permet pas a la Lambda de router via le VPC/DX

explication: En configurant la fonction Lambda pour s'executer dans le VPC (avec un security group adapte), son trafic emprunte le routage du VPC : le trafic non-VPC part vers le virtual private gateway et donc vers le data center via Direct Connect. Aucun VPN supplementaire n'est necessaire.

question: Organizers for a global event want to put daily reports online as static HTML pages. The pages are expected to generate millions of views from users around the world. The files are stored in an Amazon S3 bucket. A solutions architect has been asked to design an efficient and effective solution. Which action should the solutions architect take to accomplish this?

options.A: Generate presigned URLs for the files.
options.B: Use cross-Region replication to all Regions.
options.C: Use the geoproximity feature of Amazon Route 53.
options.D: Use Amazon CloudFront with the S3 bucket as its origin.

radar.signal: Diffuser du statique mondialement en dechargeant l'origine -> Amazon CloudFront avec le bucket S3 en origine

pieges.A: Des presigned URLs servent a l'acces temporaire, pas a diffuser massivement du contenu public
pieges.B: Repliquer dans toutes les Regions est couteux et complexe
pieges.C: Le geoproximity de Route 53 route le DNS, il ne cache pas le contenu

explication: Amazon CloudFront, avec le bucket S3 en origine, met en cache les pages HTML statiques aux points de presence proches des utilisateurs, servant des millions de vues mondiales a faible latence tout en dechargeant l'origine. Les presigned URLs et la replication multi-Region ne repondent pas a une diffusion publique massive.

question: A company runs a production application on a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances. The application reads the data from an Amazon SQS queue and processes the messages in parallel. The message volume is unpredictable and often has intermittent traffic. This application should continually process messages without any downtime. Which solution meets these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

options.A: Use Spot Instances exclusively to handle the maximum capacity required.
options.B: Use Reserved Instances exclusively to handle the maximum capacity required.
options.C: Use Reserved Instances for the baseline capacity and use Spot Instances to handle additional capacity.
options.D: Use Reserved Instances for the baseline capacity and use On-Demand Instances to handle additional capacity.

declencheurs: reads from SQS, processes in parallel
radar.signal: Base garantie sans interruption + surcapacite economique -> Reserved Instances pour la base + Spot pour la capacite supplementaire

pieges.A: Spot exclusif risque des interruptions sur toute la charge (downtime possible)
pieges.B: Reserved pour la capacite MAX paie en permanence une capacite rarement utilisee
pieges.D: On-Demand pour le supplement coute plus cher que Spot

explication: Des Reserved Instances couvrent la capacite de base (traitement continu garanti sans downtime), et des Spot Instances absorbent les pics intermittents a bas cout. Comme le traitement lit une file SQS et tolere que des Spot supplementaires disparaissent, c'est le meilleur compromis cout/continuite.

question: A company is migrating its on-premises workload to the AWS Cloud. The company already uses several Amazon EC2 instances and Amazon RDS DB instances. The company wants a solution that automatically starts and stops the EC2 instances and DB instances outside of business hours. The solution must minimize cost and infrastructure maintenance. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Scale the EC2 instances by using elastic resize. Scale the DB instances to zero outside of business hours.
options.B: Explore AWS Marketplace for partner solutions that will automatically start and stop the EC2 instances and DB instances on a schedule.
options.C: Launch another EC2 instance. Configure a crontab schedule to run shell scripts that will start and stop the existing EC2 instances and DB instances on a schedule.
options.D: Create an AWS Lambda function that will start and stop the EC2 instances and DB instances. Configure Amazon EventBridge to invoke the Lambda function on a schedule.

declencheurs: start/stop EC2 and RDS outside business hours
radar.signal: Demarrer/arreter sur planning sans serveur -> Lambda declenchee par Amazon EventBridge sur horaire

pieges.A: L'elastic resize/'scale to zero' ne correspond pas au demarrage/arret planifie d'EC2/RDS
pieges.B: Une solution Marketplace partenaire ajoute cout et dependance
pieges.C: Un EC2 avec crontab = une instance a maintenir en permanence

explication: Une fonction Lambda qui demarre et arrete les instances EC2 et RDS, declenchee par Amazon EventBridge selon un planning, est entierement serverless : aucun serveur a maintenir. C'est plus economique et moins d'infrastructure qu'un EC2 avec crontab ou une solution Marketplace.

question: A company hosts a three-tier web application that includes a PostgreSQL database. The database stores the metadata from documents. The company searches the metadata for key terms to retrieve documents that the company reviews in a report each month. The documents are stored in Amazon S3. The documents are usually written only once, but they are updated frequently. The reporting process takes a few hours with the use of relational queries. The reporting process must not prevent any document modifications or the addition of new documents. A solutions architect needs to implement a solution to speed up the reporting process. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST amount of change to the application code?

options.A: Set up a new Amazon DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility) cluster that includes a read replica. Scale the read replica to generate the reports.
options.B: Set up a new Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL DB cluster that includes an Aurora Replica. Issue queries to the Aurora Replica to generate the reports.
options.C: Set up a new Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL Multi-AZ DB instance. Configure the reporting module to query the secondary RDS node so that the reporting module does not affect the primary node.
options.D: Set up a new Amazon DynamoDB table to store the documents. Use a fixed write capacity to support new document entries. Automatically scale the read capacity to support the reports.

radar.signal: Decharger les rapports sans bloquer les ecritures, en restant PostgreSQL -> Aurora PostgreSQL + Aurora Replica interrogee pour les rapports

pieges.A: DocumentDB (MongoDB) change le modele de donnees relationnel
pieges.C: Le secondaire d'un RDS Multi-AZ 'instance' n'est pas interrogeable
pieges.D: DynamoDB abandonne le relationnel (les requetes relationnelles ne fonctionnent plus)

explication: En migrant vers Aurora PostgreSQL (compatible, donc peu de changements de code) et en dirigeant les requetes de reporting vers une Aurora Replica, le rapport mensuel s'execute sans bloquer les ecritures/ajouts de documents sur le primaire. Le standby d'un RDS Multi-AZ n'est pas lisible, et DocumentDB/DynamoDB changeraient le modele.

question: A company needs to ingest and handle large amounts of streaming data that its application generates. The application runs on Amazon EC2 instances and sends data to Amazon Kinesis Data Streams, which is configured with default settings. Every other day, the application consumes the data and writes the data to an Amazon S3 bucket for business intelligence (BI) processing. The company observes that Amazon S3 is not receiving all the data that the application sends to Kinesis Data Streams. What should a solutions architect do to resolve this issue?

options.A: Update the Kinesis Data Streams default settings by modifying the data retention period.
options.B: Update the application to use the Kinesis Producer Library (KPL) to send the data to Kinesis Data Streams.
options.C: Update the number of Kinesis shards to handle the throughput of the data that is sent to Kinesis Data Streams.
options.D: Turn on S3 Versioning within the S3 bucket to preserve every version of every object that is ingested in the S3 bucket.

radar.signal: Perte de donnees car debit > capacite des shards -> augmenter le nombre de shards Kinesis

pieges.A: Modifier la retention garde les donnees plus longtemps, mais ne resout pas le debit insuffisant
pieges.B: La KPL ameliore l'envoi mais ne cree pas la capacite de shards manquante
pieges.D: Le versioning S3 ne recupere pas des donnees jamais arrivees dans le stream

explication: Avec les reglages par defaut, le stream n'a pas assez de shards pour absorber le debit : des enregistrements sont throttled/perdus avant d'atteindre S3. Augmenter le nombre de shards accroit le debit et permet de capter toutes les donnees. La retention ou le versioning ne resolvent pas un manque de capacite d'ingestion.

question: A developer has an application that uses an AWS Lambda function to upload files to Amazon S3 and needs the required permissions to perform the task. The developer already has an IAM user with valid IAM credentials required for Amazon S3. What should a solutions architect do to grant the permissions?

options.A: Add required IAM permissions in the resource policy of the Lambda function.
options.B: Create a signed request using the existing IAM credentials in the Lambda function.
options.C: Create a new IAM user and use the existing IAM credentials in the Lambda function.
options.D: Create an IAM execution role with the required permissions and attach the IAM role to the Lambda function.

radar.signal: Donner des permissions a une Lambda -> role d'execution IAM avec les permissions requises, attache a la fonction

pieges.A: La resource policy de Lambda controle qui l'invoque, pas ses permissions vers S3
pieges.B: Une signed request avec des cles IAM = secrets a gerer (mauvaise pratique)
pieges.C: Reutiliser des cles d'un IAM user dans le code expose des secrets

explication: Le mecanisme correct est un role d'execution IAM avec les permissions S3 requises, attache a la fonction Lambda : elle obtient des identifiants temporaires automatiquement, sans cles en dur. La resource policy ne gere que l'invocation, et reutiliser des cles d'un IAM user exposerait des secrets.

question: A company observes an increase in Amazon EC2 costs in its most recent bill. The billing team notices unwanted vertical scaling of instance types on a couple of EC2 instances. A solutions architect needs to create a graph comparing the last 2 months of EC2 costs and perform an in-depth analysis to identify the root cause of the vertical scaling. How should the solutions architect generate the information with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.A: Use AWS Budgets to create a budget report and compare EC2 costs based on instance types.
