options.B: Use Cost Explorer granular filtering feature to perform an in-depth analysis of EC2 costs based on instance types.
options.C: Use graphs from the AWS Billing and Cost Management dashboard to compare EC2 costs based on instance types for the last 2 months.
options.D: Use AWS Cost and Usage Reports to create a report and send it to an Amazon S3 bucket. Use Amazon QuickSight with Amazon S3 as a source to generate an interactive graph based on instance types.

declencheurs: compare last 2 months of EC2 costs
radar.signal: Analyse fine des couts EC2 par type d'instance -> filtrage granulaire d'AWS Cost Explorer

pieges.A: AWS Budgets alerte sur des seuils, il ne fait pas d'analyse comparative fine
pieges.C: Les graphes du dashboard Billing sont moins detailles que le filtrage Cost Explorer
pieges.D: CUR + QuickSight = beaucoup plus de mise en place pour le meme resultat

explication: Cost Explorer permet, sans configuration lourde, de comparer les couts EC2 des deux derniers mois et d'appliquer un filtrage granulaire par type d'instance pour identifier la cause du scaling vertical. CUR + QuickSight donnerait le meme resultat au prix d'une mise en place bien plus lourde.

question: A company is designing an application. The application uses an AWS Lambda function to receive information through Amazon API Gateway and to store the information in an Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL database. During the proof-of-concept stage, the company has to increase the Lambda quotas significantly to handle the high volumes of data that the company needs to load into the database. A solutions architect must recommend a new design to improve scalability and minimize the configuration effort. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Refactor the Lambda function code to Apache Tomcat code that runs on Amazon EC2 instances. Connect the database by using native Java Database Connectivity (JDBC) drivers.
options.B: Change the platform from Aurora to Amazon DynamoDB. Provision a DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) cluster. Use the DAX client SDK to point the existing DynamoDB API calls at the DAX cluster.
options.C: Set up two Lambda functions. Configure one function to receive the information. Configure the other function to load the information into the database. Integrate the Lambda functions by using Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS).
options.D: Set up two Lambda functions. Configure one function to receive the information. Configure the other function to load the information into the database. Integrate the Lambda functions by using an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue.

declencheurs: API Gateway + Lambda writes to Aurora PostgreSQL
had to raise Lambda quotas for high data volumes
radar.signal: Decoupler reception et chargement pour lisser les pics -> deux Lambda integrees par une file SQS (tampon)

pieges.A: Refactorer en Tomcat sur EC2 = beaucoup de changements et d'infrastructure
pieges.B: Passer a DynamoDB/DAX change le modele de donnees relationnel
pieges.C: SNS (pub/sub) ne tamponne pas de facon durable comme SQS

explication: En separant la reception et le chargement en deux Lambda reliees par une file SQS, la file absorbe les gros volumes et regule le rythme d'ecriture vers Aurora, evitant d'avoir a relever fortement les quotas Lambda. SNS ne tamponne pas durablement, et refactorer/changer de base serait bien plus intrusif.

question: A financial services company that runs on AWS has designed its security controls to meet industry standards. The industry standards include the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) and the Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard (PCI DSS). The company's third-party auditors need proof that the designed controls have been implemented and are functioning correctly. The company has hundreds of AWS accounts in a single organization in AWS Organizations. The company needs to monitor the current state of the controls across accounts. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Designate one account as the Amazon Inspector delegated administrator account from the Organizations management account. Integrate Inspector with Organizations to discover and scan resources across all AWS accounts. Enable Inspector industry standards for NIST and PCI DSS.
options.B: Designate one account as the Amazon GuardDuty delegated administrator account from the Organizations management account. In the designated GuardDuty administrator account, enable GuardDuty to protect all member accounts. Enable GuardDuty industry standards for NIST and PCI DSS.
options.C: Configure an AWS CloudTrail organization trail in the Organizations management account. Designate one account as the compliance account. Enable CloudTrail security standards for NIST and PCI DSS in the compliance account.
options.D: Designate one account as the AWS Security Hub delegated administrator account from the Organizations management account. In the designated Security Hub administrator account, enable Security Hub for all member accounts. Enable Security Hub standards for NIST and PCI DSS.

declencheurs: monitor current state of controls across accounts
radar.signal: Etat de conformite aux standards a travers tous les comptes -> AWS Security Hub (delegated admin) avec standards NIST et PCI DSS actives pour tous les membres

pieges.A: Inspector scanne des vulnerabilites, il n'evalue pas la conformite aux standards NIST/PCI
pieges.B: GuardDuty detecte des menaces, pas la conformite aux controles
pieges.C: CloudTrail journalise des evenements, il n'evalue pas l'etat des controles

explication: AWS Security Hub agrege et evalue en continu la conformite aux standards de securite (dont NIST et PCI DSS) sur tous les comptes. En designant un compte administrateur delegue et en activant Security Hub pour tous les membres, l'entreprise obtient l'etat des controles a fournir aux auditeurs. Inspector/GuardDuty/CloudTrail ne mesurent pas la conformite aux standards.

question: A company uses an Amazon S3 bucket as its data lake storage platform. The S3 bucket contains a massive amount of data that is accessed randomly by multiple teams and hundreds of applications. The company wants to reduce the S3 storage costs and provide immediate availability for frequently accessed objects. What is the MOST operationally efficient solution that meets these requirements?

options.A: Create an S3 Lifecycle rule to transition objects to the S3 Intelligent-Tiering storage class.
options.B: Store objects in Amazon S3 Glacier. Use S3 Select to provide applications with access to the data.
options.C: Use data from S3 storage class analysis to create S3 Lifecycle rules to automatically transition objects to the S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) storage class.
options.D: Transition objects to the S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) storage class. Create an AWS Lambda function to transition objects to the S3 Standard storage class when they are accessed by an application.

radar.signal: Pattern d'acces aleatoire/imprevisible -> Lifecycle vers S3 Intelligent-Tiering

pieges.B: Glacier n'offre pas la disponibilite immediate des objets frequemment consultes
pieges.C: Storage class analysis + regles Standard-IA suppose un acces peu frequent connu et ajoute du travail
pieges.D: Transitionner vers IA puis remonter via Lambda a l'acces = solution complexe a maintenir

explication: S3 Intelligent-Tiering deplace automatiquement chaque objet entre paliers selon son usage reel, sans frais de recuperation, en gardant les objets frequemment consultes immediatement disponibles. Pour un acces aleatoire et imprevisible, c'est la solution la plus efficace, sans analyse ni Lambda a maintenir.

question: A 5-year-old media company is using the AWS Organizations all features feature set to organize its AWS accounts. According to the company's finance team, the billing information on the member accounts must not be accessible to anyone, including the root user of the member accounts. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Add all finance team users to an IAM group. Attach an AWS managed policy named Billing to the group.
options.B: Attach an identity-based policy to deny access to the billing information to all users, including the root user.
options.C: Create a service control policy (SCP) to deny access to the billing information. Attach the SCP to the root organizational unit (OU).
options.D: Convert from the Organizations all features feature set to the Organizations consolidated billing feature set.

declencheurs: billing info of member accounts not accessible to anyone including root
radar.signal: Interdire l'acces a la facturation meme au root des comptes membres -> Service Control Policy (SCP) de refus attachee a l'OU racine

pieges.A: Attacher une policy Billing a un groupe donne au contraire l'acces
pieges.B: Une policy identity-based ne s'applique pas au root et n'empeche pas son acces
pieges.D: Passer en consolidated billing feature set perd les SCP (all features) necessaires ici

explication: Seule une Service Control Policy (disponible avec le feature set 'all features') peut restreindre les principals des comptes membres, y compris leur root user. En attachant une SCP qui refuse l'acces aux informations de facturation a l'OU racine, personne dans les comptes membres, meme root, n'y accede. Les policies identity-based ne s'appliquent pas au root.

question: An ecommerce company runs an application in the AWS Cloud that is integrated with an on-premises warehouse solution. The company uses Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) to send order messages to an on-premises HTTPS endpoint so the warehouse application can process the orders. The local data center team has detected that some of the order messages were not received. A solutions architect needs to retain messages that are not delivered and analyze the messages for up to 14 days. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST development effort?

options.A: Configure an Amazon SNS dead letter queue that has an Amazon Kinesis Data Stream target with a retention period of 14 days.
options.B: Add an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue with a retention period of 14 days between the application and Amazon SNS.
options.C: Configure an Amazon SNS dead letter queue that has an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) target with a retention period of 14 days.
options.D: Configure an Amazon SNS dead letter queue that has an Amazon DynamoDB target with a TTL attribute set for a retention period of 14 days.

declencheurs: retain undelivered + analyze up to 14 days
radar.signal: Conserver et analyser les messages SNS non delivres -> dead letter queue SNS avec cible SQS (retention 14 jours)

pieges.A: Une DLQ SNS cible une file SQS, pas directement un Kinesis Data Stream
pieges.B: Ajouter une SQS entre l'app et SNS ne capture pas les echecs de livraison vers l'endpoint on-prem
pieges.D: Une DLQ SNS ne cible pas DynamoDB (mecanisme incorrect)

explication: Une dead letter queue SNS adossee a une file Amazon SQS (retention 14 jours) capture automatiquement les messages qui n'ont pas pu etre delivres a l'endpoint HTTPS on-prem, permettant de les conserver et de les analyser. C'est natif et sans developpement. La DLQ SNS ne cible ni Kinesis ni DynamoDB.

question: A company wants to send all AWS Systems Manager Session Manager logs to an Amazon S3 bucket for archival purposes. Which solution will meet this requirement with the MOST operational efficiency?

options.A: Enable S3 logging in the Systems Manager console. Choose an S3 bucket to send the session data to.
options.B: Install the Amazon CloudWatch agent. Push all logs to a CloudWatch log group. Export the logs to an S3 bucket from the group for archival purposes.
options.C: Create a Systems Manager document to upload all server logs to a central S3 bucket. Use Amazon EventBridge to run the Systems Manager document against all servers that are in the account daily.
options.D: Install an Amazon CloudWatch agent. Push all logs to a CloudWatch log group. Create a CloudWatch logs subscription that pushes any incoming log events to an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream. Set Amazon S3 as the destination.

radar.signal: Archiver les logs Session Manager dans S3 -> activer le logging S3 dans la console Systems Manager (choisir le bucket)

pieges.B: Agent CloudWatch + export = plus d'etapes que le logging S3 natif
pieges.C: Un document SSM lance par EventBridge quotidiennement = solution custom
pieges.D: Agent CloudWatch + subscription + Firehose = pipeline complexe

explication: Session Manager propose nativement l'envoi des logs de session vers un bucket S3 : il suffit d'activer le logging S3 dans la console et de choisir le bucket. C'est le plus efficace, sans agent, pipeline ou document custom a maintenir.

question: An application uses an Amazon RDS MySQL DB instance. The RDS database is becoming low on disk space. A solutions architect wants to increase the disk space without downtime. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST amount of effort?

options.A: Enable storage autoscaling in RDS.
options.B: Increase the RDS database instance size.
options.C: Change the RDS database instance storage type to Provisioned IOPS.
options.D: Back up the RDS database, increase the storage capacity, restore the database, and stop the previous instance.

radar.signal: Augmenter l'espace disque RDS sans interruption -> activer le storage autoscaling

pieges.B: Changer la taille de l'instance concerne le calcul, pas l'espace disque, et peut interrompre
pieges.C: Passer en Provisioned IOPS ameliore les IOPS, pas l'espace
pieges.D: Backup/restore/increase = beaucoup d'effort et du downtime

explication: Le storage autoscaling d'RDS augmente automatiquement l'espace de stockage quand il se remplit, sans interruption ni intervention. C'est le moindre effort, contrairement a un changement d'instance (calcul) ou a un cycle backup/restore manuel.

question: A company deploys an application on five Amazon EC2 instances. An Application Load Balancer (ALB) distributes traffic to the instances by using a target group. The average CPU usage on each of the instances is below 10% most of the time, with occasional surges to 65%. A solutions architect needs to implement a solution to automate the scalability of the application. The solution must optimize the cost of the architecture and must ensure that the application has enough CPU resources when surges occur. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm that enters the ALARM state when the CPUUtilization metric is less than 20%. Create an AWS Lambda function that the CloudWatch alarm invokes to terminate one of the EC2 instances in the ALB target group.
options.B: Create an EC2 Auto Scaling group. Select the existing ALB as the load balancer and the existing target group as the target group. Set a target tracking scaling policy that is based on the ASGAverageCPUUtilization metric. Set the minimum instances to 2, the desired capacity to 3, the maximum instances to 6, and the target value to 50%. Add the EC2 instances to the Auto Scaling group.
options.C: Create an EC2 Auto Scaling group. Select the existing ALB as the load balancer and the existing target group as the target group. Set the minimum instances to 2, the desired capacity to 3, and the maximum instances to 6. Add the EC2 instances to the Auto Scaling group.
options.D: Create two Amazon CloudWatch alarms. Configure the first CloudWatch alarm to enter the ALARM state when the average CPUUtilization metric is below 20%. Configure the second CloudWatch alarm to enter the ALARM state when the average CPUUtilization metric is above 50%. Configure the alarms to publish to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic to send an email message. After receiving the message, log in to decrease or increase the number of EC2 instances that are running.

declencheurs: optimize cost + enough CPU on surge
radar.signal: Scaler automatiquement selon le CPU tout en optimisant le cout -> EC2 Auto Scaling group (ALB/target group existants) + target tracking sur ASGAverageCPUUtilization (min 2, desired 3, max 6, cible 50%)

pieges.A: Une alarme qui termine des instances a <20% ne scale pas a la hausse lors des pics
pieges.C: Un ASG sans policy de scaling ne s'ajuste pas automatiquement a la charge
pieges.D: Des alarmes qui envoient un email pour agir a la main n'automatisent rien

explication: Un Auto Scaling group reutilisant l'ALB et le target group, avec une target tracking policy sur le CPU moyen (cible 50%, min 2/desired 3/max 6), reduit le nombre d'instances quand le CPU est bas (cout optimise) et en ajoute lors des pics a 65% (CPU suffisant), le tout automatiquement. Les alarmes manuelles (D) ou sans policy (C) n'automatisent pas le scaling.

question: A company is running a critical business application on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. The EC2 instances run in an Auto Scaling group and access an Amazon RDS DB instance. The design did not pass an operational review because the EC2 instances and the DB instance are all located in a single Availability Zone. A solutions architect must update the design to use a second Availability Zone. Which solution will make the application highly available?

options.A: Provision a subnet in each Availability Zone. Configure the Auto Scaling group to distribute the EC2 instances across both Availability Zones. Configure the DB instance with connections to each network.
options.B: Provision two subnets that extend across both Availability Zones. Configure the Auto Scaling group to distribute the EC2 instances across both Availability Zones. Configure the DB instance with connections to each network.
options.C: Provision a subnet in each Availability Zone. Configure the Auto Scaling group to distribute the EC2 instances across both Availability Zones. Configure the DB instance for Multi-AZ deployment.
options.D: Provision a subnet that extends across both Availability Zones. Configure the Auto Scaling group to distribute the EC2 instances across both Availability Zones. Configure the DB instance for Multi-AZ deployment.

declencheurs: EC2 + RDS all in a single AZ
radar.signal: Rendre l'ensemble HA sur deux AZ -> un subnet par AZ + ASG reparti sur les deux AZ + RDS en Multi-AZ

pieges.A: Configurer la DB 'avec des connexions a chaque reseau' n'est pas la HA d'RDS (c'est Multi-AZ)
pieges.B: Un subnet ne peut pas s'etendre sur deux AZ (un subnet = une AZ)
pieges.D: Un subnet ne peut pas s'etendre sur deux AZ

explication: Un subnet appartient a une seule AZ : on cree donc un subnet dans chaque AZ, on repartit les instances de l'Auto Scaling group sur les deux, et on configure la base en RDS Multi-AZ (bascule automatique vers un standby dans l'autre AZ). Les options parlant d'un subnet 's'etendant sur deux AZ' sont techniquement impossibles.

question: A company has implemented a self-managed DNS service on AWS. The solution consists of the following: - Amazon EC2 instances in different AWS Regions. - Endpoints of a standard accelerator in AWS Global Accelerator. The company wants to protect the solution against DDoS attacks. What should a solutions architect do to meet this requirement?

options.A: Subscribe to AWS Shield Advanced. Add the accelerator as a resource to protect.
options.B: Subscribe to AWS Shield Advanced. Add the EC2 instances as resources to protect.
options.C: Create an AWS WAF web ACL that includes a rate-based rule. Associate the web ACL with the accelerator.
options.D: Create an AWS WAF web ACL that includes a rate-based rule. Associate the web ACL with the EC2 instances.

radar.signal: Proteger contre les DDoS une solution derriere Global Accelerator -> AWS Shield Advanced, en ajoutant l'accelerateur comme ressource protegee

pieges.B: Proteger les EC2 individuellement est moins pertinent que proteger le point d'entree (l'accelerateur)
pieges.C: AWS WAF ne s'associe pas a un Global Accelerator (et cible le HTTP applicatif)
pieges.D: WAF ne s'associe pas a des EC2 directement

explication: AWS Shield Advanced protege contre les DDoS et prend en charge AWS Global Accelerator comme ressource protegee. En ajoutant l'accelerateur (le point d'entree) comme ressource, on couvre l'ensemble de la solution. AWS WAF ne s'associe pas a un accelerateur, et proteger chaque EC2 est moins pertinent.

question: An ecommerce company needs to run a scheduled daily job to aggregate and filter sales records for analytics. The company stores the sales records in an Amazon S3 bucket. Each object can be up to 10 GB in size. Based on the number of sales events, the job can take up to an hour to complete. The CPU and memory usage of the job are constant and are known in advance. A solutions architect needs to minimize the amount of operational effort that is needed for the job to run. Which solution meets these requirements?

options.A: Create an AWS Lambda function that has an Amazon EventBridge notification. Schedule the EventBridge event to run once a day.
options.B: Create an AWS Lambda function. Create an Amazon API Gateway HTTP API and integrate the API with the function. Create an Amazon EventBridge scheduled event that calls the API and invokes the function.
options.C: Create an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster with an AWS Fargate launch type. Create an Amazon EventBridge scheduled event that launches an ECS task on the cluster to run the job.
options.D: Create an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster with an Amazon EC2 launch type and an Auto Scaling group with at least one EC2 instance. Create an Amazon EventBridge scheduled event that launches an ECS task on the cluster to run the job.

radar.signal: Job planifie long (1h) a ressources connues, serverless -> ECS Fargate + evenement EventBridge planifie qui lance une tache ECS

pieges.A: Lambda est limitee a 15 min (le job dure jusqu'a 1h)
pieges.B: Lambda via API Gateway reste bornee a 15 min
pieges.D: ECS avec launch type EC2 impose de gerer des instances (plus d'overhead que Fargate)

explication: Le job pouvant durer jusqu'a une heure, Lambda (max 15 min) est exclu. Une tache ECS en Fargate (serverless, ressources fixes connues) lancee par un evenement EventBridge planifie execute le job quotidien sans gerer de serveurs, contrairement au launch type EC2.

question: A company is running a multi-tier ecommerce web application in the AWS Cloud. The application runs on Amazon EC2 instances with an Amazon RDS for MySQL Multi-AZ DB instance. Amazon RDS is configured with the latest generation DB instance with 2,000 GB of storage in a General Purpose SSD (gp3) Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume. The database performance affects the application during periods of high demand. A database administrator analyzes the logs in Amazon CloudWatch Logs and discovers that the application performance always degrades when the number of read and write IOPS is higher than 20,000. What should a solutions architect do to improve the application performance?

options.A: Replace the volume with a magnetic volume.
options.B: Increase the number of IOPS on the gp3 volume.
options.C: Replace the volume with a Provisioned IOPS SSD (io2) volume.
options.D: Replace the 2,000 GB gp3 volume with two 1,000 GB gp3 volumes.

radar.signal: Besoin d'IOPS au-dela de la limite gp3 (16000) -> volume Provisioned IOPS SSD (io2)

pieges.A: Un volume magnetique est bien plus lent
pieges.B: gp3 plafonne a 16000 IOPS, insuffisant pour >20000
pieges.D: Deux volumes gp3 compliquent l'architecture et restent limites chacun a 16000 IOPS

explication: Un volume gp3 est limite a 16000 IOPS, or l'application a besoin de plus de 20000 IOPS. Un volume Provisioned IOPS SSD (io2) permet de provisionner des IOPS bien superieures (jusqu'a 64000+), resolvant la degradation. Le magnetique ou le decoupage en deux gp3 ne conviennent pas.

question: An IAM user made several configuration changes to AWS resources in their company's account during a production deployment last week. A solutions architect learned that a couple of security group rules are not configured as desired. The solutions architect wants to confirm which IAM user was responsible for making changes. Which service should the solutions architect use to find the desired information?

options.A: Amazon GuardDuty
options.B: Amazon Inspector
options.C: AWS CloudTrail
options.D: AWS Config

declencheurs: which IAM user made configuration changes
security group rules changed last week
radar.signal: Retrouver qui a effectue une action d'API -> AWS CloudTrail (journal des appels d'API)

pieges.A: GuardDuty detecte des menaces, il n'attribue pas des changements a un utilisateur
pieges.B: Inspector scanne des vulnerabilites
pieges.D: AWS Config montre l'historique de configuration, mais CloudTrail identifie l'appelant de l'action

explication: AWS CloudTrail journalise chaque appel d'API avec l'identite du principal qui l'a effectue : c'est le service pour determiner quel IAM user a modifie les regles de security group. Config montre l'evolution de configuration, mais l'attribution de l'action revient a CloudTrail.

question: A company created a new organization in AWS Organizations. The organization has multiple accounts for the company's development teams. The development team members use AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On) to access the accounts. For each of the company's applications, the development teams must use a predefined application name to tag resources that are created. A solutions architect needs to design a solution that gives the development team the ability to create resources only if the application name tag has an approved value. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Create an IAM group that has a conditional Allow policy that requires the application name tag to be specified for resources to be created.
options.B: Create a cross-account role that has a Deny policy for any resource that has the application name tag.
options.C: Create a resource group in AWS Resource Groups to validate that the tags are applied to all resources in all accounts.
options.D: Create a tag policy in Organizations that has a list of allowed application names.

declencheurs: resources tagged with predefined application name
create only if application name tag has an approved value
radar.signal: Imposer des valeurs de tag approuvees a l'echelle de l'organisation -> tag policy dans AWS Organizations avec la liste des noms autorises

pieges.A: Une IAM policy conditionnelle par groupe est plus complexe et non centralisee a l'echelle de l'organisation
pieges.B: Un role cross-account avec Deny ne definit pas des valeurs de tag autorisees
pieges.C: Resource Groups valide/consulte des tags, il ne les impose pas a la creation

explication: Une tag policy dans AWS Organizations definit centralement les valeurs autorisees pour un tag (ici la liste des noms d'application approuves) et empeche la creation de ressources avec une valeur non conforme, sur tous les comptes. C'est plus simple et centralise qu'une IAM policy conditionnelle par groupe.

question: A company runs its databases on Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL. The company wants a secure solution to manage the master user password by rotating the password every 30 days. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.A: Use Amazon EventBridge to schedule a custom AWS Lambda function to rotate the password every 30 days.
options.B: Use the modify-db-instance command in the AWS CLI to change the password.
options.C: Integrate AWS Secrets Manager with Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL to automate password rotation.
options.D: Integrate AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store with Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL to automate password rotation.

radar.signal: Rotation manageee du mot de passe master RDS -> integration AWS Secrets Manager avec RDS for PostgreSQL

pieges.A: EventBridge + Lambda custom = code de rotation a ecrire et maintenir
pieges.B: modify-db-instance en CLI = changement manuel a repeter
pieges.D: Parameter Store n'offre pas la rotation automatique native des identifiants RDS

explication: L'integration native d'AWS Secrets Manager avec Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL gere et fait tourner automatiquement le mot de passe du master user (ici tous les 30 jours), sans code custom. Une Lambda maison ou une commande CLI manuelle demanderaient bien plus d'operations.

question: A company has an AWS Glue extract, transform, and load (ETL) job that runs every day at the same time. The job processes XML data that is in an Amazon S3 bucket. New data is added to the S3 bucket every day. A solutions architect notices that AWS Glue is processing all the data during each run. What should the solutions architect do to prevent AWS Glue from reprocessing old data?

options.A: Edit the job to use job bookmarks.
options.B: Edit the job to delete data after the data is processed.
options.C: Edit the job by setting the NumberOfWorkers field to 1.
options.D: Use a FindMatches machine learning (ML) transform.

radar.signal: Ne traiter que les nouvelles donnees a chaque run Glue -> activer les job bookmarks

pieges.B: Supprimer les donnees traitees est destructif et risque
pieges.C: NumberOfWorkers=1 change la capacite, pas le reprocessing
pieges.D: FindMatches sert au dedoublonnage ML, pas a suivre les donnees deja traitees

explication: Les job bookmarks d'AWS Glue memorisent les donnees deja traitees lors des executions precedentes, si bien que chaque run ne traite que les nouvelles donnees, sans reprocesser l'existant. Supprimer les donnees (B) serait destructif, et FindMatches/NumberOfWorkers ne repondent pas au besoin.

question: A solutions architect must design a highly available infrastructure for a website. The website is powered by Windows web servers that run on Amazon EC2 instances. The solutions architect must implement a solution that can mitigate a large-scale DDoS attack that originates from thousands of IP addresses. Downtime is not acceptable for the website. Which actions should the solutions architect take to protect the website from such an attack? (Choose two.)

options.A: Use AWS Shield Advanced to stop the DDoS attack.
options.B: Configure Amazon GuardDuty to automatically block the attackers.
options.C: Configure the website to use Amazon CloudFront for both static and dynamic content.
options.D: Use an AWS Lambda function to automatically add attacker IP addresses to VPC network ACLs.
options.E: Use EC2 Spot Instances in an Auto Scaling group with a target tracking scaling policy that is set to 80% CPU utilization.

declencheurs: highly available website on Windows EC2
mitigate large-scale DDoS from thousands of IPs
radar.signal: Attenuer une DDoS massive sans downtime -> AWS Shield Advanced (A) + CloudFront pour le contenu statique ET dynamique (C)

pieges.B: GuardDuty detecte des menaces, il ne bloque pas automatiquement une DDoS
pieges.D: Ajouter des IP a des NACL via Lambda = fragile et inefficace face a des milliers d'IP
pieges.E: Des Spot en Auto Scaling ne protegent pas contre une DDoS

explication: AWS Shield Advanced fournit une attenuation DDoS renforcee (A), et servir tout le contenu (statique et dynamique) via Amazon CloudFront absorbe et disperse l'attaque au niveau du reseau edge tout en gardant le site disponible (C). GuardDuty (detection), les NACL via Lambda (fragile) et les Spot (scaling) ne protegent pas d'une DDoS massive.

question: A company is preparing to deploy a new serverless workload. A solutions architect must use the principle of least privilege to configure permissions that will be used to run an AWS Lambda function. An Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) rule will invoke the function. Which solution meets these requirements?

options.A: Add an execution role to the function with lambda:InvokeFunction as the action and * as the principal.
options.B: Add an execution role to the function with lambda:InvokeFunction as the action and Service: lambda.amazonaws.com as the principal.
options.C: Add a resource-based policy to the function with lambda:InvokeFunction as the action and Service: events.amazonaws.com as the principal.
options.D: Add a resource-based policy to the function with lambda:InvokeFunction as the action and Service: events.amazonaws.com as the principal.

radar.signal: Autoriser EventBridge a invoquer la Lambda -> resource-based policy sur la fonction avec l'action lambda:InvokeFunction et le principal Service events.amazonaws.com

pieges.A: Un execution role avec principal '*' viole le moindre privilege
pieges.B: Le principal lambda.amazonaws.com n'est pas EventBridge ; ce n'est pas ainsi qu'on autorise l'invocation
pieges.note: Les options C et D sont identiques dans le dump ; la reponse est cette resource-based policy avec events.amazonaws.com

explication: Pour qu'une regle Amazon EventBridge puisse invoquer la fonction, on ajoute une resource-based policy sur la Lambda autorisant lambda:InvokeFunction pour le principal de service events.amazonaws.com, ce qui respecte le moindre privilege. (Note : les options C et D sont formulees a l'identique dans le dump.)

question: A hospital recently deployed a RESTful API with Amazon API Gateway and AWS Lambda. The hospital uses API Gateway and Lambda to upload reports that are in PDF format and JPEG format. The hospital needs to modify the Lambda code to identify protected health information (PHI) in the reports. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.A: Use existing Python libraries to extract the text from the reports and to identify the PHI from the extracted text.
options.B: Use Amazon Textract to extract the text from the reports. Use Amazon SageMaker to identify the PHI from the extracted text.
options.C: Use Amazon Textract to extract the text from the reports. Use Amazon Comprehend Medical to identify the PHI from the extracted text.
options.D: Use Amazon Rekognition to extract the text from the reports. Use Amazon Comprehend Medical to identify the PHI from the extracted text.

radar.signal: Extraire le texte de documents/images + detecter des PHI -> Amazon Textract (extraction) + Amazon Comprehend Medical (detection de PHI)

pieges.A: Des librairies Python custom = beaucoup de code a ecrire et maintenir
pieges.B: SageMaker imposerait de construire/entrainer un modele (plus d'overhead que Comprehend Medical)
pieges.D: Rekognition est pour l'analyse d'images/objets, pas l'extraction de texte de documents comme Textract

explication: Amazon Textract extrait le texte des PDF et JPEG, et Amazon Comprehend Medical identifie nativement les informations de sante protegees (PHI) dans ce texte. Ces services manages evitent d'ecrire des librairies custom ou d'entrainer un modele SageMaker, d'ou le plus faible overhead.

question: A company has an application that generates a large number of files, each approximately 5 MB in size. The files are stored in Amazon S3. Company policy requires the files to be stored for 4 years before they can be deleted. Immediate accessibility is always required as the files contain critical business data that is not easy to reproduce. The files are frequently accessed in the first 30 days of the object creation but are rarely accessed after the first 30 days. Which storage solution is MOST cost-effective?

options.A: Create an S3 bucket lifecycle policy to move files from S3 Standard to S3 Glacier 30 days from object creation. Delete the files 4 years after object creation.
options.B: Create an S3 bucket lifecycle policy to move files from S3 Standard to S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA) 30 days from object creation. Delete the files 4 years after object creation.
options.C: Create an S3 bucket lifecycle policy to move files from S3 Standard to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) 30 days from object creation. Delete the files 4 years after object creation.
options.D: Create an S3 bucket lifecycle policy to move files from S3 Standard to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) 30 days from object creation. Move the files to S3 Glacier 4 years after object creation.

declencheurs: frequent first 30 days then rarely accessed
radar.signal: Acces immediat + rare apres 30 jours -> Lifecycle vers S3 Standard-IA a 30 jours, suppression a 4 ans

pieges.A: Glacier n'offre pas l'acces immediat exige
pieges.B: One Zone-IA est moins durable/disponible pour des donnees critiques difficiles a reproduire
pieges.D: Passer en Glacier a 4 ans juste avant la suppression n'apporte rien (les fichiers sont supprimes)

explication: Comme l'acces immediat est toujours requis, on ne peut pas utiliser Glacier. S3 Standard-IA offre un acces instantane a moindre cout de stockage pour des donnees rarement consultees apres 30 jours, tout en restant multi-AZ (durabilite pour des donnees critiques). One Zone-IA serait moins durable.

question: A global company runs its applications in multiple AWS accounts in AWS Organizations. The company's applications use multipart uploads to upload data to multiple Amazon S3 buckets across AWS Regions. The company wants to report on incomplete multipart uploads for cost compliance purposes. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.A: Configure AWS Config with a rule to report the incomplete multipart upload object count.
options.B: Create a service control policy (SCP) to report the incomplete multipart upload object count.
options.C: Configure S3 Storage Lens to report the incomplete multipart upload object count.
options.D: Create an S3 Multi-Region Access Point to report the incomplete multipart upload object count.

declencheurs: report on incomplete multipart uploads for cost compliance
radar.signal: Rapport transverse sur les multipart uploads incomplets -> Amazon S3 Storage Lens

pieges.A: AWS Config n'a pas de regle native pour compter les multipart uploads incomplets
pieges.B: Une SCP restreint des actions, elle ne genere pas de rapport
pieges.D: Un Multi-Region Access Point route l'acces, il ne rapporte pas ces metriques

explication: S3 Storage Lens fournit des metriques d'usage et d'activite a l'echelle de l'organisation, dont le nombre d'objets de multipart uploads incomplets, avec des tableaux de bord agreges multi-comptes/multi-Regions. C'est la solution de reporting avec le moins d'overhead.

question: A company runs a production database on Amazon RDS for MySQL. The company wants to upgrade the database version for security compliance reasons. Because the database contains critical data, the company wants a quick solution to upgrade and test functionality without losing any data. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.A: Create an RDS manual snapshot. Upgrade to the new version of Amazon RDS for MySQL.
options.B: Use native backup and restore. Restore the data to the upgraded new version of Amazon RDS for MySQL.
options.C: Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to replicate the data to the upgraded new version of Amazon RDS for MySQL.
options.D: Use Amazon RDS Blue/Green Deployments to deploy and test production changes.

declencheurs: upgrade RDS MySQL version for compliance
quick, test functionality without losing data
radar.signal: Mise a niveau testable sans perte de donnees -> Amazon RDS Blue/Green Deployments

pieges.A: Snapshot + upgrade in-place ne permet pas de tester avant bascule sans effort
pieges.B: Native backup/restore = plus d'etapes manuelles
pieges.C: DMS pour un simple upgrade de version = surdimensionne et plus d'effort

explication: RDS Blue/Green Deployments cree un environnement 'green' (version mise a niveau) synchronise avec la production 'blue', ce qui permet de tester la nouvelle version puis de basculer rapidement avec un minimum d'interruption et sans perte de donnees. C'est le moins d'overhead pour un upgrade teste.

question: A solutions architect wants all new users to have specific complexity requirements and mandatory rotation periods for IAM user passwords. What should the solutions architect do to accomplish this?

options.A: Set an overall password policy for the entire AWS account.
options.B: Set a password policy for each IAM user in the AWS account.
options.C: Use third-party vendor software to set password requirements.
options.D: Attach an Amazon CloudWatch rule to the Create_new_user event to set the password with the appropriate requirements.

declencheurs: password complexity + mandatory rotation for IAM user passwords
radar.signal: Imposer complexite et rotation des mots de passe IAM -> definir une password policy globale au niveau du compte AWS

pieges.B: Il n'existe pas de password policy par utilisateur IAM individuel
pieges.C: Un logiciel tiers est inutile : la fonction est native
pieges.D: Une regle CloudWatch sur la creation d'utilisateur ne definit pas la politique de mot de passe

explication: IAM propose une password policy au niveau du compte qui s'applique a tous les utilisateurs : on y definit la complexite et la periode de rotation obligatoire. Il n'existe pas de politique par utilisateur, et aucun logiciel tiers ni regle CloudWatch n'est necessaire.

question: A company has migrated an application to Amazon EC2 Linux instances. One of these EC2 instances runs several 1-hour tasks on a schedule. These tasks were written by different teams and have no common programming language. The company is concerned about performance and scalability while these tasks run on a single instance. A solutions architect needs to implement a solution to resolve these concerns. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.A: Use AWS Batch to run the tasks as jobs. Schedule the jobs by using Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events).
options.B: Convert the EC2 instance to a container. Use AWS App Runner to create the container on demand to run the tasks as jobs.
options.C: Copy the tasks into AWS Lambda functions. Schedule the Lambda functions by using Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events).
options.D: Create an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) of the EC2 instance that runs the tasks. Create an Auto Scaling group with the AMI to run multiple copies of the instance.

radar.signal: Executer des taches planifiees d'1h, heterogenes, sans gerer de serveur -> AWS Batch (jobs) planifie par Amazon EventBridge

pieges.B: App Runner cible des services web/conteneurs a la demande, pas des jobs batch planifies heterogenes
pieges.C: Lambda est limitee a 15 min (les taches durent 1h)
pieges.D: Une AMI + Auto Scaling group = infrastructure a gerer

explication: AWS Batch execute des jobs conteneurises (quel que soit le langage) en provisionnant et scalant automatiquement le calcul, planifies via Amazon EventBridge. Les taches durant 1h, Lambda (15 min) est exclu, et App Runner/une AMI+ASG n'offrent pas cette execution de jobs batch manageee.

question: A company is migrating a three-tier application to AWS. The application requires a MySQL database. In the past, the application users reported poor application performance when creating new entries. These performance issues were caused by users generating different real-time reports from the application during working hours. Which solution will improve the performance of the application when it is moved to AWS?

options.A: Import the data into an Amazon DynamoDB table with provisioned capacity. Refactor the application to use DynamoDB for reports.
options.B: Create the database on a compute optimized Amazon EC2 instance. Ensure compute resources exceed the on-premises database.
options.C: Create an Amazon Aurora MySQL Multi-AZ DB cluster with multiple read replicas. Configure the application to use the reader endpoint for reports.
options.D: Create an Amazon Aurora MySQL Multi-AZ DB cluster. Configure the application to use the backup instance of the cluster as an endpoint for the reports.

declencheurs: poor performance on new entries caused by real-time reports during working hours
radar.signal: Isoler les rapports des ecritures -> Aurora MySQL Multi-AZ + read replicas, rapports diriges vers le reader endpoint

pieges.A: DynamoDB impose de refactorer l'application (changement de modele)
pieges.B: Un EC2 compute optimized ne separe pas lectures (rapports) et ecritures
pieges.D: L'instance de 'backup' d'un cluster n'est pas un endpoint de lecture (le reader endpoint l'est)

explication: Les rapports en temps reel saturent la base et ralentissent les insertions. Avec Aurora MySQL Multi-AZ et des read replicas, on dirige les rapports vers le reader endpoint, dechargeant le primaire qui gere les nouvelles entrees. L'instance de backup (D) n'est pas un endpoint de lecture, et DynamoDB imposerait une refonte.

question: A company is expanding a secure on-premises network to the AWS Cloud by using an AWS Direct Connect connection. The on-premises network has no direct internet access. An application that runs on the on-premises network needs to use an Amazon S3 bucket. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

options.A: Create a public virtual interface (VIF). Route the AWS traffic over the public VIF.
options.B: Create a VPC and a NAT gateway. Route the AWS traffic from the on-premises network to the NAT gateway.
options.C: Create a VPC and an Amazon S3 interface endpoint. Route the AWS traffic from the on-premises network to the S3 interface endpoint.
options.D: Create a VPC peering connection between the on-premises network and Direct Connect. Route the AWS traffic over the peering connection.

radar.signal: Acces prive a S3 depuis l'on-prem via DX -> VPC + S3 interface endpoint, trafic route depuis l'on-prem vers l'endpoint

pieges.A: Une public VIF expose le trafic AWS publiquement (moins securise, pas 'no internet')
pieges.B: Un NAT gateway passe par Internet (l'on-prem n'a pas d'acces Internet)
pieges.D: Il n'existe pas de 'VPC peering entre on-prem et Direct Connect'

explication: Un VPC avec un interface endpoint pour S3, atteint depuis l'on-prem via la private VIF de Direct Connect, permet d'utiliser S3 de facon privee sans acces Internet. C'est economique et sur. Une public VIF exposerait le trafic, et un NAT gateway ou un 'peering' avec Direct Connect ne conviennent pas.

question: A company has a data ingestion workflow that consists of the following: - An Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic for notifications about new data deliveries. - An AWS Lambda function to process the data and record metadata. The company observes that the ingestion workflow fails occasionally because of network connectivity issues. When such a failure occurs, the Lambda function does not ingest the corresponding data unless the company manually reruns the job. Which combination of actions should a solutions architect take to ensure that the Lambda function ingests all data in the future? (Choose two.)

options.A: Deploy the Lambda function in multiple Availability Zones.
options.B: Create an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue, and subscribe it to the SNS topic.
options.C: Increase the CPU and memory that are allocated to the Lambda function.
options.D: Increase provisioned throughput for the Lambda function.
options.E: Modify the Lambda function to read from an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue.

declencheurs: data not ingested unless manual rerun
radar.signal: Fiabiliser l'ingestion avec un tampon durable et des retries -> file SQS abonnee au topic SNS (B) + Lambda qui lit depuis SQS (E)

pieges.A: Deployer la Lambda sur plusieurs AZ ne conserve pas les messages en cas d'echec
pieges.C: Plus de CPU/memoire n'evite pas la perte lors d'un echec reseau
pieges.D: Augmenter le 'throughput' ne conserve pas les evenements non traites

explication: En intercalant une file SQS abonnee au topic SNS (B) et en faisant lire la Lambda depuis cette file (E), les messages sont conserves de facon durable et retraites automatiquement en cas d'echec, sans rerun manuel. Ajuster CPU/memoire ou les AZ ne protege pas contre la perte d'evenements.

question: A company has an application that provides marketing services to stores. The services are based on previous purchases by store customers. The stores upload transaction data to the company through SFTP and the data is processed and analyzed to generate new marketing offers. Some of the files can exceed 200 GB in size. Recently, the company discovered that some of the stores have uploaded files that contain personally identifiable information (PII) that should not have been included. The company wants administrators to be alerted if PII is shared again. The company also wants to automate remediation. What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements with the LEAST development effort?

options.A: Use an Amazon S3 bucket as a secure transfer point. Use Amazon Inspector to scan the objects in the bucket. If objects contain PII, trigger an S3 Lifecycle policy to remove the objects that contain PII.
options.B: Use an Amazon S3 bucket as a secure transfer point. Use Amazon Macie to scan the objects in the bucket. If objects contain PII, use Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) to trigger a notification to the administrators to remove the objects that contain PII.
options.C: Implement custom scanning algorithms in an AWS Lambda function. Trigger the function when objects are loaded into the bucket. If objects contain PII, use Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) to trigger a notification to the administrators to remove the objects that contain PII.
options.D: Implement custom scanning algorithms in an AWS Lambda function. Trigger the function when objects are loaded into the bucket. If objects contain PII, use Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES) to trigger a notification to the administrators and trigger an S3 Lifecycle policy to remove the objects that contain PII.

declencheurs: files via SFTP up to 200 GB
radar.signal: Detecter des PII dans S3 + alerter -> bucket S3 comme point de transfert + Amazon Macie pour scanner + notification Amazon SNS aux administrateurs

pieges.A: Amazon Inspector scanne des vulnerabilites, pas des PII dans des objets
pieges.C: Des algorithmes de scan custom en Lambda = beaucoup de developpement
pieges.D: Idem : scan custom en Lambda = effort de developpement eleve

explication: En utilisant un bucket S3 comme point de transfert et Amazon Macie pour decouvrir les PII, on detecte automatiquement les fichiers concernes ; une notification Amazon SNS alerte alors les administrateurs. Macie evite d'ecrire des algorithmes de scan custom (Lambda), d'ou le moindre effort de developpement. Inspector ne detecte pas les PII.

question: A company has an aging network attached storage (NAS) array in its data center. The NAS array presents SMB shares and NFS shares to client workstations. The company does not want to purchase a new NAS array. The company also does not want to incur the cost of renewing the NAS array support contract. Some of the data is accessed frequently, but much of the data is inactive. A solutions architect needs to implement a solution that migrates the data to Amazon S3, uses S3 Lifecycle policies, and maintains the same look and feel for the client workstations. The solutions architect has identified AWS Storage Gateway as part of the solution. Which type of storage gateway should the solutions architect provision to meet these requirements?

options.A: Volume Gateway
options.B: Tape Gateway
options.C: Amazon FSx File Gateway
options.D: Amazon S3 File Gateway

declencheurs: aging NAS presenting SMB and NFS
same look and feel for workstations
radar.signal: Remplacer un NAS SMB/NFS par du stockage S3 avec cycles de vie, sans changer l'usage -> Amazon S3 File Gateway

pieges.A: Le Volume Gateway est du block iSCSI, pas des partages de fichiers SMB/NFS
pieges.B: Le Tape Gateway emule des bandes de sauvegarde, pas des partages de fichiers
pieges.C: Le FSx File Gateway donne acces a FSx, pas a S3 avec Lifecycle policies

explication: Un Amazon S3 File Gateway presente des partages de fichiers (NFS/SMB) aux postes de travail tout en stockant les donnees dans S3, ou des Lifecycle policies deplacent les donnees inactives vers des classes moins cheres. Les clients gardent le meme mode d'acces. Le Volume Gateway (block) et le Tape Gateway (bandes) ne conviennent pas.

question: A company has an application that is running on Amazon EC2 instances. A solutions architect has standardized the company on a particular instance family and various instance sizes based on the current needs of the company. The company wants to maximize cost savings for the application over the next 3 years. The company needs to be able to change the instance family and sizes in the next 6 months based on application popularity and usage. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

options.A: Compute Savings Plan
options.B: EC2 Instance Savings Plan
options.C: Zonal Reserved Instances
options.D: Standard Reserved Instances

declencheurs: may change instance family AND sizes in 6 months
radar.signal: Economies sur 3 ans mais liberte de changer famille/taille -> Compute Savings Plan (le plus flexible)

pieges.B: L'EC2 Instance Savings Plan verrouille une famille d'instances
pieges.C: Les Zonal Reserved Instances figent le type et l'AZ
pieges.D: Les Standard Reserved Instances figent la famille (peu de flexibilite)

explication: Le Compute Savings Plan offre la remise sur 3 ans tout en laissant changer librement la famille, la taille, l'OS, la Region ou meme passer a Fargate/Lambda. C'est le seul qui autorise le changement de famille prevu dans 6 mois, contrairement a l'EC2 Instance Savings Plan ou aux Reserved Instances qui figent la famille.

question: A company experienced a breach that affected several applications in its on-premises data center. The attacker took advantage of vulnerabilities in the custom applications that were running on the servers. The company is now migrating its applications to run on Amazon EC2 instances. The company wants to implement a solution that actively scans for vulnerabilities on the EC2 instances and sends a report that details the findings. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Deploy AWS Shield to scan the EC2 instances for vulnerabilities. Create an AWS Lambda function to log any findings to AWS CloudTrail.
options.B: Deploy Amazon Macie and AWS Lambda functions to scan the EC2 instances for vulnerabilities. Log any findings to AWS CloudTrail.
options.C: Turn on Amazon GuardDuty. Deploy the GuardDuty agents to the EC2 instances. Configure an AWS Lambda function to automate the generation and distribution of reports that detail the findings.
options.D: Turn on Amazon Inspector. Deploy the Amazon Inspector agent to the EC2 instances. Configure an AWS Lambda function to automate the generation and distribution of reports that detail the findings.

radar.signal: Scanner activement les vulnerabilites des EC2 + rapport -> Amazon Inspector (agent) + Lambda pour generer/distribuer les rapports

pieges.A: AWS Shield protege des DDoS, il ne scanne pas de vulnerabilites
pieges.B: Macie decouvre des donnees sensibles, pas des vulnerabilites d'instances
pieges.C: GuardDuty detecte des menaces, il ne scanne pas les CVE des instances

explication: Amazon Inspector analyse en continu les instances EC2 a la recherche de vulnerabilites (CVE) et de configurations a risque. Une fonction Lambda automatise la generation et la distribution des rapports de findings. Shield (DDoS), Macie (donnees sensibles) et GuardDuty (menaces) ne scannent pas les vulnerabilites d'instances.

question: A company uses an Amazon EC2 instance to run a script to poll for and process messages in an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. The company wants to reduce operational costs while maintaining its ability to process a growing number of messages that are added to the queue. What should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?

options.A: Increase the size of the EC2 instance to process messages faster.
options.B: Use Amazon EventBridge to turn off the EC2 instance when the instance is underutilized.
options.C: Migrate the script on the EC2 instance to an AWS Lambda function with the appropriate runtime.
options.D: Use AWS Systems Manager Run Command to run the script on demand.

declencheurs: EC2 polls SQS and processes messages
process a growing number of messages
radar.signal: Remplacer un EC2 de polling par du serverless scalable -> migrer le script vers une fonction AWS Lambda

pieges.A: Agrandir l'EC2 augmente le cout et reste une instance a gerer
pieges.B: Eteindre l'EC2 quand sous-utilise ne traite plus les messages
pieges.D: Run Command execute a la demande, il ne remplace pas un traitement continu et scalable

explication: En migrant le script vers AWS Lambda (declenchee par la file SQS), on supprime l'instance EC2 (reduction de cout) et le traitement scale automatiquement avec le nombre de messages, sans serveur a gerer. Agrandir ou eteindre l'EC2 ne repond pas au besoin de scalabilite economique.

question: A company wants to use an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL DB cluster to simplify time-consuming database administrative tasks for production database workloads. The company wants to ensure that its database is highly available and will provide automatic failover support in most scenarios in less than 40 seconds. The company wants to offload reads off of the primary instance and keep costs as low as possible. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Use an Amazon RDS Multi-AZ DB instance deployment. Create one read replica and point the read workload to the read replica.
options.B: Use an Amazon RDS Multi-AZ DB cluster deployment. Create two read replicas and point the read workload to the read replicas.
options.C: Use an Amazon RDS Multi-AZ DB instance deployment. Point the read workload to the secondary instances in the Multi-AZ pair.
options.D: Use an Amazon RDS Multi-AZ DB cluster deployment. Point the read workload to the reader endpoint.

declencheurs: automatic failover in most scenarios < 40 seconds
keep costs as low as possible
radar.signal: Failover < 40 s + lectures dechargees + cout maitrise -> RDS Multi-AZ DB cluster deployment, lectures via le reader endpoint

pieges.A: Un Multi-AZ DB instance bascule en 60-120 s (ne tient pas les <40 s)
pieges.B: Le Multi-AZ DB cluster inclut deja des standby lisibles ; ajouter deux read replicas augmente le cout
pieges.C: Le standby d'un Multi-AZ DB instance n'est pas lisible

alerte_cle: La cle du fichier indique A, mais un Multi-AZ DB instance bascule en 60-120 s, ce qui ne respecte pas l'exigence de failover en moins de 40 s. Le Multi-AZ DB cluster (bascule ~35 s, standby lisibles) est requis : reponse D.
explication: Un failover en moins de 40 secondes est la signature du deploiement RDS Multi-AZ DB cluster (typiquement ~35 s), alors qu'un Multi-AZ DB instance bascule en 60-120 s. Le cluster fournit en plus deux standby lisibles : en pointant les lectures vers le reader endpoint, on decharge le primaire sans ajouter de read replica, gardant le cout bas.

question: A company runs a highly available SFTP service. The SFTP service uses two Amazon EC2 Linux instances that use Elastic IP addresses to accept traffic from trusted IP sources on the internet. The SFTP service is backed by shared storage that is attached to the instances. User accounts are created and managed as Linux users on the SFTP servers. The company wants a serverless option that provides high IOPS performance and highly configurable security. The company also wants to maintain control over user permissions. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Create an encrypted Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume. Create an AWS Transfer Family SFTP service with a public endpoint that allows only trusted IP addresses. Attach the EBS volume to the SFTP service endpoint. Grant users access to the SFTP service.
options.B: Create an encrypted Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) volume. Create an AWS Transfer Family SFTP service with Elastic IP addresses and a VPC endpoint that has internet-facing access. Attach a security group to the endpoint that allows only trusted IP addresses. Attach the EFS volume to the SFTP service endpoint. Grant users access to the SFTP service.
options.C: Create an Amazon S3 bucket with default encryption enabled. Create an AWS Transfer Family SFTP service with a public endpoint that allows only trusted IP addresses. Attach the S3 bucket to the SFTP service endpoint. Grant users access to the SFTP service.
options.D: Create an Amazon S3 bucket with default encryption enabled. Create an AWS Transfer Family SFTP service with a VPC endpoint that has internal access in a private subnet. Attach a security group that allows only trusted IP addresses. Attach the S3 bucket to the SFTP service endpoint. Grant users access to the SFTP service.

radar.signal: SFTP serverless, scalable et securise -> bucket S3 (chiffrement par defaut) + AWS Transfer Family SFTP avec endpoint public limite aux IP de confiance

pieges.A: Un volume EBS ne s'attache pas a un service Transfer Family et n'est pas 'serverless'
pieges.B: EFS + Elastic IP + VPC endpoint = montage complexe non standard pour Transfer Family
pieges.D: Un endpoint VPC en subnet prive n'accepte pas le trafic Internet des sources de confiance

explication: AWS Transfer Family fournit un service SFTP serverless et hautement disponible ; adosse a un bucket S3 (chiffrement par defaut, IOPS eleves et scalables), avec un endpoint public restreint aux IP de confiance et une gestion fine des permissions utilisateurs. EBS/EFS ne conviennent pas comme stockage d'un service Transfer Family de cette maniere.

question: A company is building an application on AWS that connects to an Amazon RDS database. The company wants to manage the application configuration and to securely store and retrieve credentials for the database and other services. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST administrative overhead?

options.A: Use AWS AppConfig to store and manage the application configuration. Use AWS Secrets Manager to store and retrieve the credentials.
options.B: Use AWS Lambda to store and manage the application configuration. Use AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store to store and retrieve the credentials.
options.C: Use an encrypted application configuration file. Store the file in Amazon S3 for the application configuration. Create another S3 file to store and retrieve the credentials.
options.D: Use AWS AppConfig to store and manage the application configuration. Use Amazon RDS to store and retrieve the credentials.

declencheurs: securely store/retrieve DB and service credentials
radar.signal: Configuration applicative + secrets manages -> AWS AppConfig (config) + AWS Secrets Manager (identifiants)

pieges.B: Lambda ne 'stocke' pas la configuration ; Parameter Store gere des parametres mais sans rotation native comme Secrets Manager
pieges.C: Des fichiers chiffres dans S3 = gestion manuelle
pieges.D: RDS n'est pas un magasin d'identifiants securise

explication: AWS AppConfig gere et deploie la configuration applicative, et AWS Secrets Manager stocke et fait tourner les identifiants (base et autres services) de facon securisee. Cette combinaison manageee minimise l'administration, contrairement aux fichiers S3 chiffres ou a un stockage maison.

question: To meet security requirements, a company needs to encrypt all of its application data in transit while communicating with an Amazon RDS MySQL DB instance. A recent security audit revealed that encryption at rest is enabled using AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS), but data in transit is not enabled. What should a solutions architect do to satisfy the security requirements?

options.A: Enable IAM database authentication on the database.
options.B: Provide self-signed certificates. Use the certificates in all connections to the RDS instance.
options.C: Take a snapshot of the RDS instance. Restore the snapshot to a new instance with encryption enabled.
options.D: Download AWS-provided root certificates. Provide the certificates in all connections to the RDS instance.

declencheurs: encrypt data IN TRANSIT to RDS MySQL
radar.signal: Chiffrer en transit vers RDS -> telecharger les certificats racine fournis par AWS et les utiliser dans toutes les connexions (TLS/SSL)

pieges.A: L'authentification IAM concerne l'acces, pas le chiffrement en transit
pieges.B: Des certificats auto-signes ne sont pas la methode AWS pour le TLS RDS
pieges.C: Snapshot/restore avec chiffrement concerne le repos, pas le transit

explication: Pour chiffrer les donnees en transit vers RDS, on telecharge les certificats racine fournis par AWS (bundle CA) et on configure les connexions clientes pour utiliser SSL/TLS avec ces certificats. L'authentification IAM (acces) et le snapshot chiffre (repos) ne repondent pas au chiffrement en transit.

question: A company application uses Network Load Balancers, Auto Scaling groups, Amazon EC2 instances, and databases that are deployed in an Amazon VPC. The company wants to capture information about traffic to and from the network interfaces in near real time in its Amazon VPC. The company wants to send the information to Amazon OpenSearch Service for analysis. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Create a log group in Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Configure VPC Flow Logs to send the log data to the log group. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to stream the logs from the log group to OpenSearch Service.
options.B: Create a log group in Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Configure VPC Flow Logs to send the log data to the log group. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to stream the logs from the log group to OpenSearch Service.
options.C: Create a trail in AWS CloudTrail. Configure VPC Flow Logs to send the log data to the trail. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to stream the logs from the trail to OpenSearch Service.
options.D: Create a trail in AWS CloudTrail. Configure VPC Flow Logs to send the log data to the trail. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to stream the logs from the trail to OpenSearch Service.

declencheurs: capture traffic to/from network interfaces in near real time
radar.signal: Flux de VPC Flow Logs vers OpenSearch -> CloudWatch Logs (Flow Logs) + Kinesis Data Firehose vers OpenSearch

pieges.A: Kinesis Data Streams necessite plus de code pour livrer vers OpenSearch que Firehose (livraison manageee)
pieges.C: CloudTrail journalise des appels d'API, pas le trafic reseau (VPC Flow Logs ne s'envoient pas a un trail)
pieges.D: Idem : les VPC Flow Logs ne se configurent pas vers un trail CloudTrail

explication: Les VPC Flow Logs capturent le trafic des interfaces reseau et s'envoient a un log group CloudWatch Logs. Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose livre ensuite ces logs vers OpenSearch Service de facon manageee (sans code). Kinesis Data Streams demanderait plus de developpement, et CloudTrail ne capture pas le trafic reseau.

question: A company is developing an application that will run on a production Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster. The EKS cluster has managed node groups that are provisioned with On-Demand Instances. The company needs a dedicated EKS cluster for development work. The company will use the development cluster infrequently to test the resiliency of the application. The EKS cluster must manage all the nodes. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

options.A: Create a managed node group that contains only Spot Instances.
options.B: Create two managed node groups. Provision one node group with On-Demand Instances. Provision the second node group with Spot Instances.
options.C: Create an Auto Scaling group that has a launch configuration that uses Spot Instances. Configure the user data to add the nodes to the EKS cluster.
options.D: Create a managed node group that contains only On-Demand Instances.

radar.signal: Cluster de dev peu utilise, tolerant aux interruptions, manage -> managed node group compose uniquement de Spot Instances

pieges.B: Melanger On-Demand et Spot coute plus cher qu'un groupe 100% Spot pour du dev
pieges.C: Un Auto Scaling group avec user data n'est pas un managed node group (EKS ne gere pas tout)
pieges.D: Un groupe 100% On-Demand est le plus cher

explication: Pour un cluster de developpement utilise rarement et destine a tester la resilience (donc tolerant aux interruptions), un managed node group compose uniquement de Spot Instances est le plus economique, tout en laissant EKS gerer les noeuds. Un Auto Scaling group custom (C) ne serait pas un managed node group.

question: A company stores text files in Amazon S3. The text files include customer chat messages, date and time information, and customer personally identifiable information (PII). The company needs a solution to provide samples of the conversations to an external service provider for quality control. The external service provider needs to randomly pick sample conversations up to the most recent conversation. The company must not share the customer PII with the external service provider. The solution must scale when the number of customer conversations increases. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.A: Create an Object Lambda Access Point. Create an AWS Lambda function that redacts the PII when the function reads the file. Instruct the external service provider to access the Object Lambda Access Point.
options.B: Create a batch process on an Amazon EC2 instance that regularly reads all new files, redacts the PII from the files, and writes the redacted files to a different S3 bucket. Instruct the external service provider to access the bucket that does not contain the PII.
options.C: Create a web application on an Amazon EC2 instance that presents a list of the files, redacts the PII from the files, and allows the external service provider to download new versions of the files that have the PII redacted.
options.D: Create an Amazon DynamoDB table. Create an AWS Lambda function that reads only the data in the files that does not contain PII. Configure the Lambda function to store the non-PII data in the DynamoDB table when a new file is written to Amazon S3. Grant the external service provider access to the DynamoDB table.

declencheurs: provide sample conversations to external provider
radar.signal: Expurger les PII a la lecture, sans copie -> S3 Object Lambda Access Point + Lambda qui redige les PII

pieges.B: Un batch EC2 qui reecrit des fichiers redacted dans un autre bucket = infrastructure et duplication
pieges.C: Une web app EC2 = serveur a gerer
pieges.D: Copier les donnees non-PII dans DynamoDB = pipeline custom a maintenir

explication: Un S3 Object Lambda Access Point invoque une fonction Lambda qui expurge les PII au moment ou le fichier est lu : le prestataire accede aux conversations sans jamais voir les PII, sans dupliquer ni transformer les donnees a l'avance. Ca scale automatiquement et evite tout serveur ou pipeline a maintenir.

question: A company is running a legacy system on an Amazon EC2 instance. The application code cannot be modified, and the system cannot run on more than one instance. A solutions architect must design a resilient solution that can improve the recovery time for the system. What should the solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?

options.A: Enable termination protection for the EC2 instance.
options.B: Configure the EC2 instance for Multi-AZ deployment.
options.C: Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm to recover the EC2 instance in case of failure.
options.D: Launch the EC2 instance with two Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes that use RAID configurations for storage redundancy.

declencheurs: legacy on a single EC2, code cannot be modified
cannot run on more than one instance
radar.signal: Ameliorer le temps de reprise d'une instance unique -> alarme Amazon CloudWatch de recovery de l'EC2 en cas de panne

pieges.A: La termination protection empeche la suppression, elle n'accelere pas la reprise
pieges.B: Le 'Multi-AZ' ne s'applique pas a une EC2 mono-instance (l'app ne peut pas tourner sur plusieurs)
pieges.D: Le RAID EBS ameliore le stockage, pas la reprise de l'instance

explication: Comme l'application ne peut tourner que sur une seule instance et n'est pas modifiable, une alarme CloudWatch configuree pour recuperer automatiquement l'instance EC2 en cas de defaillance materielle ameliore le temps de reprise, sans changer l'application. La termination protection ou le RAID ne traitent pas la reprise.

question: A company wants to migrate its three-tier application from on premises to AWS. The web tier and the application tier are running on third-party virtual machines (VMs). The database tier is running on MySQL. The company needs to migrate the application by making the fewest possible changes to the architecture. The company also needs a database solution that can restore data to a specific point in time. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.A: Migrate the web tier and the application tier to Amazon EC2 instances in private subnets. Migrate the database tier to Amazon RDS for MySQL in private subnets.
options.B: Migrate the web tier to Amazon EC2 instances in public subnets. Migrate the application tier to EC2 instances in private subnets. Migrate the database tier to Amazon Aurora MySQL in private subnets.
options.C: Migrate the web tier to Amazon EC2 instances in public subnets. Migrate the application tier to EC2 instances in private subnets. Migrate the database tier to Amazon RDS for MySQL in private subnets.
options.D: Migrate the web tier and the application tier to Amazon EC2 instances in public subnets. Migrate the database tier to Amazon Aurora MySQL in public subnets.

radar.signal: Rehost avec peu de changements + PITR manage -> web et app sur EC2 (subnets prives) + base sur Amazon RDS for MySQL

pieges.B: Aurora MySQL est un moteur different (plus de changements que RDS for MySQL)
pieges.C: Placement different mais Aurora dans les autres options ; ici RDS for MySQL suffit et change le moins
pieges.D: Une base en subnet public est un risque de securite

explication: En migrant le web et l'application vers des EC2 (subnets prives) et la base vers Amazon RDS for MySQL, on conserve le meme moteur MySQL (changements minimes) et on beneficie du point-in-time restore natif d'RDS. Aurora impliquerait un moteur different, et placer la base en subnet public serait moins securise.

question: A development team is collaborating with another company to create an integrated product. The other company needs to access an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue that is contained in the development team's account. The other company wants to poll the queue without giving up its own account permissions to do so. How should a solutions architect provide access to the SQS queue?

options.A: Create an instance profile that provides the other company access to the SQS queue.
options.B: Create an IAM policy that provides the other company access to the SQS queue.
options.C: Create an SQS access policy that provides the other company access to the SQS queue.
options.D: Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) access policy that provides the other company access to the SQS queue.

declencheurs: other company polls our SQS queue
without giving up its own account permissions
radar.signal: Autoriser un autre compte a acceder a une file SQS -> SQS access policy (resource-based) accordant l'acces a ce compte

pieges.A: Un instance profile s'applique a des EC2, pas a un acces cross-account a SQS
pieges.B: Une IAM policy s'attache a des identites de NOTRE compte, elle n'accorde pas l'acces a un autre compte a la file
pieges.D: Une access policy SNS ne concerne pas la file SQS

explication: Une SQS access policy (resource-based) attachee a la file peut accorder l'acces a un autre compte AWS, qui l'interroge avec ses propres identifiants sans y renoncer. Les IAM policies s'attachent aux identites de notre compte, et un instance profile/SNS ne conviennent pas a ce partage cross-account de la file.

question: A company has applications that run on Amazon EC2 instances in a VPC. One of the applications needs to call the Amazon S3 API to store and read objects. According to the company's security regulations, no traffic from the applications is allowed to travel across the internet. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Configure an S3 gateway endpoint.
options.B: Create an S3 bucket in a private subnet.
options.C: Create an S3 bucket in the same AWS Region as the EC2 instances.
options.D: Configure a NAT gateway in the same subnet as the EC2 instances.

declencheurs: EC2 in VPC call S3 API
no traffic allowed across the internet
radar.signal: Acces prive a S3 depuis un VPC -> gateway endpoint S3

pieges.B: Un bucket n'est pas 'dans un subnet' (S3 est un service regional)
pieges.C: La meme Region ne rend pas l'acces prive (le trafic peut passer par Internet)
pieges.D: Un NAT gateway achemine justement le trafic via Internet

explication: Un gateway endpoint pour S3 ajoute une route privee vers S3 via le reseau AWS, si bien que le trafic ne traverse jamais Internet. Un bucket n'appartient pas a un subnet, la meme Region ne garantit pas la confidentialite du chemin, et un NAT gateway sort sur Internet.

question: A company is storing sensitive user information in an Amazon S3 bucket. The company wants to provide secure access to this bucket from the application tier running on Amazon EC2 instances inside a VPC. Which combination of steps should a solutions architect take to accomplish this? (Choose two.)

options.A: Configure a VPC gateway endpoint for Amazon S3 within the VPC.
options.B: Create a bucket policy to make the objects in the S3 bucket public.
options.C: Create a bucket policy that limits access to only the application tier running in the VPC.
options.D: Create an IAM user with an S3 access policy and copy the IAM credentials to the EC2 instance.
options.E: Create a NAT instance and have the EC2 instances use the NAT instance to access the S3 bucket.

declencheurs: EC2 in VPC secure access to S3
radar.signal: Acces prive et restreint a S3 -> gateway endpoint S3 dans le VPC (A) + bucket policy limitant l'acces au tier applicatif du VPC (C)

pieges.B: Rendre les objets publics est l'oppose de la securite
pieges.D: Copier des cles IAM sur l'EC2 = secrets a gerer (mauvaise pratique)
pieges.E: Une NAT instance route via Internet et n'ajoute pas de restriction fine

explication: Un gateway endpoint pour S3 permet un acces prive depuis le VPC (A), et une bucket policy qui limite l'acces au tier applicatif (par ex. via le VPC endpoint ou le role des EC2) restreint qui peut lire les donnees sensibles (C). Rendre le bucket public ou copier des cles IAM serait insecure.

question: A company is developing an ecommerce application that will consist of a load-balanced front end, a container-based application, and a relational database. A solutions architect needs to create a highly available solution that operates with as little manual intervention as possible. Which solutions meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.A: Create an Amazon RDS DB instance in Multi-AZ mode.
