options.B: Create an Amazon RDS DB instance and one or more replicas in another Availability Zone.
options.C: Create an Amazon EC2 instance-based Docker cluster to handle the dynamic application load.
options.D: Create an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster with a Fargate launch type to handle the dynamic application load.
options.E: Create an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster with an Amazon EC2 launch type to handle the dynamic application load.

declencheurs: load-balanced front end + container app + relational DB
radar.signal: HA sans gestion manuelle -> Amazon RDS Multi-AZ (A) + cluster ECS en Fargate pour la charge conteneurisee (D)

pieges.B: Des replicas dans une autre AZ (au lieu de Multi-AZ) impliquent une bascule manuelle
pieges.C: Un cluster Docker sur EC2 auto-gere = intervention/maintenance manuelle
pieges.E: ECS avec launch type EC2 = instances a gerer

explication: Amazon RDS en Multi-AZ fournit une base relationnelle hautement disponible avec bascule automatique (A), et un cluster ECS en Fargate execute les conteneurs sans gerer d'instances, avec scaling automatique (D). Les replicas manuels ou les clusters Docker/ECS sur EC2 demanderaient de l'intervention et de la maintenance.

question: A company uses Amazon S3 as its data lake. The company has a new partner that must use SFTP to upload data files. A solutions architect needs to implement a highly available SFTP solution that minimizes operational overhead. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Use AWS Transfer Family to configure an SFTP-enabled server with a publicly accessible endpoint. Choose the S3 data lake as the destination.
options.B: Use Amazon S3 File Gateway as an SFTP server. Expose the S3 File Gateway endpoint URL to the new partner. Share the S3 File Gateway endpoint with the new partner.
options.C: Launch an Amazon EC2 instance in a private subnet in a VPC. Instruct the new partner to upload files to the EC2 instance by using a VPN. Run a cron job script on the EC2 instance to upload files to the S3 data lake.
options.D: Launch Amazon EC2 instances in a private subnet in a VPC. Place a Network Load Balancer (NLB) in front of the EC2 instances. Create an SFTP listener port for the NLB. Share the NLB hostname with the new partner. Run a cron job script on the EC2 instances to upload files to the S3 data lake.

declencheurs: partner uploads via SFTP to S3 data lake
radar.signal: SFTP manage et HA vers S3 -> AWS Transfer Family (serveur SFTP, endpoint public) avec le data lake S3 en destination

pieges.B: S3 File Gateway n'est pas un serveur SFTP
pieges.C: Un EC2 + VPN + cron = infrastructure a gerer et non HA nativement
pieges.D: Des EC2 derriere un NLB + cron = beaucoup d'overhead et de maintenance

explication: AWS Transfer Family fournit un serveur SFTP manage et hautement disponible, avec un endpoint public, qui depose directement les fichiers dans le data lake S3. C'est le minimum d'overhead, contrairement aux options a base d'EC2, NLB, VPN et scripts cron a exploiter.

question: An ecommerce company wants to use machine learning (ML) algorithms to build and train models. The company will use the models to visualize complex scenarios and to detect trends in customer data. The architecture team wants to integrate its ML models with a reporting platform to analyze the augmented data and use the data directly in its business intelligence dashboards. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.A: Use AWS Glue to create an ML transform to build and train models. Use Amazon OpenSearch Service to visualize the data.
options.B: Use Amazon SageMaker to build and train models. Use Amazon QuickSight to visualize the data.
options.C: Use a pre-built ML Amazon Machine Image (AMI) from the AWS Marketplace to build and train models. Use Amazon OpenSearch Service to visualize the data.
options.D: Use Amazon QuickSight to build and train models by using calculated fields. Use Amazon QuickSight to visualize the data.

radar.signal: Construire/entrainer des modeles ML manages + BI -> Amazon SageMaker (modeles) + Amazon QuickSight (visualisation)

pieges.A: Glue ML transform est limite (surtout FindMatches), pas une plateforme ML complete ; OpenSearch n'est pas de la BI
pieges.C: Une AMI ML du Marketplace = infrastructure a gerer
pieges.D: QuickSight avec des champs calcules ne construit pas et n'entraine pas des modeles ML

explication: Amazon SageMaker est le service manage pour construire et entrainer des modeles ML, et Amazon QuickSight fournit la visualisation/BI avec integration des donnees augmentees. Une AMI ML imposerait de gerer des serveurs, et QuickSight seul ne construit pas de modeles ML.

question: A company is running its production and nonproduction environment workloads in multiple AWS accounts. The accounts are in an organization in AWS Organizations. The company needs to design a solution that will prevent the modification of cost usage tags. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Create a custom AWS Config rule to prevent tag modification except by authorized principals.
options.B: Create a custom trail in AWS CloudTrail to prevent tag modification.
options.C: Create a service control policy (SCP) to prevent tag modification except by authorized principals.
options.D: Create custom Amazon CloudWatch logs to prevent tag modification.

declencheurs: prevent modification of cost usage tags
radar.signal: Empecher la modification de tags a l'echelle de l'organisation -> Service Control Policy (SCP) refusant la modification sauf par des principals autorises

pieges.A: AWS Config detecte/evalue, il n'empeche pas la modification
pieges.B: Un trail CloudTrail journalise, il ne bloque pas
pieges.D: Des logs CloudWatch enregistrent, ils n'empechent rien

explication: Une Service Control Policy dans AWS Organizations peut refuser les actions de modification des tags (sauf pour des principals explicitement autorises) sur tous les comptes. C'est un garde-fou preventif, contrairement a Config/CloudTrail/CloudWatch qui ne font que detecter ou journaliser.

question: An image-hosting company stores its objects in Amazon S3 buckets. The company wants to avoid accidental exposure of the objects in the S3 buckets to the public. All S3 objects in the entire AWS account need to remain private. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Use Amazon GuardDuty to monitor S3 bucket policies. Create an automatic remediation action rule that uses an AWS Lambda function to remediate any change that makes the objects public.
options.B: Use AWS Trusted Advisor to find publicly accessible S3 buckets. Configure email notifications in Trusted Advisor when a change is detected. Manually change the S3 bucket policy if it allows public access.
options.C: Use AWS Resource Access Manager to find publicly accessible S3 buckets. Use Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) to invoke an AWS Lambda function when a change is detected. Deploy a Lambda function that programmatically remediates the change.
options.D: Use the S3 Block Public Access feature on the account level. Use AWS Organizations to create a service control policy (SCP) that prevents IAM users from changing the setting. Apply the SCP to the account.

declencheurs: avoid accidental public exposure of S3 objects
ALL objects in the entire account must remain private
radar.signal: Garantir que tous les objets restent prives -> S3 Block Public Access au niveau du compte + SCP empechant la modification du reglage

pieges.A: GuardDuty ne surveille pas/ne remedie pas les policies de bucket publiques
pieges.B: Trusted Advisor + correction manuelle = reactif, pas preventif a l'echelle du compte
pieges.C: Resource Access Manager ne detecte pas les buckets publics

explication: Activer S3 Block Public Access au niveau du compte empeche toute exposition publique des objets. Une SCP AWS Organizations qui interdit de modifier ce reglage garantit qu'aucun utilisateur IAM ne peut le desactiver. C'est preventif et couvre tout le compte, contrairement aux approches de detection/remediation reactives.

question: An ecommerce company is experiencing an increase in user traffic. The company store is deployed on Amazon EC2 instances as a two-tier web application consisting of a web tier and a separate database tier. As traffic increases, the company notices that the architecture is causing significant delays in sending timely marketing and order confirmation email to users. The company wants to reduce the time it spends resolving complex email delivery issues and minimize operational overhead. What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

options.A: Create a separate application tier using EC2 instances dedicated to email processing.
options.B: Configure the web instance to send email through Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES).
options.C: Configure the web instance to send email through Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS).
options.D: Create a separate application tier using EC2 instances dedicated to email processing. Place the instances in an Auto Scaling group.

declencheurs: delays sending marketing and order confirmation emails
reduce time resolving email delivery issues
radar.signal: Deleguer l'envoi d'emails a un service manage -> Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES)

pieges.A: Un tier EC2 dedie aux emails = infrastructure et gestion de la deliverabilite a la charge de l'entreprise
pieges.C: SNS envoie des notifications/messages, ce n'est pas un service d'email transactionnel comme SES
pieges.D: Un tier EC2 en Auto Scaling ne resout pas la complexite de deliverabilite des emails

explication: Amazon SES est un service manage d'envoi d'emails (marketing et transactionnels comme les confirmations de commande) qui gere la deliverabilite, la mise a l'echelle et la reputation. En configurant les instances web pour envoyer via SES, l'entreprise reduit le temps passe sur les problemes d'email sans gerer d'infrastructure dediee.

question: A company has an AWS Direct Connect connection from its on-premises location to an AWS account. The AWS account has 30 different VPCs in the same AWS Region. The VPCs use private virtual interfaces (VIFs). Each VPC has a CIDR block that does not overlap with other networks under the company's control. The company wants to centrally manage the networking architecture while still allowing each VPC to communicate with all other VPCs and on-premises networks. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST amount of operational overhead?

options.A: Create a transit gateway, and associate the Direct Connect connection with a new transit VIF. Turn on the transit gateway route propagation feature.
options.B: Create a Direct Connect gateway. Recreate the private VIFs to use the new gateway. Associate each VPC by creating new virtual private gateways.
options.C: Create a transit VPC. Connect the Direct Connect connection to the transit VPC. Create a peering connection between all other VPCs in the Region. Update the route tables.
options.D: Create AWS Site-to-Site VPN connections from on premises to each VPC. Ensure that both VPN tunnels are UP for each connection. Turn on the route propagation feature.

declencheurs: each VPC communicates with all VPCs and on-prem
radar.signal: Interconnexion centralisee VPC + on-prem via DX -> Transit Gateway associe a la Direct Connect (transit VIF) + propagation des routes

pieges.B: Un Direct Connect gateway + virtual private gateways par VPC ne fait pas communiquer les VPC entre eux facilement
pieges.C: Un transit VPC + peering de tous les VPC = maillage a gerer
pieges.D: Des VPN Site-to-Site vers chaque VPC = 30 connexions a exploiter

explication: Un Transit Gateway centralise le routage : en l'associant a la connexion Direct Connect via une transit VIF et en activant la propagation des routes, les 30 VPC communiquent entre eux et avec l'on-prem depuis un point de gestion unique. Le Direct Connect gateway, le peering ou des VPN par VPC ajouteraient beaucoup d'administration.

question: A company has applications that run on Amazon EC2 instances. The EC2 instances connect to Amazon RDS databases by using an IAM role that has associated policies. The company wants to use AWS Systems Manager to patch the EC2 instances without disrupting the running applications. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Create a new IAM role. Attach the AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore policy to the new IAM role. Attach the new IAM role to the EC2 instances and the existing IAM role.
options.B: Create an IAM user. Attach the AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore policy to the IAM user. Configure Systems Manager to use the IAM user to manage the EC2 instances.
options.C: Enable Default Host Configuration Management in Systems Manager to manage the EC2 instances.
options.D: Remove the existing policies from the existing IAM role. Add the AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore policy to the existing IAM role.

declencheurs: EC2 already use an IAM role for RDS
radar.signal: Ajouter les permissions SSM sans casser l'acces RDS existant -> nouveau role IAM avec AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore, attache en plus du role existant

pieges.B: Un IAM user avec cles = mauvaise pratique et non gere par instance profile
pieges.C: Default Host Configuration Management ne conserve pas forcement les permissions RDS specifiques de l'instance
pieges.D: Retirer les policies existantes casserait l'acces des applications a RDS

explication: En creant un nouveau role IAM avec la policy AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore et en l'ajoutant aux instances (en plus du role existant), on active la gestion par Systems Manager sans retirer les permissions d'acces a RDS. Supprimer les policies du role existant (D) interromprait les applications.

question: A company is planning to deploy a business-critical application in the AWS Cloud. The application requires durable storage with consistent low latency performance. Which type of storage should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?

options.A: Instance store volume
options.B: Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached cluster
options.C: Provisioned IOPS SSD Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume
options.D: Throughput Optimized HDD Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume

radar.signal: Stockage durable a latence faible et constante -> volume Amazon EBS Provisioned IOPS SSD (io1/io2)

pieges.A: L'instance store est ephemere (non durable)
pieges.B: ElastiCache Memcached est un cache en memoire, pas du stockage durable
pieges.D: Throughput Optimized HDD (st1) privilegie le debit sequentiel, pas la latence faible constante

explication: Un volume EBS Provisioned IOPS SSD (io1/io2) offre un stockage durable avec des performances d'IOPS et une latence faibles et constantes, adapte a une application critique. L'instance store est ephemere, Memcached n'est pas du stockage persistant, et le HDD Throughput Optimized vise le debit, pas la latence.

question: An online photo-sharing company stores its photos in an Amazon S3 bucket that exists in the us-west-1 Region. The company needs to store a copy of all new photos in the us-east-1 Region. Which solution will meet this requirement with the LEAST operational effort?

options.A: Create a second S3 bucket in us-east-1. Use S3 Cross-Region Replication to copy photos from the existing S3 bucket to the second S3 bucket.
options.B: Create a cross origin resource sharing (CORS) configuration of the existing S3 bucket. Specify us-east-1 in the CORS rule's AllowedOrigin element.
options.C: Create a second S3 bucket in us-east-1 across multiple Availability Zones. Create an S3 Lifecycle rule to save photos into the second S3 bucket.
options.D: Create a second S3 bucket in us-east-1. Configure S3 event notifications on object creation and update events to invoke an AWS Lambda function to copy photos from the existing S3 bucket to the second S3 bucket.

declencheurs: copy all NEW photos from us-west-1 to us-east-1
radar.signal: Copier automatiquement les nouveaux objets vers une autre Region -> S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR)

pieges.B: CORS gere les acces cross-origin des navigateurs, il ne copie pas d'objets
pieges.C: Une Lifecycle rule ne copie pas d'objets vers un autre bucket/Region
pieges.D: Des event notifications + Lambda = pipeline custom a maintenir face au CRR natif

explication: S3 Cross-Region Replication copie automatiquement chaque nouvel objet du bucket us-west-1 vers un bucket us-east-1, sans code ni maintenance. CORS (acces navigateur) et les Lifecycle rules (transition/expiration) ne copient pas d'objets entre Regions, et une solution Lambda ajouterait de l'overhead.

question: A company has an ordering application that stores customer information in Amazon RDS for MySQL. During regular business hours, employees run one-time queries for reporting purposes. Timeouts are occurring during order processing because the reporting queries are taking too long to run. The company needs to eliminate the timeouts without preventing employees from performing queries. What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

options.A: Create a read replica. Move reporting queries to the read replica.
options.B: Create a read replica. Distribute the ordering application to the primary DB instance and the read replica.
options.C: Migrate the ordering application to Amazon DynamoDB with on-demand capacity.
options.D: Schedule the reporting queries for non-peak hours.

declencheurs: reporting queries cause timeouts during order processing
eliminate timeouts without preventing employee queries
radar.signal: Isoler les requetes de reporting du traitement -> creer un read replica, y deplacer les requetes de reporting

pieges.B: Repartir l'application d'ordering sur le replica ne resout pas le conflit avec le reporting
pieges.C: Migrer vers DynamoDB change le modele de donnees
pieges.D: Planifier les requetes hors pointe empeche les employes de requeter quand ils veulent

explication: En creant un read replica RDS et en y dirigeant les requetes de reporting, celles-ci ne pesent plus sur l'instance primaire qui traite les commandes : les timeouts disparaissent et les employes continuent d'interroger librement le replica. Migrer vers DynamoDB ou restreindre les horaires ne conviennent pas.

question: A hospital wants to create digital copies for its large collection of historical written records. The hospital will continue to add hundreds of new documents each day. The hospital's data team will scan the documents and will upload the documents to the AWS Cloud. A solutions architect must implement a solution to analyze the documents, extract the medical information, and store the documents so that an application can run SQL queries on the data. The solution must maximize scalability and operational efficiency. Which combination of steps should the solutions architect take to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.A: Write the document information to an Amazon EC2 instance that runs a MySQL database.
options.B: Write the document information to an Amazon S3 bucket. Use Amazon Athena to query the data.
options.C: Create an Auto Scaling group of Amazon EC2 instances to run a custom application that processes the scanned files and extracts the medical information.
options.D: Create an AWS Lambda function that runs when new documents are uploaded. Use Amazon Rekognition to convert the documents to raw text. Use Amazon Transcribe Medical to detect and extract relevant medical information from the text.
options.E: Create an AWS Lambda function that runs when new documents are uploaded. Use Amazon Textract to convert the documents to raw text. Use Amazon Comprehend Medical to detect and extract relevant medical information from the text.

declencheurs: run SQL queries on the data
radar.signal: OCR + extraction medicale + SQL serverless -> Lambda + Amazon Textract + Amazon Comprehend Medical (E) ; stocker dans S3 et interroger avec Athena (B)

pieges.A: Un MySQL sur EC2 = base a gerer, moins scalable qu'S3 + Athena
pieges.C: Un Auto Scaling group d'EC2 avec app custom = infrastructure a gerer
pieges.D: Rekognition/Transcribe Medical ne conviennent pas (Rekognition = images/objets, Transcribe = audio)

explication: Une Lambda declenchee a l'upload utilise Amazon Textract pour extraire le texte des documents scannes et Amazon Comprehend Medical pour en tirer les informations medicales (E). Les donnees sont ecrites dans S3 et interrogees en SQL via Amazon Athena (B). C'est serverless et scalable, la ou un MySQL sur EC2 ou une app EC2 custom ajouteraient de l'overhead. Rekognition/Transcribe Medical ne conviennent pas au texte de documents.

question: A company website provides users with downloadable historical performance reports. The website needs a solution that will scale to meet the company website demands globally. The solution should be cost-effective, limit the provisioning of infrastructure resources, and provide the fastest possible response time. Which combination should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?

options.A: Amazon CloudFront and Amazon S3
options.B: AWS Lambda and Amazon DynamoDB
options.C: Application Load Balancer with Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling
options.D: Amazon Route 53 with internal Application Load Balancers

radar.signal: Diffuser des fichiers mondialement, sans infra a provisionner, au plus vite -> Amazon CloudFront + Amazon S3

pieges.B: Lambda + DynamoDB sert des donnees dynamiques, pas la diffusion rapide de fichiers telechargeables
pieges.C: ALB + EC2 Auto Scaling = infrastructure a provisionner et gerer
pieges.D: Route 53 + ALB internes n'est pas une diffusion mondiale de contenu statique

explication: Heberger les rapports dans Amazon S3 et les diffuser via Amazon CloudFront met le contenu en cache aux points de presence proches des utilisateurs du monde entier, pour le temps de reponse le plus rapide, sans provisionner d'infrastructure et a faible cout. Les options a base d'EC2/ALB imposent de gerer des serveurs.

question: A company runs an Oracle database on premises. As part of the company's migration to AWS, the company wants to upgrade the database to the most recent available version. The company also wants to set up disaster recovery (DR) for the database. The company needs to minimize the operational overhead for normal operations and DR setup. The company also needs to maintain access to the database's underlying operating system. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Migrate the Oracle database to an Amazon EC2 instance. Set up database replication to a different AWS Region.
options.B: Migrate the Oracle database to Amazon RDS for Oracle. Activate Cross-Region automated backups to replicate the snapshots to another AWS Region.
options.C: Migrate the Oracle database to Amazon RDS Custom for Oracle. Create a read replica for the database in another AWS Region.
options.D: Migrate the Oracle database to Amazon RDS for Oracle. Create a standby database in another Availability Zone.

radar.signal: Oracle manage MAIS avec acces a l'OS + DR cross-Region -> Amazon RDS Custom for Oracle + read replica dans une autre Region

pieges.A: Oracle sur EC2 = tout auto-gere (plus d'overhead)
pieges.B: RDS for Oracle standard ne donne pas l'acces a l'OS sous-jacent
pieges.D: Un standby dans une autre AZ n'est pas du DR cross-Region

explication: Amazon RDS Custom for Oracle apporte le caractere manage d'RDS tout en donnant l'acces au systeme d'exploitation sous-jacent, requis ici. Un read replica dans une autre Region fournit le DR cross-Region. RDS for Oracle standard ne donne pas l'acces OS, et Oracle sur EC2 maximiserait l'overhead.

question: A company hosts its web application on AWS using seven Amazon EC2 instances. The company requires that the IP addresses of all healthy EC2 instances be returned in response to DNS queries. Which policy should be used to meet this requirement?

options.A: Simple routing policy
options.B: Latency routing policy
options.C: Multivalue routing policy
options.D: Geolocation routing policy

declencheurs: return IP addresses of all healthy instances in DNS response
radar.signal: Renvoyer plusieurs IP saines en reponse DNS -> multivalue routing policy (avec health checks)

pieges.A: La simple routing policy ne fait pas de health check et renvoie un seul enregistrement (ou aleatoire)
pieges.B: La latency routing choisit par latence, pas 'toutes les instances saines'
pieges.D: La geolocation routing choisit par pays

explication: La multivalue answer routing policy de Route 53 renvoie jusqu'a plusieurs enregistrements (les IP des instances) et, associee a des health checks, n'inclut que les instances saines. C'est exactement le besoin de retourner les IP de toutes les instances EC2 en bonne sante.

question: A medical research lab produces data that is related to a new study. The lab wants to make the data available with minimum latency to clinics across the country for their on-premises, file-based applications. The data files are stored in an Amazon S3 bucket that has read-only permissions for each clinic. What should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?

options.A: Deploy an AWS Storage Gateway file gateway as a virtual machine (VM) on premises at each clinic.
options.B: Migrate the files to each clinic's on-premises applications by using AWS DataSync for processing.
options.C: Deploy an AWS Storage Gateway volume gateway as a virtual machine (VM) on premises at each clinic.
options.D: Attach an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system to each clinic's on-premises servers.

declencheurs: make S3 data available with minimum latency
radar.signal: Acces fichier local a faible latence a des donnees S3 -> AWS Storage Gateway file gateway (VM) sur site dans chaque clinique

pieges.B: DataSync copie les fichiers (duplication), il ne fournit pas un acces fichier local a la demande
pieges.C: Le volume gateway est du block iSCSI, pas un acces fichier aux objets S3
pieges.D: EFS ne se monte pas directement sur des serveurs on-prem comme cache local S3

explication: Un AWS Storage Gateway file gateway deploye en VM dans chaque clinique presente les fichiers du bucket S3 en acces fichier local, avec cache pour une faible latence, tout en respectant les permissions en lecture seule. Le volume gateway (block) et DataSync (copie) ne repondent pas a cet acces fichier local a la demande.

question: A company hosts its application in the AWS Cloud. The application runs on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Elastic Load Balancer in an Auto Scaling group and with an Amazon DynamoDB table. The company wants to ensure the application can be made available in another AWS Region with minimal downtime. What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements with the LEAST amount of downtime?

options.A: Create an Auto Scaling group and a load balancer in the disaster recovery Region. Configure the DynamoDB table as a global table. Configure DNS failover to point to the new disaster recovery Region's load balancer.
options.B: Create an AWS CloudFormation template to create EC2 instances, load balancers, and DynamoDB tables to be launched when needed. Configure DNS failover to point to the new disaster recovery Region's load balancer.
options.C: Create an AWS CloudFormation template to create EC2 instances and a load balancer to be launched when needed. Configure the DynamoDB table as a global table. Configure DNS failover to point to the new disaster recovery Region's load balancer.
options.D: Create an Auto Scaling group and load balancer in the disaster recovery Region. Configure the DynamoDB table as a global table. Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm to trigger an AWS Lambda function that updates Amazon Route 53 pointing to the disaster recovery load balancer.

radar.signal: DR a downtime minimal -> ASG + load balancer deja provisionnes dans la Region DR + DynamoDB global table + bascule DNS

pieges.B: Creer l'infra via CloudFormation au moment du sinistre allonge le downtime
pieges.C: Provisionner EC2/LB a la demande = plus de downtime qu'une infra prete
pieges.D: Attendre une alarme + Lambda pour mettre a jour Route 53 = downtime supplementaire evitable

explication: Pour minimiser le downtime, l'Auto Scaling group et le load balancer doivent deja exister dans la Region DR, avec la table DynamoDB en global table (replication active multi-Region). Une bascule DNS redirige alors le trafic quasi immediatement, contrairement aux options qui creent l'infra apres le sinistre.

question: A company needs to migrate a MySQL database from its on-premises data center to AWS within 2 weeks. The database is 20 TB in size. The company wants to complete the migration with minimal downtime. Which solution will migrate the database MOST cost-effectively?

options.A: Order an AWS Snowball Edge Storage Optimized device. Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) with AWS Schema Conversion Tool (AWS SCT) to migrate the database with replication of ongoing changes. Send the Snowball Edge device to AWS to finish the migration and continue the ongoing replication.
options.B: Order an AWS Snowmobile vehicle. Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) with AWS Schema Conversion Tool (AWS SCT) to migrate the database with ongoing changes. Send the Snowmobile vehicle back to AWS to finish the migration and continue the ongoing replication.
options.C: Order an AWS Snowball Edge Compute Optimized with GPU device. Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) with AWS Schema Conversion Tool (AWS SCT) to migrate the database with ongoing changes. Send the Snowball device to AWS to finish the migration and continue the ongoing replication.
options.D: Order a 1 GB dedicated AWS Direct Connect connection to establish a connection with the data center. Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) with AWS Schema Conversion Tool (AWS SCT) to migrate the database with replication of ongoing changes.

radar.signal: Gros volume + delai court + downtime minimal -> Snowball Edge Storage Optimized + DMS (avec SCT) et replication continue des changements

pieges.B: Snowmobile = echelle petaoctet, surdimensionne pour 20 To
pieges.C: Le Snowball Edge Compute Optimized avec GPU est inutile (pas de besoin de calcul GPU)
pieges.D: Un Direct Connect 1 Gbps a commander/installer ne tient pas les 2 semaines pour 20 To

explication: Un Snowball Edge Storage Optimized transfere physiquement les 20 To dans les delais, et AWS DMS (avec SCT) replique les changements en continu pour un basculement a downtime minimal. Snowmobile (petaoctet) est surdimensionne, la variante GPU est inutile, et un Direct Connect a provisionner serait trop lent a mettre en place.

question: A company wants to experiment with individual AWS accounts for its engineer team. The company wants to be notified as soon as the Amazon EC2 instance usage for a given month exceeds a specific threshold for each account. What should a solutions architect do to meet this requirement MOST cost-effectively?

options.A: Use Cost Explorer to create a daily report of costs by service. Filter the report by EC2 instances. Configure Cost Explorer to send an Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES) notification when a threshold is exceeded.
options.B: Use Cost Explorer to create a monthly report of costs by service. Filter the report by EC2 instances. Configure Cost Explorer to send an Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES) notification when a threshold is exceeded.
options.C: Use AWS Budgets to create a cost budget for each account. Set the period to monthly. Set the scope to EC2 instances. Set an alert threshold for the budget. Configure an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic to receive a notification when a threshold is exceeded.
options.D: Use AWS Cost and Usage Reports to create a report with hourly granularity. Integrate the report data with Amazon Athena. Use Amazon EventBridge to schedule an Athena query. Configure an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic to receive a notification when a threshold is exceeded.

declencheurs: notify when monthly EC2 usage exceeds a threshold per account
radar.signal: Alerte de depassement de seuil de cout EC2 par compte -> AWS Budgets (budget mensuel, scope EC2, seuil) + notification SNS

pieges.A: Cost Explorer n'envoie pas d'alertes de seuil comme AWS Budgets ; report quotidien inadapte
pieges.B: Cost Explorer ne declenche pas de notification sur seuil
pieges.D: CUR + Athena + EventBridge = solution complexe et couteuse pour un simple seuil

explication: AWS Budgets permet de creer, par compte, un budget mensuel limite aux instances EC2 avec un seuil d'alerte ; une notification SNS est envoyee des le depassement. C'est le moyen le plus simple et economique, la ou Cost Explorer ne gere pas d'alertes de seuil et CUR + Athena serait bien plus lourd.

question: A solutions architect needs to design a new microservice for a company's application. Clients must be able to call an HTTPS endpoint to reach the microservice. The microservice also must use AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) to authenticate calls. The solutions architect will write the logic for this microservice by using a single AWS Lambda function that is written in Go 1.x. Which solution will deploy the function in the MOST operationally efficient way?

options.A: Create an Amazon API Gateway REST API. Configure the method to use the Lambda function. Enable IAM authentication on the API.
options.B: Create a Lambda function URL for the function. Specify AWS_IAM as the authentication type.
options.C: Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution. Deploy the function to Lambda@Edge. Integrate IAM authentication logic into the Lambda@Edge function.
options.D: Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution. Deploy the function to CloudFront Functions. Specify AWS_IAM as the authentication type.

radar.signal: Exposer une seule Lambda en HTTPS avec auth IAM au plus simple -> Lambda function URL avec type d'authentification AWS_IAM

pieges.A: Une REST API API Gateway fonctionne mais ajoute un service a gerer (moins 'efficient' pour une seule fonction)
pieges.C: Lambda@Edge avec logique IAM custom = complexe
pieges.D: CloudFront Functions ne supporte pas AWS_IAM ni ce cas d'usage

alerte_cle: La cle du fichier indique A (API Gateway REST), mais pour exposer UNE seule Lambda en HTTPS avec auth IAM 'le plus efficacement', une Lambda function URL avec AWS_IAM (B) est plus legere (pas de service supplementaire a gerer). A verifier selon la formulation attendue.
explication: Une Lambda function URL fournit directement un endpoint HTTPS a la fonction et, en definissant le type d'authentification AWS_IAM, impose l'authentification IAM des appels, sans deployer ni gerer API Gateway. Pour une fonction unique, c'est la maniere la plus efficace operationnellement. API Gateway (A) reste valable mais ajoute un composant a exploiter.

question: A solutions architect is designing a highly available Amazon ElastiCache for Redis based solution. The solutions architect needs to ensure that failures do not result in performance degradation or loss of data locally and within an AWS Region. The solution needs to provide high availability at the node level and at the Region level. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Use Multi-AZ Redis replication groups with shards that contain multiple nodes.
options.B: Use Redis shards that contain multiple nodes with Redis append only files (AOF) turned on.
options.C: Use a Multi-AZ Redis cluster with more than one read replica in the replication group.
options.D: Use Redis shards that contain multiple nodes with Auto Scaling turned on.

declencheurs: no data loss locally and within a Region
HA at node level AND Region level
radar.signal: HA au niveau noeud et Region + pas de perte -> replication groups Redis Multi-AZ avec des shards contenant plusieurs noeuds

pieges.B: Les AOF n'assurent pas la haute disponibilite au niveau Region
pieges.C: Un cluster Multi-AZ avec des replicas de lecture couvre la HA de noeud, mais la formulation ne garantit pas la resilience decrite comme les replication groups multi-noeuds
pieges.D: L'Auto Scaling ne fournit pas la replication/HA requise

explication: Des replication groups Redis Multi-AZ, avec des shards comportant plusieurs noeuds (primaire + replicas repartis sur les AZ), offrent la haute disponibilite au niveau des noeuds et de la Region avec bascule automatique, evitant la perte de donnees. Les AOF (persistance locale) ou l'Auto Scaling ne fournissent pas cette HA multi-AZ.

question: A company plans to migrate to AWS and use Amazon EC2 On-Demand Instances for its application. During the migration testing phase, a technical team observes that the application takes a long time to launch and load memory to become fully productive. Which solution will reduce the launch time of the application during the next testing phase?

options.A: Launch two or more EC2 On-Demand Instances. Turn on auto scaling features and make the EC2 On-Demand Instances available during the next testing phase.
options.B: Launch EC2 Spot Instances to support the application and to scale the application so it is available during the next testing phase.
options.C: Launch the EC2 On-Demand Instances with hibernation turned on. Configure EC2 Auto Scaling warm pools during the next testing phase.
options.D: Launch EC2 On-Demand Instances with Capacity Reservations. Start additional EC2 instances during the next testing phase.

declencheurs: application takes long to launch and load memory
radar.signal: Reduire le temps de demarrage/chargement memoire -> EC2 avec hibernation + Auto Scaling warm pools

pieges.A: Lancer plusieurs instances + auto scaling ne reduit pas le temps de chargement individuel
pieges.B: Les Spot ne reduisent pas le temps de demarrage (et peuvent etre interrompues)
pieges.D: Les Capacity Reservations garantissent la capacite, pas le temps de chargement memoire

explication: L'hibernation EC2 preserve l'etat de la memoire, et les warm pools d'Auto Scaling maintiennent des instances pre-initialisees pretes a servir : au lancement, l'application est deja chargee en memoire, ce qui reduit fortement le temps de mise en service. Les Capacity Reservations ou les Spot ne traitent pas le temps de chargement.

question: A weather forecasting company needs to process hundreds of gigabytes of data with sub-millisecond latency. The company has a high performance computing (HPC) environment in its data center and wants to expand its forecasting capabilities. A solutions architect must identify a highly available cloud storage solution that can handle large amounts of sustained throughput. Files that are stored in the solution should be accessible to thousands of compute instances that will simultaneously access and process the entire dataset. What should the solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

options.A: Use Amazon FSx for Lustre scratch file systems.
options.B: Use Amazon FSx for Lustre persistent file systems.
options.C: Use Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) with Bursting Throughput mode.
options.D: Use Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) with Provisioned Throughput mode.

declencheurs: thousands of instances access entire dataset simultaneously
radar.signal: Debit soutenu + faible latence + HA pour du HPC -> Amazon FSx for Lustre en persistent file system

pieges.A: Le scratch file system n'est pas hautement disponible/durable (stockage temporaire)
pieges.C: EFS en Bursting Throughput ne soutient pas le debit HPC requis
pieges.D: EFS meme en Provisioned Throughput n'atteint pas la latence/debit d'FSx for Lustre pour le HPC

explication: Amazon FSx for Lustre en mode persistant offre un stockage hautement disponible et durable avec latence sub-milliseconde et debit soutenu eleve, accessible en parallele par des milliers d'instances : c'est le systeme de fichiers HPC adapte. Le scratch (temporaire, non HA) et EFS ne tiennent pas ces exigences.

question: An ecommerce company runs a PostgreSQL database on premises. The database stores data by using high IOPS Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) block storage. The daily peak I/O transactions per second do not exceed 15,000 IOPS. The company wants to migrate the database to Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL and provision disk IOPS performance independent of disk storage capacity. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

options.A: Configure the General Purpose SSD (gp2) EBS volume storage type and provision 15,000 IOPS.
options.B: Configure the Provisioned IOPS SSD (io1) EBS volume storage type and provision 15,000 IOPS.
options.C: Configure the General Purpose SSD (gp3) EBS volume storage type and provision 15,000 IOPS.
options.D: Configure the EBS magnetic volume type to achieve maximum IOPS.

declencheurs: provision IOPS independent of storage capacity
radar.signal: IOPS decouplees de la capacite jusqu'a 16000, au meilleur cout -> stockage gp3 avec 15000 IOPS provisionnees

pieges.A: gp2 lie les IOPS a la taille du volume (non decouple)
pieges.B: io1 provisionne 15000 IOPS mais coute plus cher que gp3
pieges.D: Le magnetique n'atteint pas ces IOPS

explication: gp3 permet de provisionner les IOPS (jusqu'a 16000) independamment de la capacite de stockage, ce qui couvre les 15000 IOPS a un cout inferieur a io1. gp2 fait dependre les IOPS de la taille du volume, et le magnetique est trop lent.

question: A meteorological startup company has a custom web application to sell weather data to its users online. The company uses Amazon DynamoDB to store its data and wants to build a new service that sends an alert to the managers of four internal teams every time a new weather event is recorded. The company does not want this new service to affect the performance of the current application. What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements with the LEAST amount of operational overhead?

options.A: Use DynamoDB transactions to write new event data to the table. Configure the transactions to notify internal teams.
options.B: Have the current application publish a message to four Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topics. Have each team subscribe to one topic.
options.C: Enable Amazon DynamoDB Streams on the table. Use triggers to write to a single Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic to which the teams can subscribe.
options.D: Add a custom attribute to each record to flag new items. Write a cron job that scans the table every minute for items that are new and notifies an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue to which the teams can subscribe.

declencheurs: alert 4 internal teams on each new weather event in DynamoDB
do not affect current application performance
radar.signal: Reagir aux nouveaux items DynamoDB sans impacter l'app -> DynamoDB Streams + trigger vers un topic SNS auquel les equipes s'abonnent

pieges.A: Les transactions DynamoDB n'envoient pas de notifications aux equipes
pieges.B: Publier sur 4 topics depuis l'application couple la notification a l'app (impact possible) et multiplie les topics
pieges.D: Un cron qui scanne chaque minute = solution custom couteuse et non temps reel

explication: En activant DynamoDB Streams, un trigger (Lambda) publie chaque nouvel evenement vers un unique topic SNS auquel les quatre equipes s'abonnent. Le mecanisme est decouple de l'application (aucun impact sur ses performances) et sans scan periodique. Faire publier l'application elle-meme couplerait la notification a son execution.

question: A company wants to use the AWS Cloud to make an existing application highly available and resilient. The current version of the application resides in the company's data center. The application recently experienced data loss after a database server crashed because of an unexpected power outage. The company needs a solution that avoids any single points of failure. The solution must give the application the ability to scale to meet user demand. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Deploy the application servers by using Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones. Use an Amazon RDS DB instance in a Multi-AZ configuration.
options.B: Deploy the application servers by using Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group in a single Availability Zone. Deploy the database on an EC2 instance. Enable EC2 Auto Recovery.
options.C: Deploy the application servers by using Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones. Use an Amazon RDS DB instance with a read replica in a single Availability Zone. Promote the read replica to replace the primary DB instance if the primary DB instance fails.
options.D: Deploy the application servers by using Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones. Deploy the primary and secondary database servers on EC2 instances across multiple Availability Zones. Use Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) Multi-Attach to create shared storage between the instances.

declencheurs: make existing app highly available and resilient
recent data loss after DB server crash
avoid any single point of failure
radar.signal: Eliminer les SPOF + scaler -> EC2 en Auto Scaling group multi-AZ + Amazon RDS en Multi-AZ

pieges.B: Une seule AZ + base sur EC2 = points de defaillance uniques
pieges.C: Un read replica dans une seule AZ avec promotion manuelle n'est pas une HA automatique
pieges.D: EBS Multi-Attach + bases sur EC2 = complexe et non hautement disponible nativement

explication: Un Auto Scaling group d'EC2 reparti sur plusieurs AZ (scalabilite + pas de SPOF applicatif) et une base Amazon RDS en Multi-AZ (bascule automatique vers un standby dans une autre AZ, pas de perte de donnees) eliminent les points de defaillance uniques. Les options mono-AZ ou base sur EC2 laissent des SPOF.

question: A solutions architect needs to allow team members to access Amazon S3 buckets in two different AWS accounts: a development account and a production account. The team currently has access to S3 buckets in the development account by using unique IAM users that are assigned to an IAM group that has appropriate permissions in the account. The solutions architect has created an IAM role in the production account. The role has a policy that grants access to an S3 bucket in the production account. Which solution will meet these requirements while complying with the principle of least privilege?

options.A: Attach the Administrator Access policy to the development account users.
options.B: Add the development account as a principal in the trust policy of the role in the production account.
options.C: Turn off the S3 Block Public Access feature on the S3 bucket in the production account.
options.D: Create a user in the production account with unique credentials for each team member.

declencheurs: team access S3 in dev and prod accounts
IAM role created in prod granting bucket access
radar.signal: Acces cross-account par role -> ajouter le compte de developpement comme principal dans la trust policy du role du compte de production

pieges.A: AdministratorAccess viole totalement le moindre privilege
pieges.C: Desactiver Block Public Access exposerait le bucket (dangereux)
pieges.D: Creer des IAM users dedies dans le compte prod = gestion d'identites en double

explication: Le role de production existe deja avec la policy d'acces au bucket ; il suffit d'ajouter le compte de developpement comme principal de confiance dans sa trust policy. Les utilisateurs du dev assument alors ce role pour acceder au bucket prod, en respectant le moindre privilege, sans creer d'identites en double ni exposer le bucket.

question: A company uses AWS Organizations with all features enabled and runs multiple Amazon EC2 workloads in the ap-southeast-2 Region. The company has a service control policy (SCP) that prevents any resources from being created in any other Region. A security policy requires the company to encrypt all data at rest. An audit discovers that employees have created Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes for EC2 instances without encrypting the volumes. The company wants any new EC2 instances that any IAM user or root user launches in ap-southeast-2 to use encrypted EBS volumes. The company wants a solution that will have minimal effect on employees who create EBS volumes. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.A: In the Amazon EC2 console, select the EBS encryption account attribute and define a default encryption key.
options.B: Create an IAM permission boundary. Attach the permission boundary to the root organizational unit (OU). Define the boundary to deny the ec2:CreateVolume action when the ec2:Encrypted condition equals false.
options.C: Create an SCP. Attach the SCP to the root organizational unit (OU). Define the SCP to deny the ec2:CreateVolume action when the ec2:Encrypted condition equals false.
options.D: Update the IAM policies for each account to deny the ec2:CreateVolume action when the ec2:Encrypted condition equals false.
options.E: In the Organizations management account, specify the Default EBS volume encryption setting.

declencheurs: all new EC2 in ap-southeast-2 must use encrypted EBS
radar.signal: Chiffrement EBS transparent + garde-fou -> activer l'attribut de chiffrement EBS par defaut avec une cle par defaut dans EC2 (A) + IAM policies refusant ec2:CreateVolume si non chiffre (D)

pieges.B: Un permission boundary ne s'attache pas a une OU (ce n'est pas une SCP)
pieges.C: Une SCP est un garde-fou valable, mais la cle retient les IAM policies (D) ; noter que l'attribut par defaut (A) est ce qui rend l'effet transparent
pieges.E: Il n'y a pas de reglage 'default EBS encryption' global depuis le compte de gestion (c'est par compte/Region)

explication: Activer l'attribut de chiffrement EBS par defaut (avec une cle par defaut) dans EC2 rend tous les nouveaux volumes chiffres de facon transparente, sans changer les habitudes des employes (A). En complement, des IAM policies qui refusent ec2:CreateVolume quand ec2:Encrypted est false imposent le chiffrement comme garde-fou (D). Un permission boundary ne s'attache pas a une OU, et il n'existe pas de reglage global depuis le compte de gestion.

question: A company has launched an Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance. Most of the connections to the database come from serverless applications. Application traffic to the database changes significantly at random intervals. At times of high demand, users report that their applications experience database connection rejection errors. Which solution will resolve this issue with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.A: Create a proxy in RDS Proxy. Configure the users' applications to use the DB instance through RDS Proxy.
options.B: Deploy Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached between the users' applications and the DB instance.
options.C: Migrate the DB instance to a different instance class that has higher I/O capacity. Configure the users' applications to use the new DB instance.
options.D: Configure Multi-AZ for the DB instance. Configure the users' applications to switch between the DB instances.

declencheurs: serverless apps, traffic changes at random
connection rejection errors at high demand
radar.signal: Trop de connexions depuis des apps serverless -> RDS Proxy (pooling de connexions)

pieges.B: ElastiCache Memcached cache des donnees, il ne gere pas les connexions rejetees
pieges.C: Changer de classe d'instance ne resout pas la saturation des connexions et coute plus
pieges.D: Multi-AZ ameliore la disponibilite, pas le nombre de connexions

explication: Les applications serverless (Lambda) ouvrent de nombreuses connexions lors des pics, saturant la base. RDS Proxy mutualise et reutilise les connexions, absorbant les variations sans rejets, avec un minimum d'overhead. Un changement d'instance ou Multi-AZ ne traitent pas le probleme de connexions.

question: A company recently deployed a new auditing system to centralize information about operating system versions, patching, and installed software on Amazon EC2 instances. A solutions architect must ensure all instances provisioned through EC2 Auto Scaling groups successfully send reports to the auditing system as soon as they are launched and terminated. Which solution achieves these goals MOST efficiently?

options.A: Use a scheduled AWS Lambda function and run a script remotely on all EC2 instances to send data to the audit system.
options.B: Use EC2 Auto Scaling lifecycle hooks to run a custom script to send data to the audit system when instances are launched and terminated.
options.C: Use an EC2 Auto Scaling launch configuration to run a custom script through user data to send data to the audit system when instances are launched and terminated.
options.D: Run a custom script on the instance operating system to send data to the audit system. Configure the script to be invoked by the EC2 Auto Scaling group when the instance starts and is terminated.

declencheurs: auditing at instance launch AND termination
instances from EC2 Auto Scaling groups
radar.signal: Executer un script au lancement ET a la terminaison des instances de l'ASG -> Auto Scaling lifecycle hooks

pieges.A: Une Lambda planifiee n'est pas synchronisee avec les evenements de lancement/terminaison
pieges.C: Le user data ne s'execute qu'au lancement, pas a la terminaison
pieges.D: Un script 'invoque par l'ASG au demarrage/terminaison' n'est pas un mecanisme natif sans lifecycle hooks

explication: Les lifecycle hooks d'EC2 Auto Scaling declenchent un script personnalise a la fois au lancement et a la terminaison des instances, ce qui permet d'envoyer les rapports d'audit aux deux moments. Le user data (C) ne s'execute qu'au demarrage, et une Lambda planifiee (A) n'est pas synchronisee avec ces evenements.

question: A solutions architect is creating a data processing job that runs once daily and can take up to 2 hours to complete. If the job is interrupted, it has to restart from the beginning. How should the solutions architect address this issue in the MOST cost-effective manner?

options.A: Create a script that runs locally on an Amazon EC2 Reserved Instance that is triggered by a cron job.
options.B: Create an AWS Lambda function triggered by an Amazon EventBridge scheduled event.
options.C: Use an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) Fargate task triggered by an Amazon EventBridge scheduled event.
options.D: Use an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) task running on Amazon EC2 triggered by an Amazon EventBridge scheduled event.

declencheurs: job once daily up to 2 hours
if interrupted must restart from beginning
radar.signal: Job de 2h non interruptible, planifie, sans gerer de serveur -> tache ECS Fargate declenchee par un evenement EventBridge planifie

pieges.A: Un EC2 Reserved facture en permanence pour un job quotidien
pieges.B: Lambda est limitee a 15 min (le job dure 2h)
pieges.D: ECS sur EC2 impose de gerer des instances (moins economique/plus d'overhead que Fargate)

explication: Le job durant jusqu'a 2h, Lambda (15 min) est exclu. Une tache ECS en Fargate declenchee par un evenement EventBridge planifie execute le traitement quotidien sans serveur a gerer et ne facture que le temps d'execution, ce qui est plus economique qu'un EC2 Reserved permanent ou qu'ECS sur EC2.

question: A social media company wants to store its database of user profiles, relationships, and interactions in the AWS Cloud. The company needs an application to monitor any changes in the database. The application needs to analyze the relationships between the data entities and to provide recommendations to users. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.A: Use Amazon Neptune to store the information. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to process changes in the database.
options.B: Use Amazon Neptune to store the information. Use Neptune Streams to process changes in the database.
options.C: Use Amazon Quantum Ledger Database (Amazon QLDB) to store the information. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to process changes in the database.
options.D: Use Amazon Quantum Ledger Database (Amazon QLDB) to store the information. Use Neptune Streams to process changes in the database.

radar.signal: Donnees de graphe + suivi des changements natif -> Amazon Neptune + Neptune Streams

pieges.A: Kinesis Data Streams pour suivre les changements Neptune = pipeline supplementaire (Neptune Streams est natif)
pieges.C: QLDB est un registre immuable, pas une base de graphe pour l'analyse de relations
pieges.D: QLDB + Neptune Streams est incoherent (Neptune Streams appartient a Neptune)

explication: Amazon Neptune, base de donnees graphe manageee, est ideale pour analyser les relations entre entites et generer des recommandations. Neptune Streams capture nativement les changements de la base pour l'application de suivi, sans pipeline additionnel. QLDB (registre immuable) ne convient pas a l'analyse de graphe.

question: A company wants to analyze and generate reports to track the usage of its mobile app. The app is popular and has a global user base. The company uses a custom report building program to analyze application usage. The program generates multiple reports during the last week of each month. The program takes less than 10 minutes to produce each report. The company rarely uses the program to generate reports outside of the last week of each month. The company wants to generate reports in the least amount of time when the reports are requested. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

options.A: Run the program by using Amazon EC2 On-Demand Instances. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to start the EC2 instances when reports are requested. Run the EC2 instances continuously during the last week of each month.
options.B: Run the program in AWS Lambda. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to run a Lambda function when reports are requested.
options.C: Run the program in Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS). Schedule Amazon ECS to run the program when reports are requested.
options.D: Run the program by using Amazon EC2 Spot Instances. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to start the EC2 instances when reports are requested. Run the EC2 instances continuously during the last week of each month.

declencheurs: reports mostly during last week of month
radar.signal: Traitement bref (<10 min), intermittent, a la demande -> AWS Lambda declenchee par une regle EventBridge

pieges.A: Faire tourner des EC2 On-Demand en continu une semaine par mois = cout inutile hors execution
pieges.C: ECS a la demande est plus lourd qu'une Lambda pour un job de <10 min
pieges.D: Des Spot en continu une semaine = cout continu et risque d'interruption

explication: Chaque rapport prenant moins de 10 minutes (sous la limite de 15 min de Lambda) et etant demande de facon intermittente, AWS Lambda declenchee par une regle EventBridge ne coute rien au repos et demarre instantanement a la demande. Faire tourner des EC2 en continu une semaine par mois serait bien plus cher.

question: A company is designing a tightly coupled high performance computing (HPC) environment in the AWS Cloud. The company needs to include features that will optimize the HPC environment for networking and storage. Which combination of solutions will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.A: Create an accelerator in AWS Global Accelerator. Configure custom routing for the accelerator.
options.B: Create an Amazon FSx for Lustre file system. Configure the file system with scratch storage.
options.C: Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution. Configure the viewer protocol policy to be HTTP and HTTPS.
options.D: Launch Amazon EC2 instances. Attach an Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA) to the instances.
options.E: Create an AWS Elastic Beanstalk deployment to manage the environment.

radar.signal: Optimiser reseau et stockage HPC -> FSx for Lustre (scratch) pour le stockage (B) + Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA) pour le reseau (D)

pieges.A: Global Accelerator optimise l'acces mondial d'applications, pas un HPC tightly coupled
pieges.C: CloudFront est un CDN, sans rapport avec le HPC
pieges.E: Elastic Beanstalk gere des apps web, pas un environnement HPC

explication: Pour un HPC tightly coupled, l'Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA) fournit un reseau a faible latence et haut debit entre instances (D), et Amazon FSx for Lustre (scratch) offre le stockage parallele hautes performances (B). Global Accelerator, CloudFront et Elastic Beanstalk ne concernent pas ce type d'environnement HPC.

question: A solutions architect needs to host a high performance computing (HPC) workload in the AWS Cloud. The workload will run on hundreds of Amazon EC2 instances and will require parallel access to a shared file system to enable distributed processing of large datasets. Datasets will be accessed across multiple instances simultaneously. The workload requires access latency within 1 ms. After processing has completed, engineers will need access to the dataset for manual postprocessing. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Use Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) as a shared file system. Access the dataset from Amazon EFS.
options.B: Mount an Amazon S3 bucket to serve as the shared file system. Perform postprocessing directly from the S3 bucket.
options.C: Use Amazon FSx for Lustre as a shared file system. Link the file system to an Amazon S3 bucket for postprocessing.
options.D: Configure AWS Resource Access Manager to share an Amazon S3 bucket so that it can be mounted to all instances for processing and postprocessing.

declencheurs: parallel access to shared file system
radar.signal: Systeme de fichiers parallele <1 ms + postprocessing -> Amazon FSx for Lustre lie a un bucket S3

pieges.A: EFS n'atteint pas la latence <1 ms ni le debit parallele HPC requis
pieges.B: Monter un bucket S3 comme systeme de fichiers ne fournit pas la latence <1 ms d'un systeme parallele
pieges.D: RAM partage un bucket S3, ce qui n'est pas un systeme de fichiers HPC a faible latence

explication: Amazon FSx for Lustre fournit un systeme de fichiers parallele avec une latence inferieure a 1 ms, accessible simultanement par des centaines d'instances pour le calcul distribue. En le liant a un bucket S3, les donnees restent disponibles pour le postprocessing manuel des ingenieurs. EFS et S3 monte ne tiennent pas la latence <1 ms exigee.
